# Experiment log — what we ran, and what it concluded

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/eval/build-experiments.mjs from scripts/eval/experiments/*.md
     on main, after each merge (eval-ledgers-regenerate.yml). Do not edit this file:
     add ONE file under scripts/eval/experiments/ (see its README.md) and never touch
     this one in a PR — two PRs appending here is the conflict #5436 removed. -->

PRIOR ART: `recommend-experiments.mjs` ranks experiments still *worth running*;
`INDEX.md` lists the scripts that exist. Neither records **what a run concluded**,
which is the thing that evaporates. This is that record.

**Where to write (#5436).** One entry = ONE new file in `scripts/eval/experiments/`,
named `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`, beginning with the heading `## YYYY-MM-DD · <question>`
(the date in the name and the heading must agree). Never edit `EXPERIMENTS.md`
itself: it is generated from these files on `main` after every merge
(`.github/workflows/eval-ledgers-regenerate.yml`), and CI refuses a PR that
hand-edits it. Why: when every eval PR appended to the same tail of one file, two
PRs on the same day were a textual conflict every time — 6 of 11 conflicting PRs
on 2026-10-01 — and auto-merge never merges a conflicting PR. Two files never
conflict. To read the whole log locally without waiting for main:
`node scripts/eval/build-experiments.mjs --print`.

Standing series (one table, a row per run, e.g. the monthly corpus audit) live in
`_series-<slug>.md` and render before the dated entries; notes about the log itself
in `_note-<slug>.md`, rendered last. The series files are `merge=union` in
`.gitattributes` so two rows appended by two PRs both survive a local rebase.

Newest first in the generated file. One entry per *question*, not per invocation. A
null result and a retraction are both first-class entries — the retractions are the
most valuable rows here, because a wrong number that stays uncorrected in a PR
description is how a mistake becomes doctrine.

**Rare-event discipline.** These runs happen a few times a month at most, so
nobody remembers them and nobody will re-read the code. Two lines here when you
finish is the whole mechanism. If you ran something and did not log it, the next
person pays for it again.

**Format.** Date · question · design · result · *replicated?* · artifact.
The replication column exists because of 2026-09-02, below.

## The header (#5939)

Every dated entry opens with YAML front matter: the first line of the file is `---`,
above any `PRIOR ART` line and the `## YYYY-MM-DD` heading. It is what lets the
index (`index.json`), the `/quality` Experiments section and the canon pages read an
entry without anyone editing a page by hand, and what lets a superseded result drop
off them. The builder leaves it out of `EXPERIMENTS.md`.

```yaml
---
stage: translation
measure: judged_vs_reference
languages: [sa, pi, lzh]
scripts: [Deva, Hani]
canons: [sanskrit, pali, chinese-buddhist]
n_books: 68
n_pages: 68
verdict: "Flash reverses fewer statements than Flash-Lite in all three languages."
status: adopted
decision: "Flash routes Sanskrit, Pali and Chinese translation (PR #5740)"
superseded_by: null
issue: [5695, 5740]
---
```

| field | required | value |
|---|---|---|
| `stage` | yes | `ocr` \| `translation` \| `metadata` \| `image` \| `pipeline` — the stage the result is about |
| `measure` | yes | `accuracy` \| `agreement` \| `stability` \| `preference` \| `judged` \| `judged_vs_reference` (eval-design.md §2, §5.2), or `none` for a plan, census or repair log. A list when one entry reports two, the deciding one first |
| `languages` | no | ISO 639 codes, `[la, grc, lzh]`; `[]` when not language-specific |
| `scripts` | no | ISO 15924 codes, `[Latn, Grek, Tibt]`; `[]` when not script-specific |
| `canons` | no | canon-gap ids (`derge-tengyur`, `pali`, `sanskrit` … the `corpora` and `traditions` ids in `scripts/catalog-coverage/results/canon-gap-status-*.json`); `[]` for none |
| `n_books`, `n_pages` | no | whole numbers, the sample the verdict rests on; `null` if not stated |
| `verdict` | yes | one line, quoted: what the run found |
| `status` | yes | `adopted` (a lane or prompt changed) \| `rejected` (tested, not taken) \| `undecided` (a decision is still owed) \| `superseded` (a later file answers the same question) \| `informational` (a measurement, no decision asked of it) |
| `decision` | no | what it changed, with the PR or issue: `"v19.1 is the production OCR prompt (PR #5655)"` |
| `superseded_by` | with `superseded` | the later file's name in this directory |
| `issue` | no | the issue number, or a list |
| `router_evidence` | for a judged `ocr` / `translation` result | the router-table cells (`scripts/eval/estimator/router-table/rules.json` `cells[].id`) this run added evidence to, `[latin-lite, german-lite]` — or `"none — <why>"` (a prompt test, no route compared). Required on NEW entries whose `measure` includes `judged` or `judged_vs_reference` (#7263): a judged result the router never reads does not change a route |
| `defect_rates` | for an `ocr` / `translation` result dated 2026-10-30 or later | a repo path to the JSON with, per route, misleads and wrong_text per 1,000 words and the mean fidelity (`scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/defect-rate.py` writes one: run its `inventory` stage, then the `.py`) — or `"none — <why>"` (nothing was judged for defects). Required on NEW entries with a `measure` other than `none` (#6740): routes are decided on severity-weighted defect rates against the live route; accept k/n is a summary (eval-design.md §10.3, proposed in `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/results/defect-rate-2026-10-30/eval-design-10.3.md`) |

Strings are double-quoted; lists sit on one line; nothing else of YAML is read
(`scripts/eval/lib/experiment-header.mjs`). **Changing a result's status is
editing the header only** — e.g. when a later run overturns this one, set
`status: superseded` and `superseded_by:` here, in the same PR that adds the later
file. Never rewrite the body of an entry that has already landed: add a new entry.

CI (`scripts/eval/experiments-lint.mjs`, in `unit-tests.yml`) refuses a new dated
entry without a valid header, a new judged OCR or translation entry without
`router_evidence`, a new OCR or translation entry (from 2026-10-30) without
`defect_rates`, and an invalid header on any file. A weekly detector
(`scripts/audit/experiments-garden.mjs`) lists entries with no header, `undecided`
entries left over 21 days, public pages that cite a superseded entry, and live
entries whose verdicts disagree.

## Fortnightly spot check (#5914) — what does a reader meet, read against the page images?

One row per fortnight (newest first), written by the review routine (`scripts/eval/spot-check/ROUTINE.md`) from
`scripts/eval/spot-check/score.mjs`. Design: every other Monday, 10 public books drawn uniformly per BOOK (seed = the
draw date), a random run of 3 consecutive translated pages each, read against the images by 2 blind Opus reviewers
with the frozen brief `scripts/eval/spot-check/REVIEWER.md`. A **serious** error misleads a reader about what the
source says or is (sense reversed, text invented or dropped, wrong leaf). An **on-sight defect** is anything an expert
would flag opening the book: a serious error, a wrong shelf, a rights problem, broken structure, or leaked markup.

**The headline is the rolling 8-week window** (about 40 books, 120 pages), with a 95% CI resampled by BOOK, because the
3 pages of one book are one observation. One fortnight's 10 books move by chance; read the window. The window pools
only runs from the same frame.

Not comparable with the monthly audit's "any major" rate (whole corpus, one interior page, translation only, page
ends excluded). This arm counts transcription, wrong-leaf and structure errors too.

| date | frame | books | pages | pages with ≥ 1 serious (%) | books with an on-sight defect | rolling 8-week: pages with a serious error (CI) | rolling 8-week: books with an on-sight defect (CI) | top 3 classes (pages) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-06 (month 0) | canon shelves, any visibility, 30 books | 30 | 91 | 21 (23%) | ≈ 18 | 23% (12–35)¹ — baseline, not pooled | 60% (43–77)² | by books, no classes recorded: reversed sense (7 books), broken structure (6), text not on the page (5) |

¹ Month 0 CI resampled by book from the 25 books whose per-book results survive (ops `rights-screen/2026-10-06-canon-shelves/spot30/result0–4.json`)
plus batch 5's 16 pages and 2 serious pages, assumed spread over two of its five books (the batch's JSON was not written). The 25 books alone give
25% (13–39). Entry: `2026-10-06-random-book-spot-check-canon-shelves-5914.md`.
² Month 0 judged on-sight defects as a count (≈ 18 of 30), not per book; the CI treats it as exactly 18.

**Design change before the first fortnightly draw (2026-10-19):** `draw.mjs` now draws runs only from pages with
`page_number > 0`. Records at ≤ 0 are soft-hidden and never render (`scripts/lib/page-counts.mjs`, #3293), but they can carry
translations, so the unfiltered draw could pick a run no reader sees. That hole was found by the #6056 shelf overview, which drew 6 of 96.
Replayed over the eight draw dates 2026-10-19 → 2027-01-25, the old filter put 2 of 80 runs on such pages (2026-11-30, 2026-12-28).
The new filter puts 0 there. It draws the same books, and every other book keeps the same run. Month 0's draw is in the
ops repo and was not re-checked here.

## 2026-11-01 · Which pages carry another leaf's text? A judge-free screen over every live OCR'd book (#7866)

PRIOR ART:
- `scripts/audit/page-integrity.mjs` walks a local mirror this box lacks, and its duplicate check compares N with N+1 and N+2 only (`duplicateScan`).
- `scripts/audit/ia-model-ocr-off-leaf.mjs` covers IA books only. It matches the text against the Archive's own OCR and abstains where that OCR is junk: on the 1488 incunable `69af4864…`, 3 of 248 pages scored.
- `scripts/audit/bulk-archive-alignment.mjs` / `scripts/lib/page-alignment.mjs checkAlignment` dHash the archived image against its source at offsets 0 and +1 only, so `69af4864…` (−3) reads `ambiguous`.
- `scripts/eval/jev/clef-*` (#5803) puts a model on every page.
- `scripts/audit/page-repeat-images.mjs` compares images with no text.
- Reused unchanged: `block-drift.mjs sourceProse`, `page-integrity.mjs foldWord`, `page-alignment.mjs hashBuffer`/`hammingHex`, and the thumbnail correlation `page-repeat-images.mjs` validated on #5056.

Code:
- `scripts/lib/leaf-alignment.mjs` (pure signals and the confirm rule; tests in `tests/unit/leaf-alignment.test.ts`).
- `scripts/audit/leaf-alignment-screen.mjs` (stages `scan`, `arbitrate`, `rank`).
- Results: `scripts/eval/results/leaf-alignment-screen-7866/`.
- Raw rows (47,435 scan rows, every arbitration): R2 `sl-corpus-snapshots` `cold/l7a/leaf-screen-7866/leaf-alignment-screen-2026-11-01.tar.zst` (9,571,154 bytes, sha256 `8d818e31…7b96c4`).

**Question.** Both books contained on #7866 showed the same failure: page text that is another leaf's. In one, the text sits 3+ leaves off its images; in the other, a blank leaf carries text and the opening is repeated. Can that be found in every live book without a judge?

### Method

**1. Scan (free: Mongo only, 22 min on earthai-l7a; no API, no model).** Per book, for every visible page, the scan reads: the first 1,200 characters of `ocr.data` and its length, `page_type`, `archive_metadata.{bytes,source}`, and `image_width`/`image_height`. Three signals come out of it:
- **Repeat.** Word 5-gram shingles (letter 8-grams in unsegmented scripts) are compared across all pages of a book. Shingles on more than a quarter of the pages are dropped as boilerplate. A pair is kept at containment ≥ 0.6.
- **Text on a near-blank image.** A text of ≥ 300 prose characters, mostly letters, whose image weighs under 0.25 of the median for that archiver. Weight is bytes per megapixel, from bytes the archiver already stored.
- **Offset.** Text length against image weight, correlated at shifts −6…6. Illustrated pages are left out (a herbal alternates plate and description).
  - A #3368 repair re-archived images without rewriting `archive_metadata.bytes`. Bytes on repaired books' `bulk_jp2` pages are stale (`69e41331…` p.29: stored 534,384 B is the old leaf 30), so they are ignored.

**2. Arbitrate (free: our R2 images and the providers' source images).** Each candidate is checked against the images themselves:
- **Image shift.** The shown image is dHashed against the source image of pages n−6…n+6. Where dHash cannot separate two pages of one layout, a 64×80 thumbnail correlation decides.
  - The Archive's `page/nK_s4.jpg` is the same leaf as its IIIF form (dHash 2) and ~4× faster.
- **Blank.** The shown image's ink share: pixels 15 grey levels under the paper.
- **Repeat.** dHash between the two shown images.

**Confirmed (`confirmed()`)** when any of these holds:
- ≥ 2 of 3 sampled pages show an image off its source leaf (k ≠ 0, not necessarily the same k: a #3368 shift grows, e.g. `69e53425…` −6/−4);
- a text sits on an image with < 0.5% ink;
- one whole text sits on two different images (containment ≥ 0.9, sizes within 0.8, ≥ 50 shingles, no cover/title page, image dHash ≥ 20).

### Validation, before the corpus run

The ink and repeat thresholds were set on these two sets (every false alarm opened by eye is a shape the rule now refuses), so the top-20 spot check below is the out-of-sample test.

| set | n | recall | precision | specificity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #5803 Clef audit, read by eye 2026-10-17/18 (43 wrong-leaf + #7321; 8 read right) | 52 | 29/44 = 0.66 (0.51–0.78) | 29/29 = 1.00 (0.88–1.00) | 8/8 (0.68–1.00) |
| #7866 Opus draw, positive = an I1 page | 160 | 2/2 | 2/4 vs Opus labels; 4/4 by eye | 156/158 (0.96–1.00) |
| #7866 I1 pages | 800 | 4/6 (0.30–0.90) | 4/5 (0.38–0.96) | — |

- **The two extra Opus-set flags are real defects on pages Opus did not sample**, opened by eye:
  - `6a060d36…` p.1: a blank leaf carrying invented Latin ("De natura et proprietatibus elementorum") in a Sanskrit book.
  - `69ac5f7c…` p.8: a blank leaf whose mirrored show-through was transcribed as its text.
- **Missed:**
  - text-side shifts on e-rara books whose images are their own leaves and whose text has no blank leaf or repeat at the shift;
  - books with no stored image bytes;
  - #7321, whose text comes from ~650 pages away, outside every window.
- **O1 confabulation is not this class:** recall 0/20.
- **False alarms found by eye and designed out:**
  - a printed wrapper repeating its title page; a leaf re-shot inside a spread; a leaf re-shot under a BSB calibration card;
  - the Archive's OCR noise on a tissue leaf;
  - a washed-out contents page read as blank at a 50-level ink threshold;
  - bytes offsets driven by book structure (`6992cf0e…` herbal, `6990795b…` pothi). Because of these the bytes offset only nominates; it never confirms.

### Corpus run (2026-11-01, 47,435 books)

**Scan coverage:**
- 46,844 books can be judged for repeats, 34,560 for ink and 29,941 for the offset.
- Candidates: 836 books with text on a near-blank image, 2,811 with a near-complete repeat, 539 with a bytes offset, and 18,994 with `bulk_jp2` pages the #3368 repair never re-archived (4,205,486 pages).

**Arbitrated:**
- every blank and repeat candidate (3,469 books);
- a seeded random 200 of the 18,994 bulk-JP2 books (seed 7866);
- 49 of the 539 offset candidates. **Stopped there**: the Archive answers at ~2 s an image, and the offset signal is the weakest.

**Confirmed: 631 books, 2,336 pages named** (`ranked.md`, `ranked.json`):

| class | books | pages named |
|---|---|---|
| text on a blank leaf (+ any repeats in the same book) | 206 | 558 |
| one text on two different leaves | 408 | 1,679 |
| image off its source leaf | 17 | 99 |

- Languages: English 248, Latin 128, German 68, French 40, Greek 30, Italian 20, Sanskrit 16, Chinese 10, Russian 9, Hebrew 7, and others.
- These are counts of books with ≥ 1 confirmed page, not of bad books. The precision is the spot check below.

**Bulk-JP2 prevalence (sample n = 200 of 18,994):**
- 182 aligned, 8 shifted, 1 single off page, 7 undecided, 2 with no source.
- Shifted: **8/200 = 4.0% (2.0–7.7%), about 760 books (388–1,461)**. All of them are outside the #3368 repair, which only handled +1.
- Reader-visible (text OCR'd from the source before the archive): **1/200 (0.5%)**, about 95 books. In the other 7 the text was OCR'd from the shifted image and agrees with it on screen; only the record's source pointer is wrong.

### Spot check: top 20, by eye (`spot-check.json`)

| class | opened | reader-visible defect | not a reader defect |
|---|---|---|---|
| image off its source leaf | 12 | 3 (`69af2362…` Festus −5, `69af37bc…` Lomonosov −3, `69af13c5…` Ptolemy −3) | 8 consistent on screen (2 are BSB numbering drift); 1 has no OCR on the sampled pages |
| text on a blank leaf | 4 | 4 | — |
| one text on two leaves | 4 | 4 | — |

- Inside the opened books, 5 of 6 repeat pairs were true misplacements. 1 was the same printed page photographed twice (an opening and a flat shot).
- **An image shift is a reader-visible defect only where the text was read from the source leaf before the archive.** In the Archive books the dates predict which: `image-shift-ocr-dates.json` (Festus 425 pages before, Lomonosov 523, Ptolemy 472). In BSB books they do not, because BSB's numbering moved under both.
- The repeat class is dominated by that same mixed state. A book OCR'd partly before and partly after a shifted archive holds each text twice, |k| pages apart: Festus p.439 = p.444, Grammatici Latini 516 = 537.

### Containment (containment-on-finding.md, by eye only)

- **13 books held**, under three reasons:
  - `wrong-leaf-blank-7866` (2 books);
  - `wrong-leaf-image-shift-7866` (3 books);
  - `wrong-leaf-screen-7866` (7 books, plus one already held for `title-leaf-recitation-6297`).
- **17 pages' English withheld:**
  - `6a060d36…` 1, `69ac5f7c…` 8;
  - `69af2362…` 439, `69af37bc…` 433, `69af13c5…` 120;
  - `6a357a2a…` 7, 520; `69e745f6…` 13, 24; `69b63e85…` 5, 17; `69e72994…` 7;
  - `69af4395…` 516; `69af3988…` 516; `69af453b…` 515; `69af4a2f…` 500.
- Undo: `restore-withheld-translation.mjs`; `hold-pipeline-books.mjs --release-held --reason <reason>`.
- No OCR or translation write, no re-read. The other pages on the ranked list are a detector's output and are not withheld (containment-on-finding.md: a predicate over thousands of pages goes through a dry run and approval).

### Limits

- The offset class is barely run (49/539).
- The bulk-JP2 census is a 200-book sample, not a census.
- Recall on text-side shifts with no blank leaf or repeat is low.
- Books without stored image bytes (27% of the frame) get no ink or offset signal.
- Thresholds were set on the validation sets. The spot check is n = 20.
- Run: 2026-11-01 00:50–03:00Z on earthai-l7a. $0, no model call.

## 2026-11-01 · Latin first reads: PERO > agy one a call (live), PERO > agy four a call, or agy read four a call? Paired, queue-weighted (#6740)

PRIOR ART:
- `2026-10-31-queue-routes-7853.md` and `scripts/eval/queue-routes-7853/`: the whole design. Reused: the PPS draw on pages owed inside strata with one uniform a book drawn before exclusions, the agy face tag with replacement (`agyFace`), the arm machinery (`dryApply` with `--emit-written`, `callsOf`, the agy pool of 2, retry of a read the box killed), the hand-queued GPU task, the judge driver (`judgeAbsolute`, `paceCheck`, the call budget, wrong-page and planted controls), HT weights and the stratified bootstrap, Wilcoxon and Holm, the write-back rule, `exportScore` and the router check.
- `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/judge.mjs drawBlank` and `cheap-routes-7701/run.mjs` (#7701): the first-read frame (`FIRST_READ_BOOKS` + `firstReadSkip`, `spreadReason`), the page's block of up to 4 consecutive unread pages, the la-armc arms (PERO > agy at 1 and 4 a call through `cli-ocr.mjs read --gpu-draft --image-dir`, written by `apply --diff-guard=gpu-draft --print-only`), the read@4 arm's `apply --first-read-only --print-only`, the per-arm wrong-page control.
- `scripts/batch/cli-ocr-lane.mjs armcRun --frame=first-read`: the live route exactly as production runs it (GPU template `0601ef30e816f7a7`, no `--over-stored`, lane `pero-agy-first-read-7701`).
- `2026-10-28-euro-print-gpu-draft-flash-correct-7567.md`, `scripts/batch/pero-draft.py`: PERO-OCR (`pero_eu_cz_print_newspapers_2022-09-26`) on this box.
- `scripts/eval/estimator/router-table/build.py decide_defects` (#7862) and `route-judge-6740/results/defect-rate-2026-10-30/RULE.md` amendment S1 (#7824): the decision rule, restated over this study's data; its constants are read from `rules.json decision_rule`.
- `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/defect-rate.py --add-pooled`: how this study's defect counts join the router's rates.

Code: `scripts/eval/latin-paired-6740/` (`lib.mjs`, `frame.mjs`, `arms.mjs`, `gpu-task.sh`, `judge.mjs`, `analyze.mjs`, `writeback.mjs`). The analysis is committed in this PR, before any verdict exists.

**Why.** In the #7862 build the defect rule turns latin-blank/print to HOLD: the live route `pero>agy-flash-low-written` carries 2.33 wrong-text defects per 1,000 words, about six times `pero>agy-flash-low@4-written` and `agy-flash-low@4-written`, and the pick between those two moves with the misleads weight ($0.001 / $0.01 → pero@4, $0.1 → agy@4). Those rates come from 22 to 26 books drawn separately for each route, much of the live route's from a 4-book depth sample. Derek took the default on 2026-11-01: test the three routes on the same pages before moving the cell.

### Frame (`frame.mjs census`, run 2026-11-01 00:55Z)

- **The queue** is latin-blank/print: the first-read lane's Latin books, `FIRST_READ_BOOKS` + `firstReadSkip(languages: lat)` (visible, held as scans with a first-read hold, print route, no manuscript by library, title or date, not a known unsplit spread). The live armc `--frame=first-read` lane plans from the same set.
- **Owed pages** per book = `pages_count − pages_ocr`, the lane's own count. 15,356 books, 4,741,905 owed pages (15,300 books have no OCR at all).
- **The queue's make-up** (owed pages): ≤ 1600 41%, 17th 37%, 18th 22%, 19th+ and undated under 0.1%. e-rara holds 85% of owed pages, BSB 11%.
- **Exclusions** (`frame.mjs exclusions`): every queue book that a committed `.json/.jsonl/.gz/.md/.tsv/.csv` file under `scripts/eval/` names, by book id or by a page id resolved to its book. A file naming more than 1,000 queue books is a census, not a test, and is not used (one file: `output/book-class-5768/classes.jsonl.gz`, 15,265). 1,666 books (460,477 owed pages) are excluded. Declared gap: tests whose page rows sit only in a job's scratch or on R2 are not seen.

### Strata, allocation, draw (`frame.mjs draw` / `tag` / `select`, seed 67401)

- **Strata**: the century band of the book's year (≤ 1600, 17th, 18th, 19th+, undated).
- **Allocation**: 40 pages, proportional to owed pages by largest remainder. A stratum under 1% of owed pages gets none and is reported as uncovered (19th+ and undated, 0.07%). Each covered stratum gets at least 2. Result: ≤ 1600 16, 17th 15, 18th 9.
- **Draw**: sequential Poisson sampling, PPS on owed pages. One uniform a book (`makeRng(67401)` over all owing books in id order, before exclusions), key = U / owed; a stratum's books in ascending key, the rest its reserves in order.
- **The page**: one interior unread page of the book (`isInterior` on `pages_count`), uniform from a stream seeded by the book id. Its block is the run of consecutive unread pages around it, cut to 4 with the page at a seeded position. A book that left the frame, that `spreadReason` marks as a possible unsplit spread, or that has no interior unread page is replaced by the stratum's next reserve.
- **Typeface** (post-stratum): one agy call a page (`agyFace`, unchanged). A page tagged `none` (no printed body text) or an unfetchable image is replaced by the next reserve.
- **Done before this file merged:** the census, exclusions, draw, page choice and face tags (98 books tagged; 52 drawn books replaced as possible unsplit spreads, 1 as `none`). The sample: 40 pages in 40 books, all e-rara; 37 Antiqua and 3 Fraktur; every block 4 pages. While this PR's checks ran, the PERO drafts were made (158 of 160 block pages) and the arms ran (dry applies only). No text has been judged.
- **Weights**: Horvitz–Thompson, a page stands for w = owed / π pages, π = min(1, n_h · owed / M_h). Every weighted figure uses w; unweighted k/n are reported beside it. The 52 spread replacements mean the weighted estimates describe the part of the queue the lane can read now, not the books waiting on a split check.

### Arms, all on the same page (`arms.mjs`; every apply is a DRY run with `--emit-written`; nothing is written)

- **GPU drafts.** PERO-OCR on the block pages' image bytes, the same bytes the correctors and the judge see (`gpu-stage`, then one hand-queued gex45 gpu-queue task, `gpu-task.sh`; `gpu-collect` makes one draft a page with `armcDraftText`). A draft under 30 word characters is no draft (armcRun's rule).
- **1, `live` = `pero>agy-flash-low-written`**: the live route as armcRun `--frame=first-read` runs it. `cli-ocr.mjs read --correct-prompt=<GPU template 0601ef30e816f7a7> --lane=pero-agy-first-read-7701 --gpu-draft --image-dir`, the page alone, then `apply --diff-guard=gpu-draft --print-only`.
- **2, `pero4` = `pero>agy-flash-low@4-written`**: the same, the block's drafted pages 4 a call (`--per-call=4`), lane `pero-agy4-first-read-6740`.
- **3, `read4` = `agy-flash-low@4-written`**: a fresh read of the block, 4 a call, on the live first-read prompt, then `apply --first-read-only --print-only --lane=agy-first-read-7701`.
- **A page an arm does not write stays scans-only** (it serves no text). It is not accepted in the all-drawn accept, and has no defect rate.
- **Common.** `gemini-3.8-flash-low` on agy's default pool, 2 calls at a time. Reads are not `--fresh` (a kept read of the identical request is reused and costs 0 calls). A read killed by the box (`exit -9`) is retried once. If a lane writes a sampled page between this test's read and its dry apply, the apply refuses ("the page has OCR now"): for `read4` the read stands as its text, and it is never written back; for the GPU arms the page counts as not written. Either case is counted.
- **GPU in front of production.** The task is hand-queued in `/root/gpu-queue/pending` with `/root/gpu-queue/ocr-filler/PAUSE` touched while it runs, and removed after.

### Judge (`judge.mjs`)

- Opus via `claude -p --model opus` on this box's subscription, `judgePrompt` (task ocr, language Latin) unchanged, the page image attached, one text a call, blind to the arm. A text identical to one already queued for the page is judged once and stands for every arm that wrote it.
- Order: `makeRng(67402)` over the items. 3 calls at a time.
- **Budget**: at most 220 Opus calls (about 120 items + 6 wrong-page + 5 planted). Pace: weekly ≥ 85% or 5-hour ≥ 95% stops; resume after the reset.
- **Controls.**
  - Wrong-page: 2 per arm, this page's image with another book's written text of the same arm (`mulberry32(67403)`). Passes when not accepted at fidelity ≤ 2.
  - Planted: 5 on accepted texts, kinds B–E rotating (`plantError`, `makeRng(67404)`), scored by `scorePlant`.
  - The judge is **valid for this study** when every wrong-page control passes and at least 0.80 of plants are caught. If not, the judged outcomes are reported as invalid and nothing is decided or written back.
- Noise floor: #7818's κ 0.87, same judge, prompt and kind of task (not rerun).

### Outcomes (`analyze.mjs score`)

- **Primary: severity-weighted defects per 1,000 words** (#7824, MQM weights cosmetic 1, misleads 5, wrong_text 25; words by #7824 `words()`).
  - Contrasts: `pero4` against `live`, and `read4` against `live`, each paired on the pages both arms wrote and the judge read.
  - Effect: the difference of the HT-weighted ratios (Σ w·points / Σ w·words), with a book-cluster bootstrap 95% CI (one page a book, so books are resampled within their strata; 4,000 resamples).
  - Test: Wilcoxon signed-rank on the per-page severity rates. **Holm over the two contrasts.** Supported = Holm-adjusted p < 0.05.
- **Gate: accept.** Weighted accept over every drawn page (a page not written is not accepted). A candidate passes when it is no more than 5 points below `live`.
- **Decision: #7862's S1 rule**, restated over this study (`decideS1`; constants from `rules.json decision_rule` as on main):
  - Bar = `live`. Rated arms have ≥ `min_books` (10) judged written pages.
  - Rates: gamma-Poisson posterior means per 1,000 words, one common prior for the three arms (their pooled rate, worth 2,000 words, defect-rate.py's `A0_WORDS`), deflated by the re-check (misleads × 0.625, wrong text × 0.80, from `defect-rates.json recheck`).
  - Gate 1, wrong text: ≤ the bar's + 0.15 per 1,000 words.
  - Gate 2, acceptance floor: P(acc_arm ≥ acc_live − 0.05) ≥ 0.5 under the paired Dirichlet(1 + both, 1 + arm only, 1 + live only, 1 + neither) on every drawn page.
  - Pick: the lowest price per raw page (agy calls a page × $0.00087; GPU card time unpriced, as build.py prices the pero stages) + W/1000 × w_m × (misleads + 3 × wrong text), W = the median of the arms' median words a page.
  - A pick that changes across w_m ∈ {$0.001, $0.01, $0.1} is **HOLD**, not switch. Otherwise keep (pick = live) or switch.
  - Reported beside it: the same rule with GPU time priced (3 s a page at gex45's $249 a month), and what `build.py` decides on a copy of main with this export in rules.json and these defect counts pooled into `defect-rates.json` (`analyze.mjs router`).
- **Secondary**: `read4` against `pero4` (severity and accept); accept McNemar for each contrast with the weighted effect and CI; wrong text, misleads and cosmetic per 1,000 words per arm with CIs; wrong-text pages added and removed; written share and the arms' refusal reasons; fidelity; agy calls and GPU seconds a page; $ per accepted page; by stratum and face.
- **CER on CAMENA-matched pages** (#6012 `kgram-vote-v2`, same edition, congruent). Checked before this file: none of the 40 sampled books is in the CAMENA manifest (an aligned page needs a stored read, and these books have none). With fewer than 5 matched pages no CER is computed, and the outcome is reported as not available at this n.

### Write-back (the only production write)

- On each page, the best judged arm: accepted, then fidelity, then fewer wrong_text, misleads, cosmetic defects; ties go to the cheaper arm (read4 < pero4 < live).
- Written only where it is accepted, its own dry apply would write it, and the page was unread when the arm read it.
- Through `cli-ocr.mjs apply --apply --only=<page>` from the arm's own read directory, with its guards (first reads only, printed only; the GPU arms' put-back against the draft), revision row and provenance (`writeback.mjs`, dry run first). The lane stamps are those of the arms. Books keep their scans-only hold. There is no `--mark-stale` (no translation exists).
- Every page written is listed in the results with its run id for `revert-run.mjs`.

### Declared deviations from the brief

- n = 40, as briefed. Severity contrasts are on pages both arms wrote; a page one arm leaves unwritten enters through the accept gate.
- The S1 rule is restated over this study's paired pages with an in-study prior. build.py's own decision on the pooled rates is reported beside it, not used.
- The face tag is one agy call a page (#7835 T4), not by eye: 98 calls on top of the arms' ~160.
- Limits: Claude only via `claude -p` on this box's subscription; Gemini only through agy flash-low; no paid API; no cron or routing change; `current.json` is not moved.

- **Gate** (accept, all drawn, within 5 points of live's 0.48): all three pass.

  - Wrong text per 1,000 words: live 0.24, pero@4 0.12, read@4 0.70.
  - Misleads per 1,000 words: 0.58, 0.55, 1.65.
  - Gate 1: read@4 fails the wrong-text gate (0.70 > 0.24 + 0.15). pero@4 passes both gates (acceptance floor P = 0.98).

  - Price a raw page: live $0.00085, pero@4 $0.00021.

- **build.py on main** (`results/router-check.json`) with this export named in rules.json and the defect counts pooled through defect-rate.py `ADD`:

  - Pooled wrong text per 1,000 words, before → after:
    - live: 2.33 (22 books) → 1.98 (44 books, 0.97–3.28);
    - pero@4: 0.37 → 0.17 (39 books);
    - read@4: 0.23 → 0.68 (63 books).

### What the coverage gap means (post hoc, exploratory: `cascade.mjs`, chosen after seeing the write rates)

- **pero@4, then read@4 on the pages pero@4 does not write**: accept, all drawn 0.75, severity 38.8 / 1,000 words, wrong text 0.89.
- **read@4 alone**: 0.75, 41.9, 0.92.
- **On the pages both wrote**, read@4 and pero@4 carry the same wrong text (0 and 0 defects, n = 23; severity +4.5, −0.3 to +9.2, p 0.11).
- So read@4's higher rate comes from the pages the PERO put-back refuses: harder pages that the live route leaves unread today.
- The S1 rule compares rates over written pages and prices raw pages, not coverage. It therefore picks the PERO route that writes fewer, easier pages. That is the preregistered rule, and it is reported as such.

### What this says
- **The #7862 HOLD resolves.** On the same pages, PERO 4 a call leaves no more severity than PERO 1 a call (−5.5 per 1,000 words, CI −18.8 to +3.0) and accepts as many pages or more. It does this at a quarter of the agy calls. The S1 rule picks it at every weight.
- **The live route's 2.33 wrong-text figure did not reproduce**: 0.20 per 1,000 words here (1 defect in 4,989 words, 22 pages; CI 0 to 0.66), as of 2026-11-01.
- **Coverage is the open question.** Both PERO routes leave about 45% of the queue's pages unread. They accept 0.48 (live) and 0.55 (pero@4) of all drawn pages, against read@4's 0.75. Read@4's wrong text sits on those extra pages: all 5 of its wrong-text pages are pages pero@4 did not write (4 of them neither PERO route wrote; 3 are the Fraktur pages), 0.92 per 1,000 words overall.
- **Implementing pero@4 needs code.** The armc lane has no 4-a-call mode yet: `armcRun` reads one page a call. The test drove `cli-ocr.mjs read --per-call=4` directly.

## 2026-11-01 · How good is the route judge? Opus against CHURRO-DS human transcriptions, 7 strata (#7263)

Part of #7263. This is step 2 of the R&D plan of 2026-11-01: judge calibration against an external gold set.

PRIOR ART:
- `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/judge.mjs`: `judgePrompt`, `opusCall`, `parseVerdict`, unchanged. They are reached through `scripts/eval/correction-pass-7818/lib.mjs` `judgeAbsolute`: the page image sits in the workspace, and Opus runs as `claude -p --model opus` on this box's subscription. `paceCheck` is the box's pace guard.
- `scripts/eval/lib/metrics.mjs` (`scoreAgainstReference`, `normalizeForScript` v4, `windowedErrorRate`) supplies the CER. `scripts/eval/lib/agreement-stats.mjs` `wilson` and `scripts/eval/lib/paired-stats.mjs` `makeRng` are imported.
- `scripts/eval/lib/plant-ocr-errors.mjs` was read and does not fit. It plants ONE grammatical error in la/de/fr body lines found through our markup. It has no English, Italian or Greek, and it cannot grade a text by CER. The graded planter here (`lib.mjs plantGraded`) adds OCR-shaped character confusions, dropped words and one dropped line, and re-scores until the band is reached.
- #7866 used wrong-page and planted controls (8/8, 12/12). The same kind of controls are run here.
- Searched `scripts/eval/INDEX.md` and `EXPERIMENTS.md` for "CHURRO", "sensitivity", "specificity", "self-preference" and "gold". bench-2 (2026-09-03) ran CHURRO-3B as an engine. No record calibrates the judge against an external human transcription.

Code: `scripts/eval/judge-calibration-7263/` (`lib.mjs`, `run.mjs`). Committed results are in `results/`: `score.json`, `rows.jsonl` (one row per judged item: example id, kind, CERs, accept, fidelity, defect classes), `sample.json`, and `ppi-latin_lite_print-{all,synthetic,reads}.json`.

**Licence.** The CHURRO-DS card says: "Due to licensing restrictions on the original datasets used in Churro, use is permitted for research purposes only." Calibrating an evaluation instrument is research use. No CHURRO text or image is committed (this repo is public): only example ids, CERs and verdict fields. Defect quotes are left out because they quote CHURRO text. Bulky files stay in `$JOB_SCRATCH/judge-cal-7263`.

### 1. Design

**Gold.** CHURRO-DS (Stanford, EMNLP 2025, arXiv 2509.19768), test and dev splits. That is 2,340 pages, 60 per (language, print/handwriting) cluster, fetched through the HF datasets-server rows API. The gold is the text of each `cleaned_transcription` `<Page>`: one `<Line>` per line, inline tags dropped, their text kept (`lib.mjs goldText`).

**Strata** (`run.mjs draw`, salt `cal7263`). The languages we route that CHURRO holds: Latin, German, French and English print. Italian and Greek occur only as manuscripts in test and dev, and the train-split filter API was down. Latin manuscripts are the manuscript cluster. Each stratum has 20 pages, 140 in all:
- one page per source document across all strata (`docKey`: the example id less its page token);
- round-robin over collections, so 6 to 20 collections per stratum;
- 200 to 6,000 scored characters per page.

**Candidates per page** (`run.mjs packet`):
- **One real read.** agy `gemini-3.8-flash-low` (via agy-guard) on alternate pages, Opus through `claude -p --model opus` on the others: 70 each. Both use the live OCR prompt (v19.1, read from Mongo; no writes) on the image alone, the request `cli-ocr.mjs read` sends.
- **One planted gold.** S1 (target CER 0.3%, median reached 0.35%), S2 (3%, median 3.0%) or S3 (10% with a whole line dropped, median 8.6% order-free), rotating: 49 / 49 / 42.
- **The gold itself** on alternate pages (70).

Controls:
- 2 wrong-page items per stratum (this image, another page's gold);
- 20 seeded repeats (judged twice).

**Budget.** 384 judge items, 385 Opus judge calls (one retried after an unparsed reply), under the 400 cap. Reads took another 70 Opus and about 70 agy calls. The Claude meter stood at 2% of the week at the start. No paid API was used.

**Truth.** A candidate is truly acceptable when its CER against the gold is ≤ τ.
- The primary τ is **1%**: the router's accept is judged acceptance, and the fitted 50% point below lands there. The record also reports 0.5%, 2% and 5%.
- The primary CER is **order-free** (`lib.mjs cerLines`): each gold line is aligned on its own (fitting alignment) anywhere in the candidate. It was added after the first score, before any conclusion was drawn.
- Why order-free: the windowed CER charged correct reads up to 50% when a page's columns or blocks were read in another order than CHURRO's transcriber chose, for example a two-column play page or a multi-article newspaper. The diffs are in `$JOB_SCRATCH/judge-cal-7263/read-diffs.txt`.
- The windowed CER is kept as a sensitivity. An abbreviation-tolerant word error (`werTolerant`: "dni" → "domini" is not charged) checks the manuscript strata, where the gold is diplomatic.

**Statistics.**
- Sensitivity = P(judge accepts | truly acceptable); specificity = P(judge rejects | not).
- Wilson intervals; kappa with a page-cluster bootstrap (2,000).
- Self-preference as the DBG score (arXiv 2506.02592): bias = judge verdict − gold verdict, Opus-written minus Gemini-written, with a page bootstrap. A CER-adjusted logistic is the second check.

### 2. Controls

| control | result |
|---|---|
| wrong page (another page's gold on this image) | **16/16** rejected with fidelity ≤ 2 |
| repeat judgement | **19/20** same accept |
| S2 plants (3.0% CER) | **0/49** accepted |
| S3 plants (8.6%) | **0/42** accepted |
| S1 plants (0.35%) | 20/49 accepted (0.28 to 0.55) |
| the gold itself (0%) | 57/70 accepted (0.71 to 0.89) |

The judge never let a ≥ 3% text through in any stratum.

| **print** | 200 | 108/132 | 0.82 (0.74–0.87) | 58/68 | 0.85 (0.75–0.92) | 0.64 (0.51–0.76) | 0.66 / 1.00 | 0.98 / 0.38 | 0.52 |
| **manuscript** | 150 | 35/54 | 0.65 (0.51–0.76) | 63/96 | 0.66 (0.56–0.74) | 0.29 (0.14–0.45) | 0.63 / 1.00 | 1.00 / 0.42 | 0.27 |
| Latin print | 50 | 24/30 | 0.80 (0.63–0.90) | 15/20 | 0.75 (0.53–0.89) | 0.55 (0.21–0.83) | 0.65 / 1.00 | 1.00 / 0.29 | 0.40 |
| German print | 50 | 25/34 | 0.74 (0.57–0.85) | 13/16 | 0.81 (0.57–0.93) | 0.50 (0.23–0.78) | 0.53 / 1.00 | 0.94 / 0.00 | 0.43 |
| French print | 50 | 28/33 | 0.85 (0.69–0.93) | 15/17 | 0.88 (0.66–0.97) | 0.70 (0.50–0.88) | 0.71 / 1.00 | 1.00 / 0.50 | 0.58 |
| English print | 50 | 31/35 | 0.89 (0.74–0.95) | 15/15 | 1.00 (0.80–1.00) | 0.82 (0.64–0.96) | 0.76 / 1.00 | 1.00 / 1.00 | 0.70 |
| Italian MS | 50 | 13/19 | 0.68 (0.46–0.85) | 16/31 | 0.52 (0.35–0.68) | 0.18 (−0.11–0.42) | 0.65 / 1.00 | 1.00 / 0.17 | 0.15 |
| Greek MS | 50 | 12/18 | 0.67 (0.44–0.84) | 23/32 | 0.72 (0.55–0.84) | 0.37 (0.14–0.61) | 0.65 / 1.00 | 1.00 / 0.53 | 0.37 |
| Latin MS | 50 | 10/17 | 0.59 (0.36–0.78) | 24/33 | 0.73 (0.56–0.85) | 0.31 (0.02–0.58) | 0.59 / 1.00 | – / 0.55 | 0.31 |

The reads columns rest on few truth-reject reads per stratum: German print has 3 and English print 2. Read them as direction, not value.

Pooled at other bars:

| τ | sensitivity | specificity | kappa |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5% | 0.77 | 0.70 | 0.46 (0.36–0.56) |
| 2% | 0.77 | 0.77 | 0.55 (0.44–0.64) |
| 5% | 0.63 | 0.76 | 0.30 (0.21–0.40) |

Agreement peaks between 1% and 2%.

**Where the judge's bar sits.** Fitting a logistic of accept on log₁₀ order-free CER (gold excluded), the judge accepts half the time at **1.0% (0.7 to 1.4)**: print 0.7%, manuscripts 0.8%.

**Two operating points, not one.**
- *Strict on planted errors.* Specificity is 1.00, but sensitivity is 0.65. The judge rejects 59% of 0.35% slips (21/49 carry a `wrong_text` tag: one changed letter that makes another word) and 13 of 70 untouched human transcriptions.
- The rejected golds are listed in `score.json` `gold_rejected`. The defects cited are concrete: a signature not on the leaf, three columns read straight across, interlinear notes merged, misread names.
- One was checked by eye (`ocrd/heyden_paedono_1548_0014`): the gold carries a page number and a signature `D iij` that this leaf does not print (show-through only). **The judge was right and the gold wrong.** CHURRO's gold is not error-free, so part of the 0.65 is the gold, not the judge. That check was made by a model of the same family as the judge; it is a hint, not an independent verdict.
- *Lenient on real reads.* Specificity on real model reads is 0.41: 43 of 73 reads that miss the gold by > 1% were accepted. Part of this is the gold's own conventions and errors, as above. Part is real: a model's misreads are fluent, while a planted `c` for `e` is not. **Planted errors overstate the judge's specificity on what routes actually produce.**

**Side finding.** agy Flash-low reads Latin manuscripts badly: 1/10 accepted. 12 of its 30 manuscript reads miss the gold by > 10% order-free; Opus has 14 such reads.

### 4. Self-preference (DBG, arXiv 2506.02592)

bias = judge accept − gold accept (order-free CER ≤ τ) on each real read. DBG = mean bias on Opus-written reads − mean bias on Gemini-written reads. The pages are balanced: the two readers alternate within each stratum.

| τ | Opus: judged / gold-accept | Gemini: judged / gold-accept | DBG pooled | DBG print | DBG manuscript |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5% | 63 / 32 of 70 | 46 / 25 of 70 | +0.14 (−0.02, +0.30) | +0.00 (−0.20, +0.19) | +0.33 (+0.10, +0.57) |
| **1%** | 63 / 36 | 46 / 31 | **+0.17 (+0.02, +0.33)** | **−0.02 (−0.18, +0.12)** | **+0.43 (+0.20, +0.66)** |
| 2% | 63 / 41 | 46 / 35 | +0.16 (+0.01, +0.30) | −0.02 (−0.17, +0.12) | +0.40 (+0.16, +0.62) |
| 5% | 63 / 46 | 46 / 48 | +0.27 (+0.14, +0.41) | +0.08 (−0.07, +0.23) | +0.53 (+0.33, +0.74) |

On windowed CER the 1% DBG is +0.21 (+0.06, +0.37); print +0.08 (−0.12, +0.28), manuscript +0.40 (+0.17, +0.62). CER-adjusted logistic (accept ~ log₁₀ CER + Opus-written, reads only): coefficient +2.56 (95% CI +1.18, +3.94), an odds ratio of about 13 at equal CER.

Where it sits (`score.json` `reads_by_band`), accepted / reads:

| reader, type | order-free CER < 1% | 1–3% | 3–10% | ≥ 10% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opus, print | 36/36 | 3/3 | 1/1 | — |
| Gemini, print | 27/28 | 2/4 | 4/7 | 0/1 |
| Opus, manuscript | — | 6/6 | 9/10 | **8/14** |
| Gemini, manuscript | 3/3 | 5/5 | 4/10 | **1/12** |

The gap is in the manuscripts. It survives forgiving abbreviation expansion: at ≥ 15% abbreviation-tolerant word error, Opus manuscript reads are accepted 13/20 and Gemini's 3/19.

What remains confounded:
- Opus may regularise a manuscript in ways the diplomatic gold does not (word division, punctuation, i/j, u/v are folded; expansions are now forgiven).
- The judge reads such output as faithful, which it may be.
- A third, non-Claude judge, or a by-eye panel, is the way to separate these.

On print there is nothing to separate: Opus reads print very well (36/40 under 1%), and the judge treats both authors' text alike.

**Against the prior figure.** The −0.11 to −0.13 used so far (estimator v2) is a diff-in-diff between two judges (Opus and Gemini Pro) on #6545 translations. It has no gold, so it cannot tell bias from quality: the plan's concern was right. For print OCR this record agrees there is no measurable self-preference. For manuscripts it finds a large one.

### 5. Correcting a router k/n: the plug-in, worked on one cell

The method is the sensitivity–specificity plug-in of prediction-powered inference for an imperfect judge (Angelopoulos et al. 2023; Lee et al., arXiv 2511.21140, which stays unbiased under a shift between calibration and test sets). The corrected rate is

θ = (p + spec − 1) / (sens + spec − 1),

with a delta-method interval over three sources (the router's n, and the calibration set's m₁ truly-acceptable and m₀ not-acceptable items) and a Beta bootstrap (`lib.mjs plugIn`; `run.mjs ppi`).

**Cell:** `latin-lite/print`, live table `2026-10-31-correction-pass-7818`, decision *keep lite>opus*, 835,238 pages waiting. k/n is the book-scaled `eff` the Beta posterior uses. Calibration: print pooled (all items), order-free CER ≤ 1%: sens 0.82, spec 0.85, Youden 0.67, so the plug-in scales distances by 1/0.67 = 1.5×.

| route | judged k/n | judged | corrected θ | delta 95% CI | bootstrap 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lite (the draft) | 90.1/131 | 0.69 (0.60–0.76) | **0.81** | 0.66–0.95 | 0.66–0.96 |
| lite>opus | 118.8/127 | 0.94 (0.88–0.97) | 1.00 (raw 1.18) | — | 1.00–1.00 |
| lite>agy-flash-low | 119.1/126 | 0.95 (0.89–0.97) | 1.00 (raw 1.19) | — | 1.00–1.00 |
| agy-flash-low-read | 31.0/44 | 0.70 (0.56–0.82) | 0.83 | 0.61–1.00 | 0.60–1.00 |

Reading it:
1. **The decision does not move.** The plug-in is monotone in p, so with one (sens, spec) pair for the cell the routes keep their order. The two top routes both sit above sens, so the correction clips them both at 1.
2. **The judge's k/n underestimates CER-defined acceptance on the drafts.** lite 0.69 → 0.81. The judge is stricter than 1% CER on slips, and that strictness counts as a false negative here.
3. **But a single pair does not transfer.** With the synthetic-only pair (sens 0.66, spec 1.00), every route corrects to 1.00. With the real-read pair (sens 0.98, spec 0.38), lite corrects to 0.17 (0.00–0.56) and lite>opus to 0.86 (0.61–1.00) (`ppi-latin_lite_print-{synthetic,reads}.json`).
4. The answer depends on which kind of error the calibration items carry. The plug-in is valid only when the calibration set's errors are the kind the route makes. CHURRO's planted errors are not. Its real reads are, but their truth is CER against a gold that has its own conventions and errors.

What this means for the router (a recommendation, not applied):
- **Print.** Keep relative decisions on judged k/n. The judge's bar is the router's bar (1.0%), it has no measured self-preference, and a monotone correction cannot reorder routes within a cell. Absolute acceptance figures (on /quality) should carry the interval from the plug-in with the real-read calibration, not the raw k/n.
- **Manuscripts.** Do not let the Opus judge decide an Opus-written route: +0.43 DBG is larger than any `switch.within` margin (0.08). The manuscript cells are HOLD now (< 10 pages a route), so nothing has been decided on this bias yet.
- **Next calibration.** It should use our own pages with a clean external reference (Wikisource and DTA print pages as in #7818 Arm W, Derge for Tibetan). Real route outputs scored against a reference that shares the routes' conventions would give a (sens, spec) the plug-in can carry. CHURRO stays useful for manuscripts and for languages we have no reference in.

### 6. Limits

- 20 pages a stratum: per-language intervals are wide (Latin print kappa 0.21–0.83). The pooled print and manuscript rows are the ones to quote.
- CHURRO's pages are not ours. Its print skews to the 19th and 20th centuries and to newspapers in places; our queue is 1500–1800 print.
- The gold has errors, one confirmed by eye. Sensitivity on gold items is a lower bound on the judge's.
- Italian and Greek are manuscripts only, and Greek is mostly Byzantine liturgical hands and papyri.
- The order-free CER does not charge text a read ADDS outside the gold's lines. The judge's `wrong_text` tags on the reads show where that happened.
- Self-preference is measured on OCR reads, not translations, and only between Opus and Gemini 3.8 Flash-low.

TAKEN: train split not used (the HF filter API was down, and Greek print was absent from its index); test + dev only, so Italian and Greek are manuscripts.

## 2026-11-01 · Does a hierarchical fit of acceptance predict router cells it has not seen, and how many pages is it worth? (#7263)

PRIOR ART:
- `router-table/fit_prior.py` (#7263 backfill-all, router-next) fits ONE weight W and a calibration slope for the v1/v2 prior means. It uses the 15 (now 24) routes those models cover, and its leave-one-cell-out check rejected the calibration (rules.json `prior.calibration.in_force = false`). It never asks whether one cell's acceptance predicts another's, and it cannot score the 230 routes with a flat prior. Its beta-binomial likelihood, its W grid and its profile interval are reused here.
- `router-table/build.py` supplies the outcome unchanged: `eff` is the accepted and judged pages after book scaling, the same numbers the posterior uses. Its per-route `prior` (a, b) is model (b) below.
- `2026-10-28-router-backfill-all-and-prior-weight-7263.md` is the 7-page weight in force today.
- `loo_v1.py` / `loo_v2.py` score v1/v2 against their own references (CER, 1–5), not against acceptance, so they cannot answer this.
- Nothing in `scripts/eval/INDEX.md` or `EXPERIMENTS.md` does a held-out test across cells.

**Why.** This is step 1 of the 2026-11-01 R&D plan on #7263. The router has to find optima across 109 cells, where the median route has n = 8. It can only do that if one cell's evidence informs another's (hierarchical Bayesian bandits, Hong et al., AISTATS 2022). The v1 hierarchical prior failed a held-out check and sits behind a fixed page weight, so first: does a hierarchical fit predict cells it has not seen?

### Design

- **Data.** Every TESTED route in `router-table/2026-10-31-correction-pass-7818.json`:
  - 254 routes, in 93 cell × script rows, 46 base cells and 23 languages;
  - 11,334 judged pages, which become 5,403.5 book-scaled units.
  - **The outcome is build.py's book-scaled `eff` k of n**, so a book counts once whatever its pages. That is the "weighted by books" the brief asks for, and it is the unit `rules.json prior.pages_*` is applied in.
- **Factors** (`heldout/factors.py`):
  - engine: the stage that wrote the text, with 15 levels, translation engines included;
  - draft: what a corrector corrected, or none;
  - language;
  - writing system;
  - script type: print, manuscript or unknown;
  - engine × writing system, and engine × script type.
- **Models**, each scored on routes it did not see:

| | model |
|---|---|
| (a) flat | Beta(1, 1), what an untested route gets today |
| (a′) grand | one Beta(m W, (1 − m) W) for every route, fitted on the training folds |
| (b) table | the table's own prior: the v1/v2 mean worth 7 pages on 24 routes, flat on the rest. Not refitted per fold, and its 7 was fitted on these routes, so it is flattered |
| (c-eng) | engine + draft, partially pooled |
| (c-add) | + language + writing system + script type |
| **(c) hier** | (c-add) + engine × writing system + engine × script type |

- **How (c) works.**
  - logit p = μ + Σ effects. Each group is N(0, s_g²); the engine s is fixed at 2.5, nearly a fixed effect.
  - The route's p is beta-binomial around that mean, with concentration W.
  - The s_g and W come from the Laplace-approximate marginal likelihood (coordinate ascent on log grids), refitted in every fold.
  - A level that no training route has keeps its prior. An unseen language therefore widens the prediction by s_lang² instead of guessing.
- **Folds.**
  - Leave one ROW out (cell × script, the 109-cell grain).
  - Leave one BASE out: print, manuscript and unknown share books, so they leave together, and the `german-blank*` cells are one base.
  - Leave one LANGUAGE out.
- **Scores.**
  - Held-out log predictive density of the book-scaled k of n, binomial coefficient included.
  - Calibration: predicted against observed acceptance, binned and book-weighted, with the expected calibration error (ECE).
  - The prior's worth: the W that maximises the held-out beta-binomial likelihood around each model's held-out mean, with a profile 90% interval.
- Stdlib only. About 20 minutes on 8 processes. No model calls, no DB.

### Result

Held-out log predictive density (higher is better), MAE and ECE, both book-weighted:

| model | leave one row out | leave one base out | leave one language out |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) flat | −622.8 · 0.333 · 0.281 | −622.8 · 0.333 · 0.281 | −622.8 · 0.333 · 0.281 |
| (a′) grand | −580.7 · 0.216 · 0.098 | −581.6 · 0.219 · 0.126 | −581.8 · 0.223 · 0.155 |
| (b) table | −614.6 · 0.302 · 0.249 | −614.6 · 0.302 · 0.249 | −614.6 · 0.302 · 0.249 |
| (c-eng) | −540.1 · 0.152 · 0.055 | −549.5 · 0.154 · 0.052 | −555.1 · 0.154 · 0.050 |
| (c-add) | **−507.7** · 0.116 · 0.020 | **−528.1** · 0.124 · 0.014 | **−538.3** · 0.129 · 0.027 |
| **(c) hier** | −510.7 · 0.117 · 0.020 | −528.5 · 0.124 · 0.014 | −539.7 · 0.128 · 0.031 |

- **It shares strength.** Leaving one base out, (c) beats flat by 94 nats, the grand mean by 53 and the table's prior by 86. Per route, (c) is better than flat on 180 of 254, and than the table on 173.
  - The gain holds where it matters, on small routes (n_eff < 10, 123 routes): +12.9 nats over flat and +10.9 over the grand mean, leaving one base out.
  - Leaving a whole language out, it shrinks to +5.0 and +3.1.
- **Which factors matter.**
  - Engine and draft carry most of it: (c-eng) gains 73 nats over flat, leaving one base out.
  - Language, writing system and print/manuscript add another 21.
  - **The engine × script interaction adds nothing.** Its scale goes to the grid floor (s = 0.05) in every fold, and (c) ≈ (c-add). "Lite fails on non-Latin" is a writing-system effect common to every engine in this evidence, not one engine's weakness.
  - Fitted effects on the full data (logit):
    - engine: Opus correction +2.0, agy translation +1.6, agy correction +0.85, agy read +0.76, Flash 3 +0.36, Flash-Lite −0.21, GPU −0.70, PERO −1.23, kraken −3.7;
    - writing system: Latin +1.09, Cyrillic +1.16, Han −0.48, Hebrew −1.09, Greek −1.14;
    - print +0.18, manuscript −0.12;
    - language s = 0.5, writing system s = 1.0. The residual spread between routes is W = 13.
- **Calibration** (leave one base out, book-weighted), predicted → observed by bin: 0.39 → 0.42 | 0.59 → 0.60 | 0.74 → 0.77 | 0.85 → 0.87 | 0.93 → 0.94 | 0.95 → 0.94.
  - The model is slightly pessimistic everywhere, by at most 0.03.
  - Leaving one language out, the bottom bin misses most: 0.44 → 0.55, on 405 books.
- **Where it misses.** These are cells whose language defies its writing system, and the misses are visible in `breakdown.py`:
  - higher than predicted: Hindi (0.87 against 0.48) and Russian (0.89 against 0.53);
  - lower than predicted: Greek (0.27 against 0.62), Hebrew (0.24 against 0.57), Chinese 3 Flash (0.22 against 0.68) and MHG (0.10 against 0.66).
  - A prior worth 5 pages is overturned by about 10 books of evidence, so these misses are recoverable. They are also the argument against a larger weight.

### What the prior is worth (the cap)

The fitted W is the number of pages (book-scaled) that a Beta prior centred on the held-out mean is worth. Δ is the log likelihood at W = 5 and W = 7 against the best W.

| prior mean | held out by | W (pages) | profile 90% | Δ at W = 5 | Δ at W = 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| hierarchical (c), all 254 routes | row | 6.4 | [5.2, 7.8] | −1.5 | −0.2 |
| hierarchical (c), all 254 routes | base | **5.5** | [4.5, 6.7] | −0.2 | −1.6 |
| hierarchical (c), all 254 routes | language | **5.2** | [4.3, 6.4] | 0.0 | −2.6 |
| grand mean | base | 2.2 | [1.9, 2.7] | −25 | −51 |
| table's v1/v2 mean, its 24 routes | (not refitted) | 5.5 | [3.3, 9.0] | −0.05 | −0.3 |
| hierarchical (c), the same 24 routes | base | 12.8 | [6.1, 28.5] | −2.1 | −0.8 |

The model's own predictive spread agrees: a moment-matched W with a median of 8.8 (leave one base out) and 6.3 (leave one language out).

**Recommendation.**
1. **The cap is 5 pages** for a prior centred on the hierarchical mean.
   - It sits inside the 90% interval for a new base cell and for a new language.
   - It costs at most 1.5 nats against the best W under every fold scheme.
   - 7, the value in `rules.json` today (`prior.pages_measured = pages_pooled = 7`; the brief's "5" is not what is in force), lies above the upper bound for new languages and costs 2.6 nats there.
   - For a new script split of a known cell, 6 would be justified. One number is simpler and the difference is under 1.5 nats.
2. **Take the prior's mean from the hierarchical fit for every route.** Today the table uses v1/v2 for 24 routes and a flat prior for the rest.
   - On the 24 routes v1/v2 cover, the hierarchical mean scores −60.5 held out against −66.7 for the table prior.
   - It extends an informative prior to the 230 routes, and to every untested route of a known engine, that get Beta(1, 1) today.
3. **Drop the engine × script interaction.** Keep engine + draft + language + writing system + script type.

### Caveats

- **The outcome is Opus's acceptance**, pooled across four verdict scales (the 11-01 audit on #7263). This model predicts the judge. Step 2 (CHURRO-DS calibration) decides whether the judge is right.
- **Book scaling treats the correlation within a book as 1** (`eff`; ICC 0.38 in #7866). W is in book-scaled units because that is how build.py applies it. If the scaling changes, refit W with `heldout.py`.
- **(b) is flattered.** It is not refitted per fold, and its 7 came from these routes.
- **Engines with few routes have imprecise effects**, so their place in the ranking above is not established: kraken and agy-flash-high have 1 route each, PERO and Paddle 3.
- No decision moves in this PR: `rules.json` is unchanged.

### Artifacts

- `scripts/eval/estimator/heldout/heldout.py`: the three fold schemes, all six models, worth and calibration.
- `factors.py`: route → factors.
- `breakdown.py`: per-language and per-base gains, and the gain by route size.
- `results/2026-11-01-correction-pass-7818.json`: per route, every model's held-out mean and log density under each scheme; the full-data effects; the hyperparameters by fold.
- Reproduce: `python3 scripts/eval/estimator/heldout/heldout.py --out <file>` (repo root, HELDOUT_PROCS=8).

*Replicated?* No. The next table build can rerun it unchanged.

## 2026-10-31 · The stored Flash-Lite queue: correct it, GPU draft + correct, or re-read with agy 4 a call or 1 a call? Paired, queue-weighted (#7853)

PRIOR ART:
- `2026-10-31-fraktur-paired-7835.md` and `scripts/eval/fraktur-paired-7835/`: T2 is this test at n = 40, Fraktur only, books drawn equally. Reused: the #7558 frame rule (`correctablePages` restated, the gex45 ledger, `lane_judge_verdicts`), the block of the page and the next 3 pages, the face tag (`agyFace`), the arm runners (the stored text, the lane's own correction with its dry apply, read@4 with its dry apply, `callsOf`, Amendment 1's retry of reads the box killed), the judge driver, McNemar / bootstrap, the write-back rule, the export through `exportScore` and the router check.
- `2026-10-31-correction-pass-paired-7818.md` and `scripts/eval/correction-pass-7818/`: `judgeAbsolute` (route-judge-6740 `judgePrompt`, unchanged), `paceCheck`, `wrongText`; the noise floor (accept κ 0.87, 29/30).

Code: `scripts/eval/queue-routes-7853/` (`lib.mjs`, `frame.mjs`, `arms.mjs`, `gpu-task.sh`, `judge.mjs`, `analyze.mjs`, `writeback.mjs`). The analysis, `analyze.mjs score`, is committed in this PR, before any verdict exists.

**Why.** The German and French print pages that hold stored Flash-Lite text are being corrected by the #7558 lane. #7835 T2 found a fresh read@4 ahead of the correction on 40 Fraktur pages (33/40 against 27/40, p 0.11). Arm c (GPU draft, then agy) had the lowest diplomatic CER in #7835 T3, but was never judged on these books. Those samples were small, Fraktur-only, and drew every book equally. The queue is not equal: a few books owe most of the pages. Derek, 2026-10-31: "the sample matters".

### Frame (`frame.mjs census`, run 2026-10-31 14:45Z)

- **Books.** The correction lane's own query (`correctMain`): visible, `pages_count > 0`, `language` /^(German|French)/, `pipeline_auto.status` idle, no `hold`, not `held`. 2,690 German and 847 French books.
- **Owed pages.** Per book, the lane's `correctablePages` restated: Flash-Lite OCR (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite[-preview]`), not edited, not manual, not withheld, page type not skipped, ≥ 300 characters, not tagged handwritten, interior (`isInterior` on the last page number). Less the pages in the lane's gex45 ledger (`/root/jobs/cli-ocr-correct/correct-ledger.jsonl`, 27,119 rows) and in `lane_judge_verdicts`.
- **The queue.** German 234,953 owed pages in 1,233 books; French 76,165 in 337. (The issue's "about 410K" counted before the lane's last runs and without the interior rule.)
- **Exclusions** (`frame.mjs exclusions`): the books of #7701, #7818 and #7835, from every page and book id in their committed results and samples (`route-judge-6740/results/*7701*`, `correction-pass-7818/results/release/`, `fraktur-paired-7835/results/`, the router evidence): 418 books, of which 74 German (14,984 owed pages) and 8 French (722) are in the queue. Left to draw from: German 219,969 pages in 1,159 books, French 75,443 in 329. Declared gap: #7835's T2 pages that were judged but not written are not in its committed results, so up to about 10 of its books may remain in the frame.
- **"Next".** The lane takes books in `processing_priority`, then id, order; every owed page is one it will take. The frame is the whole queue. `results/frame.json` also reports the head of the queue (the first 20,000 owed pages a language in the lane's order) against the whole, so a reader can see whether the books taken first differ.

### Strata, weights, draw (`frame.mjs draw`, seed 78531)

- **Explicit strata**, per language: century band of the book's year (≤ 1600, 17th, 18th, 19th+, undated) × scan band. A book's scan band is `good` when at least half of its owed pages carry the stored read's own `<scan-quality>good</scan-quality>` tag, else `fair-poor`. That tag is on every Flash-Lite page. The book-level `scan_quality.score` is missing on many books, so it is reported but not used.
- **Allocation.** German 150 pages, French 60, proportional to owed pages by largest remainder. A stratum under 1% of its language's owed pages gets no page and is reported as uncovered (German 1.1% of pages, French 0.1%). Each covered stratum gets at least 2.
  - German: 17th good 25, 17th fair-poor 4, 18th good 77, 18th fair-poor 10, 19th+ good 14, 19th+ fair-poor 7, ≤ 1600 good 13.
  - French: 17th good 14, 17th fair-poor 2, 18th good 20, 18th fair-poor 2, 19th+ good 14, 19th+ fair-poor 3, ≤ 1600 good 5.
- **Draw.** Sequential Poisson sampling, PPS on owed pages. Each book gets one uniform (`makeRng(78531)` over all owing books in id order, drawn before exclusions, so the exclusion list cannot move the draw), key = U / owed. A stratum's books are taken in ascending key; the first n_h are the sample and the rest are its reserves, in order.
- **The page.** One owed page of the book, uniform from a stream seeded by the book id, with an image source. Its block is the page and the next 3 visible pages of the book (shifted back at the book's end); a book of under 4 pages is replaced.
- **Typeface** (post-stratum). One agy call a page (`agyFace`, #7835 T4, unchanged): fraktur / antiqua / mixed / none. A page tagged `none` (no printed body text), an unfetchable image (e-rara answers 403 to this box), or a failed tag is replaced by the stratum's next reserve, and counted. Tags run in stratum order, 2 at a time, until each stratum holds n_h usable pages.
- **Weights.** Horvitz–Thompson: a page stands for w = owed / π pages, with π = min(1, n_h · owed / M_h) (M_h is the stratum's owed pages). Inside a stratum the draw is self-weighting unless a book is big enough to be certain. Every weighted figure below uses w within the language. Unweighted k/n are reported beside it.

### Arms, all on the same page (`arms.mjs`; every apply is a DRY run with `--emit-written`; nothing is written)

- **lite**: the stored text. It is the reference, and what every refused arm serves.
- **1, `corr`**: the live #7558 path. `cli-ocr.mjs read --correct-prompt=<fc-prompt.mjs template> --lane=agy-correct-lite-7558` on the stored draft, 1 a call, then `apply --mark-stale=agy-correct-lite-7558`, with all of its guards (the 25% cap, UNCHANGED, CONTAIN). Refused → lite.
- **2, `gpu`**: arm c as the armc lane runs it. The GPU draft is PERO for a page tagged fraktur or mixed, and LightOnOCR-3-1B for antiqua. It is made from the exact image bytes the judge sees (`gpu-stage`), as one hand-queued gex45 gpu-queue task (`gpu-task.sh`) ahead of production, then turned into one draft a page by armc-collect's `armcDraftText`. Then `cli-ocr.mjs read --correct-prompt=<GPU_TEMPLATE 0601ef30e816f7a7> --lane=gpu-agy-correct-lite-7567 --gpu-draft --image-dir --over-stored` and `apply --only --mark-stale=gpu-agy-correct-lite-7567` (the 40% floor against the stored text, then the E3 diff guard). No draft, or a draft under 30 word characters, serves lite.
- **3, `read4`**: a fresh read of the block, 4 a call, on the live first-read prompt (`read --per-call=4`), then the plain `apply`: the 40% shared-words floor against the stored text. Refused → lite.
- **4, `read1`**: the same read of the page alone, 1 a call, then the plain `apply`. Refused → lite.
- **Common.** Model `gemini-3.8-flash-low` on agy's default pool. agy runs 2 calls at a time in all (#7835 A1). Reads are not `--fresh`: a kept read of the identical request is reused, as the lanes do, and costs 0 calls. A read the box's OOM killer took (`exit -9`) is retried once (#7835 A1's rule, `arms.mjs retry-killed`); a second kill stands.
- **GPU.** Hand-queued in `/root/gpu-queue/pending` with `/root/gpu-queue/ocr-filler/PAUSE` touched while it runs, removed after. If a running `zy-ocr-gpu-*` filler chunk would delay it by more than 20 minutes, that chunk may be stopped after confirming that its written pages are kept and the rest are re-picked; the stop is logged on #6871.

### Judge (`judge.mjs`)

- **Judge call.** Opus via `claude -p --model opus` on this box's subscription, with `judgePrompt` (task ocr, language German or French) unchanged. The page image is in the workspace, one text a call, and the judge is blind to the arm. A text identical to one already queued for the page is judged once and stands for every arm that served it.
- **Order.** `makeRng(78532)` over the items. Texts some arm served (tier 0) go first; texts only the stored lite holds (tier 1) go last, so if the meter binds, the stored-text baseline is what gets cut, and the cut is reported. 3 calls at a time.
- **Budget.** At most 1,100 Opus calls, counted from the verdict file. The plan is about 210 × 4 distinct texts, the lite-only texts, and 16 controls. Pace: the box's guard, stopping at weekly ≥ 85% or 5-hour ≥ 95%, and resuming after the 5-hour reset. Never probe after a limit.
- **Controls.**
  - Wrong-page: 2 per language × face (de fraktur, de antiqua, fr antiqua, fr fraktur where it exists), this page's image with another page's text (`mulberry32(78533)`). It passes when not accepted at fidelity ≤ 2.
  - Planted: 4 per language on accepted texts, kinds B–E rotating (`plantError`, `makeRng(78534 + language index)`), scored by `scorePlant`.
  - The judge is **valid for this study** when every wrong-page control passes and at least 0.80 of plants are caught. If it is not, the judged outcomes are reported as invalid.
- **Noise floor.** #7818's κ 0.87 on the same judge, prompt and kind of page (not rerun).

### Outcomes (`analyze.mjs score`)

- **Primary (German).** Paired blind accept, with an arm that served no text of its own counting as the text it served (lite).
  - Arm 2 against arm 3, and arm 1 against arm 3: exact McNemar on the discordant pairs, Holm over the two.
  - Supported = Holm-adjusted p < 0.05.
  - Effect = the weighted difference in accept, with a stratified page bootstrap 95% CI (4,000 resamples, pages resampled within their stratum).
- **French.** The same contrasts, exploratory at n = 60.
- **Secondary**, per language:
  - arm 4 against arm 3; arm 2 against arm 1; each arm against lite;
  - wrong text and misleads per 1,000 words (#7824 `words()`), weighted (Σw·defects / Σw·words), with the stratified bootstrap CI;
  - wrong-text pages added / removed; made worse by severity (pages with more wrong_text / misleads / cosmetic defects than lite);
  - agy calls a page (the arm's calls over the pages its calls covered; a reused kept read costs 0), accepted pages per agy call, agy calls per accepted page, $ per accepted page at #7701's $0.00087 a call (GPU time not priced; reported apart);
  - by stratum, by face (weighted), and the arms' outcome tallies (written / refused and why).
- **CER at OCR-D Levels 1 and 2 on DTA-matched pages.** Sampled pages that are in #6012's same-edition congruent DTA pages (`kgram-vote-v2`) are listed. #7835 T3's DTA books are excluded, so few or none are expected. If there are fewer than 5, the CER outcome is reported as not available at this n, and no CER is computed.

### Decision rule (per language, `analyze.mjs decide`)

1. **Best** = the route arm (1–4) with the highest weighted accept.
2. **Eligible** = best, and every arm within 5 points of best's weighted accept whose paired wrong-text pages against best, added minus removed, are under 2. Below 2 is #7835's line: "no more wrong text", allowing one page of noise.
3. **Route** = the eligible arm with the most accepted pages per agy call. An arm within 10% of that rate is a tie, and a tie goes to the cheaper arm in the order read4 < corr < read1 < gpu (gpu last: it also holds the GPU).
- The rule is applied to German (the primary cell) and French separately. Arms that did not run are left out and named. A primary contrast that is supported in best's disfavour is reported beside the rule's pick.

### Write-back (the only production write)

- **Which pages.** On each page: the best judged text (accepted, then fidelity, then fewer wrong_text, misleads, cosmetic defects; ties to the cheaper, the stored text first). It is written only where it is accepted, no other text (the stored one included) was judged better, it is not the stored text, and its own dry apply would write it.
- **How.** Written through `cli-ocr.mjs apply --apply --only=<page>` from the arm's own read directory, with its guards, revision row and provenance (`writeback.mjs`, dry run first):
  - arm 1 `--mark-stale=agy-correct-lite-7558`;
  - arms 3 and 4 `--mark-stale=queue-routes-7853-reread`;
  - arm 2 `--mark-stale=gpu-agy-correct-lite-7567`.
- Every page written is listed in the results, with its run id for `revert-run.mjs`.

### Declared deviations from the issue

- The face is tagged by one agy call a page (#7835 T4: 29/29 agreement with Opus on parsed check pages), not by eye. About 230 tag calls come on top of the issue's ~850 agy calls.
- The scan-quality stratum is the stored read's own `<scan-quality>` tag, aggregated to the book, because the book-level `scan_quality` rollup is often missing.
- The stored text is judged as a reference (tier 1, last). The issue did not list it, but the made-worse outcome and the write-back rule need it. That is why the Opus budget is 1,100 rather than ~900.
- A French page tagged fraktur or mixed gets PERO (`pero_eu_cz_print_newspapers_2022-09-26`, a Czech/European print model), as German Fraktur does.
- The frame is the whole queue in the lane's order, weighted by pages owed; the head of the queue is reported beside it.
- Limits: Claude only via `claude -p` on this box's subscription; Gemini only through agy (flash-low); no paid API call; no Tesseract; no cron or routing change.
- **Done before this file merged**, deterministic and with no judge call: the census, the exclusion list, the draw (seed fixed above), and the face tags in progress. No arm had run.

## Amendment 1 (2026-10-31, 16:40Z): severity-weighted defects co-primary; the decision rule (Derek, inbox note 16:05Z)

Made before any judge call. What existed when this was written:
- the frame, the sample and the face tags (complete);
- arms lite, 1 and 3 complete, arm 4 running, and arm 2's GPU drafts made;
- no Opus call.

`analyze.mjs` changes as follows. The first-preregistered rule is still computed and reported, as `decision_as_first_preregistered`, beside the amended one.

**A1.1 Co-primary outcome: severity-weighted defects per 1,000 words.**
- The measure is #7824's, with MQM weights: cosmetic 1, misleads 5, wrong_text 25.
- It is counted on the judge's own defect tags, per 1,000 words of the served text (`words()`).
- **Comparisons** (the same as for accept): arm 2 against arm 3, and arm 1 against arm 3, German primary, French exploratory.
- **Test.** Paired per page. The difference is the HT-weighted mean of per-page differences, with a book-cluster bootstrap 95% CI (one page per book, so books are resampled, within their strata, 4,000 resamples) and a Wilcoxon signed-rank p.
- **Holm** over the two contrasts. Holm over all four primary tests (2 outcomes × 2 contrasts) is also reported.
- Supported = Holm-adjusted p < 0.05.

**A1.2 Accept is the gate, not the objective.** An arm passes when its weighted accept is no more than 5 points below the best arm's.

**A1.3 Fidelity (1–5).** A secondary outcome: the HT-weighted mean per arm.

**A1.4 Decision rule (replaces §Decision rule's steps 2–3).** Among the arms that pass the gate, the lowest weighted defect rate per agy call wins; a tie goes to the cheaper arm.
- **How "per agy call" is read** (`decideV2`): the arm that removes the most severity per agy call, that is (the stored text's weighted severity per 1,000 words − the arm's) / the arm's agy calls a page.
- **Why that reading.** agy quota is the binding constraint, so this is the route that takes the most weighted defects out of the queue for a fixed number of calls. A literal "rate ÷ calls" would reward the arm that spends more calls.
- If no gated arm removes any severity, the arm with the lowest rate wins.
- **Ties**: an arm within 10% of the top is a tie, and goes to the cheaper arm in the order read4 < corr < read1 < gpu.
- The gated arm with the lowest severity rate (cost aside) is reported beside the pick.
- The first rule's wrong-text condition is dropped: wrong_text now carries weight 25 in the measure itself.

**A1.5 Re-score of earlier studies** (`rescore-severity.mjs`, no new judge call).
- **#7818:** from its committed verdicts (`correction-pass-7818/results/release`, rep 1). Arm P's texts are not committed, so each page's points are put on one common length: the page's current stored text for Arm P, and the Wikisource draft's characters / 6.5 for Arm W. The paired difference in points is exact.
- **#7835 T1/T2:** its per-page verdicts are in its scratch on main (`$JOB_SCRATCH/fraktur-7835`), which this box cannot read (the box mesh has no file verb). The same script runs there with `--study=7835 --dir=<that folder>`; if no session runs it, it is listed as not done.
- **Reported for each contrast:** whether severity differs at p < 0.05 where accept does not ("a difference the binary missed").

**Code fix (no change of method).** In the analysis, an arm that did not run is not compared. Before, an arm with no text and no run row counted as "not accepted".

### Decisions (the rules)

- **German, Amendment 1's rule.**
  - Gate: weighted accept ≥ 0.77, which passes read4 and read1.
  - Severity removed per agy call: read4 150.6, read1 51.0.
  - **Route: read@4.** It also has the lowest severity among the gated arms.
- **French, Amendment 1's rule.**

### Router evidence

`router-evidence.score.json` (`exportScore`) is also at `scripts/eval/estimator/router-table/evidence/queue-routes-7853.score.json`, with its by-script cut. Cells: german-lite and french-lite. Routes: lite, lite>agy-flash-low, pero>agy-flash-low / lighton>agy-flash-low, agy-flash-low@4-read, agy-flash-low-read.

**No rules.json entry was added.** If rules.json named the export, `build.py` on main (`results/router-check.json`) would do this:
- **german-lite/print** keeps lite>opus. Pooled: lite 340/497, lite>agy-flash-low 235/307, agy-flash-low-read 366/430, lite>opus 299/307. rules.json carries agy-flash-low-read (1 a call), not the @4 read this test picks, so read@4's evidence is not pooled at all until rules.json names the route.
- **french-lite/print** switches from HOLD (lite>agy-flash-low) to agy-flash-low-read, 79/90.

### What this says

- **German.**
  - Correcting the stored Flash-Lite text is worse than re-reading the page, by 10 points of accept and 19 severity points per 1,000 words, at three times the agy calls a page. The #7558 lane's 25% cap and UNCHANGED answers left 27 of the 150 stored drafts in place (and foreign-letter refusals 5 more); a re-read replaces such pages.
  - The GPU draft route sits between the two. It is not measurably worse than read@4 at n = 150 (p 0.11). E3's put-back refused 46 of its 150 pages, which then served the stored text.
- **French.** The same ordering. At n = 60, the correction does not measurably beat the stored text it corrects.
- **Quality on the queue now.** The stored text is accepted on 0.55 of German pages (0.48–0.63) and 0.70 of French (0.60–0.80), weighted to pages owed, as of 2026-10-31. After a read@4 it would be 0.82 (0.76–0.88) and 0.91 (0.84–0.97).
