## 2026-10-31 · Does a life-words block stop the translator from glossing breath as "life force"? (#7458)

**Question.** The model's own `<gloss>`, `<note>` and `<term>` apparatus says "life force" or "vital energy" on 17,696
stored pages (count 2026-10-26, #7458). `<gloss>vital energy</gloss>` alone is on 4,550 pages, nearly all of them 氣.
That imports a modern vitalist reading into sources that say breath, vapour or lifespan. Does one block in the prompt
stop this on new writes, and does it cost anything elsewhere?

**The block** (`LIFE_WORDS` in `scripts/maintenance/translation-prompt-v21-life-words.mjs`, inserted before
`**Instructions:**`):
- render 氣 as breath, vapour or air, or keep `<term>qi</term> <gloss>breath, vapour</gloss>`;
- render prāṇa as breath, āyus as lifespan, and 命 as life, lifespan or allotted fate;
- render pneuma, spiritus, ruach, rlung and srog as the source uses them;
- write "life force", "vital force" or "vital energy" only where the source names such a force itself (vis vitalis,
  Lebenskraft, force vitale).

**Design.** Rule pre-registered in `scripts/eval/PREREGISTRATION-gloss-life-words-7458.md`, committed (79169b122)
before any arm ran. Runner: `scripts/eval/gloss-life-words-7458/run.mjs`.
- **Arms:** `v13a` (the live default as production sends it: page-break rules, previous page's English, neighbouring
  OCR), `v13b` (the same again, as the noise floor) and `v21`.
- **Engine:** agy `gemini-3.8-flash-low`, one page per call, $0. In the week to 2026-10-31 this engine wrote 73% of new
  translations (94,815 of 130,798) and 826 of the 976 flagged pages. Opus wrote the rest, and the paid lite lane wrote
  under 1%.
- **Pages:** 40, one per work, live books only, seed 7458.
  - 35 target pages: the stored English has an unlicensed life phrase in its apparatus. Chinese 12 (OCR has 氣),
    Sanskrit 9, Latin 7, German 7.
  - 5 controls: the OCR itself says Lebenskraft (3) or force vitale (2).
- **Mechanical measure:** `lifeWordFindings` (`scripts/lib/life-word-gloss.mjs`).
- **Judges:** 5 blind Opus subagents, 8 pages each, with the page image opened, the OCR, and the three translations
  under shuffled letters (`JUDGE.md`). The images come from `getPageSource()`; the first run's own pick matched it
  on all 40 pages. Per translation they gave fidelity 1–5, life-word renderings right and wrong,
  and serious errors.

### Results

**P1, effect (mechanical): pass.** Target pages with an unlicensed life phrase in gloss, note or term:

| | stored English | v13a | v13b | v21 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| all target pages (35) | 35 | 7 | 4 | **0** |
| Chinese (12) | 12 | 5 | 3 | 0 |
| Sanskrit (9) | 9 | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| Latin (7) | 7 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| German (7) | 7 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

- v21 vs v13a: 7 discordant pages, all favouring v21 (exact two-sided p = 0.016).
- v13b vs v13a: 4 vs 1 (p = 0.38).
- The stored English is flagged on every page because these pages were drawn for it. 3.8 Flash under v13 already
  does it far less often than the older writers did (7 and 4 pages of 35, against 35).

**P2, judged life-word accuracy on target pages: pass.**

| | right | wrong | accuracy | pages with a wrong one |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v13a | 136 | 20 | 0.872 | 13 |
| v13b | 153 | 7 | 0.956 | 7 |
| v21 | 151 | 5 | 0.968 | 5 |

The two v13 runs differ by nearly as much as v21 differs from the better of them. Read this as "no worse, probably
better", not as a measured gain.

**P3, no regression: pass.**
- Judged fidelity means: v13a 4.23, v13b 4.43, v21 4.43.
  - v21 − v13a: +0.20, 95% bootstrap [+0.03, +0.38]; the bound was ≥ −0.15.
  - The floor, v13b − v13a: +0.20 [+0.05, +0.35]. v13a was simply the weaker draw.
  - v21 − mean(v13a, v13b): +0.10 [−0.05, +0.25].
- Pages with a serious error: v13a 10, v13b 8, v21 12. The rule allowed v13a + 2 = 12, so this is at the limit.
  - Of v21's 12, one comes from the block: on zh-4, yin and yang are glossed "receptive breath" and "active breath".
  - The rest are unrelated to it:
    - a page header turned into a book title;
    - a garbled Sanskrit line and numeral slips;
    - a cropped margin note;
    - a continuity `<meta>` that quotes the previous page (the #7085 defect v18 fixes);
    - errors that the v13 arms share (zh-1, zh-2, la-2, ctl-3, sa-3, sa-4).

**P4, controls: pass.** All three arms keep "life force" / "vital force" on all 5 pages where the source names
Lebenskraft or force vitale. The judges marked none of those renderings wrong.

### What the judges saw, by eye

- v13 arms wrote, for 氣:
  - `<term>qi</term> <gloss>vital energy</gloss>` (補氣, zh-10, both runs);
  - "the vital energy endures" for 氣久 (zh-5, both runs);
  - `<gloss>vital cosmic energy</gloss>` for 天地之氣 (zh-9).
- v13 arms wrote, for prāṇa:
  - `<gloss>vital life force</gloss>` for prāṇa-śakti (sa-6);
  - `<gloss>vital force</gloss>` for prāṇasya (sa-8).
- **The template can overreach.** v21 glossed 胃氣 (stomach qi) as `<gloss>breath, vapour</gloss>`, where the judge
  wanted the medical sense (zh-12). It also carried "breath" over to yin and yang (zh-4). These are the cost of naming
  one gloss: a reading that is literal where the context is technical. They are rarer than the error they replace
  (2 pages, against 13 and 7 with a wrong life word).

### Decision

All four pre-registered clauses hold, so v21 is seeded and made the default. That is the `--promote` step of
`translation-prompt-v21-life-words.mjs`. It refuses unless v13 is the single default with its registered hash. It
stamps both rows. **Rollback:** set `is_default` true on v13 and false on v21.

### Limits
- One engine. Opus (27% of this week's writes, 3.8 flagged pages per 1,000 against Flash's 8.7) and lite were not
  run. The block is a vocabulary instruction and changes no structure, so this was not tested further.
- 40 pages, one draw, one judge per page. The noise floor on the judged measures is as wide as the effects, so only
  the mechanical measure is a measured gain.
- **Stacking:** the #7499 v20 candidate (unmerged, on `job-prompt-bench-7499`) and PLAIN are built from v13. If either
  is adopted, it should carry this block: `buildV21()` anchors on `**Instructions:**`, which v20 also has.
- **Not done:** the 17,696 stored pages are not rewritten (brief). The standing count for new writes is
  `scripts/audit/life-word-glosses.mjs`. Under v13, 2026-10-24 → 2026-10-31, it found 976 of 130,798 new translations
  with an unlicensed phrase: Chinese 915 (9.5 per 1,000), Tibetan 44, German 8, French 5, Latin 4.

Files: `scripts/eval/results/gloss-life-words-7458/` holds `units.json`, `reads.jsonl`, `prompts/`,
`verdicts-*.json`, `judge-key.json` and `report.json`.

## 2026-10-31 · Fraktur: correct the first read or not, correct or re-read the stored text, and diplomatic accuracy against DTA (#7835)

PRIOR ART:
- `2026-10-31-correction-pass-paired-7818.md` and `scripts/eval/correction-pass-7818/`: the design, the judge driver, `servedCorrection` (checked 320/320 against the lane's own reads), `servedArmc`, `spanSeverity`, `fca`, the pooled defects-per-1,000-words CI and the export through `exportScore`. Imported from its `lib.mjs`, unchanged; its judge loop, Wilcoxon and bootstrap are restated with the same rules (they live in top-level scripts).
- `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/judge.mjs`: `judgePrompt`, `opusCall`, `parseVerdict`, `clusterCI`, unchanged. `defect-rate.mjs` `words()`: #7824's word count, imported (it is on main now; #7818 had to restate it).
- `2026-10-30-german-cheaper-first-reads-7701.md`: the first-read frame and the Fraktur / Antiqua split (labelled by eye there on 170 pages: 141 Fraktur, 12 Antiqua, 17 other). Here one agy call labels each page and Opus checks 30 (T4).
- `2026-10-06-typed-references-dta-camena-eebo-6012.md` and `scripts/eval/typed-refs-6012/`: the DTA page matches (`kgram-vote-v2`), the typed pages (`tei-pages-v1`, private R2), 35/36 leaves right by eye.
- `scripts/batch/cli-ocr-lane.mjs` / `cli-ocr.mjs`: the live first read (read@4), the #7558 correction (`fc-prompt.mjs` template), the block correction (`--per-call` with `--correct-prompt`, #7701 arm C), the arm-c GPU template (`GPU_TEMPLATE`, hash 0601ef30e816f7a7).
- `.claude/docs/quality-rubric-and-sampling.md` §4.2: the OCR-D level names.

Code: `scripts/eval/fraktur-paired-7835/` (`lib.mjs`, `frame.mjs`, `arms.mjs`, `judge.mjs`, `analyze.mjs`, `writeback.mjs`). The analysis, `analyze.mjs score`, is committed in this PR, before any tag, verdict or CER exists.

**Why.** About 83% of unread German books are Fraktur (141/170, #7701), and 409,596 pages of stored Flash-Lite German text wait in german-lite/print. Three route choices rest on small unpaired samples: correct the first read or not (63/68 without, 43/44 and 20/20 with, on different pages); correct the stored lite text or re-read it (100/117 against 243/280, not paired, not split by face); and how accurate the letters are (every German rate so far is against references that modernise ſ).

### Instrument

- **Judge.** Opus `claude -p --model opus` on this box's subscription, `judgePrompt` (task ocr, language German) unchanged, the page image in the workspace, one text a call, blind to arm. A text identical to one already queued for the page is judged once and stands for every arm that served it. Queue order `makeRng(78355)`, 3 at a time.
- **Noise floor: not rerun.** #7818's test-retest on the same judge, prompt and kind of page (German and French print, 30 items twice): accept κ 0.87 (α 0.87), 29/30. It is reused as this study's A-vs-A floor.
- **Controls.** Wrong-page: 2 per stratum (T1 Fraktur, T1 Antiqua, T2, T3), this page's image with another page's text (`mulberry32(78356)`); passes when not accepted at fidelity ≤ 2. Planted: 4 per test (T1, T2, T3) on accepted texts, kinds B, C, D, E rotating (`plantError`, `makeRng(78357 + test)`), scored by `scorePlant`. The judge is **valid for this study** when every wrong-page control passes and at least 0.80 of plants are caught (the sampler's bar). If not, the judged outcomes are reported as invalid, not as results.
- **Budget.** At most **600** Opus calls (abs + controls + T4 check), counted from the verdict files. Planned: T1 ≤ 180, T2 ≤ 120, T3 ≤ 160, T4 30, controls 20. Pace: stop at weekly ≥ 85% or 5-hour ≥ 95% (the sampler's guard); never probe after a limit. If the plan will not fit, T3 is judged in queue order as far as it goes and the cut is reported.
- **Face tag (T4, and the T1–T3 strata).** One agy call a page (`gemini-3.8-flash-low`, agy's default model, gated workspace, `lib.mjs facePrompt`): fraktur (any blackletter) / antiqua (roman or italic) / mixed (both set substantial body text) / none (no printed body text). One retry on an unparsed reply.

### T4 — how much of the German holdings is Fraktur

- **Frame.** Visible books, `pages_count > 0`, `language` /^German/: 7,682 books (2026-10-31).
- **Draw (`frame.mjs t4-draw`, seed 78354).** Books sorted by id, shuffled; the first 300; in each, one interior page (`isInterior`) with an image, picked from the same stream. Drawn: 300 of 300 tried.
- **Outcome.** Fraktur share = fraktur / (fraktur + antiqua + mixed), pages tagged `none` excluded, with Wilson 95%; also fraktur-or-mixed; by century of the book's year. Opus tags 30 of the tagged pages (`mulberry32(78358)`) with the same question, blind to the agy tag: agreement k/30 and κ on fraktur-vs-not.
- **Weight.** w = fraktur / (fraktur + antiqua) from T4 weights T1's two strata: corpus accept = w · Fraktur + (1 − w) · Antiqua, per arm, reported beside the strata.

### T1 — first reads: read against read + correction, paired

- **Frame.** The first-read lane's German frame: `FIRST_READ_BOOKS`, language /^German/, `firstReadSkip(…, ['deu'])` null: 3,129 books.
- **Draw (`frame.mjs t1-draw`, seed 78351).** Books sorted by id, shuffled. Per book: its unread pages (`UNREAD`); `spreadReason` must be null; one interior unread page with an image, picked from the stream; its **block** is that page and the next 3 unread pages (shifted back at the end of the book; a book with < 4 unread pages is skipped). 450 candidates (462 tried: 8 no interior unread page, 4 short).
- **Strata.** Candidates are tagged in draw order (4 at a time) until 40 Fraktur and 20 Antiqua are found; the strata are the first 40 Fraktur and the first 20 Antiqua in draw order (`frame.mjs select`). Mixed and none are counted, not tested. If the 450 candidates hold fewer than 20 Antiqua, all are taken and n is reported.
- **Arms**, all on the same page, through `cli-ocr.mjs` exactly as the lanes call it, every `apply` a DRY run with `--emit-written` (nothing is written):
  - **(a)** the live route: `read --per-call=4 --model=gemini-3.8-flash-low` on the block, then `apply --lane=agy-first-read-7701 --first-read-only --print-only`. Served text = what apply would write. A refused page serves no text. If the live lane reads the page in between (apply refuses on "has OCR now" / "rewritten after this read"), the read stands as made, and the case is flagged.
  - **(b)** `agy-flash-low@4>agy-flash-low@4-written`: (a)'s served texts of the block's pages as `--draft-file`, `read --correct-prompt=<fc-prompt.mjs template> --lane=agy-first-read-correct-7701 --per-call=4`. Served by `servedCorrection` (apply refuses a draft-file read by design; #7818 §W3).
  - **(c)** the same correction 1 a call, on the judged page only.
  - Reads are not `--fresh`: a kept read of the identical request is reused, as the lanes do.
- **Primary outcome.** Paired accept, **(b) against (a), Fraktur only**: exact McNemar (two-sided binomial on the discordant pairs), α 0.05. An arm with no served text is not accepted.
- **Secondary.** (c) vs (a), (b) vs (c), the Antiqua stratum and all pages; wrong-text pages added / removed; defects per 1,000 words (#7824 `words()`), pooled with a page-bootstrap 95% CI (4,000 resamples) and paired per-page differences (Wilcoxon); made worse by severity (pages with more wrong_text / misleads / cosmetic defects than (a)); agy calls per page and $ per accepted page at #7701's $0.00087 a call.

### T2 — stored Flash-Lite text: correct against re-read, paired

- **Frame.** The #7558 correction lane's German frame (`correctMain`'s book query: visible, idle, no hold, not held; `correctablePages` restated: Flash-Lite OCR, not edited, ≥ 300 characters, not handwritten, interior), less pages in the lane's gex45 ledger (26,911 processed) and pages in `lane_judge_verdicts`: 2,690 books.
- **Draw (`frame.mjs t2-draw`, seed 78352).** Books sorted and shuffled; one eligible page a book from the stream; its block = it and the next 3 pages of the book. 120 candidates (251 tried, 131 with no eligible page). Strata: the first 40 Fraktur in draw order.
- **Arms**, same page:
  - **(a)** the stored lite text.
  - **(b)** the #7558 lane's own correction: `read --correct-prompt=<template> --lane=agy-correct-lite-7558` on the stored draft, `apply --mark-stale` DRY: its real guards. Refused → (a) stands.
  - **(c)** a fresh read, 4 a call, of the block (`read --per-call=4`), `apply` DRY (the 40% shared-words floor against the stored text). Refused → (a) stands.
- **Primary outcome.** Paired accept, **(b) against (c)**, exact McNemar, α 0.05. Secondary as T1, against (a) as well.

### T3 — diplomatic accuracy against DTA

- **Frame.** #6012's DTA same-edition books with a congruent page (our page is one typed page: both edges on its page breaks), ≥ 600 of our letters, whose stored OCR is still Flash-Lite: 87 books with congruent pages, 42 with a lite page (2 more had no typed text at the index).
- **Draw (`frame.mjs t3-draw`, seed 78353).** Books sorted and shuffled; one such page a book; up to 40. Drawn: 40 pages (16th c. 1, 17th 8, 18th 10, 19th 21). All are tagged for face and reported by face. The reference is the typed page's body text (`tei-pages-v1`), notes not included.
- **Arms**, same page: **lite** (stored); **(a)** agy read@4 on the block, served as the plain apply would (`--print-only`, dry; a refused read is missing for that arm and counted); **(b)** (a) then the block correction (T1's (b)); **(c)** arm c: PERO-OCR `pero_eu_cz_print_newspapers_2022-09-26` on gex45 (`pero-draft.py`; `--device=gpu` if the card is under 10% and 2 GB, else the CPU config; the configs differ only in USE_CPU), the same image bytes the judge sees, then agy Flash-low on `GPU_TEMPLATE`, served by `servedArmc` over the stored lite (E3 put-back).
- **Normalisation (`lib.mjs`, fixed here).**
  - Base, both sides: NFC; line-break hyphens (- ¬ ⸗ before a line break) rejoined (layout at every level, §4.3); whitespace collapsed and not scored. OCR: #7818's furniture tags removed with their content (header, page-num, sig, catchword, catch, meta, vocab, summary, keywords, language, script, page-type, scan-quality, columns, warning, note), other tags dropped and their text kept, markdown heading marks, `*`, `_` and `|` dropped. Reference: gap marks ◊ dropped.
  - **Level 2 (diplomatic)**: the base text. Case, punctuation, ſ, ß, the superscript-e umlaut (aͤ, U+0364), ꝛ and ligature code points are kept.
  - **Level 1**: Level 2, then ſ→s, ꝛ→r, ligature code points split, aͤ/oͤ/uͤ → ä/ö/ü, u/v → u and i/j → i in both cases. Abbreviation marks are not resolved (the live prompt expands abbreviations; DTA keeps them: a declared convention difference charged at both levels).
  - **Level 1 + case/punctuation + diacritics**: #7818's `scoreText` (`normalizeForScript` v4 'latin', ß→ss), for continuity with #7818's tables. It is not called Level 1.
  - **CER** over NFC grapheme clusters, windowed (`metrics.mjs windowedErrorRate`: OCR text before and after the page's text is free, interior insertions charged). **FCA** (#7818 A3) at the third level, alongside.
- **Error kinds (`errorKinds`, `nameErrors`; a fixed rule).** A fitting alignment with backtrace over the Level-2 grapheme strings (spaces removed); per aligned reference grapheme:
  - **ſ / s / f**: reference ſ kept, → s, → f, dropped, other; and reference s or f read as ſ. Rates per reference ſ.
  - **umlaut**: reference aͤ/oͤ/uͤ kept, → ä/ö/ü, → the bare vowel, other; reference ä/ö/ü read as the e form.
  - **ligatures**: ligature code points in the reference kept; ligature code points the OCR emits (DTA writes none, so every one is a Level-2 error).
  - **r rotunda**: ꝛ in the reference kept; ꝛ the OCR emits (DTA writes r).
  - **numbers**: edit operations touching a digit on either side, per reference digit.
  - **proper names (approximation)**: a reference word that is capitalised, not sentence-initial, ≥ 3 letters, whose Level-1 key occurs in at most 2 of the 84 typed works of the frame's books; an error when its aligned OCR word (word alignment on Level-1 keys) has another key. German capitalises every noun, so this counts rare capitalised words, names and rare nouns alike. Declared.
  - **capital I/J**: DTA writes the Fraktur I/J capital as J; reference J read as I is counted apart (a Level-2 convention, folded at Level 1).
- **Leaf / edition check.** A page where no arm aligns with the typed page (#7818's fold WER guard, 0.35) is excluded and counted (a leaf or edition that differs).
- **Outcomes.** Per arm: mean Level-2, Level-1 and fold CER, median Level-1 CER, FCA, the error kinds, judge accept. Paired contrasts (a vs lite, b vs a, c vs lite, c vs b) on each CER level: mean difference, page-bootstrap 95% CI, Wilcoxon. **Judge against diff**: on every judged T3 text, the judge's wrong_text against #7818's span rule (`spanSeverity`, A2) as a confusion table, the judge's recall of span-rule wrong-text texts, AUC of accept against Level-1 CER and against span severity, Spearman of the judge's defects per 1,000 words against span severity.

### Analysis (`analyze.mjs score`, committed here)

- Wilson 95% for every k/n; page-bootstrap 95% CIs (`clusterCI`, one page per book) for differences; exact McNemar for paired accept; Wilcoxon signed-rank for paired continuous measures.
- **Supported** = exact McNemar p < 0.05 and gained > lost. Below that the effect and its interval are reported, not "no effect".
- **Decision rule, German first reads (T1, Fraktur primary).**
  - **YES, put the correction back** (b, 4 a call) if the primary is supported and (b) adds no more wrong-text pages than it removes.
  - **NO** if (b) loses more than it gains at p < 0.05, or adds wrong text on ≥ 2 more pages than it removes.
  - Otherwise **NO** (no measured gain at this n; the pass spends agy quota the first reads need). If (c) vs (a) is supported where (b) is not, that is reported as a secondary result for a follow-up test, not as the decision.
- **Decision rule, stored-lite queue (T2).**
  - If (b) vs (c) is supported in either direction, the winner.
  - Otherwise the arm with the lower $ per accepted page, unless it has ≥ 2 more wrong-text pages than the other, in which case the other.
- T3 and T4 decide nothing; they weight and qualify the two rules.

### Write-back (the only production write)

On T1 and T2 pages, only the best judged arm, only where it was accepted and no other arm was judged better:
- **Best** = accepted, then higher fidelity, then fewer wrong_text, misleads and cosmetic defects. Ties go to the cheaper arm (T1: a, b, c; T2: a, c, b).
- T2 pages whose best is the stored text (a) are left alone.
- Written through the lanes' own `cli-ocr.mjs apply --apply` from the arm's read directory, with its guards and provenance (`writeback.mjs`; dry run first):
  - T1 (a): `--lane=agy-first-read-7701 --first-read-only --print-only`;
  - T1 (c): (a) first by the same apply, then the correction re-requested by the lane's own `read --correct-prompt --lane=agy-first-read-correct-7701` on the now-stored draft (the identical request, so the kept read is reused) and applied;
  - T1 (b): a block correction over drafts on disk, which the lane apply cannot take; not written, listed;
  - T2 (b): `--mark-stale=agy-correct-lite-7558`; T2 (c): the plain apply.
- Every page written is listed in the results. T3 and T4 are read-only.

## Amendment 1 (2026-10-31, 10:30Z): reads the box killed, the Antiqua shortfall, e-rara

Made before any T1 arm, any T3 verdict, any CER score and any judge call on the texts it changes.

**What existed when this was written:**
- face tags: T2, T3 and T4 complete; T1 about 300 of 450;
- arms: T2 (a), (b), (c) and T3 lite, (a), (c) complete; T3 (b) stopped after it started (no row written); no T1 arm;
- Opus verdicts: about 45 of T2's 104 items; nothing else judged; no CER, FCA or error kind computed.

**A1. A read the box killed is retried once.** Between 09:50Z and 10:20Z the box ran out of memory and the kernel's OOM killer took agy processes (`dmesg`: "Out of memory: Killed process … (agy)"). Their reads end with `exit -9` and no model reply: an infrastructure kill, not an answer of the route.
- Affected: T2 (c) 6 of 40 judged pages (whole blocks), T3 (a) 1 judged page and killed neighbours in 4 other blocks.
- Rule: `arms.mjs retry-killed --set=… --arm=…` moves each `exit -9` read aside (kept under `killed/`), re-opens the key once, and the arm's own stage reads the missing pages again. A second kill stands as the outcome. The first outcome stays in `arms.jsonl` and is reported.
- This study's agy concurrency is cut to 2 calls at a time in all from here.
- T2 (c)'s 6 pages had served the stored text and were judged as (a)'s item; their retried (c) texts are judged as new items.

**A2. T1's Antiqua stratum will be short.** About 3% of the tagged T1 candidates are Antiqua (10 of about 300), against #7701's 7% (12/170, by eye). As preregistered, all Antiqua among the 450 candidates are taken and the stratum's n is reported. Below 20 it is exploratory: only Fraktur carries the primary outcome.

**A3. T4: 17 of 300 pages could not be fetched.** They are all e-rara (`www.e-rara.ch/i3f/…`) images, which answer HTTP 403 to this box for any user agent. They are reported untagged, and the Fraktur share is over the 283 tagged pages. e-rara's books are therefore missing from T4's share.

**Code fix (no change of method).** `arms.mjs t3-pero` compared PERO's image hash with a hash of the image as a string (always a mismatch). It now hashes the bytes. The PERO drafts were not re-run.

### T2: stored Flash-Lite text, correct against re-read (preregistered primary: (b) against (c))

40 Fraktur pages in the #7558 lane's frame that the lane had not processed. Arms on the same page; a refused correction or re-read leaves the stored text.

| arm | accepted (Wilson 95%) | wrong-text pages | wrong_text / misleads per 1,000 words (95% CI) | agy calls a page | $ per accepted page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) stored lite | 25/40 (0.63, 0.47–0.76) | 13 | 2.64 (1.33–4.22) / 4.59 | 0 | — |
| (b) #7558 correction, 1 a call | 27/40 (0.68, 0.52–0.80) | 7 | 0.88 (0.30–1.61) / 3.11 | 1.00 | 0.00129 |
| **(c) fresh read@4** | **33/40 (0.83, 0.68–0.91)** | **4** | **0.38 (0.10–0.72) / 1.81** | **0.39** | **0.00042** |

- **Primary: (b) against (c): 2 gained, 8 lost, exact McNemar p 0.11, effect −15 points (95% CI −30 to 0). Not supported in either direction.**
  - Against (c), (b) has wrong text on 5 more pages and on 2 fewer.
- (c) against (a): 10 gained, 2 lost, **p 0.039**, +20 points (+5 to +35). Wrong text removed on 9 pages, added on 0. Per-page wrong_text −5.2 per 1,000 words (−12.0 to −1.2).
- (b) against (a): 5 / 3, p 0.73, +5 (−7.5 to +17.5). Wrong text removed 6, added 0. Per page −4.7 per 1,000 words (−11.5 to −0.7).
- **Why (b) trails (c).** The lane's guards left 9 of 40 drafts standing:
  - 3 UNCHANGED;
  - 6 refused by the 25% word-change cap, at 26%, 35%, 43%, 67%, 750% and 817%.

  The last two are Flash-Lite drafts that dropped most of the page. A correction cannot be written over such a draft, but a re-read replaces it.
- **Rule (§Analysis):** primary not supported. The arm with the lower $ per accepted page is (c), and (c) has 3 fewer wrong-text pages than (b). Result: **RE-READ.**
- **Caveat.** This is Fraktur only, with n = 40. (c) cannot be served on a page where the 40% shared-words floor refuses it. Here that floor refused none of the 40 (6 reads killed by the box were retried under A1).

### T3: diplomatic accuracy against DTA (40 pages; 35 Fraktur, 5 Antiqua; all leaves matched, none excluded)

CER over grapheme clusters, windowed; the mean over pages (the median in brackets). Error kinds are pooled over the pages.

| arm | pages | Level 2 (diplomatic) | Level 1 | L1 + case/punct + diacritics (#7818) | FCA | judge accept |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lite (stored) | 40 | 6.8% | 3.3% (0.8%) | 1.0% | 0.975 | 27/40 |
| (a) agy read@4 | 35 | 8.4% | 5.0% (0.5%) | 1.1% | 0.978 | 34/35 |
| (b) (a) + correction @4 | 35 | 8.4% | 5.0% (0.5%) | 1.1% | 0.978 | 35/35 |
| (c) PERO > agy (arm c) | 40 | 5.9% | 2.3% (0.7%) | 0.9% | 0.980 | 32/40 |

- **Long s.** In the reference, 1,143 to 1,384 ſ per arm.
  - Kept: lite 0, (a)/(b) 1, (c) 0.
  - Read as s: 96 to 99%.
  - Read as f: 14 to 16 per arm (about 1%), a real misread at every level.
  - No arm wrote ſ where the print has s or f.
- **Superscript-e umlaut (aͤ, oͤ, uͤ).** Kept: 0 of 264 to 296 in every arm. Written as ä/ö/ü: 92 to 95%.
- **Ligatures and r rotunda.** DTA writes neither. No arm emitted a ligature code point; one (a) read emitted one ꝛ.
- **Capital I/J.** DTA writes J for the Fraktur I/J capital. The arms wrote I for 28 to 35% of them.
- **Numbers.** Errors touched a digit at 0.18 to 0.20 per reference digit (lite 37 of 205; (a) 33 of 162; (c) 37 of 205).
- **Rare capitalised words** (names and rare nouns, the declared approximation): 10.5 to 12.0% are not read as the reference has them.
- **Paired contrasts (Level 1).** None of the CER contrasts is significant at Level 2 or Level 1:
  - (a) against lite: +1.5 points (−0.2 to +4.2), p 0.48;
  - (b) against (a): 0;
  - (c) against lite: −1.0 (−3.8 to +0.7);
  - (c) against (b): −2.7 (−7.2 to +0.5).

  At the folded level, on Fraktur, (a) is below lite: 0.5% against 0.7%, −0.2 points (−0.4 to −0.1), p 0.0004. The means at Levels 1 and 2 are driven by a few pages each arm reads badly; the medians all sit between 0.5 and 0.8%.
- **What this says.** Every route here is a Level-1 transcription. At OCR-D Level 2, which the rubric names as our serving target, every German page we serve is wrong on every long s and every superscript-e umlaut. The live prompt says "preserve original spelling" but names neither sign.
- **Judge against the diff** (150 judged T3 texts):
  - The span rule finds wrong text in 38; the judge rejects or tags wrong text on 8 of those (0.21, 0.11–0.36).
  - The judge tags wrong text on 9 texts the rule does not.
  - AUC of accept against Level-1 CER: 0.75; against span severity: 0.69. Spearman, judge defects per 1,000 words against span severity: ρ 0.39.
  - As in #7818 (51/132), the span rule's number spans include printed digits the judge reads as minor. So 0.21 is a lower bound on the judge's recall, not a miss rate.

### Recommendations (the preregistered rules)

- **German first reads: no correction.** Keep read@4 alone. On Fraktur the correction gained 2 pages and lost none of 40, which is not measurable (p 0.50), at 1.7 times the agy calls, and it added wrong text on 1 page. On Antiqua (n 14, exploratory) it changed no verdict.
- **Stored-lite German queue: re-read, do not correct.**
  - The re-read was accepted on 33/40 Fraktur pages against 27/40 for the correction (not significant, p 0.11) and 25/40 for the stored text (+20 points, p 0.039). It cost $0.00042 against $0.00129 per accepted page.
  - The correction's 25% cap leaves exactly the worst drafts, the truncated ones, in place.
  - Against #7818. #7818's correction-ON result compared the pass with no pass and stands as such. This test compares it with a re-read, which is the cheaper and better arm here.
- **Diplomatic transcription is a prompt question, not a route question.** No engine keeps ſ or the e-umlaut. If Level 2 is the target, the prompt has to ask for it, and that needs its own test.

## 2026-10-31 · Fraktur: can an open OCR model trained on 1500–1750 print read our Fraktur, and was Kraken's 0/18 a segmentation failure? (#7845)

PRIOR ART:
- `2026-10-30-german-cheaper-first-reads-7701.md` and `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/german-cheaper-7701/run.mjs`: the 18 Fraktur pages, their read@4 / LightOnOCR / PERO / Kraken texts and Opus verdicts, `gpuAloneWritten` (what a GPU-alone route would write), the wrong-page and planted controls, the score. Reused; the new harness is a copy cut to these arms.
- `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/judge.mjs`: `judgePrompt` and the `judge` stage, unchanged (Opus `claude -p`, page image, blind, one text a call, paced by `claudeBlocked`).
- `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/defect-rate.mjs` `words()`: the #7824 word count for wrong text per 1,000 words.
- `2026-10-31-fraktur-paired-7835.md` and `scripts/eval/fraktur-paired-7835/lib.mjs`: the T3 DTA page draw (seed 78353), its references (`tei-pages-v1`), `levelCers` (Level 2 diplomatic, Level 1 normalised) and the fold-WER leaf guard, unchanged. Its PERO draft of each T3 page (arm c's draft) is the phase-2 comparator.
- `2026-09-03-bench-2-complete-can-self-hosted-ocr-replace-gemini.md`: the source of the "segmentation" lead (read again below).

Code: `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/fraktur-models-7845/` (lands with the results; nothing in it decides anything this file does not fix here).

### Why

German print with no OCR is read by agy Flash-low, 4 pages a call (#7752). About 83% of it is Fraktur (141/170 by eye, #7701). Open engines failed on these pages: LightOnOCR 2/18, PERO 3/18, Kraken `austriannewspapers` 0/18 accepted (wrong text on 17/18). But both trained models came from the wrong period (19th-century newspapers; Czech newspaper microfilm). The survey on #7845 names models trained on 15th–19th-century print. If one reads our Fraktur well, the first read of about 140K pages could be nearly free, or a cheap draft in front of the Flash correction.

### What bench-2 actually measured (read before this test, not a result of it)

The issue's lead says the same Kraken model scored 98.5–99.8% on three early Fraktur pages in bench-2. The bench-2 file says otherwise. The 98.5–99.8% on 1618/1645/1772 belongs to **Surya and CHURRO**. Kraken `austriannewspapers` got 95–99% "on 1618/1645, decaying with era distance". Its per-page rows (`observations/ocr-observations-2026-09-03.jsonl`):

| page | year | Kraken austriannewspapers |
|---|---|---|
| Weigel | 1618 | 95.9% raw, not aligned (word guard 0.45) |
| Zesen | 1645 | 94.8% (CER 5.2%) |
| Herder | 1772 | 84.3% raw, not aligned |
| Hegel, Logik | 1812 | 99.0% |
| Humboldt | 1845 | 98.1% |

So on early print the model was already at about 5% CER in bench-2. On a 300-word page that is about 15 wrong words, which the judge does not accept. The two results do not conflict, and the lead needs no segmentation failure to explain it. It is still tested below, because the same rows cannot rule it out.

Also checked before any scoring: the 18 #7701 Fraktur pages are **single pages, not spreads** (width/height 0.57–0.80, by the stored image sizes). So "blla on whole spreads" cannot be what happened. Whether blla cut the lines badly on single pages remains open.

### Pages

- **Phase 1.** The 18 Fraktur pages of the #7701 frame (`results/german-cheaper-7701-2026-10-30/sample.json`, `script_face: fraktur`), the same image bytes the judge saw there. The **gate set** is the 15 of them that read@4 wrote (13 accepted there, 0 wrong text).
- **Phase 2.** #7835 T3's DTA-matched pages (`frame.mjs t3-draw`, seed 78353; 40 pages, 16th c. 1, 17th 8, 18th 10, 19th 21) with their typed-page references. I wait for #7835's T3 files rather than build references myself. If they are not on the box when phase 1 ends, I run #7835's own `t3-draw` (its code and seed, read-only) into this job's scratch and check that it yields the same 40 page ids whose images #7835 already holds on gex45. Face comes from #7835's T3 tags. The primary stratum is Fraktur; Antiqua pages are reported apart.

### Arms (all zero-shot, CPU on gex45, nothing trained)

The card is held by another tenant's vLLM (20.7 of 24.5 GB, 100% busy at 10:54Z), so every arm runs on CPU, 8 threads.

**One segmenter (S1)** for every arm except the segmentation test: kraken 7.1.1 `blla` with its default model (`blla.mlmodel` shipped in kraken 7.1.1), on the stored page image, no split. The same baseline segmentation and the same dewarped line crops (`kraken.lib.segmentation.extract_polygons`) go to every recogniser, in blla's reading order. A page's text is its lines joined by newlines.

**The second segmenter (S2)** for the segmentation test: kraken 7.1.1's legacy box segmenter (`kraken.binarization.nlbin`, then `kraken.pageseg.segment`, defaults), which shares no model and no code path with blla.

| arm | recogniser | weights (sha256 of the file downloaded 2026-10-31) | source | licence as found |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **a** | Calamari 2.3.1, `deep3_lsh4`, 5 checkpoints voting | `deep3_lsh4.tar.gz` e68d22e41d1d33ee7681e7199ff4f0221f5bd862b4bb1f4c7341d39495fd15e7 | github.com/Calamari-OCR/calamari_models_experimental release v0.0.3; Reul et al. 2021, doi 10.1145/3476887.3476910 | MIT (repo) |
| **a2** | Calamari 2.3.1, `deep3_fraktur-hist`, 5 voting | `deep3_fraktur-hist.tar.gz` 0be64a5189563de44c39bedc02a0b1b422de63790b4e4d7d5c815cad56ede52e | same release; refined from LSH-4 on historical Fraktur (README) | MIT (repo) |
| **b** | Calamari 2.3.1, `fraktur_historical` (GT4HistOCR Fraktur parts), 5 voting | `fraktur_historical.tar.gz` 49ac046b40fa3c97fdd973055caa2f2b2332010bd08f0bccb2aaa599c4730111 | github.com/Calamari-OCR/calamari_models release 2.2 (listed by OCR-D); GT4HistOCR doi 10.5281/zenodo.1344132 | MIT (repo); data CC BY 4.0 |
| **c1** | Kraken 7.1.1, `austriannewspapers.mlmodel` v2 on S1 | 376a3aa7af40161913bfbf25a799943ca1497cb9360f2cc18e6f3ea0e7feb069 (md5 = Zenodo's) | doi 10.5281/zenodo.7933402 (UB Mannheim) | CC BY-SA 4.0 |
| **c2** | the same model on **S2** | same | same | same |
| **d** | Kraken 7.1.1, `McCATMuS_nfd_nofix_V1.mlmodel` on S1 | dfb911ba25fd11f93efc1b0c340957162981ecfdaac0ee1e26793d491f770244 (md5 = Zenodo's) | doi 10.5281/zenodo.13788177 | CC BY 4.0 |
| **e** | Kraken 7.1.1, `CATMuS-Gothic-Print-1.0.0.mlmodel` on S1 | f088ab5322840273bee686c5275b9b30ea5d6cb188f428af15ea47d0618452e1 (md5 = Zenodo's) | doi 10.5281/zenodo.10599911 | CC BY 4.0 |

Two departures from the issue, both decided before any read:
- **Arm b is not "GT4HistOCR 1.0".** The OCR-D resource `qurator-gt4histocr-1.0` lives only at qurator-data.de. On 2026-10-31 that host failed TLS on this box (a Let's Encrypt "Root YE" chain the box does not trust). With a verified chain it returned HTTP/2 protocol errors, then empty replies. It is also a Calamari 1.x model (OCR-D: `version_range >= 1.0.0, < 2.0.0`). The control is the Calamari-2 GT4HistOCR Fraktur model that OCR-D lists for Calamari ≥ 2.0. It keeps the question the control asks: does LSH-4's in-period training add anything over a GT4HistOCR model?
- **Arm a2 is added.** The same release ships a Fraktur model refined from LSH-4. It costs one more pass on the same lines.

The #7701 Kraken run (blla through the `kraken` CLI, same model and version) stays in the tables as **c0**, with its verdicts as judged there. Nothing is re-judged.

### Outcomes

**Phase 1 (the 18 pages).**
- **Written.** What a GPU-alone route would write: `gpuAloneWritten` from #7701, unchanged (≥ 30 word characters, no 4× repeated line).
- **Judge.** Opus blind accept against the image (`judgePrompt`, task ocr, German, unchanged), with its defects. The outcome is wrong text per 1,000 words (#7824 `words()`), pooled per arm.
- **Agreement (screening, not accuracy).** On the 13 pages where #7701's read@4 was accepted with no wrong text: each arm's Level-1 CER against that accepted read (`levelCers`, #7835). It is labelled "agreement with an accepted Flash read". It decides nothing.
- **Speed.** Seconds a page on 8 CPU threads, for segmentation and for each recogniser, and pages an hour.

**Phase 2 (T3 DTA pages).**
- Per arm: mean Level-2 (diplomatic) and Level-1 (normalised) CER, median Level-1 CER, with a page-bootstrap 95% CI (one page a book, 4,000 resamples).
- Paired against the stored Flash-Lite text and against #7835's PERO draft of the same image (the draft #7701's pero>agy@4 route corrected: 9/13 Fraktur accepted).
- A page where nothing aligns (stored lite and every arm over the fold-WER 0.35 guard) is excluded and counted.

### Judging, rounds and controls

- **Budget.** At most 160 Opus calls, counted from the verdict file. Pace: stop at weekly ≥ 85% or 5-hour ≥ 95%; never probe after a limit.
- **Rounds.** Round 1 judges every arm on the first 6 gate pages (seeded shuffle of the 15, `makeRng(78451)`). An arm continues to round 2 (the other 9 gate pages) only while it can still reach the gate, i.e. fewer than 5 gate pages not accepted or with wrong text. Round 3 (the 3 non-gate pages) runs only for arms that pass the gate. An arm stopped early is reported as "failed the gate in round r at k/n", not as an accept rate over 18.
- **Controls.**
  - Wrong-page: 4 in round 1 (this page's image, another book's text from a seeded arm, `makeRng(78452)`), then 2 for each arm that enters round 2.
  - Planted: 2 on #7701's accepted read@4 texts of the round-1 pages (kinds B and C, `plantError`, `makeRng(78453)`), and 2 on any arm's accepted text if one exists.
  - The judge is valid here when every wrong-page control is refused at fidelity ≤ 2 and at least 3 of 4 plants (or 2 of 2) are caught.

### Gate and what follows

- **Gate (the issue's).** An arm passes when it is accepted on ≥ 11 of the 15 gate pages with no wrong text on any of them, and its controls pass.
- **A passing arm** gets the draft > agy-flash-low correction on the 18 pages. That is #7567 arm C's shape through `cli-ocr.mjs read --gpu-draft` and the GPU-draft apply with `--diff-guard=gpu-draft`, dry. It is judged blind the same way and compared paired with read@4 and lighton>agy@4 (11/14).
- **If no arm passes,** no correction arm runs. Phase 3 (fine-tuning) is not started. Its plan, with GPU hours and engineering days, goes to Derek as a DECISION.

### The segmentation finding (rule fixed here)

Three measurements, reported together:
1. **Line coverage.** On the 13 accepted pages: lines found by S1 and S2 against the body lines of the accepted read@4 text. A ratio under 0.9 or over 1.2 on a page marks that page as mis-segmented.
2. **Same lines, other models.** c1 against a, a2, b, d and e on S1 (judge, and phase-2 CER). If a different model on the same lines reads much better, the lines were not the failure.
3. **Same model, other lines.** c1 (S1) against c2 (S2) and c0.

- **Segmentation was the failure** if c2 (or c1, through this pipeline's crops) lifts austriannewspapers from c0's 0/18 to ≥ 6 accepted, or halves its phase-2 mean Level-1 CER relative to c1.
- **The model was the failure** if neither happens and the line coverage of S1 is within 0.9–1.2 on ≥ 11 of the 13 pages.
- Anything else is reported as mixed, with the numbers.

### Write-back

None. Read-only throughout: no page, revision or route is written, no cron or routing change. Every quality figure is given with its n, interval and date.

### Amendment 1 (2026-10-31, before any judge call or CER score)

- **Arm b would not run.** On every one of its 5 checkpoints, Calamari 2.3.1 with `fraktur_historical` (calamari_models 2.2) returns blanks and stray marks: one checkpoint on 3 lines gave `'    '`, `'ũ'`, `'DT¶¶ n'`.
  - It does the same on crops cut from the nlbin image (same S1 polygons). So it is not the input form the model card names ("normalized grayscale").
  - Its whole-page drafts are 45–296 bytes, against 574–2,869 for LSH-4 on the same lines.
  - Its codec has 131 symbols, of which the only digits are 3 and 4. That suggests a checkpoint for a narrower subcorpus than the OCR-D description says.
  - b is **not judged**. Its phase-2 CER is computed and reported as "did not run", not as a reading.
- **Arm b2 replaces it as the period control.** `deep3_fraktur19` is from the same release as LSH-4 (calamari_models_experimental v0.0.3, MIT), with the same deep3 network and 5 voting checkpoints. It is trained on 19th-century Fraktur. sha256 of `deep3_fraktur19.tar.gz`: eb933c4ee5ea85435edf1e18abfb2c5ef97cab8abcbcd6f193a775e6a603d7aa. It reads the same S1 crops.
  - The question the control asks stays the same: does in-period training (a, a2) beat a model of the 19th-century bulk?
  - b2 enters the judging rounds like every other arm.
- **CPU, not the GPU queue.** Derek's note (11:27Z) asks for GPU work to go through `/root/gpu-queue` ahead of the OCR filler, with CPU only where that is not possible. All arms stay on CPU:
  - The Calamari venv is TensorFlow 2.15 CPU (no build here has kernels for this Blackwell card).
  - The Kraken arms read a page in about 4 s on 6 threads and the Calamari arms in about 7 s on 8, so both phases together take under an hour of CPU.
  - Pausing production OCR on the card for that would cost more card time than it saves.
  - Speed is therefore reported as CPU pages an hour, with the thread count.

### Amendment 2 (2026-10-31, after round 1 was judged; Calamari arms only)

- **What went wrong.** Round 1 was judged at 12:10–12:25Z on 42 items. After that I found that the line crops fed to the Calamari arms (a, a2, b2) were wrong for Calamari. `kraken.lib.segmentation.extract_polygons` fills everything outside a line's polygon with black.
  - Kraken models are trained on exactly those crops (ketos cuts training lines the same way), so the Kraken arms read what they expect.
  - Calamari inverts and normalises its input, so the black corners read as heavy ink. On one page LSH-4 gave "gach dea nu dent Liebhaber"; on the same polygons with the outside filled, it gave "nach dem nun der Liebhaber".
  - Round 1's Calamari verdicts (a, a2, b2: 0/6 each) therefore measure the harness, not the models. They are kept in the results and reported as such.
- **The fix.** The same S1 polygons, one extraction, with the outside of each polygon filled with the line's own paper tone (the 90th percentile of the grey values inside it), as OCR-D's `image_from_segment` fills a segment's background (`kraken_arms.py paperlines`). The Calamari arms on these crops are **aw, a2w, b2w**.
- **Judged afresh.** aw, a2w and b2w are judged from round 1 under the unchanged rules, rounds, gate, seeds and controls, in their own packet (4 wrong-page controls, 2 planted on round-1 read@4 texts). Nothing else changes.
- **Kraken arms stay as judged.** Round 1 judged them on their own crops: c1, c2, d and e were each 0/6 with wrong text on all 6. All four stop, as the round rule says.
- **Arm b still does not run** on the filled crops (whole-page drafts 225–1,291 bytes of stray letters), so it stays unjudged (Amendment 1).
- The judge's validity in round 1 (4/4 wrong-page refused, 2/2 plants caught) carries over to this amendment's packet, which has its own controls.

## Results (2026-10-31)

Code: `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/fraktur-models-7845/` (`kraken_arms.py`, `calamari_arms.py`, `run.mjs`). Results: `route-judge-6740/results/fraktur-models-7845-2026-10-31/` (scores, keys, verdicts; the DTA reference texts are not copied).

**The judge was valid** in both packets.
- Wrong-page controls: 4/4 and 4/4 refused at fidelity ≤ 2.
- Planted errors on read@4 texts: 2/2 and 2/2 caught (kinds B and C, both named).
- Opus calls: 71 (48 in round 1, 23 for Amendment 2), under the 160 budget. No agy call was made for reading. The 40 phase-2 face tags were #7835's tagger, one agy flash-low call a page.

### Phase 1: the 18 #7701 Fraktur pages, round 1 (6 gate pages each)

**No arm passes the gate. Every arm failed at least 5 of its 6 round-1 gate pages and stopped** (round rule). So step 4, the draft > agy correction, was not run.

| context: c0 (#7701 Kraken, its own verdicts) | blla via CLI | 0/18 | 17/18 | | | 15.7% (10.2%), identical to c1 | 2.8 (#7701 basis) | |
| context: LightOnOCR / PERO (#7701) | | 2/18 / 3/18 | 10/18 / 7/18 | | | 5.7% (3.4%) / 12.1% (4.6%) | | |

- **Agreement is not accuracy.** It is measured against Flash's accepted read, which expands and normalises some forms, so its floor is above zero. It decides nothing.
- **n is 6 pages an arm.** At 0/6 the one-sided 95% upper bound on the accept rate is 39%; at 1/6 it is 58%. Both are below the gate's 73% (11/15).
- **How the open models fail, in the judge's words.** Single misread letters that make non-words or other words: "genug" read as "gelig", "Fluxionibus … Flüssen foviert" as "Axionihus … Küſſen foriert". Numbers: the section mark "§. 9." as "17", a page number 54 as 34. A word fragment at the top of a page left garbled ("(or)dinari Zeit" as "den ri Ʒeit"). Running-head ornaments ")o(" read as stray lines ("6", "V7").
  - A line recogniser has no page model and no language model, so each of these is a wrong word the judge must count.
  - LSH-4's errors are the fewest of the open arms: 4.6 wrong-text defects per 1,000 words against 20–31 for Kraken. But 4 of its 6 pages still carry wrong text.

### Phase 2: CER against DTA on #7835 T3's 40 pages

The draw was run by me (`frame.mjs t3-draw`, #7835's code and seed, read-only) because #7835's files were not on gex45. It gave the same 40 page ids as #7835's images. Faces from #7835's tagger: 35 Fraktur, 5 Antiqua. Excluded for leaf or edition: 0.

Fraktur, n = 35 pages (one a book). Level-1 (normalised) and Level-2 (diplomatic) CER, mean; page-bootstrap 95% CI on the Level-1 mean:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| stored Flash-Lite | **2.9%** | 1.0–6.1 | 0.8% | 6.9% |
| PERO draft (#7835 arm c's) | 5.8% | 2.6–10.8 | 2.3% | 7.7% |
| **aw** LSH-4 | 9.6% | 5.3–15.4 | 3.9% | 10.9% |
| b2w 19th-c. Fraktur | 10.1% | 5.9–15.6 | 4.9% | 11.4% |

| c2 austriannewspapers (S2) | 56.0% | 48.8–62.9 | 62.3% | 56.5% |

Level 2 sits above Level 1 for the Flash-Lite read (6.9% against 2.9%) because Flash modernises ſ and the e-umlaut. The line recognisers keep ſ, so their two levels are close.

**Paired, Fraktur, Level 1** (difference = first minus second; negative = first better):
- LSH-4 against PERO: +3.8 points (95% CI +1.5 to +6.3); PERO better on 25 of 34 pages.
- LSH-4 against stored Flash-Lite: +6.7 points (+2.3 to +11.9).
- LSH-4 against Kraken c1: −1.9 points (−3.0 to −0.9); LSH-4 better on 25.
- LSH-4 against the 19th-century control b2w: −0.5 points (−1.4 to +0.5).

**By period (Fraktur, L1 mean):**

| pages | n | Flash-Lite | PERO | LSH-4 | 19th-c. control | Kraken c1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before 1700 | 8 | 4.1% | 8.6% | 10.8% | 14.4% | 16.3% |
| 1700s | 10 | 5.7% | 10.6% | 14.6% | 13.9% | 15.7% |
| 1800s | 17 | 0.7% | 1.7% | 6.1% | 5.8% | 6.8% |
| before 1750 | 10 | 3.3% | 7.4% | 9.3% | 12.7% | 13.9% |

On the 10 pre-1750 Fraktur pages, in-period training helps as the survey predicted: LSH-4 beats the 19th-century model by 3.4 points (95% CI 2.5–4.2). But it is still not better than PERO (+1.9, CI −1.0 to +6.5), and it is 6 points worse than Flash-Lite.

Antiqua (n = 5, too few to rank): LSH-4 6.6%, Kraken c1 7.3%, PERO 2.4%, Flash-Lite 5.6%.

### The segmentation finding

**The Kraken 0/18 in #7701 was the model, not the segmentation.** By the preregistered rule the result is formally "mixed": the coverage clause is 9/13 against the 11/13 it asks for. The 3 pages that miss it are a defect of the proxy, explained below.

1. **No spreads.** The 18 pages are single pages (width/height 0.57–0.80).
2. **bench-2 never showed the model reading early Fraktur well.** The 98.5–99.8% belonged to Surya and CHURRO. Kraken `austriannewspapers` was at 94.8–95.9% on 1618/1645 there.
3. **Same model, other lines.** The legacy segmenter (S2) makes it much worse, not better: 0/6 with 57.1 wrong-text defects per 1,000 words, and +44.5 points Level-1 CER on DTA (95% CI 37.8–51.1, worse on 35/35).
   - Through this pipeline, blla gives exactly #7701's text. Agreement and judge are identical to c0.
   - No segmentation lifted it to ≥ 6 accepted.
4. **Same lines, other models.** On blla's lines, LSH-4 makes a quarter of Kraken's wrong text (4.6 against 20.3 per 1,000 words) and less CER (−1.9 points on DTA). The lines carry the text; this model misreads it.
5. **Line coverage.** blla's line count is within 0.9–1.2 of the accepted read's on 9 of 13 pages.
   - On 3 of the other 4, the read itself wrote 6–8 reflowed lines for 23–35 printed ones. The proxy cannot measure those pages.
   - The fourth is a bloodletting calendar table at 1.23.
   - Where the read keeps line breaks, 9 of 10 are in the window.

### Speed and cost

All on CPU on gex45 (the card was held by production OCR; Amendment 1).
- blla segmentation is the slow step: 14.7 s a page on 8 threads.
- Reading takes 4–9 s.
- One process reads 150–190 pages an hour. Three in parallel on the box's 20 threads would read about 500 an hour, with no API cost.
- That cost advantage does not matter while no arm writes an accepted page.

### What it means

- **No open model trained on early print is a usable first read of our Fraktur today.** The best one (LSH-4) writes wrong words on most pages.
- **As a draft in front of the agy correction it is not the best open draft either.** On DTA it is worse than PERO's draft (+3.8 points), and on agreement worse than LightOnOCR's. Both PERO and LightOnOCR already have measured draft > agy routes in #7701 (9/13 and 11/14 on Fraktur).
- **Kraken's failure is the model's period**, as the survey suspected, not blla.
- **Fine-tuning (phase 3) is not started.** Its plan and cost are below and go to Derek as a DECISION.

### Phase 3, the plan if Derek wants it (not run)

- **Data.**
  - #6012's DTA same-edition books with congruent pages: 87 books, of which ~60 for training and ~25 held out whole.
  - blla lines on each congruent page. DTA's page text is aligned to the lines with the windowed aligner (`metrics.mjs`), keeping lines whose own CER is under 10%.
  - About 500 pages, or 10–20k lines.
- **Training.** LSH-4 fine-tuned with Calamari, as in Reul et al.
  - On this box's CPU (the TF build here has no Blackwell kernels): about 1–2 days of 8 threads.
  - Or 4–8 GPU-hours, after installing a TF build that supports the card.
  - Segmenting the pages: about 2 CPU-hours.
- **Engineering.** 1–2 job-days for the aligner and the training scripts.
- **Evaluation.** About 100 Opus calls on held-out books, the same gate. $0 in API spend.
- **Expected effect.** The literature's 30–50% CER reduction would take LSH-4 from 9.6% to about 5–7% Level 1 on our Fraktur. That is about PERO's draft today, and far above the ~1% at which the judge accepts a page.
- **Recommendation: not now.** Revisit if a self-hosted Fraktur reader is needed for a reason other than first-read cost (e.g. a Gemini outage plan, or #5730's own-model track).

## 2026-10-31 · Does the cheap correction pass help? A paired blind test on production pages and Wikisource ground truth (#7818)

PRIOR ART:
- `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/judge.mjs`: the router's judge. `judgePrompt`, `opusCall`, `parseVerdict` and `clusterCI` are imported unchanged.
- `scripts/eval/lane-judge-sampler.mjs`: the live-lane sampler. Its pace guard, `scriptClass` and `exportScore` are imported. Its frame cannot answer H1: the lane writes only pages it CHANGED, so the sampler never sees a page the corrector left.
- `2026-10-28-lane-judge-sampler-first-run-7611.md` and `2026-10-29-judge-planted-controls-7611.md`: the conditioned first run (German +0.35 fidelity on 20 changed pages) and the planted-error validation (143/144 caught).
- `scripts/eval/flash-reread-5924/PREREGISTRATION-flash-correct.md`, `pairs.mjs`, `score.mjs`, `C-TASK.md`: the pairwise words, the X/Y key and the "worse" rule.
- `scripts/eval/harvest-wikisource-gt.mjs`: the Wikisource harvest. One flag is added: `--ref-chars=0` keeps the whole page as the reference. The default of 2,000 characters is unchanged.
- `.claude/docs/eval-design.md`: shared pages, accuracy ≠ agreement, one page per book.

Code: `scripts/eval/correction-pass-7818/` (`lib.mjs`, `frame.mjs`, `armw.mjs`, `judge.mjs`, `analyze.mjs`, `writeback.mjs`). The analysis script, `analyze.mjs score`, is committed in this PR, before any verdict exists.

**Why.** Three numbers disagree about the #7558 correction lane (lite > agy Flash-low, German and French print). The router test (#7263) accepted German 28/30 corrected pages. The live sampler (#7611) accepted German 16/25 corrected against 14/21 drafts. The sampler's paired run gave +0.35 fidelity. The sampler sees only pages the lane changed, so none of these is the population effect. The population effect is the share of all processed pages served correctly with the pass against without it. About 550K waiting German and French pages ride on that number (#7809).

### Questions

- **H1 (primary, production).** Take one page per book from the pages the lane PROCESSED, changed or not. Is the Opus judge's acceptance higher on the served text than on the Flash-Lite draft? German and French are tested separately.
  - Test: exact McNemar, the two-sided binomial on the discordant pairs, at α 0.05.
  - Effect of interest: +10 points. The 95% interval is reported against it.
  - Secondary measures: paired fidelity (Wilcoxon signed-rank) and wrong-text pages before and after.
- **H2 (model-free).** On human-proofread Wikisource pages we do not hold, does the lane's correction lower body CER and WER against the Flash-Lite draft? Measured per language by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test on paired CER.
  - Added words not explained by the draft are counted. These are words of the correction found in neither the reference nor the draft. Runs of 3 or more such words are counted as invented phrases.
- **H3 (instrument).**
  - Test-retest: 30 items judged twice, Cohen's κ on accept. This is the A-vs-A noise floor, and it runs FIRST.
  - Acceptance against CER on the Arm W texts: the AUC (an accepted text has lower CER than a rejected one), and the CER at which acceptance falls to 50% (a logistic fit, with a page bootstrap).
  - Agreement with a second judge, Gemini via agy. It is reported only and never decides anything.
- **H4 (exploratory).** Why did the router test read higher than the live lane? This compares models, CLI, mode and prompt between the lane's reads and the test. It also compares page covariates (century, draft length, draft acceptance) and records whether Fraktur or Antiqua is recorded anywhere.
- **H5 (exploratory).** The latin-blank 35/76 in `lane_judge_verdicts` is split by sampler stratum (flagged against random), by route and lane, and by script, before anyone quotes it against arm c's 18/18.

### Arm P (production)

- **Frame.** The lane's own ledger on gex45 (`/root/jobs/cli-ocr-correct/correct-ledger.jsonl`), rows dated before **2026-10-30T12:00Z**.
  - The ledger has one row per page tried, with outcome `written` / `unchanged` / `contain` / `other`. `other` is mostly the apply guard's 25% word-change refusal.
  - The copy used here has sha256 `852cf844…b323` and 27,119 rows.
  - Books in German (`/^German/`) and French (`/^French/`, French/Greek included) only. The Latin rows are the Claude fallback lane, a different route.
  - The sampler store is never the frame. Pages it already judged are skipped, so this export never double-counts them.
- **Frame shares.**

  | language | processed pages | books | written | unchanged | contain | other | changed share (pages) | changed share (book mean) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | German | 18,065 | 90 | 13,868 | 680 | 26 | 3,491 | 0.765 | 0.711 |
  | French | 8,827 | 45 | 5,932 | 1,625 | 8 | 1,262 | 0.672 | 0.544 |
- **Draw (`frame.mjs draw`, seed 7818).**
  - Books are sorted by id and shuffled with `makeRng(7818 + 1)` for German and `+ 2` for French. In each book the ledgered pages are shuffled with the same stream. The first eligible page is taken, one per book, up to 60 books per language.
  - Eligible means all of the following:
    - The book is visible, has pages and is not held.
    - The page is print by `scriptClass` (print or mixed).
    - For a `written` page: the newest `page_revisions` row with reason `#7558 correction lane…` has a `next_hash` that is still the page's text, and its `data` (the draft) is a Flash-Lite read.
    - For any other outcome: the stored OCR is still a Flash-Lite read, not updated since the ledger row. The draft is the served text.
  - **French has 45 books in the frame, so n = 43, not 60.** Two books had no eligible page (5 pages not print, 1 judged by the sampler).
  - The draw ran while this file was written, to check the code. It reads no verdict.
    - German: 60 pages, 47 written, 1 contain, 12 other; 14 pages serve the draft text unchanged.
    - French: 43 pages, 28 written, 5 unchanged, 10 other; 15 serve the draft.
- **Items.**
  - Where served ≠ draft, the page gives two items: the draft (route `lite`) and the served text (route `lite>agy-flash-low` as readers get it).
  - Where they are equal, the page gives one item, which stands for both. The judge.mjs rule is that a text is judged once.
- **Population effect.** One page per book makes the sample estimate book-weighted. It is reported as is. The page-weighted effect is also reported: (changed share of the frame's pages) × (effect on the sample's changed pages), with the bootstrap interval of the second factor.

### Arm W (Wikisource ground truth)

- **W1. Harvest (`armw.mjs harvest`).**
  - Command: `harvest-wikisource-gt.mjs --wiki=de|fr --from=1500 --to=1850 --max=80 --seed=20261031 --ref-chars=0`, run at `--level=4` and at `--level=3`.
  - One page per work, from the middle 35–75% of the work, with at least 600 characters. This is the harvester's standing rule.
  - Pages are taken level-4 first, in harvest order, then level-3 pages of works not yet taken. The first 40 per language are used.
  - A work is dropped as HELD when a book in `books` (any visibility) has a year within 2 of it and shares at least 60% (and at least 2) of the first six 4+-letter title words. Drops are listed in `ws/set.json`.
  - Known biases (the harvester's CAVEAT 2) select easier pages: volunteer-chosen works, pages of 600+ characters, middle of the book, the first ~6,000 index titles before the seeded shuffle. Every Arm W number is quoted with this.
- **W2. Draft.** The production Flash-Lite request, as `realtime-ocr.mjs` sends it:
  - `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` on the paid API, through `gemini-script-client.mjs callGemini`, which meters it;
  - the live OCR prompt (`liveOcrPrompt`), temperature 0.1, 16,384 output tokens, thinking budget 0, the Commons 1800 px page image;
  - a hard cap of **$3**, counted at $0.25 / $1.50 per million tokens. Nothing other than flash-lite touches the paid API.
- **W3. Correction.**
  - The template is the lane's own: `fc-prompt.mjs`, built as `cli-ocr-lane.mjs correct` builds it. It refuses if the live prompt moved. Its content hash is recorded.
  - The read is the lane's request byte for byte: `template.split('{draft}').join(draft) + ' @./<key>.jpg'`, `agy -p --model gemini-3.8-flash-low` with `CLI_SAFE_ARGS` and the tool gate. Like `cli-ocr.mjs read`, it nudges once on a denied tool and re-reads once on a wrapper, chatter or truncation problem.
  - The served text follows `cli-ocr.mjs apply`'s correct-mode guards: UNCHANGED, CONTAIN, refusal, chatter, loop, the truncation guard, foreign script, extra headers, and the 25% word-change refusal. Where one fires, the draft is served.
  - **Deviation from the brief, declared.** `cli-ocr.mjs` is a top-level script and cannot be imported, so the call and the served-text rule are restated in `lib.mjs` (`correctionRead`, `servedCorrection`). Every guard that lives in a library is imported. Only the REFUSAL regex and the 25% word count are restated.
    - The check: `servedCorrection` was run on the lane's OWN reads, 400 seeded ledger rows. 320 had their read files and an outcome decided by the read; the rest were pages whose OCR changed under the lane, or reads no longer on disk.
    - It reproduced the ledger outcome on **320/320** (`frame/replica-check.json`: written 229, unchanged 28, other 63).
- **W4. Scoring (`lib.mjs scoreText`, normalisation fixed here).**
  - From every OCR text, these tags are removed WITH their content: header, page-num, sig, catchword, catch, meta, vocab, summary, keywords, language, script, page-type, scan-quality, columns, warning, note. Wikisource keeps running heads, page numbers and footnotes out of the page body.
  - ß and ẞ fold to ss on both sides.
  - Then `scoreAgainstReference(reference, ocr, 'latin')` (`normalizeForScript` v4): lowercase, diacritics folded, ſ→s, u/v and i/j folded, & → et, letters and digits only, line-break hyphens rejoined.
  - **CER** is the windowed CER (interior insertions charged, leading and trailing text free).
  - **WER** is `subsequenceWER`.
  - A page whose DRAFT fails the guard (WER > 0.35) has no clean reference on the image (a page offset between Wikisource and Commons, say). It is excluded from every Arm W roll-up and listed.

### Judging (`judge.mjs`)

- **Absolute.** `judgePrompt` (task ocr), unchanged, with the page image as `./page.jpg`. Opus via `claude -p --model opus` on this box's subscription (`opusCall`; the env is scrubbed of API keys).
  - One text per call, so the judge never sees the other arm.
  - Items are queued in a seeded shuffle (78185), 3 at a time.
  - A call counts once parsed. A quota reply stops the run.
- **Pairwise.** Pages whose two texts differ, in both arms. Both texts are inline with the image under X/Y.
  - The order is fixed per page by `mulberry32(78182)` in sorted page-key order. The key file is opened only by `analyze.mjs`.
  - The words are C-TASK.md's (misleading / flawed / sound; prefer X / Y / tie; loser material), with the language named.
  - "Worse" (served misleading where the draft is not, or the draft preferred with a material loss) and "better" (the mirror) follow `score.mjs`.
- **Noise floor first (H3).** 30 Arm P items, 15 per language, drawn with `mulberry32(78181)`, each judged twice in separate calls.
  - κ on accept is computed and posted to #7818 BEFORE any other item is judged.
  - The first judgment of each is its verdict.
- **Controls.**
  - **Wrong-page:** 2 per language × arm. The image of one page is shown with another book's served text (`mulberry32(78184)`). A control passes when the judge does not accept it and gives fidelity ≤ 2.
  - **Planted:** 4 per language on Arm P served texts the judge accepted, one error each. The kinds B, C, D, E rotate (`plantError`, seed 78183). A plant is caught by `scorePlant`.
  - The judge is **valid for this study** when every wrong-page control passes and at least 0.80 of plants are caught (the sampler's bar). If it is not valid, H1 and H2's judged numbers are reported as invalid, not as results.
- **Second judge.** The same `judgePrompt` through agy's default model (`gemini-3.8-flash-low`), one call per item, with the JSON between markers. It covers every absolute item the pool allows. It is reported as κ against Opus and decides nothing.
  - Note: it is the same model family and tier as the corrector, so self-preference is possible.
- **Budget.** At most **650** Opus calls for the study, counted from the verdict files. Planned:
  - Arm P: 177 absolute + 74 pairwise;
  - Arm W: about 150 absolute + about 70 pairwise;
  - noise: 30; controls: 16.

  Pace: the run stops at weekly ≥ 85% or 5-hour ≥ 95% (the sampler's guard) and never probes after a limit. If the meter shows the plan will not fit, Arm P German is cut to its first 40 books in draw order, and the cut is reported.

### Analysis (`analyze.mjs score`, committed here)

- **Rules.** Wilson 95% intervals for every k/n. Page-bootstrap 95% intervals (4,000 resamples, `clusterCI`; one page per book or work, so the page is the cluster) for differences.
- **H1 supported** in a language if the exact McNemar p < 0.05 and gained > lost. Below that, the effect and its interval are reported, not "no effect". The +10-point effect of interest is reported as above, below, or inside the interval.
- **H2 supported** in a language if the Wilcoxon p < 0.05 and the mean CER difference is negative.
- **H3.** κ is reported with its n. AUC and the CER at 50% acceptance (logistic fit; bootstrap over pages, 2,000 resamples) are computed on Arm W texts with a clean reference: each draft, plus each served text the lane changed.
- **Router evidence.** The Arm P verdicts are exported in the route-judge score.json format, through the sampler's own `exportScore`, as `results/router-evidence.score.json`: served as `item` on `lite>agy-flash-low`, draft as `draft` on `lite`, with the controls.
- **Recommendation rule** for the correction cron (#7809), per language, fixed now:
  - **ON** if H1 is supported, or if H2 is supported with H1's interval lower bound above −5 points and no more wrong-text pages added than removed.
  - **OFF** if lost > gained at p < 0.05, or CER is worse at p < 0.05, or wrong text is added on at least 2 more pages than it is removed.
  - Otherwise **OFF** (no measured gain at this n; the pass spends the agy pool the first-read lane could use). The one-line note gives the interval.

### Write-back (the only production write)

An Arm P page is restored to its draft when all of the following hold:
- the lane WROTE it;
- the judge accepted the draft;
- the judge rejected the correction;
- the judge tagged `wrong_text` in the correction.

The restore uses `scripts/maintenance/revert-run.mjs --run-id <the lane run> --page-ids-file=<that page>`. That is the lane's named undo: it restores only while the page still holds the run's text, and it leaves a revision row. Nothing else is written. Wikisource pages are not ours and are never written.

## Amendment 1 (2026-10-30, 22:00Z; Derek's notes of 20:57Z–21:18Z, which arrived after #7819 merged)

Made before any judge call on the arms it adds, and before any CER, WER, FCA or span scoring of any arm.

**What existed when this was written:**
- every preregistered absolute Opus verdict: 295 Arm P and Arm W items, plus the 30 noise-floor repeats;
- 290 of 295 second-judge (agy) verdicts;
- 25 of 114 preregistered pairwise verdicts;
- no controls;
- PERO drafts of the Wikisource pages, still being made.

Severity outcomes computed from those verdicts are allowed, because the judge output already carries severity. Everything below is reported **apart** from the preregistered outcomes. Code: `lib.mjs` (`severityScore`, `spanSeverity`, `fca`, `servedArmc`), `armw.mjs gpu-collect | gpu-correct`, `judge.mjs items` (arm WG), `analyze.mjs` (`amendment_1`).

**A1. Severity from the judge's own tags.** Every arm and route (Arm P draft / served; Arm W lite, lite+correct, gpu, gpu+correct).
- **(a) Severity-weighted error per 100 words.** MQM-style weights are applied to the judge's defect severities: cosmetic 1, misleads 5, wrong_text 25. Freitag et al. (2021) weight a minor error 1, a major error 5 and a non-translation 25; 25 is their non-translation weight, not a "critical" one (RELATED-WORK-SOURCES.md). Words are the judged text's whitespace tokens holding a letter or digit, tags removed.
  - Reported as paired differences, with page-bootstrap 95% CIs (one page per book or work) and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
  - Sensitivity sets: 1/5/10 and 1/10/100.
- **(b) Share of pages with ANY wrong_text, paired.** Exact McNemar.
- **(c) Made worse, by severity.** Pages where the correction has more wrong_text, misleads or cosmetic defects than its draft. A correction that ADDS a wrong_text defect is listed page by page, apart.

**A2. Model-free severity of every reference diff (Arm W).**
- **Alignment.** The text and the reference are aligned word by word on folded keys (`normalizeForScript` 'latin'). A span is a run of words that are unaligned or unequal. OCR-only words before the first aligned word or after the last are free; reference words missing there count.
- **wrong_text:**
  - a span with a digit on either side;
  - an inserted run (no reference words) holding a word found in neither the reference nor the draft. For the corrections, the draft is lite for lite+correct, and lite plus gpu for gpu+correct;
  - a dropped run of 5 or more reference words (a line);
  - French only: a substituted reference word that is capitalised and not sentence-initial (a name).
  - **German capitalises every noun, so names are not detected in German.** This is a declared limitation.
- **misleads:** every other substitution or insertion, and a dropped run of under 5 words.
- **cosmetic:** an aligned word whose folded key matches but whose spelling differs (long-s, ligature, case, accent, u/v, attached punctuation).
- **Score.** Severity-weighted error per 100 reference words, with A1's weights, reported beside CER.

**A3. Flexible Character Accuracy beside CER (Arm W).** An order-independent accuracy after Clausner, Pletschacher and Antonacopoulos (2020).
- The reference is cut into chunks: its lines, with a line over 120 characters cut into pieces of about 80 characters at word breaks.
- Each chunk, longest first, is matched to its best substring among the OCR characters not yet used (fitting alignment). Those characters are then used up.
- OCR characters left over count as insertions.
- FCA = 1 − (chunk distances + leftover) / reference characters, floored at 0.
- This is not Clausner's exact chunking, and it is declared as such.

**A4. Normalisation level (OCR-D).** Scoring folds more than OCR-D Level 1: long-s, ligatures and u/v, i/j, and also case, diacritics, punctuation and line-break hyphens. The German Wikisource references are word-faithful: the harvest found no long-s in any de reference. So no diplomatic (Level 2/3) score can be computed on this set, and none is claimed.

**A5. H3 on REAL errors.** On every judged Arm W text whose lite draft has a clean reference:
- the page-level confusion of the judge's wrong_text against the span rule's wrong_text;
- the judge's recall of span-rule wrong_text pages (the judge rejects the page or tags wrong_text) and its precision;
- the AUC of accept against span severity, and against CER;
- per span kind (number / invented / dropped line / name): the share of span-rule wrong_text spans the judge NAMED (a defect quote holds a word of 3+ letters of the span).

This answers #5647's warning: planted catch (143/144) is not real recall.

**A6. Agreement as κ and Krippendorff's α.** For the Opus test-retest (accept nominal, fidelity ordinal) and for Opus against agy (accept; wrong_text).

**A7. Arm W-G, the GPU route, and H6.**
- **Draft.** PERO-OCR `pero_eu_cz_print_newspapers_2022-09-26` drafts the same Wikisource images on gex45, through `scripts/batch/pero-draft.py --device=cpu`. That is the #7263 TEST's configuration. The arm-c lane uses the same model on the card, with a config that differs only in USE_CPU.
  - TAKEN: it is run directly on gex45's CPU (no cost) rather than through the GPU queue, whose order other jobs reshuffle.
  - A draft under 30 word characters is dropped, as the GPU-draft read does.
- **Correction.** The lane's GPU template (`GPU_TEMPLATE`, hash 0601ef30e816f7a7, checked) through the same agy Flash-low call.
- **Served text.** `servedArmc`: `cli-ocr.mjs apply`'s gpu + `--over-stored` rules, restated:
  - print only;
  - the 40% shared-words floor against the stored lite draft;
  - the long-s pass;
  - every flagged number, negation and expansion put back to the lite reading (#7567 E3 / #7695);
  - a page refused at any step serves the lite draft.
- **Rows.** Four per page: lite, lite+correct, gpu, gpu+correct. All are scored by CER, WER, FCA and span severity, and judged the same way: absolute Opus, one text per call. A text identical to one already judged for that page is not judged again.
- **Budget.** The study's 650 Opus calls stand. If W-G does not fit, it is judged in seeded queue order as far as it goes, and the cut is reported.
- **H6.** In a language, gpu+correct REACHES lite+correct when both hold:
  - the 95% CI upper bound of the mean paired CER difference (gpu+correct − lite+correct) is ≤ +0.005;
  - the 95% CI lower bound of the paired accept difference is ≥ −10 points.
- **Fraktur rule.** If raw PERO's median CER on a language's pages exceeds 0.25, the engine is recorded as unable to read that language's type. Most German Wikisource pages of 1500–1850 are Fraktur, and typeface is not recorded per page. H6 is then reported for the other language.
- **Arm P GPU comparison: not possible.** Production has arm-c-written pages only in Latin (103) and Italian (102), and none in German or French (Mongo `ocr.pipeline = gpu-agy-correct-lite-7567`, 2026-10-30). This is recorded as a result.

**A8. Not done.** The ICDAR 2019 post-OCR benchmark arm (optional) is listed as future work.

**A9. Docs.** `scripts/eval/correction-pass-7818/METHODS-REVIEW.md` and `RELATED-WORK-SOURCES.md` are Derek's review, committed with each kept citation checked against the paper itself. A citation that could not be opened is dropped.

### Preregistered outcomes

**H3 first: the instrument is valid for this study.**
- Test-retest on accept (30 items): κ 0.87 (α 0.87), 29/30 agree. Fidelity: 27/30 identical, weighted κ 0.88.
- Wrong-page controls: 8/8 rejected at fidelity 1.
- Planted errors: 8/8 caught and named.
- Arm W, acceptance against CER: AUC 0.74 (119 texts on 78 pages). Accepted texts have lower CER, but nearly every text sits under 2% CER (accepted 83/103 there). So the CER at which acceptance falls to 50% cannot be estimated: logistic point 0.28, 95% CI −2.1 to 2.4. It is reported as not estimable.
- Second judge (Gemini 3.8 Flash-low via agy, the corrector's own model): accept κ 0.44 on 432 items (observed agreement 0.76). It is reported only; PR #7807 is the cross-family measure.

**H1, production: supported in both languages.** Arm P: one page per book from the pages the lane PROCESSED.

- On the pages the lane changed: German accepted 29/47 → 37/47, French 20/28 → 27/28.
- Where the lane's guard refused a correction (`other`, mostly the 25% word-change cap: German 12, French 10), the draft is served unchanged: German 7/12, French 4/10 accepted.

**H4 (exploratory): why the router test read higher.** The lane's reads and the router test (#7263, 2026-10-26) match on everything checked:

**Agreement, κ and α.** Opus test-retest: accept κ 0.87, α 0.87; fidelity α 0.88 (ordinal). Opus against agy Gemini: accept κ 0.44, α 0.44; wrong_text κ 0.45 (432 items).

### Recommendation (#7809, the preregistered rule)

H1 is supported in both languages, so the rule gives **ON** for German and for French print.

**Default: run the #7558 correction cron on German and French print** (lite>agy-flash-low, agy spare quota, current guards). It raised acceptance by 13 points (5–22) in German and 16 (7–28) in French, lost no page, added no wrong text, and in German cut wrong-text defects from 2.0 to 0.6 per 1,000 words.

Whether Opus correction should replace it for German is a separate, cost question; the router answers it, and this evidence moves the router that way.
