Code: `scripts/eval/confidence-7866/` (`lib.mjs`, `frame.mjs`, `judge.mjs`, `analyze.mjs`). The analysis, `analyze.mjs score`, is committed in this PR, before any judge call.

**Question (Derek, 2026-10-31).** "Focus on books where we have less confidence, to understand whether we need more testing, and whether our current measures work." If the stored signals predict what a careful reader finds, the corpus can be triaged by them; if not, no book-level claim can rest on them.

### 1. Signals: what exists, and on how many books

**Frame.** Live books with OCR: `visible: true`, `pages_count > 0`, `pages_ocr > 0`: **47,435 books** (2026-10-31). Signals are read once by `frame.mjs signals` (one aggregation per 250 books over `pages` with `ocr.data`) and written to `$JOB_SCRATCH/confidence-7866/signals.json.gz`.

Coverage (share of frame books on which the signal is present; `frame.mjs score`, `results/frame-summary.json`):

| signal | source | books with it |
|---|---|---|
| router cell + served route measured (n ≥ 10) | `current.json` table × page stamps | 34,693 (73.1%) |
| cell decision known (keep / switch / HOLD / UNTESTED) | the same | 38,074 (80.3%) |
| route wrong-text per 1,000 words (#7824) | `routes[].defects` | 33,901 (71.5%) |
| any score flag | pages | 26,228 (55.3%) |
| `ocr.has_warning` | pages | 5,081 (10.7%) |
| `<scan-quality>poor` (self-reported) | `ocr.data` | 9,085 (19.2%) |
| `<scan-quality>` fair or poor | `ocr.data` | 15,331 (32.3%) |
| any `<scan-quality>` tag | `ocr.data` | 36,092 (76.1%) |
| model chatter in the text | `ocr.data` | 1,813 (3.8%) |
| near-empty text page | `ocr.data` | 11,151 (23.5%) |
| `translation_withheld` | pages | 4,432 (9.3%) |
| `needs_reocr` / `ocr.unreadable` / `ocr.verdict` ≠ SERVE | pages | 305 / 203 / 190 (0.6 / 0.4 / 0.4%) |
| page `scan_quality.scan_score` | pages | 22,442 (47.3%) |
| book `scan_quality` | books | 23,314 (49.1%) |
| `<language>` tag | `ocr.data` | 44,723 (94.3%); disagrees with `books.language` on > 10% of pages: 9,690 (20.4%) |
| `page_revisions` re-read row | `page_revisions` (seeded 1,000-book sample) | 313/1,000 (31.3%) |

Read off it:
- The router posterior covers 73.1% of books. That share is enough to rank the corpus, so it is the backbone of the score.
- The page flags are present on enough books to enter as a share (most books carry none).
- `page_revisions` re-read disagreement: 313 of a seeded 1,000-book sample (31.3%, `frame.mjs revisions`, seed 78667) have at least one re-read row; the other sources on those books are sweeps (`longs-pass-5924` on 194 books, `loop-guard-refused-2026-09` 35, `bdrc` 25 …), which are not disagreement. It is too thin to rank the corpus, so it is evaluated as a standalone signal on the drawn books only (`frame.mjs book-revisions`).
- Not used, and why:
  - `books.quality_score` / `quality_assessment` (55%) score historical significance and visual appeal, not text.
  - `ocr.verdict` and `ocr.qa_screen` are Tibetan- and Kanripo-specific (< 1% of books flagged).
  - Book and page `scan_quality` scores (49% / 47%) are image-quality rollups. They are evaluated on their own but kept out of the score, because they cover half the frame.

**The served route per page (`lib.mjs routeOf`)**, from the page's own stamps, the way `lane-judge-sampler.mjs` credits a write:
- Flash-Lite with no lane stamp: `lite`;
- `gemini-3-flash-preview`: `3flash`;
- `ocr.pipeline = agy-correct-lite-7558`: `lite>agy-flash-low`;
- the #7701 first-read lanes: their `-written` routes;
- `reocr_bdrc_4523` / `tib-correct-6560`: `yigdzin` / `yigdzin>agy-flash-low`;
- the Paddle lanes: `zh-paddle-dice-lt090` / `zh-6561-served` / `zh-frame-6871`;
- `gpu-print-en-2026-10`: `english-blank-pre1800 lighton-written`;
- held-book agy reads with no stamp: `agy-flash-low-read`.

The cell is `<language prefix>-<engine>/<script>`, with the script from `pages.script_type` (printed → print, handwritten → manuscript, else unknown). IA, corpus and e-text imports have no cell, and neither does any engine the router never tested. A route counts as **measured** in its cell from **10 judged pages** (the table's HOLD floor).

Approximations, declared:
- The Paddle and English GPU cells are study frames (dice < 0.90; pre-1800), applied to every page of that lane.
- A page's script comes from the field alone, not from the `<script>` tag.

### 2. The confidence score (fixed here)

Over a book's OCR'd pages:
- **p_route** is the page-weighted mean, over the routes that served the book, of the router's posterior acceptance (`mean`) for that route in that cell. Only pages on a measured route enter it.
- **flag_share** is the share of the book's OCR'd pages carrying any of these flags:
  - `ocr.has_warning`;
  - a self-reported `<scan-quality>poor`;
  - model chatter in the first 400 characters (`I cannot`, `I'm sorry`, `Here is the transcription`, `<<<BEGIN` …);
  - near-empty: under 120 characters, on a page neither its `page_type` nor its own `<page-type>` tag marks as blank, plate or front matter;
  - `translation_withheld`, `needs_reocr`, `ocr.unreadable`;
  - an `ocr.verdict` other than SERVE.
- **confidence = p_route × (1 − flag_share)**: the expected share of the book's pages that are accepted and unflagged.
- A book is **unmeasured** when fewer than half of its OCR'd pages sit on a measured route. It gets no score.

**Strata.** Cut points are the terciles of the measured books' scores in this frame:
- **low** < 0.4636;
- **middle** from 0.4636 up to 0.7345;
- **high** ≥ 0.7345;
- **unmeasured**.

Frame sizes: high 11,967, middle 11,181, low 11,545, unmeasured 12,742. Score quantiles: p10 0.362, p25 0.458, p50 0.650, p75 0.737, p90 0.765.

### 3. Draw (`frame.mjs draw`, seed 78661; pages 78662)

- Books per stratum, sorted by id and shuffled (`makeRng(78661)`), taken in order until **high 30, middle 30, low 50, unmeasured 50**.
- A book is skipped (and logged) when any fifth of its page sequence holds no eligible page.
- **Eligible page:**
  - stored OCR text (a string);
  - an image, by `scripts/lib/page-image-url.mjs` `getPageSource` (split-aware: a page split from a spread keeps the whole spread in `archived_photo`);
  - not hidden and not a split parent;
  - neither its `page_type` nor its own `<page-type>` tag is one of blank, illustration, frontispiece, map, diagram, plate, title-page, toc, dedication, preface, digitizer-insert, archived-spread, colophon, cover.
- **Pages:** one eligible page drawn uniformly (`makeRng(78662)`) from each fifth of the book's page sequence (by position among all its pages), so 5 pages a book.
- The stored text is copied at draw time; that copy is what is judged.
- **Weights:** a book's design weight is its stratum's frame size divided by the stratum's allocation (`draw.json`).
- Realised draw: 160 books, 800 pages (`results/draw.json`). Skipped for a fifth with no eligible page: high 47, middle 14, low 10, unmeasured 17.
  - **high (30):** Latin 17, German 12, Latin-English 1. Cells: latin-flash3 18, german-lite/print `lite` 7, german-flash3/print 5.
  - **middle (30):** Chinese Paddle manuscripts 17, latin-lite and latin-flash3 print 8, English GPU 2, German 1, French 1.
  - **low (50):** Chinese Paddle manuscripts 41, Korean 3, Tibetan Yigdzin 3, Arabic 1, French 1, Sanskrit 1.
  - **unmeasured (50):** English 17, Tibetan 7, Greek 6, Russian 3, other 17. Cells: greek-flash3 6, english-lite 6, IA OCR 5, english-flash3 5, Derge e-text 3 ….
  - **The score is close to a cell label.** p_route is constant within a cell, and the cells sort by language and script: high is Latin and German print, low is Chinese manuscripts. Between-strata contrasts therefore also compare languages and scripts. One within-cell test is preregistered for that reason: in every cell with ≥ 20 classified drawn books (here zh-paddle-dice-lt090/manuscript, 58 books), Spearman and AUC of the score, which there varies only by flag share..

### 4. Judge

- **Image.** The page image is fetched once (`judge.mjs images`) and the same bytes go to both judges. A file over 4 MB is resized with `sharp` to a long edge of 3,000 px, JPEG q90. 4 of the 800 are (5–11 MB), and the original is kept beside it.
- **Primary: Opus.** One call per page, the stored text and the page image, `judgePrompt` (task ocr, `lang` = the book's `language`) unchanged.
  - The judge is blind to stratum, score and route.
  - Queue order `makeRng(78663)`, 3 at a time.
  - An unparsed reply is judged again, at most 3 times in all.
  - Records: accept, fidelity, and defects with class and severity.
- **Noise floor: not rerun.** #7818's test-retest on the same judge and prompt (30 items twice): accept κ 0.87, 29/30. It is reused as the A-vs-A floor; its pages were German and French print, and that limit is declared.
- **Controls.**
  - Wrong-page: 2 per stratum (`mulberry32(78664)`). A page's image with another book's text in the same language; passes when not accepted at fidelity ≤ 2.
  - Planted: 3 per stratum on accepted texts, kinds B / C / D / E rotating (`plantError`, `makeRng(78665 + stratum index)`), scored by `scorePlant`. The planter covers Latin, German and French only, so plants are drawn from those books.
  - **The judge is valid for this study** when every wrong-page control passes and at least 0.80 of plants are caught. If not, the outcomes are reported as invalid, not as results.
- **Secondary: agy Gemini 3.8 Flash** (Derek, inbox note 2026-10-31 18:16Z; model id `gemini-3.8-flash-low`, agy's default and the Flash judge #7611 compared).
  - The same `judgePrompt` with the image (`correction-pass-7818/lib.mjs judgeAgy`: the image as `@./page.jpg`, the marker-line output instruction, one retry on an unparsed reply). Blind.
  - Every text Opus judged, controls included. agy concurrency 2. Stops when the agy Gemini pool reads empty on `/quota`. No Argon, no Pro, no paid API.
  - Account: the second agy login (`AGY_HOME=/root/.agy-james`, held to `gemini-3.8-flash-low` by its `allowed-model`), because this box's default agy login is not signed in. At 19:25Z its Gemini pool read weekly 30% and 5-hour 99% remaining; ~830 calls is about 1% of a week (#6740's ~100K Flash-low calls a week).
  - **Gemini never changes a primary outcome, a bad-book call or containment.**
- **Budget.** At most **900** Opus calls (800 pages, 20 controls, re-asks), counted from the verdict file.
  - Pace: model-limits' local stop, then the meter. Stop at weekly ≥ 85% or 5-hour ≥ 95%; never probe after a limit.
  - If the plan will not fit, pages are judged in queue order as far as they go, and the cut is reported.
- **CER.** #7835's DTA pages and #7818's Wikisource pages are single-page references for other frames. A drawn book is scored against one only where it is in those sets. The overlap is counted after the draw: 1 drawn book (`699389a6ce15387065947dc0`, high) is in #6012's typed references, but its reference is an independent English translation (EEBO A43737), not the same text. So no drawn page has a usable reference, and no CER is reported.

### 5. Outcomes (`analyze.mjs score`)

**Per page:**
- bad = not accepted, or any `wrong_text` defect;
- MQM points = 1 · cosmetic + 5 · misleads + 25 · wrong_text;
- words by #7824 `words()`.

**Per book:**
- defect rate = Σ points / Σ words × 1,000, pooled over its judged pages;
- **bad book** = at least 2 of its judged pages bad (a book needs ≥ 4 judged pages to be classified).

**Primary.** On measured books, does confidence rank books by observed defect rate, and find the bad ones?
- Spearman ρ of score against defect rate.
- AUC of the score for bad book (P(a bad book scores lower)), each pair weighted by the two books' design weights. This one carries the decision; the unweighted AUC is reported beside it.
- Book-cluster bootstrap 95% intervals: 4,000 resamples, seed 78666+.

**Secondary:**
- **Calibration.** Per measured stratum, the mean predicted acceptance (p_route) against the observed page acceptance with a book-bootstrap 95% CI. A stratum is calibrated when the prediction lies inside the interval.
- **Unmeasured books.** Bad share and acceptance against the measured strata: is "no measurement" itself a risk signal?
- **Each signal on its own.** Spearman against defect rate and AUC for bad book, over the books that carry it:
  - p_route and flag share;
  - each flag;
  - the route's wrong-text per 1,000 words;
  - served = decided, and whether the cell is decided (keep / switch) or not;
  - page and book scan score;
  - the `<scan-quality>` tags;
  - the `<language>` tag agreeing with `books.language`;
  - re-read disagreement from `page_revisions` (sources `batch_api` / `ai` / `pipeline_preview` only): the book's median over its pages, 1 − word-multiset Dice between the latest re-read row and the current text;
  - `human_read_count`.
- **Within one cell.** Per cell with ≥ 20 classified drawn books: Spearman of score against defect rate, and AUC for bad book. p_route is constant there, so this tests the flags alone.
- **ICC.** One-way random-effects ICC(1) (ANOVA, unequal group sizes) of bad page (0/1) and of log1p(points per 1,000 words), with book-bootstrap CIs.
  - Spearman-Brown reliability of a book's mean at 3, 5 and 8 pages.
  - **Rule:** pages per book for a future sweep = the smallest of 3 / 5 / 8 with reliability ≥ 0.70 on bad page. If none reaches it, 8 pages, and a book cannot be called good from a sample of that size.
- **Re-read queue.** Bad-book share per stratum, reweighted to the corpus (Σ N_s · p_s / Σ N_s, stratified bootstrap CI), times the frame's books.
- **Gemini against Opus (secondary judge):**
  - Cohen κ on accept (#7807: 0.44) and on wrong-text pages;
  - Spearman of the two judges' points per word;
  - Gemini's catch rate on the planted and wrong-page controls;
  - **self-preference**: agreement and Gemini's miss rate on Opus-bad pages, split by whether the stored text came from a Gemini model (`ocr.model` /^gemini/) or another engine;
  - AUC for the Opus bad-book call of Gemini's bad-page share, of the confidence score, and of score × (1 − Gemini bad share). This answers whether Gemini adds to the score.
  - **Screen bar:** a book is flagged when Gemini calls ≥ 1 of its pages bad. Gemini is good enough as a cheap first screen when it flags ≥ 0.90 of the Opus-bad books and clears ≥ 30% of books.

### 6. Decision rule

- **Invalid** if the judge fails its controls (§4).
- **Triage:** if the weighted AUC is ≥ 0.75 and all three measured strata are calibrated, propose a triage sweep that judges only low-confidence (and unmeasured, if they are worse) books and re-reads those found bad. Size it from the corpus re-read queue and the ICC's pages per book.
- **More testing:** otherwise. Name the signals that failed, and the test each needs.

### 7. Write-back

- **Verdicts.** Opus verdicts (items and controls) go to `lane_judge_verdicts` in the sampler's schema: lane `confidence-7866`, run `confidence-validation-7866`, the draw block with stratum, score, weight and fifth.
  - The **cell is namespaced `study-7866/<cell>`**, and the real cell is in `cell_real`.
  - Why: the nightly `lane-judge-sampler.mjs export` pools every record in the store by (cell, route). Under real cell names, a stratified non-random draw would move router posteriors with no decision (CLAUDE.md, writing to a store a job reads is actuation).
- **Router evidence.** The same records under their real cell names are exported through `exportScore` to `scripts/eval/estimator/router-table/evidence/confidence-validation-7866.score.json`, as #7835 did. **No rules.json entry.**
- **Bad books** are listed in `results/bad-books.json` and on #7866 (book, pages, top defects). No re-read and no text write.
- **Containment.** A page whose Opus verdict carries a `wrong_text` defect of class O1, O2, O3, I1 or T17 is checked by eye (the image and the text read in this session). A page confirmed as not this leaf's text follows `containment-on-finding.md`: hold the book, withhold the confirmed pages' English, label the issue `contained`.

### Declared deviations from the issue

- Strata are terciles of the measured books plus an unmeasured stratum. The issue named the four strata but not the cuts.
- `quality_score` is not used: it scores significance, not text.
- `page_revisions` disagreement covers about 31% of books, so it is evaluated on the drawn books rather than built into the score.
- CER only where a drawn book is in an existing reference set (see §4).
- The Gemini secondary judge was added by Derek's inbox note before any judge call.
- Limits: Claude only via `claude -p` on this box's subscription; Gemini only through agy; no paid API call; no cron or routing change; read-only on page text (containment excepted, as the issue says).

## Results (run 2026-10-31 19:58Z – 21:45Z)

**Run.**
- Preregistration merged in #7868 at 19:58:37Z. Every judge call came after it.
- **Opus** (`claude-opus-5-5`, `claude -p` on this box's subscription): 821 calls (800 pages + 1 re-ask of an unparsed reply + 20 controls), against the cap of 900.
  - Meter: weekly 31% → 33%, 5-hour not reported. The account is shared, so this is an upper bound.
  - List-price equivalent $52.73, not billed.
- **Gemini** (`gemini-3.8-flash-low`, agy, `AGY_HOME=/root/.agy-james`): 820 texts, 1 unparsed.
- **Paid API: $0.**
- **Code fixed after the preregistration, method unchanged:**
  - the judge queue could index past its last job when several workers waited on the meter (crash on the one re-ask);
  - the Gemini stage skipped 4 pages whose stored text is empty; Opus had judged those, so Gemini now does too;
  - the router-evidence export attaches the controls to every (cell, route) and takes the hand from the cell's script, as #7835 did.
- Artifacts:
  - `scripts/eval/confidence-7866/results/`: `score.json`, `defect-rates.json`, `bad-books.json`, `draw.json`, `frame-summary.json`.
  - Texts, images and both verdict files: `$JOB_SCRATCH/confidence-7866/` (archived to R2).

### Instrument: valid

- Wrong-page controls: 8/8 rejected at fidelity ≤ 2 (2 per stratum).
- Planted errors: 12/12 caught (3 per stratum).
- Noise floor: #7818's κ 0.87, reused.

### Primary: does the confidence score rank books by what the judge finds?

On the 110 measured books (each classified on 5 judged pages):

| outcome | value (95% CI, book bootstrap) |
|---|---|
| Spearman ρ, score vs defect rate | **−0.26** (−0.44 to −0.06) |
| AUC for a bad book, design-weighted (primary) | **0.66** (0.55 to 0.76) |
| AUC, unweighted | 0.65 (0.54 to 0.75) |
| bad books | 51/110 |

The score carries some signal but **fails the 0.75 bar**. Even the upper end of its interval only touches it.

### By stratum

| stratum | frame books | bad books | bad share (Wilson 95%) | page accept observed (95%) | predicted (p_route) | wrong-text pages | MQM pts / 1k words (pooled; median book) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| high | 11,967 | 7/30 | 23% (12–41) | 0.73 (0.63–0.83) | 0.79 | 30/150 | 53; 37 |
| middle | 11,181 | 18/30 | 60% (42–75) | 0.59 (0.48–0.69) | 0.56 | 37/150 | 89; 78 |
| low | 11,545 | 26/50 | 52% (39–65) | 0.58 (0.49–0.68) | 0.45 | 79/250 | 153; 81 |
| unmeasured | 12,742 | 20/50 | 40% (28–54) | 0.67 (0.56–0.76) | — | 60/250 | 90; 17 |

- **Calibration.** High and middle are calibrated. **Low is not**: the router predicts 0.45 and the judge accepts 0.58. Most low books are Paddle Chinese manuscripts, whose cell posterior (14/30) is too pessimistic: here 181/278 pages were accepted.
- **Middle and low do not separate** (60% and 52% bad).
- **Unmeasured books are not worse than measured ones.** "No measurement" is not a risk signal: their median book is the cleanest of the four strata. The other English, IA OCR and e-text imports are mostly sound, while Greek and Sanskrit Flash text is poor.
- **Within one cell** (zh-paddle-dice-lt090 / paddle, 58 books, where only the flag share varies): ρ −0.20 (−0.45 to +0.08), AUC 0.57. The page flags add nothing there.

### Each signal on its own (all classified books that carry it)

| signal | books | ρ vs defect rate | AUC for a bad book (95%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| confidence score | 110 | −0.26 | 0.65 (0.55–0.75) |
| p_route (router posterior) | 110 | −0.27 | 0.62 (0.52–0.72) |
| re-read disagreement (`page_revisions`, re-read sources) | 75 | −0.26 | 0.62 (0.49–0.74) |
| route wrong-text per 1k words | 105 | −0.21 | 0.61 (0.51–0.71) |
| 1 − flag share | 160 | −0.10 | 0.59 (0.51–0.68) |
| no fair / poor `<scan-quality>` tag | 160 | −0.17 | 0.57 (0.51–0.63) |
| served route = decided route | 110 | −0.19 | 0.56 (0.51–0.62) |
| `<language>` tag agrees | 148 | 0.01 | 0.55 (0.46–0.65) |
| no near-empty pages | 160 | −0.15 | 0.53 (0.46–0.61) |
| `human_read_count` | 160 | −0.06 | 0.53 (0.47–0.58) |
| no withheld translation | 160 | 0.02 | 0.52 (0.47–0.57) |
| no `ocr.has_warning` | 160 | 0.12 | 0.50 (0.45–0.55) |
| cell decided (keep / switch) | 126 | 0.00 | 0.49 (0.43–0.55) |

| book scan score | 93 | 0.16 | 0.39 (0.29–0.50) |
| page scan score | 87 | 0.15 | 0.38 (0.27–0.50) |

AUC here is P(a bad book scores lower). Below 0.5 means the signal points the wrong way.

What carries the prediction:
- **The router posterior.** It is the backbone, and it is about as good as the whole score.
- **Re-read disagreement**, on the 75 drawn books that have a re-read row.

What is noise or worse:
- `has_warning`, withheld translations, near-empty pages, the language tag and reader counts.
- The scan-quality scores, which point the **wrong way**: better-scanned books were worse here. Language confounds this, since the manuscripts with good photographs are the hardest to read.

### How many pages a book needs (ICC)

| | ICC(1) (95%) | reliability of the book mean: 3 / 5 / 8 pages |
|---|---|---|
| bad page (0/1) | **0.38** (0.29–0.46) | 0.65 / **0.75** / 0.83 |
| log MQM points per 1k words | 0.50 (0.41–0.58) | 0.75 / 0.83 / 0.89 |

- Quality is largely a property of the book. By the preregistered rule, **5 pages a book** (reliability 0.75 ≥ 0.70) is enough to call a book from a sample.
- 3 pages is not (0.65), and 8 buys little more.

### The re-read queue, reweighted to the corpus

- Bad share of live OCR'd books: **43.4% (95% CI 36.1–50.8%)**, about **20,600 of 47,435 books** (2026-10-31).
- By stratum: high ~2,800, middle ~6,700, low ~6,000, unmeasured ~5,100.
- A sweep of the low and unmeasured strata only would reach ~11,100 of them and **miss ~9,500 (46%)**.

### Secondary judge: Gemini 3.8 Flash against Opus

| | pages | accept κ | accept, Opus / Gemini | wrong-text κ | Gemini misses of Opus-bad pages | ρ of points per word |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all | 800 | **0.34** | 0.64 / 0.43 | 0.31 | 54/289 (19%) | 0.50 |
| stored text by a Gemini model | 434 | 0.46 | 0.61 / 0.57 | 0.43 | **48/170 (28%)** | 0.57 |
| stored text by another engine | 366 | 0.25 | 0.68 / 0.27 | 0.23 | **6/119 (5%)** | 0.50 |

- **Controls:** Gemini passed 8/8 wrong-page and caught 12/12 plants.
- **Self-preference, as #7611 found.**
  - On Gemini-written text it lets through 28% of the pages Opus calls bad; on other engines' text, 5%.
  - On other engines' text it is far harsher than Opus (it accepts 27% where Opus accepts 68%).
  - Its overall κ is 0.34 (#7807: 0.44).
- **As a cheap first screen** (a book flagged when Gemini calls ≥ 1 of 5 pages bad):
  - it catches 70/71 Opus-bad books (Wilson 0.92–1.00);
  - but it flags 143/160, clearing only **11%** of books against the 30% bar. **Not good enough.**
- **Does Gemini add to the score?** On measured books the AUC rises from 0.65 (score alone) to 0.68 (Gemini's bad-page share) and 0.69 (score × (1 − Gemini bad share)). Over all books, Gemini's bad share alone reaches 0.73. Neither reaches 0.75, and Gemini changes no primary outcome here.

### CER

No drawn page has a same-text reference (§4), so no CER is reported.

### Decision (preregistered rule)

**MORE TESTING.** The AUC is 0.66 (< 0.75), and the low stratum is not calibrated. What failed, and the test each needs:

- **The router posterior is the only strong signal, but it is a cell average.** It cannot see a bad book inside a good cell: 7 of 30 high-confidence books are bad, two of them whole-book wrong-leaf.
  - Test: a book-level detector that does not need a judge. Leaf alignment, i.e. whether a page's text belongs to the leaf, as #3368 / #4790's leaf-drift check does for IA books, run over every book. The two contained books are both of that kind.
- **The page flags and scan scores carry no signal.** They should not be used to rank books until a detector is validated against judged pages.
- **The zh-paddle cell posterior is too low** (14/30 in the table; 181/278 here).
  - Test: none needed. The evidence is exported; whether rules.json takes it is Derek's call.
- **Neither judge can screen cheaply.** Gemini Flash clears 11% of books.
  - Test: Argon (#7611: Argon ≈ Opus, 143/144 plants) as the screen on these same 820 texts. That measures the clear rate at ≥ 0.90 sensitivity before any sweep.

### Containment (by eye, this session)

The judge gave 38 pages a wrong-text defect of a containment class. I opened the images of every whole-page case (fidelity 1, I1). Confirmed as another leaf's text:
- **`69af48642a821385be062737`** (*Arati Phaenomena, Geographia, Ora Maritima*, high stratum), pp. **77, 127, 188, 206**.
  - p77's leaf is the Danube/Thrace verse, and that text is stored on p74: the text is shifted three or more leaves off its images through the book.
  - The book was already held (an IA wrong-leaf hold). The 4 pages' English is withheld.
- **`6a4cb63519ae103166961ce4`** (*De Rebus Fatisque Huius Seculi…*, high stratum), pp. **2, 10**.
  - p2 is a blank leaf carrying a full page of text; p10's leaf is the opening, but it carries the closing page.
  - The same opening text is stored on pp. 2, 8, 12 and 14.
  - Held now (`wrong-leaf-confidence-7866`). The 2 pages' English is withheld.

The other 32 are invented spans inside otherwise-right pages (Paddle Chinese, Korean and Greek manuscripts): quality findings, listed as bad books, not containments. That includes the two Korean pages whose lower halves are filler syllables (`69f3296eaeeee0fa38c658ea` pp. 27, 36). Cursive Hangul could not be confirmed by eye in this session.

## Amendment 1 (2026-11-01, before any Argon call): Gemini 4 Argon as a cheap screen on the same texts

**Why.** Derek took the #7866 default on 2026-11-01: test agy Argon as a cheap first screen, on the same 820 texts, with about 820 Argon calls approved. 3.8 Flash cleared only 11% of books at the bar (above).

**Instrument, unchanged except the model.**
- `judge.mjs argon`: the `gemini` stage with `gemini-4-argon-low` and output `verdicts-argon.jsonl`.
- Same `judgePrompt`, same image bytes (`OUT/img`), same marker-line suffix and one retry on an unparsed reply (`correction-pass-7818/lib.mjs judgeAgy`).
- Blind to stratum, score, route and every other verdict.
- Same texts: the 800 items and the 20 controls Opus judged, in queue order `makeRng(78668)`.
- Concurrency 2. Stops when the account's Gemini pool reads empty on `/quota` (`AGY_GEMINI_EMPTY`), and on any agy quota refusal. At most 2 tries per text.

**Permissions and placement.**
- `AGY_ALLOW_HEAVY=7866` for this job only.
- Box and job heavy caps raised for this job only (`AGY_HEAVY_BOX_CAP=900`, `AGY_HEAVY_DAILY_CAP=900`).
- The run needs an agy login that may run Argon. The second account (`/root/.agy-james`) is held to 3.8 Flash low, and the stage refuses it.
- On the box where job `leaf-screen-7866` ran (earthai-l7a), the default agy login is not signed in (checked 2026-11-01 01:00Z). So the run goes to a box with the main login, with the inputs below.
- **Inputs:** the exact texts, controls, images and Opus verdicts of this study, tarred from `$JOB_SCRATCH/confidence-7866/` to R2:
  - key `cold/l7a/leaf-screen-7866/confidence-7866-argon-inputs.tar.zst` (bucket `sl-corpus-snapshots`, 539,287,227 bytes, sha256 `915cc6d854aa033d54094b0dc90055c17bce4d82aad2e0b189f322b19a83bec3`).
  - Restore on the running box:
    ```
    mkdir -p $JOB_SCRATCH && node scripts/workers/cold-r2.mjs get <key> | zstd -d | tar -C $JOB_SCRATCH -xf -
    ```
  - Then run:
    ```
    AGY_ALLOW_HEAVY=7866 AGY_HEAVY_BOX_CAP=900 AGY_HEAVY_DAILY_CAP=900 node scripts/eval/confidence-7866/judge.mjs argon
    node scripts/eval/confidence-7866/analyze.mjs score
    ```

**Outcomes (`analyze.mjs score` → `score.json` `argon_secondary`: `geminiBlock`, unchanged, on the Argon file).**
- **Sensitivity:** of the Opus-bad books (≥ 2 of 5 judged pages bad; 71 of 160), the share Argon flags (Argon calls ≥ 1 of the book's pages bad), with Wilson 95% CI.
- **Clears:** the share of the 160 classified books Argon does not flag.
- **Bar (preregistered):** Argon is good enough as a cheap first screen when sensitivity ≥ 0.90 **and** clears ≥ 30%.
- **Self-preference:** κ, agreement, and Argon's miss rate on Opus-bad pages, split by stored text written by a Gemini model (`ocr.model` /^gemini/) against any other engine.
- **Agreement with Opus:** Cohen κ on accept and on wrong-text pages, over all 800 pages; Spearman of points per word.
- **Controls:** wrong-page rejected (8) and planted errors caught (12), as for Flash.
- **Secondary, exploratory (not the bar):** the same screen with the Opus bad-book rule (Argon calls ≥ 2 of 5 bad), and the AUC of Argon's bad-page share for the Opus bad-book call.

**What Argon cannot change.** Opus stays the reference. Argon changes no primary outcome, bad-book call or containment, and writes nothing to Mongo.

## 2026-10-30 · Can the existing merge lane be applied as is? (#7761)
<!-- PRIOR ART: scripts/analysis/llm-verify-work-merges.mjs (the proposer; June validation 16/16); 2026-10-29-work-identity-recall-7761.md (the recall gap this closes part of); scripts/eval/work-recall/merge-precision.mjs (the second judge). -->

**Why.** About one live book in six has an edition or translation under another work_id (previous entry). The coverage report shows the merge lane has judged only 8,411 of 53,111 author-linked live books (16%).

**Run.** `llm-verify-work-merges.mjs` on all 5,226 author blocks (CONC 32, rolling pool) and `--mega` on the 37 authors with >50 work_ids: `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, thinking off, temperature 0, ~6 minutes plus ~9 minutes. 1,510 + 267 HIGH groups. Then `merge-precision.mjs --n all`: `claude -p --model sonnet` (subscription, no tools) reads every BOOK in each group (title, author, year, language, pages; up to 4 per existing id) and gives one verdict.

| | groups | all same work | volume or part | container / commentary / excerpt | different work | unsure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| normal blocks | 1,510 | **975 (64.6%)** | 116 | 162 | 110 | 147 |
| mega authors | 267 | **131 (49.1%)** | 27 | 50 | 30 | 29 |

The 40-author pilot (the largest normal blocks) was worse, 6/20, with the Suyuti, Ptolemy and Avicenna groups mixing treatises, a single book of the *Canon*, and collected volumes.

**By hand, accepted groups only.** 40 drawn uniformly from the normal 975 and 20 from the mega 131: **60/60 right.** They are respelt reprints (Linnaeus *Systema vegetabilium* 1774/1784/1797), duplicate scans (Libavius *Alchemia* 1597), translations (Alberti *De re aedificatoria* Latin 1485, Italian 1546–1833, French 1553; Medina *Arte de navegar* in Spanish, French, Dutch; Bullinger's *Confessio* in Latin, German, French), manuscript witnesses of one text (Flexel, Cod. Pal. germ. 325 and 836), and a Nôm and a quốc ngữ *Kim Vân Kiều* of 1894. Verdicts by title and record, not by page image.

**Apply plan (dry run).** 1,106 accepted groups → 1,105 planned (1 has no existing id), 1,620 book writes, 101 of them hidden books that carry a retired id, 1,370 retired ids kept as aliases. Backup: `scripts/output/verified-work-merges-backup-*.json` holds each book's full before-state.

**Applied 2026-10-30.** 1,620 books moved (0 changed since plan), 1,105 `work_id_merges` rows, `sync-books-catalog.mjs` 3,345 rows, 0 errors. Of the 59 frame books the judge found with an unlinked sibling on 2026-10-29, **15 now share a work_id with it** (27 of 228 judged pairs), so the judge-as-called miss rate on that frame falls from 59/291 (20.3%) to 44/291 (15.1%). Known flaw: the surviving work_title is the winner id's own, so Alberti's work page now reads *L'architettura* rather than *De re aedificatoria*; the proposal's uniform title should win.

**Titles, 2026-10-30.** For the 906 merged works whose books did not already all carry the proposer's title, `title-judge.mjs` (Sonnet CLI) chose between CURRENT and PROPOSED or corrected both: proposed 652, current 32, corrected 222. I read all 56: they are spelling normalisations or the original-language title (Dürer *Vier Bücher von menschlicher Proportion*, Bodin *De la démonomanie des sorciers*), and one I pinned by hand (Vesalius → *Epitome*). `retitle-verified-work-merges.mjs` wrote 2,383 books (216 hidden) in two runs, 1,814 + 569, after the first died partway. Backups are in ops `backups/work-merges-7761/`.

Pal. germ. 88). Applied: 218 books moved (9 hidden), 194 retired ids kept as aliases, `books_catalog` synced. The 10-29 frame now misses **42/291 = 14.4% [10.9–18.9]** (was 46/291 = 15.8%). ## 2026-10-30 · What share of 1400–1700 works in each vernacular has ever been published in English, and how many are scanned? (#7751)
<!-- PRIOR ART: scripts/analysis/gap-validation-sample.mjs, gap-validation-cli-adjudicate.mjs, gap-validation-estimate.mjs (the June Latin study, n=1000, #2684: its prompt, verdict schema and binary rule are reused); scripts/translation-layer/09-scan-coverage.mjs (the Latin cluster scan matcher, generalised here); the #7751 over-merge sample (40 Latin works, by hand). -->

**Question.** The per-language census (#7751, phase 11 `--lang`) counts the catalogued external translations, but outside Latin the catalogues hold almost nothing (German: 34 works of 221,931). This run measures, for each language: what share of works has really been published in English, what share has a scan somewhere, and how good the work grouping is. It is an instrument. It is blind and random, every verdict carries its evidence, and nothing was written to `books`, `translation_catalogs` or any store a cron reads. A Source Library translation never counts as evidence.

**Frames.** Phase-11 works with at least one USTC edition (`work-graph[-<lang>].jsonl`, PR #7774's K=6 run, from `/data/scratch/sl/jobs/inputs-7751/`). German 221,931 works; French 124,168; Italian 68,819; Spanish 59,582; Dutch 74,378; Latin 306,352; English 93,554.

### Part A: sampled translated share

**Design.** For each language, n=300 works were drawn uniformly (mulberry32, **seed 7751**), blind to `ext`/`sl` (`translation-share-sample.mjs`). The query card is built from the work's editions only: modal author, the 2–3 most common edition titles (shortest first), first print year, number of editions. The adjudicator is `gap-validation-cli-adjudicate.mjs --lang <l> --engine agy`. It uses the June prompt, with the language swapped in and three rules added:
- a substantial translation counts;
- a summary or encyclopaedia entry does not;
- a Source Library translation never counts.

It also reports translator, publisher, year and a quoted line. The model is Gemini 3.8 Flash-low on the second account (`AGY_HOME=/root/.agy-james`). That account may run only flash-low, so "Flash" here means Flash-low. Search is grounded: the tool gate's new `search` task allows `search_web` and nothing else. Every one of the 1,500 calls searched at least once.

Second opinion: a blind `claude -p --model sonnet` read with web search, on a seeded random 60 per language (`--subset 60`, seed 7751). Where the two disagreed, a third Sonnet read (`--tiebreak`) was given both verdicts and their evidence and had to open the URLs. Its verdict replaces Gemini's for that work.

**Binary rule** (as in `gap-validation-estimate.mjs`): translated, or not found. Unsure and container verdicts are left out of the denominator.

The **origin** of every positive was then tagged by hand, from the verdict's own prior, quote and URL text (`origin-tags.json`):
- **N:** the work was composed in that language;
- **V:** the edition is itself a translation from a third language (Latin, Greek, Italian, Spanish, French), and that work exists in English;
- **E:** the edition was translated from English, or prints the English itself (the French *Gazette de Londres* issues, Dutch versions of Stuart declarations);
- **X:** the cited evidence does not support the claim.

There are three X verdicts:
- SP081: the quoted FitzGerald line names *La hija del aire* among plays he did *not* translate.
- SP284: the evidence is for a different Granada work.
- FR033: the evidence is Nikephoros's *Breviarium*, not a life of him.

| language | n (well-posed) | any English, minus X | **composed in the language (N)** | N + V | excl. newspaper issues: any / N | Gemini only | corrected for Gemini sensitivity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| German | 299 | 1.3% [0.5–3.4] (4) | 0.3% [0.1–1.9] (1) | 1.0% (3) | 2.0% (4/198) / 0.5% | 1.7% | 1.0% [0.0–4.6] |
| French | 299 | 7.0% [4.6–10.5] (21) | 1.3% [0.5–3.4] (4) | 3.7% (11) | 5.1% (13/257) / 1.6% | 6.3% | 8.7% [3.9–18.8] |
| Italian | 295 | 4.1% [2.3–7.0] (12) | 1.7% [0.7–3.9] (5) | 4.1% (12) | same (no issues) | 4.0% | 4.9% [0.7–12.8] |
| Spanish | 299 | 4.7% [2.8–7.7] (14) | 1.7% [0.7–3.9] (5) | 4.0% (12) | same | 5.7% | 7.6% [2.7–16.6] |
| Dutch | 299 | 6.0% [3.8–9.3] (18) | 0.7% [0.2–2.4] (2) | 2.7% (8) | 8.5% (18/212) / 0.9% | 5.7% | 7.6% [2.8–16.1] |

Positives by origin (N / V / E / X):

| language | N | V | E | X |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| German | 1 | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| French | 4 | 7 | 10 | 1 |
| Italian | 5 | 7 | 0 | 0 |
| Spanish | 5 | 7 | 2 | 2 |
| Dutch | 2 | 6 | 10 | 0 |

By century of first printing (any English, final verdicts; n per cell in brackets):

| language | 1400s | 1500s | 1600s |
|---|---|---|---|
| German | 0/3 | 2.8% (1/36) | 1.2% (3/256) |
| French | 0/2 | 8.3% (5/60) | 7.3% (17/234) |
| Italian | 1/5 | 6.1% (6/98) | 2.6% (5/191) |
| Spanish | — | 22.6% (7/31) | 3.1% (8/257) |
| Dutch | 0/1 | 5.7% (2/35) | 5.8% (15/260) |

**Catalogue recall** is P(ext = true | adjudicated translated) = **0 of 72** across the five languages (95% upper bound 5–49% per language). Only one sampled work carried `ext` at all (Italian), and it was not found translated. The phase-11 external side outside Latin is the curated series plus the catalogs; #7782's LoC, Open Library and Wikidata sets are not in these inputs.

**Readable on Source Library** in the sample: German 1/300 (held 38), Italian 1/300 (held 5), French, Spanish and Dutch 0/300.

**Second opinion** (60 per language):

| language | agreement | κ (3-way) | disputes | settled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| German | 59/60 | 0.66 | 1 | GE177 van Noort: Gemini "Purchas 1625", third read: an abridged extract, not found |
| French | 56/60 | 0.47 | 4 | Sonnet found 4 Gemini missed: 3 confirmed (FR065, FR126, FR288 contemporary English pamphlets), 1 unsure |
| Italian | 58/60 | 0.49 (binary 1.0) | 2 | both unsure |
| Spanish | 59/60 | 0.66 | 1 | SP246: Gemini's claim not confirmed |
| Dutch | 53/59 | 0.52 | 6 | 2 Gemini misses confirmed (DU187 Jarrige, DU293 Oldenbarnevelt); 1 Gemini claim and 2 Sonnet claims rejected; 1 unsure |

Pooled against the reconciled truth, Gemini's **sensitivity is 0.62** (8 of 13 positives) and its **specificity 0.99** (278 of 281). Flash-low ran about one search per work, in about 8 s. It finds famous translations and misses contemporary English pamphlet versions, which Sonnet finds by opening STC and EEBO records. The "corrected" column is a pooled Rogan–Gladen correction, 2000-rep bootstrap over both the 300 and the subset. Its intervals are wide because it rests on 13 positives.

### Part B: work-grouping precision

**Design.** Gemini 3.8 Flash-low, no tools, one pair per call, blind to which list a pair came from (`work-grouping-check.mjs`).
- **Wrong merges:** 30 random works with at least 2 editions whose titles are known; two random member editions per work.
- **Missed merges:** 30 random pairs of single-edition works by the same author whose first six distinctive tokens overlap (containment ≥ 0.5, ≥ 2 shared tokens), which the graph did not merge. An author with more than 400 singles is capped at 400 random members.

The judge was checked by reading 15 Spanish wrong-merge verdicts and 12 French missed-merge verdicts by hand. All 27 hold, except that one call separates volumes of a multi-volume *Recopilación* (M23).

| language | wrong merges (k/30) | missed merges (k/30) | missed-merge pool |
|---|---|---|---|
| Latin | 5 | 7 | 35,833 |
| German | 5 | 4 | 17,201 |
| French | 7 | **22** | 10,467 |
| Italian | 4 | 6 | 19,421 |
| Spanish | **14** (+1 unsure) | 13 | 6,287 |
| Dutch | 6 | 12 | 1,333 |

What drives the two outliers:
- **Spanish wrong merges** come mostly from the anonymous identical-first-6-token join. It merges distinct legal briefs ("In processu … super apprehensione"), gazette issues, royal decrees ("Don Felipe rey de Castilla …") and *relaciones*. Two are surname-stem merges of different authors (Granados / Granados de los Ríos).
- **French missed merges** are short, generic titles that fail the specificity gate: *Le theatre du monde* (Boaistuau) is left as separate works in 1562, 1563, 1565, 1590 and 1619; *Traicté de l'amour de Dieu* too.

### Part C: scan coverage (floor)

**Design.** `09-scan-coverage.mjs --lang <l>` matches harvested IIIF manifests (Mongo `import_candidates`, read-only, `manifest_url` set) to the WORKS of phase 11. Every edition is a target.

Which manifests count: those whose `language` names the language, plus the untagged ones. There are 1,256 spellings. A value counts when it holds the language's code or word (`ger`, `German`, `pol;ger;lat`, `englat` …). Untagged means `Unknown`, `und`, null or `Multiple`: 342,010 manifests.

How a match is made:
- **Authored editions:** the author-stem anchor plus phase 11's own join: the first 6 distinctive tokens, IDF-weighted containment ≥ 0.6, and the specificity gate.
- **Anonymous editions:** an authorless manifest with an identical first-6-token title (orthography folded, ≥ 4 tokens) within 2 years.

The first pass reused 09's full-title rule, where one STRONG token anywhere is enough. Only 5 of 20 sampled Latin matches were right, because a dedicatee or toponym late in a title page is rare. With the phase-11 rule, sampled matches were right 30/30 for Latin, 30/30 for German (15 per channel), 10/10 for French, 10/10 for Italian, and 9/10 for English (*Doctor and Student*, first vs second dialogue).

Manifest counts held, by language (with `manifest_url`):

| language | spellings | manifests |
|---|---|---|
| Latin | 288 | 404,777 |
| English | 144 | 384,974 |
| German | 137 | 271,189 |
| French | 89 | 145,747 |
| Italian | 34 | 9,794 |
| Dutch | 15 | 2,538 |
| Spanish | 27 | 1,643 |

The largest groups are not European: Arabic 743K, Chinese 714K.

| language | works | newspaper-issue works | works with ≥1 manifest (floor) | excl. issues | scanned & catalogued ext | scanned & held by SL | **queue** (scanned, ext=false, no SL book) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Latin | 306,352 | 11 | 69,673 (22.7%) | 22.7% | 1,747 | 45,231 | **23,860** |
| German | 221,931 | 69,646 | 31,818 (14.3%) | 20.9% | 26 | 21,980 | **9,837** |
| French | 124,168 | 17,599 | 11,125 (9.0%) | 10.4% | 117 | 1,382 | **9,674** |
| Italian | 68,819 | 1 | 1,855 (2.7%) | 2.7% | 51 | 689 | **1,153** |
| Spanish | 59,582 | 5 | 417 (0.7%) | 0.7% | 17 | 80 | **329** |
| Dutch | 74,378 | 20,958 | 289 (0.4%) | 0.5% | 0 | 115 | **174** |
| English | 93,554 | 11,085 | 28,719 (30.7%) | 34.8% | 32 | 18,295 | **10,422** (ext is meaningless for English) |

The queue is written to `scripts/output/scan-queue-<lang>.jsonl`, one row per work: `example_manifest`, sources, and `via`.

**Caveats**
- **Phase 11 counts every USTC newspaper issue as a work.** The sn-less rows of the editions cache are issues: *Wochentliche Post-Ordinari-Zeitung*, *Gazette de Londres. No. 2209*, *Amsterdamse Dingsdaegse Courant*. That is 69,646 German "works" (31% of the denominator), 20,958 Dutch, 17,599 French and 11,085 English. They are almost never translated, except the 8 *Gazette de Londres* issues, so they dilute every share. They also broke the first draw: `eds.get(null)` gave 101 German, 42 French and 87 Dutch works the same card. Those cards were fixed and re-adjudicated before any number here was computed. The pre-fix verdicts are kept in `pre-nullsn-fix/`.
- **"Any English" is not "translated from this language".** In Dutch, 10 of 18 positives are translations *from* English (Stuart declarations, Partridge, Fuller, bilingual broadsides and emblem books). In French, 10 of 21 are, including 8 *Gazette de Londres* issues. The N column is the one comparable to the June Latin gap.
- **Gemini under-detects**, as the sensitivity of 0.62 shows. Uncorrected shares are low by about a third, and the corrected ones are imprecise. X verdicts were found only by reading the evidence text, so there may be more false positives among the 240 works without a second read: 3 of 72 positives failed on their own evidence.
- **Part C is a floor at three levels:**
  - The harvest: Italian, Spanish and Dutch manifests are barely in `import_candidates`.
  - The matcher: anonymous editions match only on an identical title.
  - Sn-less editions match only on their work's representative title.

  "Scanned" means some edition of the work has a manifest. The queue overstates what is untranslated, because `ext` is a floor (recall 0/72 above).
- **Part B** is a model reading two catalogue titles. Short titles are hard for it too.

**Replicated?** The Sonnet second read on 60 per language (above). Part B and Part C precision were checked by hand reads of the judge's verdicts and of the matches.

**Artifacts** (box earthai-l7a; worktree `scripts/output/` is gitignored, and a durable copy is in `/data/scratch/sl/jobs/translation-share-7751/artifacts/`):
- `translation-share/<lang>-{frame,blind,grouping}.json`
- `<lang>-{agy,sonnet,tiebreak}-verdicts.jsonl`: every verdict with queries, sources, URL, quote and raw reply
- `<lang>-final-verdicts.jsonl`, `<lang>-estimate.json`, `summary.json`, `origin-tags.json`, `<lang>-grouping-verdicts.jsonl`
- `scan-coverage-report-<lang>.json`, `work-scan-coverage-<lang>.jsonl.gz`, `scan-queue-<lang>.jsonl.gz`

**Cost:** about 3% of the second account's weekly Gemini pool, 51.6% → 48.4% remaining (shared). Claude: about 330 Sonnet calls on the l7a subscription. $0 API.

## 2026-10-30 · Counts, pace and clustering checks on the translation-gap sample (#7778)
<!-- PRIOR ART: scripts/analysis/gap-validation-estimate.mjs (rates only, window only; its strata, weights and bootstrap are reused); scripts/translation-layer/11-work-graph.mjs (a whole work graph, hand-checked at n=40; used as a candidate source); #7769 staged shape for the staged rows. -->

**Design.** No new adjudication of the translation question. The 1,000 seeded works (seed 2684) are read three ways: the published consensus (*paper*), the same consensus with `partial` priors counted as untranslated (*strict*), and Sonnet alone (#7691). Counts use the window's per-stratum rates and era shares, applied to the full pools (9,830 / 356,375 clusters). Pace: the first English translation cited for each of the 79 Renaissance-composed works found translated, dated by hand. Clustering audit: one `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` call per sampled cluster (titles only; about $0.16) on its member titles and up to 30 same-author clusters. Sonnet judged the first 131 before the box's Claude account hit its pace guard. Edition level: each cluster weighted by its edition count.

**Run.** Scripts: `scripts/analysis/gap-validation-counts.mjs`, `-cluster-audit.mjs`, `-stage-translations.mjs`. Flash-lite answered all 1,000. On the 131-cluster overlap, Sonnet and flash-lite agree on split versus no split 124 times, with Jaccard 0.70 on the same-work sets; flash-lite flags over-merge 13 times to Sonnet's 2. Of 78 matcher-missed translations, 42 pass the staging gate (two instruments plus a live link that names the work) and 36 are held. Gemini's cited Google Books ids were often invented.

## 2026-10-30 · Translation corpus audit, wave 2: dual judge, image-grounded (#5274, for #4916)
<!-- PRIOR ART: scripts/eval/results/translation-corpus-audit-2026-09-30/README.md (wave 1, the method repeated here); _series-monthly-translation-corpus-audit.md (the monthly rows); #5695 (a text-only judge measures fidelity to the transcription). -->

**Question.** For a page a reader opens at random, how faithful is the English to the page's source, now that routing
has changed since 2026-09-30 (router #6740/#7263, agy Flash, Opus-direct for hard scripts)? And is the judge itself
sound: does a second judge from the other model family agree with it, and does either judge favour its own family?
measure = `judged` throughout, never accuracy. Results in `scripts/eval/results/translation-corpus-audit-wave2-2026-10-30/`
(`analysis.md` for every table, `eye-notes.md` for the hand read).

### What changed in the instrument

- **`armOf()` was blind.** It knew only `gemini-3.1-flash-lite*` and `gemini-3-flash-preview`; everything else
  read `other` and the draw **excluded** it. A census of every served page of every live book (`census.mjs`,
  24,810 books, 5,742,852 pages) found: flash 2.32M, lite (preview + GA) 3.10M, **agy 3.8 Flash-low 141K**,
  no model recorded 107K, **Opus 5.5 49K**, Gemini 2.x 8K, corpus imports 6K, **Argon 3.8K**, a handful of
  Sonnet/Haiku/human. `arm.mjs` names all of them (unit test pins the census list); draw.mjs and score.mjs use it.
- **Prompt provenance:** 3.56M pages carry a prompt version and hash, 2.05M a version only, **131K neither**.
  In the draw, 7 of 365 items have neither; versions other than the current v13 are 60% of the draw, so no
  old-version supplement was needed.
- **Both judges see the page image** (`IMAGE-ADDENDUM.md`, appended verbatim for both). Fidelity is still scored
  against the transcription, so the score stays comparable with wave 1; the image adds `ocr_misread`,
  `ocr_wrong_leaf` and `image_first_words` (a check that the judge really opened the image: the words it reports
  were found in the transcription on 334/365 pages for Opus, 343/365 for Gemini; the rest are mostly scripts
  where the OCR itself misreads).
- **Image pick caveat (found by CI after the run):** the draw took `display_photo` first, as draw.mjs does. For
  33 of 410 items (5 split from a spread, 28 cropped) that can be the whole spread rather than the page's half. The
  fidelity score is unaffected (it is against the transcription); the image fields on those items may be off, but
  none carries a wrong-leaf flag, Opus marked 2 of them `ocr_misread`, and none is among the contained pages
  (`image-pick-note.json`). draw-wave2.mjs now uses `getPageSource()`.

### Design

One interior text page per book (draw.mjs's page rule), live books only, seed 20261030. Cells = language × model arm:
each arm gets its page share of the language quota, floored at 6 books where the cell has ≥ 6 live books, the floors
taken out of the larger cells; inside a cell, books are ordered by script type (print / manuscript / unknown, from
`pages.script_type`) and period (pre-1500, 1500–1700, 1700–1900, 1900+) and taken systematically, so script × period
are proportionally represented without quotas. **365 books**, more than the ~300 aimed for, because in eight
languages the floors push past the language quota (Chinese 24 for 17, Arabic and Tibetan 24 for 12, Spanish 18 for 6 …). Cells with fewer than 6 live books were not floored (17
cells, e.g. Greek/argon 1 book, Latin/claude-other 5: `draw-log.json → cells`). Headline weights: each language's
eligible translated pages × each arm's share of them (`arm-shares.json`), which undoes the floors. Controls: 15
swap, 15 drop, 15 repeat, blinded into 28 packets.

Judge A: Claude Opus, one subagent per 15-item packet, JUDGE-PROMPT.md + addendum. Judge B: Gemini through
`agy -p` on the subscription, one call per item, same text (`judge-agy.mjs`). **Positive control first:** three
items whose image was swapped for another book's page; Gemini flagged all three as wrong leaf and quoted words
visible only in the swapped image. Cost $0 API; agy used 0.6% of one account-week.

### Controls gate (read first)

| judge | swap rated ≤ 2 | drop flagged omission | repeat within one | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opus (with image) | 15/15 | 14/15 | 15/15 (13 exact) | **PASS** |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash-low (with image) | 15/15 | 15/15 | **13/15** (10 exact; Hebrew 1→4, Korean 3→5) | **FAIL** |

The Gemini judge is reported as failed: its rates below are instrument diagnostics, not corpus estimates.

### Headline (Opus judge; n = 365 books, 2026-10-30)

| statistic | lang × arm (headline) | lang only |
|---|---:|---:|
| fidelity ≥ 4 | **86.3%** (81.3–90.9) | 87.1% (82.7–91.1) |
| any major defect | **13.6%** (9.0–18.7) | 12.8% (8.9–17.1) |
| fidelity 5 | 46.8% (40.1–53.7) | 51.6% |
| fidelity ≤ 2 | 2.9% (0.8–5.4) | 3.0% |
| transcription misreads the image (`ocr_misread`) | 21.3% (15.6–26.9) | — |
| transcription is of another leaf (Opus flag) | 6 of 365 books | — |

The image field is the new number: on about one page in five the judge saw the transcription misread the leaf in
a way that changes meaning, and that sits *outside* the fidelity score, which is fidelity to the transcription.

### By language, script, period (Opus; descriptive; < 30 books exploratory, ≥ 30 directional, ≥ 50 decision-grade)

| language | books | mean | ≥ 4 % | major % |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Latin | 58 | 4.19 | 84.5 | 15.5 |
| Greek | 35 | 4.40 | 88.6 | 8.6 |
| German | 35 | 4.63 | 94.3 | 5.7 |
| English (modernisation) | 35 | 4.54 | 91.4 | 8.6 |
| Arabic | 24 | 4.25 | 83.3 | 16.7 |
| Tibetan | 24 | 4.42 | 91.7 | 8.3 |
| French | 24 | 4.83 | 100 | 0 |
| Chinese | 24 | 4.08 | 75.0 | 25.0 |
| Sanskrit | 18 | 3.50 | 44.4 | 55.6 |
| Spanish | 18 | 4.61 | 94.4 | 5.6 |
| Italian | 17 | 4.18 | 88.2 | 17.6 |
| Dutch | 17 | 4.71 | 100 | 0 |
| Korean | 12 | 4.08 | 83.3 | 16.7 |
| Japanese | 12 | 2.25 | 25.0 | 66.7 |
| Hebrew | 12 | 3.67 | 66.7 | 33.3 |

Unweighted cells (the floors over-represent small arms inside a language). Script: print 83.2% ≥ 4 (184 books),
manuscript 79.5% (73), unknown 88.9% (108). Period: pre-1500 71.0% (31), 1500–1700 86.7% (120), 1700–1900 82.6%
(144), 1900+ 90.0% (50). **Japanese is the outlier:** 8 of 12 pages carry a major defect, five of them English that
is not a translation of the page (contained, below), all on kuzushiji / early-modern books translated by lite or
flash.

**Model arms are not compared.** The router sends hard scripts to Opus, so raw arm rates (Opus 92.6% ≥ 4 on 54
books, agy-flash 92.9% on 42, flash 82.9% on 117, lite 79.5% on 146) mix model with book difficulty and prompt
era. Two or more arms share a language × script × period cell in 57 cells, and **no cell holds 10 books of
any one arm except Latin/print/1500–1700 lite (15)**: every within-cell contrast is exploratory (`analysis.md`).
By prompt version: Opus/v13 42 books 100% ≥ 4, agy-flash/v13 92.9%, lite/v10 78.5% (65), lite/11 74.1% (27),
flash/11 53.8% (13), same caveat.

### Judge reliability (Opus vs Gemini, 365 books, α bootstrap by book)

- fidelity (ordinal): α 0.53 [0.44, 0.61] — not settled
- fidelity ≥ 4 (nominal): α 0.53 [0.39, 0.65] — not settled
- major defect: α 0.52 [0.38, 0.65] — not settled
- omission 0.53, invention 0.50, ocr_misread 0.54 — all not settled
- exact 61.4%, within one 96.2%; Gemini scores 0.26 points higher on average (fidelity 5 on 72.5% of pages vs
  46.8%; major 8.7% vs 13.6%).

So the two families agree roughly on how good a page is and not on where "major" starts, as #6338/#6420 found with
human readers (α 0.46–0.55). **Every rate above is Opus's threshold, quoted per judge.**

### Self-preference (does each judge favour its own family?)

Difference in differences of (Opus score − Gemini score) on Claude-translated pages (Opus 5.5, 54 books) minus the
same on Gemini-translated pages (311 books): **+0.15 points [−0.03, +0.34]**; matched inside the 15 language ×
script cells holding both families: +0.16 [−0.02, +0.35]. On the share ≥ 4: +2.6 pp [−5.1, +9.8]; on the share
without a major defect: +3.6 pp [−4.2, +10.9]. The sign is the self-preference direction (Opus relatively kinder to
Claude text, or Gemini relatively harsher to it), but no interval excludes zero: **no self-preference detected at
this n**; an effect of about a third of a point cannot be ruled out. Caveats: the Gemini judge failed its stability
control, and the Opus-translated pages are concentrated in hard scripts (Tibetan, Chinese, Sanskrit, Arabic). The
planted-control comparison of the same two families as a lane judge is #7611 (PR #7807, preregistered 2026-10-30, no
results yet); this run does not use its control set.

### Wave 1 → wave 2, and the Oct-1 monthly draw

| run | judge | n | ≥ 4 | major |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| wave 1, 2026-09-30 (arm-corrected) | Opus, text only | 311 | 87.2% (81.7–91.9) | 14.4% (8.9–20.4) |
| **wave 2, 2026-10-30** (lang × arm) | Opus, with image | 365 | 86.3% (81.3–90.9) | 13.6% (9.0–18.7) |
| wave 2, lite/flash pages only | Opus, with image | 263 | 85.0% (79.6–90.1) | 14.8% (9.8–19.9) |
| monthly draw 2026-10-01 (lang) | Opus, text only | 103 | 83.3% (74.4–91.5) | 14.8% (6.8–23.8) |

Δ wave 2 − wave 1: ≥ 4 **−0.9 pp [−7.8, +6.1]**, major −0.8 pp [−8.5, +6.4]; on lite/flash pages only −2.2 pp
[−8.9, +5.0]. No change is detectable; the instrument changed too (the judge now sees the image), so a small
real change could hide in either direction. The Oct-1 monthly draw (judged late, unchanged instrument, gate 15/15 ·
15/15 · 15/15) fits the same picture and is the series row for 2026-10.

### By eye

The 20 books the judges disagree on most, read against the image (`eye-notes.md`): **Opus right on 12, Gemini on 0,
4 ties or splits, 4 not settled** (corrupt Tibetan, Sanskrit, Chinese). Twice Gemini lowered fidelity for an image
mismatch, which the addendum forbids; on garbled pages it gave 5 where the English papers over the garble.

**Contained, same run (14 pages, 14 books; `contained` label on #5274):** 8 pages whose English is not a
translation of the transcription (5 Japanese, 1 German, 1 Latin, 1 French label catalogued Italian), and 6 whose
transcription is another leaf's text (2 duplicate the previous page, 1 is shifted by a leaf, 2 Hebrew, 1 OCR
loop). Books held (`tca-wave2-contained-5274`), pages withheld with snapshots. List in `eye-notes.md` §2.

### What the paper can say (#4916)

1. One page in seven to eight that readers meet carries a major translation defect by the Opus judge's threshold
   (13.6% [9.0–18.7], n 365 books, 2026-10-30), unchanged since September within ±7 pp.
2. That rate is a threshold of one judge, not a fact about pages: a second family agrees at α ≈ 0.5.
3. Fidelity to the transcription is not fidelity to the page: on ~21% of pages the transcription itself misreads
   the leaf, and ~1.6% (6/365) transcribe another leaf.
4. No judge self-preference at ±0.35 points; the same-family Gemini judge also failed a stability control
   that Opus passed.
5. Do not compare models from this sample.

### Decisions taken (no ask)

- Gemini judge = `gemini-3.8-flash-low` for all items: the box's agy login may run only that model; `3.8-flash`
  and Pro/Argon are refused by the guard, so **the 40-item Pro subset was not run**.
- 365 books rather than ~300: floors of 6 where the brief asked, rather than dropping them.
- The Oct-1 draw judged as-is, text-only, and stored as judge@1 / 2026-10; wave 2 stored as judge@2 (image).
- Gemini verdicts are kept in the results dir; only the gate-passing judge (Opus) goes to the score store.

Artifacts: `scripts/eval/translation-corpus-audit/{arm,census,draw-wave2,fetch-images,judge-agy,analyze-wave2}.mjs`,
`IMAGE-ADDENDUM.md`, results dirs `translation-corpus-audit-wave2-2026-10-30/` and
`translation-corpus-audit-monthly-2026-10/`, store `translation-corpus-audit-judge@2/2026-10.jsonl` (410 rows) and
`judge@1/2026-10.jsonl` (148 rows). Census rows (24 MB) in the job scratch, gzipped; the summary is committed.

## 2026-10-30 · Siku translations: which errors, at what risk? (#5600)
<!-- PRIOR ART: scripts/eval/agy-per-call-7503/ (the judge setup, claude -p Opus with the page image; it counts "sense errors" as one bucket); .claude/docs/page-error-taxonomy.md (T7/T8/T10/O1/O6/T6 classes, used for the kinds). -->

**Question.** The #7503 route judge counts "sense errors" as one bucket (17/30 served pages). That bucket mixes wording slips with invented names. Which kinds of error do readers of the Siku English meet, and how many of them mislead?

**Design.** Frame: books held under the Siku lane's `HOLD_REASONS` (`scripts/batch/siku-translate-lane.mjs`). Arm A = the served lane (`translation.engine.call_site` `scripts/batch/cli-translate.mjs`, model `gemini-3.8-flash-low`, 349 books); arm B = the older block Batch lane (`scripts/lib/translate-batch-chained.mjs`, Gemini 3 Flash preview, 292 books). One page per book, seeded draw (mulberry32, seed 5600), AI translation, OCR ≥ 150 characters, translatable page (not furniture-only). Arm B books are disjoint from arm A. Judge: Opus via `claude -p` (l7a subscription, $0), one page per call, blind to arm (packets P01…P52 in seeded order). Each call saw the page image, the OCR, the served English (summary and keywords cut), and the last 2 lines of the previous page's source and English and the first 2 of the next page's source. Every error was returned as a span {source, English, kind, risk, evidence}. Kinds: INVENTED, WRONG-SENSE, OCR-CARRIED, OMITTED, SEAM, JUNK, STYLE. Risk: HIGH (a reader is misled and cannot tell), MEDIUM (misleading but noticeable, or a lost clause), LOW (cosmetic). A second, independent Opus pass read 10 pages (5 per arm, seeded). Intervals: by-book bootstrap (one page per book, so page = book), Wilson for shares.

**Errors per page, by kind** (pages with at least one in brackets):

| kind | A served (n=30) | B Batch (n=20) |
|---|---|---|
| WRONG-SENSE | 0.97 [0.60–1.33] (17) | 2.55 [1.35–4.10] (15) |
| STYLE | 0.37 (11) | 0.40 (7) |
| JUNK (furniture carried) | 0.23 (6) | 0.20 (4) |
| OCR-CARRIED | 0.20 [0.03–0.47] (4) | 1.40 [0.35–2.80] (9) |
| INVENTED | 0.13 [0–0.30] (3) | 0.55 [0.25–0.90] (8) |
| SEAM | 0.13 (4) | 0.25 (5) |
| OMITTED | 0.07 (2) | 0.30 (5) |
| **all** | **2.10 [1.57–2.67]** | **5.65 [3.70–7.95]** |

**By risk**

| risk | A | B |
|---|---|---|
| HIGH per page | 0.23 [0.07–0.43] (7 errors) | 1.75 [0.85–2.80] (35) |
| MEDIUM per page | 0.77 [0.40–1.20] | 2.20 [1.25–3.25] |
| LOW per page | 1.10 [0.83–1.40] | 1.70 [1.20–2.25] |
| pages with ≥ 1 HIGH | 6/30, 20% [10–37] | 10/20, 50% [30–70] |
| page verdict show / caveat / don't | 16 / 13 / 1 | 3 / 9 / 8 |

**Where the HIGH errors come from**
- **Arm A (7):** 6 made by the translator (4 WRONG-SENSE: a gloss reversed, 'Crown Prince' for the Son of Heaven, an edict's meaning reversed, a numbered list shifted by one; 1 OMITTED entry in that list; 1 INVENTED gloss giving 召南 a wrong surname and dates). 1 OCR-carried (希 for 帣). None at the seam. The served lane's risk is in translation: polarity, attribution, and glosses that add names or dates.
- **Arm B (35):** 20 translator-made (15 WRONG-SENSE, 5 INVENTED), 12 OCR-carried, 2 seam, 1 margin furniture read as a quotation. 25 of the 35 are on the 10 pages from the repeat-mark encyclopaedias (佩文韻府, 子史精華, 駢字類編), and 19 of the 35 involve the 丨 marks that repeat a headword: the translator invents a term for them or files a quotation under the wrong headword. The 12 OCR-carried errors are rare characters in dictionary and lexicon entries (康熙字典 headwords, rhyme-group words). Arm B drew no histories or classics and arm A drew 27 of 30, so **the A–B gap (1.52 more HIGH per page, [0.58–2.62]) measures lane and genre together, not the lane alone.**

**The two named seam pages, read by eye with the previous page and both images open.** 圖書編 vol 22 p33: 為正 completes p32's sentence (the year begins in the Yin month, taken as the first month), and the English instead makes the Zi and Chou months 'correct'. That is a HIGH seam error, and the page also carries the margin title as '<unclear>Shu Shu Bian</unclear>'. 圖書編 vol 77 p30: 王之 completes p29's 欲以火德王之 ('wished to rule by the Virtue of Fire'), and the English reads it as 'King Wen of Han'. The 宣室受釐 allusion does refer to Emperor Wen, so the name is an inference with the wrong title, not text from nowhere. The judge rated it MEDIUM. Neither page meets the containment bar: in both, the rest of the English is this leaf's text.

**Judge agreement (10 pages, two independent Opus passes).** Page verdict 9/10 (κ 0.84). Whether a page has a HIGH error: 10/10 (κ 1.0), and the HIGH count was identical on all 10 pages. Presence of each kind on a page: 64/70 page×kind cells (κ 0.79). STYLE was the least stable (7/10, κ 0.44), and INVENTED and WRONG-SENSE agreed 10/10. Risk presence: 28/30 cells (κ 0.86). Error totals per page differ by 0–4 (mostly STYLE and LOW).

**Contained (by eye, image open, `withhold-stale-translations.mjs --by-eye-pages`, #5600).** 御定佩文韻府 vol 719 p47: the 丨丨 marks for 拂拭 are rendered 11 times as an invented term 'shanghui' ('producing brilliance'). 御定子史精華 vol 71 p70: 因丨丨丨丨而丨丨丨丨 (斟酌前史 / 譏正得失) is rendered as invented terms 'Zheng Qi Ci Ju' and 'Shen Qi Tan Lun'. Both books were already held. The other INVENTED findings are notes or glosses on pages whose body is the leaf's text (前漢書 vol 33 p47; 子史精華 vol 129 p4 and vol 70 p39). They are recorded as findings, not contained.

**Not checked.** No human reader of classical Chinese. One AI judge family (Opus) for both passes. 50 pages, so a kind seen on 2–4 pages has a wide interval. Arm B's books are a different genre mix from arm A's. The served lane was not measured on the encyclopaedias, so this does not show that it fixes the 丨 problem.

Artifacts: `scripts/eval/siku-error-types-5600/` (`draw.mjs`, `draw.json`, `prep.mjs`, `judge.mjs`, `score.mjs`, `results.json` with every HIGH finding and its page URL, `eye.mjs`). Packets, images and raw replies are in the job's scratch directory.

## 2026-10-30 · Which combination of pages a call, image size and thinking gives the fewest agy calls a page without losing accuracy? Box-Behnken over the agy first read (#6740)

### Preregistration (committed before any agy call of this design)

**Question.** The agy first read (`cli-ocr.mjs read`, gemini-3.8-flash, live: 4 pages a call, the image as served,
thinking low) has three continuous or ordinal settings. Settings were compared one at a time (read@1 vs @4 vs @8).
Which combination gives the fewest agy calls per accepted page, per language, at no loss of accuracy?

**Factors (3 levels each, coded −1 / 0 / +1).**

| factor | −1 | 0 | +1 | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| x1 pages a call | 1 | 4 | 8 | ordinal coding (4 is the live setting) |
| x2 image long edge | 1024 px | 1600 px | 2400 px | `--long-edge`: never enlarged, so an image already within the edge is sent as served |
| x3 thinking | low | medium | high | the model id names the tier (`gemini-3.8-flash-{low,medium,high}`) |

- **Deviation from the brief, decided before any call:** the brief asked for thinking {minimal, low, medium}. agy offers
  no minimal tier (`agy models`, 2026-10-30: Flash low / medium / high only), so the levels are low / medium / high and
  the live setting (low) sits on the face of the design, not at its centre.
- **Design.** Box-Behnken, 12 edge-midpoint runs + 3 centre replicates = 15 runs per language, plus **2 live runs**
  (4 a call, image as served, low): the reference arm of the non-inferiority test and a second A-vs-A pair.

| run | x1 | x2 | x3 | | run | x1 | x2 | x3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B01 | −1 | −1 | 0 | | B09 | 0 | −1 | −1 |
| B02 | +1 | −1 | 0 | | B10 | 0 | +1 | −1 |
| B03 | −1 | +1 | 0 | | B11 | 0 | −1 | +1 |
| B04 | +1 | +1 | 0 | | B12 | 0 | +1 | +1 |
| B05 | −1 | 0 | −1 | | C1–C3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| B06 | +1 | 0 | −1 | | L1, L2 | 0 (4) | served | −1 (low) |
| B07 | −1 | 0 | +1 | | | | | |
| B08 | +1 | 0 | +1 | | | | | |

- **Pools.** The `.agy-james` account is held to flash-low (`allowed-model`), and the default pool is spent until
  2026-10-30 22:00Z. So phase A (James, now) runs the low-thinking runs B05, B06, B09, B10 and L1; phase B (default,
  after the refill) runs the rest and L2. Within a phase the order is shuffled (seed 6740). L1 vs L2 is also the
  pool-vs-pool A-vs-A check; if they differ by more than the centre runs' spread, the thinking factor's low level is
  confounded with the pool and that is reported.

**Blocking: every run reads the same pages.** `scripts/eval/read-surface-6740/panel.mjs`, seed 6740.
- German: 40 books from the DTA (#6012 same-edition books), one target page each. Latin: 40 books from CAMENA.
  Century quotas: German 1500s 2 / 1600s 14 / 1700s 14 / 1800s 14 (drawn 1 / 12 / 14 / 13: only one 1500s book is
  eligible); Latin 1500s 16 / 1600s 18 / 1700s 6 / undated 2 (drawn 16 / 18 / 4 / 2).
- The target is a typed page whose page breaks fall on ours (`congruent`, one typed page, no typed notes, ≥ 400
  letters), interior for German (front 15 % and back 5 % skipped). CAMENA targets may sit from page 4 on: #6012 aligned
  most CAMENA books only on their first 25 OCR'd pages, and the front rule leaves 12 books.
- Each target has an 8-page window of its own book (t−3 … t+4). A 1-a-call run reads the target alone; a 4-a-call run
  reads t−1 … t+2 in one call; an 8-a-call run reads the window in one call. Only the target is scored; every page read
  counts in calls a page. The same image bytes go to every run (`--image-cache`).
- Faces (Fraktur / Antiqua) are labelled by eye from the target image before scoring, and reported as a split.
- **French is not in this design.** The one typed French set (#7567's 40 fr.wikisource proofread pages) is of
  Wikisource's own scans, not our library pages, and has no 8-page windows of our books. No library French page has a
  typed reference. Skipped, as the brief allows.

**Responses (per run, per language).**
1. **CER** (`measure: accuracy`): `scripts/eval/lib/metrics.mjs` `scoreAgainstReference(ref, read, 'latin')`, the
   windowed CER (1 − `charAccuracyWindowed`; the lower bound on accuracy, the one for comparing reads), after the read's
   header tags and their content are removed (`score.py`'s list). Capped at 1. The reference is the typed page body.
2. **Wrong text**: the identity guard (`aligned: false`, word guard > 0.35) on a target page where most runs pass it.
   A target where most runs fail the guard is a reference or leaf problem, not a read: it is excluded from every run
   before the fit, listed, and checked by eye. **Loop / cut**: letters > 2× or < 0.5× the page's median over runs.
3. **agy calls a page**, production-equivalent: (calls made in the run + c1 × pages left unread) ÷ pages in the run.
   `--no-alone` leaves a twice-refused block's pages unread instead of reading them one a call (the production
   fallback), to keep the design inside the budget; c1 is the language's measured calls a page over its 1-a-call runs.
   A target left unread takes, for CER, its read from the 1-a-call run at the same image size and thinking level
   where the design has one, else the mean of the 1-a-call runs (disclosed per run).
4. **Wall seconds a page**: the summed duration of the run's calls ÷ pages read. **Tokens**: agy's own usage per call
   (input, output, thinking), reported because the pool may meter tokens, not calls.

**Fit.** Per language and response, a full quadratic in the coded factors (10 terms) by least squares on the 15 BBD
run means (the live runs are not design points: "served" is not a level). Uncertainty: 2,000 by-book bootstrap
resamples (the same books resampled for every run, so runs stay paired), refit each time.

**Noise floor.** The A-vs-A spread: the range of the three centre runs' mean CER, and the 95 % paired bootstrap
interval of C1 − C2, C1 − C3, C2 − C3; the same for L1 − L2. Printed as a band on every chart.

**The optimum, and the rule (fixed now).**
- Candidates: the 27 settings of the 3 × 3 × 3 grid, plus "live".
- A setting is **non-inferior** when the 95 % bootstrap upper bound of δ = predicted CER(setting) − mean CER(L1, L2)
  is ≤ **1.0 percentage point** (eval-design §10.2 card 1, the registered CER margin for a cheaper route), and its
  wrong-text count, where it was run, is ≤ the live runs' mean + 1 per 40 books.
- **Optimum** = the non-inferior setting with the fewest predicted agy calls a page; ties (within 0.02 calls) go to
  fewer wall seconds a page, then to the setting nearest live.
- If the optimum is live, or saves under 10 % of live's calls a page, **nothing switches** and no confirmation runs.
- **Early stop, per language:** if after C1–C3 and L1 the A-vs-A range exceeds 2 pp CER, the design cannot resolve a
  1 pp margin; that language's remaining runs are not made.

**Confirmation (only if an optimum is found).** 30 real queue pages per language (the first-read frame,
`judge.mjs draw --cells=de-blank,la-blank`, new books, none in this panel or the #7701 draws), each read by live and by
the optimum, **paired**, judged blind by Opus against the page image (route-judge-6740 harness, its wrong-page and
planted controls), scored by the router rule (`scripts/eval/estimator/router-table/rules.json`, the paired gate). The
live setting changes only through a PR, only if the router picks the optimum. Latin first reads are now arm c
(PERO draft > agy, #7752), so a Latin optimum is confirmed against read@4 here and can replace arm c only after a paired
test against arm c on gex45 (a follow-up brief, not this job).

**Budget.** At most 2,000 agy calls in all; the design is capped at 1,500 (1,750 since Amendment 1) (a run in progress finishes; runs not
started are dropped, B runs before centre and live runs). Planned: about 45–70 calls a run × 34 runs.

**Amendment 1 (2026-10-30 21:20Z, after phase A's 10 runs, before phase B and before any fit).**
- *Unusable reads.* Phase A showed Gemini filter stubs ("This request was blocked by Gemini's filters …") and one
  restarted reply returned as 1-a-call reads. The rule above scored them as wrong text, and the identity-guard
  exclusion then dropped their pages as "reference problems". They are neither: `cli-ocr.mjs` flags every one
  (`meta.chatter`), and apply never writes such a read. So: a read with `meta.chatter` set or a write guard of
  truncated / loop / empty is **unusable**, and counts as a page the setting did not deliver (as an unread page: its
  calls stay in the cost; for CER the target takes the 1-a-call read, as above). A target with **no usable read in any
  of the four 1-a-call runs** cannot be read by this route at all (production leaves it scans-only): it leaves the CER
  analysis and is reported as *unreadable by the route*. The identity-guard exclusion applies to usable reads only.
  The scorer bug found on the way (centring marks `->Name.<-` ate the text between two centred lines; Faust read at
  CER 0.88, really 0.00) is fixed in `score.mjs` and changes no rule.
- *Budget.* Phase A used 509 calls for 10 runs (15 of them in two runs restarted after image-host 429s, with the image
  cache filled first). The plan line (45–70 calls × 34 runs) did not fit its own 1,500 cap, and the drop order would
  have cut Box-Behnken runs and broken the design. The design cap is now **1,750** and the confirmation's **250**; the
  2,000 total is unchanged.
- *Observed, not a rule:* German blocks here are refused (filter cut) far more often than on the queue: the DTA holds
  famous texts (Faust, Zarathustra, Grimm), which Gemini cuts as recitation. Absolute German calls a page from this
  panel overstate the queue's; the comparison between settings is paired and stands.

**Amendment 2 (STEER 1, Derek 20:52Z; written 21:45Z, before any phase-B run and before any fit): a Bayesian,
sequential surface.**
- *Prior data.* Every earlier agy first read (a plain read of the image, not a correction) with known settings on a
  #6012 congruent typed page, this design's own reads left out, stratified by prompt version
  (`prior-inventory.mjs`: 21,590 aligned pages in 246 books; the kept and stored Flash reads there are almost all
  corrections of lite drafts; the plain reads are a few dozen pages, all at 1 a call, image as served, thinking low).
  For the calls surface, also #7701's measured agy calls a page at read@4 and read@8 on queue pages
  (`routes-7701.json`). A prior point at "served" is coded x2 = +1 (the panel's median served long edge is 2,350 px);
  L1/L2 stay out of the surface, as preregistered.
- *Power prior.* Each prior point's variance is divided by a0 (0 < a0 ≤ 1), one a0 per response and language, chosen by
  empirical Bayes (`bayes.mjs estimateA0`: the marginal likelihood of this design's results at the settings where both
  exist). Calls: earlier read@4 against L1/L2. CER: no earlier read exists at the centre or the live setting, so the
  earlier (1, served, low) reads are compared with B05 (1, 1600, low) on the same books where they overlap, else
  pooled; the surface at a0 = 0 (no prior) is reported beside it. Coefficients get a vague N(0, τ²) prior besides
  (τ = 5 pp for CER, 1 call for calls).
- *Sequential runs.* C1–C3 and L2 are made first (noise floor, a0, pool check). Then the remaining Box-Behnken runs
  are made in batches of up to 3 per language, each batch the runs that most shrink the summed posterior variance of
  predicted CER over the cheap end (the 18 settings with 4 or 8 pages a call; `bayes.mjs rankNext`). A language stops
  when every cheap-end setting with predicted calls ≤ 0.9 × live is decided (its 95 % posterior interval for δ lies
  wholly ≤ 1 pp or wholly > 1 pp), or its Box-Behnken runs run out, or the 1,750 cap is reached. Runs the prior or the
  posterior already pins down are not made; the report counts the runs and calls saved against the full 17.
- *Decision.* The preregistered rule, with the posterior interval for δ in place of the bootstrap one; the
  least-squares bootstrap fit is reported beside it wherever 10 or more runs exist. The admin page draws the
  prior-only and the posterior surfaces.

**Amendment 3 (23:20Z, before any run it names and before any CER of phase B was looked at).**
- *What happened.* The first phase-B batch (C1–C3 and L2, both languages, 8 runs × 4 calls at once on the default
  pool) timed out: 257 of 339 calls ended at the CLI's 300 s limit (first at 22:05Z). The box was at load 180 on 16
