- `estimator/router-table/evidence/lane-accept-7263.score.json`.

## 2026-10-28 · Correct or re-read, wave 2: Sanskrit and Arabic (#7568)
<!-- PRIOR ART: 2026-10-28-correct-vs-reread-wave1-zh-de-grc-7568.md (wave 1, whose clear answer opened this wave) and 2026-10-27-correct-vs-reread-wave1-prereg-7568.md (design, and amendment 2 for this wave, committed before its draws). -->

**Design.** Same as wave 1 (amendment 2 to the preregistration):
- draws `w-draw.mjs` with seeds 75684 (sa) and 75685 (ar), from books in terminal status `complete`, ≥ 70% lite-read;
- a format screen that keeps manuscripts;
- arms L / C (`correct.mjs --model=opus`) / R (`cli-ocr.mjs read`, agy `gemini-3.8-flash-low`);
- one blind Opus reader per book over all three texts (Step T);
- agy Flash-low on 30 seeded C ≠ R pages.

**Sample.**
- **Sanskrit:** the first 10 of 13 that passed, all Devanagari print. The screen failed one book with full Hindi translations.
- **Arabic:** the first 10 of 14, 6 print and 4 manuscripts (a Ḥāwāshī commentary, al-Ḥāwī, a Qurʾān, a Maghribī *Majisṭī*).

**Outcomes of the correction call.**
- **Sanskrit:** 247 corrected, 3 unchanged.
- **Arabic:** 213 corrected, 18 unchanged, 14 contain, 5 no-answer. The no-answers are all in one two-page-spread book; the chatter guard restarted the read.
- **R** read every page. Gemini's filter cut the text short on 3 Sanskrit and 17 Arabic pages.

**Result** (`flash-reread-5924/results-7568/{sa,ar}/score.json`; Wilson 95%)

| | n | misleading L | misleading **C** | misleading R | C vs R preferred (tie) | worse than L: C / R | agy C–R (Opus, same pages) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sanskrit (print) | 250 | 208 (78–87%) | **26 (7–15%)** | 125 (44–56%) | **214–14** (22), p < 10⁻⁴⁶ | **0** / 21 | 20–8 (25–1) |
| Arabic | 250 | 193 (72–82%) | **44 (13–23%)** | 144 (51–64%) | **175–41** (34), p < 10⁻²⁰ | 24 / 32 | 19–11 (21–5) |
| …Arabic print (6 books) | 150 | 111 | **24** | 66 | 98–29 (23) | | |
| …Arabic MSS (4 books) | 100 | 82 | **20** | 78 | 77–12 (11) | | |

- **Route (preregistered rule): C in both.** C halves L in both languages; R halves L in neither.
- **Bar (b) for C fails in Arabic on 24 pages.** By kind:
  - **14 contains.** By rule they count as "false contains", because readers mark only another leaf's text as `not_this_leaf`. But the readers called L misleading on 14/14:
    - 3 are blank leaves where L serves an invented "preface";
    - 11 are *Majisṭī* pages where L is a repetition loop.
  - **5 no-answers.** C serves L there.
  - **4 non-transcriptions** (below).
  - **1 real C misreading:** *al-Aʿlāq* p64, where C turns حرب لاقح ابدا into حرب لا تقع ابدا.
- **Self-preference.** The cross-family judge agrees in both languages, by smaller margins than Opus.

**The guard gap.** *Al-Durra al-Fākhira* (`6a08a754871243dce9def039`) is a modern typeset book, probably in copyright. On pp. 6, 12, 16 and 18 the corrector:
- declined to reproduce the page;
- answered with only the metadata tags and a `<warning>` that lists its corrections ("The full corrected page is not reproduced here …");
- and `correct.mjs` scored it `corrected`. The chatter guard and the write guard both passed it.

Applied, those pages would lose their whole body. Across the five languages it happened on these 4 pages only: no other correction has a body under 30% of its draft's letters, except two that cut a looping draft down to the page. A guard of "body letters ≥ some share of the draft's" would catch it. Whether that book should be public at all is a separate question.

**By eye** (image open, crops, unblinded; C is the one to serve on all 4)
- **sa `6a0eb388…` p51.** C fixes ललाटाद्यै, विलया, सशब्दं and सूक्ष्म. It also silently emends the print's own typo नन्तविधानात् to चिन्तनविधानात्. R has वरदात्तार, प्रपञ्च → पपञ्च and -तन्रे.
- **sa `69e13a96…` p37.** C fixes महार्थदृष्ट्या, रज्यति, आपद्यते and the footnote महादृगादि, with no new errors. R splits अलंग्रास and misreads the footnote.
- **ar `69ef3d42…` p60 (two-page spread).**
  - C fixes the page numbers, المساقط and الزمان, and emends الحتم → الختم.
  - C inherits L's omission of السعيد and the ف of فحينئذ, which R has.
  - R reverses the order of the two pages.
- **ar `6a477ce5…` p287 (Khiṭaṭ).** C repairs a heavily garbled L, checked against the print in 8 spots; its one slip is a lost و. R has وألوز برمحه for والوزير معه, توفيرا, ويقيمون and وتندب.
- **Pattern across the five languages:**
  - **C sometimes emends toward the expected text instead of the print.** In wave 1 the cases were the Lotus Sutra lacunae and the Homeric cento. Here they are चिन्तनविधानात् and الختم.
  - **C keeps what L dropped only when it notices the gap.**

**Cost** (Claude subscription, box account dereklomas@gmail.com; $0 billed)

| Language | Pages | Calls | Output tokens | List price | Per 1K pages |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sanskrit | 250 | 30 | 650K | $24.35 | $97 |
| Arabic | 250 | 37 | 668K | $26.15 | $105 |

- On wave 1's scale (Latin's $20.28 per 250 pages ≈ 1% of an account-week), the correction costs **about 5% of an account-week per 1K pages in both languages**.
- **Wave 2 as a whole** (corrections, 2 screens, 20 readers, by-eye): the weekly meter went **46% → 53%** (02:35Z → 04:40Z). That is an upper bound, because the account is shared.
- **R:** 530 agy calls for 500 pages.

**Human check (#7573):** `scripts/eval/dataset/judge-human-check-7573/{sanskrit,arabic}.jsonl`. It has the same shape as wave 1, with 30 `review: true` rows per language.

**Caveats.**
- Exploratory: 10 books per language, a single-family judge with a 30-page cross-family check, and no human calibration (#7573).
- The reader packets carried only the first line of each language's `lang_note`. The readers had the full note in `T-TASK.md`, and one used it explicitly. `w-packets.mjs` is fixed for later runs.

Files: `scripts/eval/flash-reread-5924/results-7568/{sa,ar}/` and the `w-*.mjs` scripts there.

## 2026-10-28 · Correct the lite text with Opus, or re-read with Flash: Chinese, German, Greek (#7568, wave 1)
<!-- PRIOR ART: 2026-10-24-latin-lite-opus-correct-vs-flash-reread-5924.md (the Latin result repeated here) and 2026-10-27-correct-vs-reread-wave1-prereg-7568.md (this run's preregistration, a766b3241, and amendment 1, 0b6739837). -->

**Question.** On 250 lite-read Latin pages, Opus correcting the stored lite text in place beat a Flash re-read on every measure (#5924). Does that hold for Chinese, German and Greek?

**Design** (preregistered in `2026-10-27-correct-vs-reread-wave1-prereg-7568.md` before any draw or model read; amendment 1 came after the draws, before any read).
- **Sample.** For each language, books in terminal status `complete`, at least 70% lite-read, with the 25-page `spread` rule (`flash-reread-5924/w-draw.mjs`, seeds 75681/2/3) and a format screen by an Opus reader.
  - **Chinese: 3 books.** The terminal frame holds only 5 lite-read Chinese books. The screen dropped a Siku Quanshu hand copy and a Japanese kunten edition. Most Chinese lite pages are in `held` books, which are out of the frame.
  - **German: 10 printed books.**
  - **Greek: 10 manuscripts.** All 14 Greek candidates were manuscripts; per amendment 1, manuscripts stay in.
- **Arms.**
  - L: the stored lite text.
  - C: `correct.mjs --model=opus --per-call=10`, unchanged. C serves the correction, or L where the outcome is unchanged, contain or no-answer.
  - R: `cli-ocr.mjs read --model=gemini-3.8-flash-low`, unchanged, one page per call through agy.
- **Step T.** One blind Opus reader per book saw the image and all three texts as X/Y/Z, in a seeded order. It gave a verdict per text (misleading / flawed / sound, using #5924's `C-TASK.md` words) and the three pairwise preferences (`T-TASK.md`).
  - This differs from Latin, where each pair of arms had its own reader. Here one reader judges every arm under the same conditions.
- **(d) Second-family check.** agy Flash-low judged C vs R blind on 30 seeded pages per language where C ≠ R.

**Outcomes of the correction call.**
- Chinese: 71 corrected, 2 contain, 2 no-answer. Both no-answers were Opus output blocked by a content filter on the Lotus Sutra.
- German: 233 corrected, 16 unchanged, 1 contain.
- Greek: 185 corrected, 65 contain.
- R read every page. Gemini's filter cut the text short on 6 Chinese, 2 German and 32 Greek pages.

**Result** (`flash-reread-5924/results-7568/<lang>/score.json`; Wilson 95%)

| | n | misleading L | misleading **C** | misleading R | C vs R preferred (tie) | worse than L: C / R | agy judge C vs R (Opus, same pages) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chinese (print) | 75 | 57 (65–84%) | **5 (3–15%)** | 37 (38–60%) | **61–7** (7), p < 10⁻¹¹ | 2 / 9 | 20–10 (26–3) |
| German (print) | 250 | 63 (20–31%) | **6 (1–5%)** | 23 (6–13%) | **167–22** (61), p < 10⁻²⁸ | 1 / 11 | **14–15** (21–1) |
| Greek (MSS) | 250 | 245 (95–99%) | **87 (29–41%)** | 221 (84–92%) | **173–59** (18), p < 10⁻¹³ | 65 / 14 | 13–17 (13–13) |
| Greek, the 185 pages C corrected | 185 | 180 | **22** | 157 | **173–4** (8) | 0 / — | 12–5 (13–1) |
| Greek, the 65 pages C contained | 65 | 65 | 65 (serves L) | 64 | 0–55 (10) | 65 by rule / — | 1–12 (0–12) |
| *Latin, #5924 (for reference)* | 250 | 111 | 31 | 20–32 | 131–43 | 1 / 7 | — |

- **Route (preregistered rule): C in all three languages.** Misleading(C) ≤ misleading(R), C is preferred, the sign test gives p < 0.05, and C halves L.
- **Bar (a), halving L:** C passes in all three languages. R passes only in German.
- **Bar (b), no page worse than L:** fails for both arms in every language, as in Latin. Every C page that failed is one where C serves L unchanged:
  - zh: 2 no-answers.
  - de: 1 contain on a blank image (below).
  - el: 65 contains. The prereg's "false contain" test only credits a reader's `not_this_leaf`. Here the readers called L misleading on 65/65 of these pages and named its text invented or looping; the corrector's reasons say the same.
  - **No correction made a page worse than lite.**
  - The R pages that failed bar (b) are misreads, Gemini filter cuts, and one German spread where R read only the right-hand page (by eye, below).
- **Bar (c), C beats R:** passes in all three.
- **Self-preference.**
  - Chinese: agy agrees, 20–10.
  - German: agy splits 14–15, against Opus's 21–1 on the same pages. Both families find few misleading pages there (agy: C 2, R 1 of 30). Read the German margin over R as "both good, C at least as good", not as a 167–22 rout.
  - Greek: agy and Opus agree once the pages are split. On corrected pages both prefer C (agy 12–5). On contained pages, where C serves the invented lite text, both prefer R.
- **Reader-noise check:** where C's text equalled L's, no reader gave the two different verdicts (0 mismatches in all three languages).
- **Facing strip.**
  - de: visible on 38 pages; read in by L on 13, C on 0, R on 0.
  - el: visible on 183; L 8, C 0, R 13.

**By eye** (image open, crops)
- **zh p82 (Lotus Sutra scroll).** C fixes L's 多寶佛塔品 → 分別功德品 and 八生, and keeps 六百八十萬億 where R has 八百.
  - Where the scroll is torn, C restores the lost characters (無生法, 陀羅尼門, most of panel 4) from the canonical sutra and tags them `<unclear>`. R restores them silently.
  - The reader counted L's "omission" of text that is lost from the leaf. On this damaged scroll the reader and C both lean on the known text. This is a caveat for damaged canonical texts.
- **zh p102.** C is sound. L drops two sentences. R has 梵王華 for 宿王華.
- **de 6a20…p15.**
  - C fixes L's invented margin note *Rom. 5.* → *v. 12.*, the initial (*Der Meinunge*) and *jhrer*. One slip: *verunehret* for *vervnehret*.
  - R normalises *außdrückliches* and *jhrer*.
- **de 69c8…p142 (a two-page spread).** R read only the right-hand page and dropped all 18 lines of p. 210. C keeps both pages, and puts one catchword into the body.
- **el 6993…p99 (Homeric cento).** Neither is clean.
  - C has *Ὀτρηρὸς* for *Ὀπτῆρ(ας)* and *Versus perfectus* for *ipfectus*.
  - R invents *φεύξασθαι*.
  - Both drift toward the printed Homer. C is better on layout and glosses.
- **el 69e8…p159 (Sextus).**
  - C rebuilds L's nonsense into the text, confirmed word by word: *ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐπιβάλλει κρίνειν*, *τοὐναντίον συστηματική*, *ὁ νήπιος καὶ ὁ μεμηνὼς*.
  - R invents whole phrases (*ὁ ἄνεμος*, *ἐκ πλειόνων σύγκειται*).
- **de `69b51cda…` p264, the only German C "worse" page.** The archived image is a 267-byte blank JPEG (so are pp. 263 and 265). C correctly answered CONTAIN ("the leaf cannot be read"). L serves a Latin page that nobody can check against an image.

**Served text that is not the page** (found by the corrector, confirmed by the blind readers; not contained by this job, which writes nothing)
- **Greek, whole books:**
  - Lucian MS `699383a150654cbbe29179f7`: 25/25 pages are invented Greek or repetition loops.
  - Euclid *Elements* MS `6993881574305116d72cef37`: 25/25 pages are invented propositions or loops.
  - Proclus *in Rempublicam* MS `6993898ace15387065947977`: 15/25 pages.
- **Chinese:** Kunqu `69de98851b234a773e438912`, pp. 269 and 341 serve another leaf's text.

**Cost** (Claude subscription, box account dereklomas@gmail.com; $0 billed. agy: plan fee)
- **Corrections (list-price equivalent of the tokens):**

  | Language | Pages | Calls | Output tokens | List price | Per 1K pages |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Chinese | 75 | 31 | 219K | $8.98 | $120 |
  | German | 250 | 30 | 377K | $18.53 | $74 |
  | Greek MSS | 250 | 46 | 1.18M | $42.05 | $168 |

  - Latin's $20.28 per 250 pages moved the account-week about 1%. On that scale a correction costs about **4% (de), 6% (zh) and 8% (Greek MSS) of an account-week per 1K pages**.
  - Greek manuscript calls ran 7–25 min each.
- **Whole job, wave 1** (corrections, 3 screens, 23 readers, by-eye): the weekly meter went **26% → 46%** (2026-10-27 21:00Z → 2026-10-28 02:35Z). Treat that as an upper bound, because the account is shared. Per language it was about zh 5, de 5, el 10 points.
  - The pace guard paused the Greek correction once (burn 6%/h, against a budget of 0.4%/h). It resumed after the window.
- **Flash re-read:** 636 agy calls for 575 pages (1.1 a page), about $0.66 per 1K pages at the plan fee.

**Human check** (Derek's addendum, for #7573): `scripts/eval/dataset/judge-human-check-7573/{chinese,german,greek}.jsonl`.
- Each file has one row per judged page: reader URL, image URL, the three arm texts, the Opus verdicts, defects and rationale, and the agy verdicts where drawn.
- 30 rows per language are marked `review: true`: the pages with the widest verdict spread, the C/R ties and the cross-family disagreements (`w-human.mjs`).

**Grade.** Exploratory. The samples are 3 to 10 books, the judge is single-family (with a 30-page cross-family check), and there is no human calibration yet (#7573 is that calibration). Chinese at n = 75 from 3 books is the thinnest.

Files: `scripts/eval/flash-reread-5924/`
- Scripts: `w-draw.mjs`, `w-set.mjs`, `w-packets.mjs`, `w-score.mjs`, `w-judge2.mjs`, `w-byeye.mjs`, `w-human.mjs` and `T-TASK.md`.
- `results-7568/<lang>/`: `sample.json`, `screen.json`, `stored-check.json`, `step-t.json` and `score.json`.

## 2026-10-28 · Is Opus through agy as good as Opus through claude -p on the cells routed to Opus? (#7545)
<!-- PRIOR ART: scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/judge.mjs (the router tests' instrument, reused unchanged except for two cells: latin-lite-7545 and german-7545); 2026-10-26 router tests (lite>opus-correct 30/30 on the Latin pilot; German opus-cli 49/60). Nothing before this run had measured Claude through agy: it was refused by assertGeminiModel until #7545. -->

**Latin correction: yes. German translation: not yet, because of a format failure rather than a reading failure.**

### Design
- **The exception.** Derek's rule (2026-10-27, restated 2026-10-28) allows Claude through agy only on an account whose Gemini weekly bucket reads 0. This test is the one exception, and it ran while Gemini quota remained. It used gex45's default login (dereklomas@, Gemini weekly 41%, Claude group 100%) on Derek's inbox note (09:21Z). The second login (`/root/.agy-james`) is held to `gemini-3.8-flash-low` and was not used. To open the gate in-process, the run pointed `AGY_QUOTA_CACHE` at a scratch reading with the Gemini weekly bucket set to 0. Nothing on any shared path was changed.
- **Pages.** Drawn with `judge.mjs draw --cells=latin-lite-7545,german-7545`, seeded, one page per book, visible books, interior pages.
  - **Latin, 15 pages.** Stored Flash-Lite OCR of at least 300 characters, books not held (the router-test frame, salt `rt-latin-lite-7545`).
  - **German, 30 pages.** Visible German books from 1500 to 1800 whose served English is 3 Flash or Flash-Lite and newer than the OCR, alternating between the two (salt `agy-opus-7545`, the pilot's 60 books left out). The cell was drawn at 15 pages and then extended to 30, because at n = 15 even 15/15 against 15/15 gives P = 0.87 under a flat prior. The first 15 pages are the same in both draws.
- **Routes.** Each pair ran on the same pages, with `CANDIDATE_READS=off` and `--fresh`. Nothing was kept or written.
  - Latin `lite>opus-correct`: `correct.mjs --model=opus` through `claude -p`, one page per call.
  - Latin `lite>agy-opus`: `cli-ocr.mjs read --correct-prompt` (the correction lane's own call and fc template) with `--model=claude-opus-5-5-low`. All 15 calls opened the image with `read_file`.
  - German `opus-cli`: `claude-translate.mjs read --model=opus --per-call=1`.
  - German `agy-opus-tr`: `cli-translate.mjs read --model=claude-opus-5-5-low`.
- **Judge.** `judge.mjs judge`: Opus through `claude -p`, blind, one output per call, the page image attached, two wrong-page controls per route. Every control passed.

### Result (`results/agy-opus-7545-2026-10-28/score.json`)
| cell | route | accepted | wrong text | fidelity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Latin lite | lite (the draft) | 8/15 | 7/15 | 3.53 |
| Latin lite | lite>opus-correct (claude -p) | **15/15** | 0/15 | 4.93 |
| Latin lite | lite>agy-opus | **15/15** | 0/15 | 4.73 |
| German tr | opus-cli (claude -p) | 26/30 | 3/30 | 4.10 |
| German tr | agy-opus-tr | 23/26 (+4 not written) | 2/26 | 4.12 |

- **Paired by page.** Latin: both routes accepted all 15 pages. agy answered UNCHANGED on 2 pages and claude -p on 1. German: both accepted 21 pages and both rejected 2. claude -p alone was accepted on 1 page, agy alone on 2. The remaining 4 were the agy marker failures, all of which claude -p got accepted.
- **The marker failure.** On 4/30 German pages, agy-Opus wrote the translation inside `<<<BEGIN>>>`/`<<<END>>>` and then the prompt's `<summary>` and `<keywords>` blocks after `<<<END>>>`. `unwrapRead` calls that "text outside the markers", and `cli-translate.mjs apply` refuses it. The translation inside the markers is complete. Fixing the call (a prompt line, or accepting a trailing summary/keywords block) and re-testing would likely clear the cell. That is a change to the writer's guard and is not made here.
- **The router's gate** (rules.json as of PR #7588: P(acc ≥ acc_ref − 0.08) ≥ 0.9, wrong text at most the reference rate + 4%):
  - Latin: P = **0.915** under the route prior Beta(3.22, 0.78), which `lite>opus` uses and the same model inherits; 0.873 under a flat prior. Wrong text 0 against 0. **Passes.**
  - German: 23/30 against 26/30 as the lane would count it, P = **0.45**. On the judged outputs alone (23/26), P = 0.85; against the pooled opus-cli record (75/90), P = 0.92. **Does not pass** until the 4 marker failures are fixed.

### Draw on the agy Claude group (`quota-readings.jsonl`, `agy-usage.json`)
Readings of `agy -p "/quota"` (free) on the main account, taken before and after each run. Nothing else on that account calls Claude models.

| run | pages | weekly bucket | 5-hour bucket |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 Latin corrections + 15 German translations | 30 | 99.93% → 92.68% | 100% → 85.51% |
| 15 German translations alone | 15 | 92.08% → 90.52% | 85.30% → 81.18% |

- **Per page.** German translation: 0.104% of the week and 0.27% of the 5-hour bucket. Latin correction, by difference: about 0.38% of the week and 0.69% of the 5-hour bucket. The weekly bucket also fell 0.6% between the runs with no calls, which is probably late accounting; with it, Latin is about 0.42%.
- **Tokens.** Latin median input is 25.6K (15.5K of it cache read: agy's system prompt plus the fc template and the image). German median input is 11.0K. The median call took 19 s for Latin and 11 s for German.
- **What that buys.** With the fallback stopping at the 10% floor, one account's Claude group holds about 235 Latin corrections, or about 870 German translations, per week. The 5-hour bucket allows about 130 Latin pages per window. This is a small pool next to the claude -p subscription: `correct.mjs` at 10 pages a call draws about 0.004% of a week per page.

### Replicated?
No. One draw per cell. The Latin result agrees with the 2026-10-26 pilot, where `lite>opus-correct` accepted 30/30.

### Artifact
`scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/results/agy-opus-7545-2026-10-28/`: sample, key, score, verdicts, per-page agy usage and the /quota readings. The reads themselves stayed on gex45 under `$JOB_SCRATCH`. The router's entries are the `fallback_routes` of the `latin-lite`, `german-tr-flash3` and `german-tr-lite` cells in `scripts/eval/estimator/router-table/rules.json`.

## 2026-10-27 · Tibetan translation router test: agy Flash-low, 4 pages a call, against Opus, 10 a call (#6948, #6740)

PRIOR ART: `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/judge.mjs` (the router tests, judge prompt and controls, reused); `scripts/eval/agy-per-call-7503/` (PR #7518: agy 1/2/4 pages a call for translation, not Tibetan and not against Opus).

**Decision it changes:** which route translates corrected Tibetan Kangyur text. This adds the router table's
`tibetan-tr` cell (`scripts/eval/estimator/router-table/rules.json`). Derek asked for it in an inbox note to job
`tib-corr-profiles-6560`, 2026-10-27 10:33Z.

**Result:** Opus at 10 pages a call **27/30** accepted, 1/30 wrong text. agy Flash-low at 4 a call **22/30**, 4/30 wrong
text. On the same 30 pages, Opus alone was accepted on 7 and agy alone on 2. The table's decision is **HOLD → opus-cli**.
- No route clears the hold bar: P(acceptance ≥ 0.8) ≥ 0.9.
- agy fails the wrong-text gate.

Nothing was written. The translations are of corrections that no page holds. `claude-translate.mjs --ocr-file` puts
the override's hash in the meta, so `cli-translate.mjs apply` refuses them.

## Set

- **Source text.** The note said to use the winning arm of the profile experiment
  (`2026-10-27-tibetan-corrector-profiles-diff-qa-6560.md`). No arm passed, so this uses **arm A**: Flash-low with
  today's prompt, unguarded, and never written.
- **Pages.** 30 pages, one per book (`translation-router/sample.json`).
  - 26 come from the profile experiment's 72-page diagnostic set (seeded, one per book). A page arm A changed by
    more than 25% was left out.
  - 4 are anchor folios of the 30-folio set where arm A caught every planted syllable.
  - The set was chosen from pages that earlier audits judged worse, so it is not the lane's frame.
- **Blocks.** Each test page is the first page of a block in its own book:
  - **agy** (`claude-translate.mjs --cli=agy --per-call=4`, #7503): the test page and the next 3 pages.
  - **Opus** (`claude-translate.mjs --per-call=10`): the test page and the next 9 pages, cut where the block reaches
    20K characters.
  - Only the test page carries the corrected text. Its neighbours carry their stored OCR (Yigdzin, or Flash where a
    volume was written).
  - The production prompt, seed and guards are unchanged. `CANDIDATE_READS=off`, `--fresh`.

## Judge

- **Prompt and setup.** One sealed Opus call per output (`replicate-6547/run-claude-arm.py`), route-judge
  `judgePrompt` (translation). The judge sees the page image and the corrected transcription, and is blind to route.
- **Planted reversals.** One per page, in alternating routes (`tengyur-characterize/plants.mjs plantReversal`).
- **Wrong-page controls.** 2 per route.
- **Page-break drift.** `block-drift.mjs` cannot see a caseless script, so drift is the judge's T4 (block shift) and
  T5 (leak / lookahead) defects.

## Results

| route | accepted | wrong text | fidelity (mean) | page-break drift (T4/T5) | planted reversals caught | controls | calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Opus `claude -p`, 10 a call** | **27/30** | **1/30** (O4: a Yigdzin duplicate line kept, with "again" added) | 4.3 | 2/30 | 15/15 | pass | 57 for 299 pages (3 refused for tags that do not match their pages, then re-read) |
| agy Gemini 3.8 Flash-low, 4 a call | 22/30 | 4/30 (T5 ×3, T9) | 3.9 | **6/30** | 15/15 | pass | 32 for 120 pages, 0 refused |

- **Paired, on the same 30 pages:** accepted only for Opus 7, only for agy 2. Mean fidelity agy − Opus is −0.4.
- **agy's commonest failure is lookahead (T5).** Where a leaf breaks off mid-word or mid-sentence, agy finishes the
  sentence from the next page in its block:
  - p.158 of `69e7ab06…`;
  - p.401 of `69e7ab28…`;
  - p.432 of `69e7ab34…`: three sentences from the next page.

  This is the page-break drift that block-drift cannot detect in Tibetan. Opus did it on 2 pages, once only in its
  summary.
- **agy has more O6** (a meaning-changing misreading), on 15/30 pages against Opus's 6/30. Most of these are tagged
  misleading, not wrong text.

**Cost.**
- Opus: 57 calls, 1.75 hours of call time, $22.35 at list prices for 299 pages (the CLI's figure). Nothing was billed:
  it ran on the subscription. The router table's size model puts it at about 0.00105 weekly points a page.
- agy: 32 calls for 120 pages, 0.27 calls a page.

## 2026-10-27 · What are the "severe" Tibetan correction errors? Re-class, Derge check, by eye, real-world rate (#6560)

PRIOR ART: `2026-10-27-tibetan-corrector-profiles-diff-qa-6560.md` (PR #7505: the 72-page diagnostic set, arms A/B/C,
span judge with `--severity`, confirm judge, whole-page judge, diff QA). This entry makes no new corrector calls. It
re-classes that run's verdicts, checks them against Derge and by eye, and then runs the same three judges on pages
the lane has already written.

**Why.** Derek (2026-10-27): "I question what those 'serious errors' are." The #7505 severity prompt labels the
*difference* between two readings. It counts mantra vowel length as severe. The 72-page set was chosen because it was
hard, so its rate is not the corpus rate.

### 1. Re-class by reader impact (no model calls)

`severity-recheck/classify.py` uses rules first and a hand table for the rest (`hand-labels.json`, 96 entries). The
hand table covers the spans the rules cannot settle, for example one letter changed in one syllable: ཚོན→ཚོགས is
another word, ཙད→ཅད is a spelling.

- **normalisation** (O8): mantra or Sanskrit vowel length, anusvara or candrabindu, visarga, a tsheg inside a Sanskrit
  cluster, a Sanskrit form put for the Tibetan one (ཀ་ཏྱའི་བུ→ཀཱ་ཏྱཱ་ཡཱ་ན).
- **mantra**: a mantra letter changed beyond normalisation (ཨཱ→ཞཱ, ཊཱ→ཏྲཱ). This class is shown separately and is
  not counted as severe.
- **minor**: a particle variant, a particle added or dropped, tsheg or shad, a split or join, the same word spelled
  another way, the tense or honorific form of the same verb.
- **severe** (O1/O5/O6/O7): another word with another meaning, a negation, a number or a name, or text added or
  dropped. It has three sub-kinds: a word swap (1–2 syllables), an add/drop, and a phrase (3+ syllables).

The judges' verdicts on which reading the leaf shows are unchanged. A page is severe under three conditions:
- a severe-class span where the span judge **and** the confirm judge saw the draft on the leaf;
- the whole-page judge finds a new wrong-text defect that is not O8;
- the page is a wreck (over 25% changed).

**Arm A, the spans #7505 counted as severe introduced** (the leaf shows the draft):

| class | spans | pages | both judges | Derge says (all) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| normalisation | 22 | 3 | 17 on 1 page (ཧུྃ→ཧཱུྃ ×17) | — |
| mantra letter | 2 | 1 | 1 | — |
| minor | 5 | 4 | 1 | — |
| severe: word swap | 16 | 13 | 12 on 10 pages | draft 10, arm 1, neither 4, not placed 1 |
| severe: added/dropped | 12 | 10 | 10 on 8 pages | draft 8, arm 3, neither 1 |
| severe: phrase 3+ | 16 | 11 | 11 on 8 pages | draft 6, arm 1, neither 6, not placed 3 |

**Derek's rule** (fewer than 2 of 10 pages severe, i.e. at most 14 of 72), with #7505's verdicts and the new classes:

| variant | #7505 severe pages | re-classed (both judges) [95%] | one judge only | rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 31 (4.3) | 28 (3.9) [2.9, 5.0] | 30 | fail |
| B | 33 (4.6) | 29 (4.0) | 31 | fail |
| C | 31 (4.3) | 28 (3.9) | 31 | fail |
| A + lane guards | 18 (2.5) | 15 (2.1) | 17 | fail |
| A + diff QA | 18 (2.5) | 17 (2.4) | 17 | fail |
| **B + diff QA** | 13 (1.8) | **12 (1.7)** | 15 | **pass** |
| C + diff QA | 17 (2.4) | 16 (2.2) | 17 | fail |

**The re-class moves the page counts by 1 to 4 pages, and no verdict changes.** The mantra spans were 24 of 73 by count,
but they sat on 4 pages, and most of those pages are severe for other reasons too. In arm A, a page is severe:
- through a confirmed span: 19 pages;
- through the whole-page judge: 12 pages (dropped or invented lines, O1/O5/O6);
- as a wreck: 4 pages.

### 2. Derge check (`severity-recheck/derge-spans.py`)

Each draft page was placed in Derge with `tib-derge.py locate` (PR #7465, OpenPecha P000001). 71 of 72 pages were
placed. The one that was not, Thadrak brGyad stong p.415, is dedication verses, not Kangyur text. Each severe draft-win span
of A, B and C (unique, 115) was set in its context and aligned locally to the window:

| sub-kind | spans | draft = Derge (Flash broke good text) | arm = Derge, leaf shows draft | neither | not placed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| word swap | 57 | 36 | 7 | 10 | 4 |
| added/dropped | 25 | 14 | 5 | 6 | 0 |
| phrase 3+ | 33 | 17 | 1 | 10 | 5 |
| **all** | **115** | **67 (58%)** | **13 (11%)** | **26** | **9** |

**Most severe spans are Flash breaking text that Derge agrees with. They are not recitation.** "arm = Derge" is a weak
signal of recitation. The by-eye sample below had 4 such spans:
- one where the arm really was right (the draft had skipped a passage);
- one spelling variant (ཁྲི་ཁྲག for ཁྲི་ཕྲག);
- one interlinear insertion the arm dropped;
- one where the alignment matched a repeated formula on the next line.

None of the 4 was Flash supplying Derge text that the leaf lacks. Derge is also not this manuscript's text, so
"neither" includes real manuscript variants.

### 3. By eye, 15 spans at full resolution (`results/.../by-eye-15.json`)

The sample is seeded (6560): 5 phrases, 5 word swaps and 5 adds/drops from arm A's severe draft-win spans. Each span
was opened in a brightened full-resolution crop of the page image (`zoom.mjs`).

| stratum | leaf shows draft | arm | neither | span judge right | counted severe (both judges) and draft by eye |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| phrase | 4 | 0 | 1 | 4/5 | 3/3 |
| word swap | 4 | 1 | 0 | 4/5 | 4/4 |
| add/drop | 4 | 1 | 0 | 4/5 | 4/4 |
| **all** | **12** | **2** | **1** | **12/15** | **11/11** |

- **The span judge alone is wrong 3 times in 15.**
  - #11: the leaf has the passage the arm added; the draft had skipped it.
  - #6: the leaf reads བླ་མར་བགྱིད, which is the arm's reading.
  - #3: the lower leaf's first line is missing from the draft; the arm puts back a shortened version of it.
- **Every span that both judges confirmed was right by eye: 11 of 11.** The confirm step is what makes the count
  trustworthy. It overruled the span judge on #6 and #11, and answered other or unclear on #1 and #3.
- One confirmed span was re-classed after the eye check: ཁྲག→ཕྲག in ཁྲི་ཁྲག is a spelling of ཁྲི་ཕྲག ("ten
  thousand"), so it is minor. It is in the hand table.

### 4. Real-world rate: pages the lane has written (`severity-recheck/realworld.mjs`)

- **Frame.** Pages whose stored OCR is the lane's write (`ocr.pipeline = tib-correct-6560`, Flash-low), excluding
  Neyphug rGyud Tsha (wave 1) and #7505's 72 pages. That is 7,284 pages in **19 books**, so one page per book gives
  19, not 20.
- **Draft.** The draft is the Yigdzin row that the write replaced, in `page_revisions`.
- **Judges.** The span judge was asked the three classes in its prompt. The confirm judge ran on every severe
  draft-win span and every line hunk. The whole-page judge ran on the draft and on the written text. 66 sealed Opus
  calls.

| | value |
|---|---|
| pages severe | **6 of 19: 3.2 per 10**, Wilson 95% [1.5, 5.4], by-book bootstrap [1.1, 5.3] |
| from confirmed spans / whole-page judge | 5 / 1 |
| spans fixed / introduced | 195 / 17 |
| introduced, by class | severe 7, minor 9, mantra 1, normalisation 0 |
| fixed severe-class spans (span judge only) | 48 on 13 pages |
| span judge: better / same / worse | 18 / 0 / 1 |
| whole-page judge: better / same / worse | 9 / 10 / 0 |
| controls (span, confirm) | 37/38, 14/18 |

The 6 severe pages:
- Thadrak 'Dus 'khor p.411: བགོ་བ→གོས་བཟང.
- Neyphug mDo sde Ma p.263: འཚལ→འཆལ ("ask" becomes "immoral").
- Kanjur dKon brtsegs Nga p.246: བས→བསལ (a second severe span there was not confirmed).
- Neyphug mDo sde Ja p.350: ན་བདེ→ནད་པ་དེ. The leaf has ན་བ་དེ; the draft was wrong too.
- Kanjur Sras sna tshogs p.150: དེ་ཅིའི→དེའི. The question "why is that?" becomes "therefore".
- Kanjur Phal chen Ka p.212: Flash **swapped two lines** of the lower leaf, the 4th and 5th. They now read in a better
  order, but not in the order the leaf has them, which I checked by eye. The line-count guard cannot see a swap.

No severe page in this sample came from mantra or normalisation. Flash's mantra habit is real, but it lands on few
pages.

### What it means

The severe errors are real word substitutions, plus dropped or reordered lines. The counts are not inflated by mantra
spelling. The two-judge count is accurate (11/11 by eye). On written pages the lane:
- fixes far more than it breaks (195 spans fixed against 17 introduced; 48 severe-class fixes against 7 severe
  introductions);
- makes no page worse by the whole-page judge;
- still leaves a new severe error on about 3 pages in 10 (1.5–5.4), which is above the rule's 2.

**Recommendation.**
- **Pause new volumes:** the rule fails at 3.2/10.
- **Revert no class wholesale.** Reverting the normalisation class removes nothing on written pages (0 introduced).
  Reverting whole pages would bring back about 7 severe errors for every 1 it removes.
- **On the written pages, put back only the spans that both judges confirm as severe.** That is the shape of the
  vol1 job's diff-QA tranche, and of B + diff QA, the only variant that passes.
- **Add a line-order check:** does each output line match the leaf line at the same position? The swap on p.212
  passes every guard the lane has.

### Cost

- 66 sealed Opus calls on the subscription: span 19, confirm 9, whole page 38.
- 0 agy calls; $0 paid. No page, book or R2 object was written.

### Artifacts

- Scripts: `scripts/eval/tibetan-correct-6560/severity-recheck/`.
- Results: `scripts/eval/results/tibetan-correct-6560/severity-recheck-6560/`:
  - `hunks-7505.jsonl.gz`: every hunk's verdicts from #7505's score;
  - `reclass-7505.json.gz`;
  - `derge-locate.jsonl`, `derge-spans.jsonl`;
  - `by-eye-15.json`;
  - `realworld-score.json.gz`.

## 2026-10-27 · Tibetan router cell: 30 more Kangyur folios, Yigdzin > agy Flash-low correction (#6740)

PRIOR ART: the pilot's Tibetan cell (`2026-10-25-route-judge-qualitative-pilot-6740.md`, #7376) and #6560's arms
(`scripts/eval/tibetan-correct-6560/`). This is a new router-test cell in the same harness,
`scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/judge.mjs` (`draw --cells=tib-kangyur`), stacked on #7434's router-test stages. It is not
a second harness.

**Why.** PR #7461 made the wrong-text bar relative to the best route. After that, the Tibetan cell was HOLD only
because Flash-low's P(acc >= 0.8) was 0.84 on 30 folios, below 0.9. Thirty more folios decide whether it switches.

**Draw.** The pilot's frame (`tibetan-proofread/draw.mjs`), with seed `rt-tib-kangyur`, recorded in `sample.json`:
- visible Tibetan books titled Kanjur/Kangyur, the pilot's 30 books left out. Lane holds are allowed
  (tibetan-retranslation, kangyur-import, specialist-ocr-lane); containment holds are not.
- the page is still served by `bdrc-yigdzin-v1` (`ocr.source` bdrc, not the #6560 volume pass), with a British Library
  EAP image, not split or cropped, interior, at least 300 characters.
- the folio is placed in Derge with identity in [0.90, 0.97], the pilot's band.
- one folio per book, books in seeded order: 30 folios from the first 80 books walked.

All 30 are two-leaf frames (a marked `<leaf-break/>`). The pilot's 10 marked + 20 single mix was not available: walking
all 195 books found only 4 single-leaf folios in band. In the pilot the marked frames were not harder: Flash-low 10/10,
Opus 9/10 and Yigdzin 5/10 there, against 16/20, 16/20 and 12/20 on single leaves.

**Routes.** Per folio, all fresh reads, `CANDIDATE_READS=off`, one page a call:
- `yigdzin`: the stored draft.
- `yigdzin>agy-flash-low`: `cli-ocr.mjs read --correct-prompt=tibetan-correct-6560/corr-prompt.txt`, agy
  `gemini-3.8-flash-low`. This is #6560's CORR request and the volume pass's.
- `yigdzin>opus-correct`: `claude -p --model opus`, the same CORR prompt, the image in a sealed folder, Read only. This is
  `replicate-6547/run-claude-arm.py`'s request.

Both correctors answered 30/30. Opus left the draft unchanged on 7 folios. No CONTAIN answers.

**Judge.** The pilot's one Opus judge and prompt: 99 calls, blind, one output a call, against the image. That covers
90 outputs (one shared text), 6 wrong-page controls and 10 planted drafts. Every route's controls passed.

**Derge.** OpenPecha P000001 is public; the Hetzner index pickle was not reachable from this box. `tib-derge.py`
rebuilds a folio's window (Pagination imgnum ± 2) from a sparse checkout, which took about a minute. It reproduces 29
of #6560's 30 committed windows syllable for syllable; the 30th has the same length, because the e-text was revised on
2026-10-22. A new folio is placed by syllable 5-gram votes over every Derge page, taking the best identity of the top 3.
Tested on the pilot's 30: 23 on the manifest's page and the rest within a page or on a repeated passage, with identity
equal or higher.

### Result (`results/tibetan-30-2026-10-27/score.json`)

| route | accepted, this run [95% by book] | pooled 60 | wrong text (run / pooled) | fidelity | Derge identity | worse than draft |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yigdzin | 17/30 [0.40, 0.73] | 34/60 | 11/30 / 23/60 | 3.6 | 0.944 | — |
| yigdzin>agy-flash-low | **27/30** [0.77, 1.00] | **53/60** | 2/30 / 5/60 | 4.2 | **0.967** | 1/30 (better 15/30) |
| yigdzin>opus-correct | 27/30 [0.80, 1.00] | 52/60 | 2/30 / 5/60 | 4.1 | 0.960 | 1/30 (better 13/30) |

- **Top defects.** Yigdzin: O6 misread 26/30 and O5 omission 11/30; its wrong text is O6, O4 and O5. Flash-low: O12
  (marginal folio labels dropped) 9/30 and O6 8/30. Opus: O6 14/30 and O12 7/30.
- **Wrong text in the corrections.** Both correctors' wrong-text pages include the same folio
  (`69e7ab225f1a22ab19a93749:82`). Flash reads ཀུན་དགའ་ར་བ as རི་རབ, twice. Opus drops a line on an eye-skip.
- **Planted syllables: caught 8/10** (0.80, at the bar), so the judge decides, not Derge. It missed a vowel
  (ཆེན → ཆིན) and a letter (ཆུས → ཇུས). It accepted 5 of the 10 planted drafts, so a single planted syllable does not
  by itself sink a page.
- **Derge order: 31/32** pairs agree with the judge (27 ties). The one disagreement is Flash against Opus on a folio
  where Derge favours Opus by 0.008.
- **Made worse (#6758's question).** Flash-low: 1/30 worse, 15/30 better, accept lost 1 and gained 11, wrong text
  added 0. Opus: 1/30, 13/30, lost 1 and gained 11, wrong text added 0. Neither corrector made a ya-btags edit
  (`tibetan-yatags-guard.mjs`). Flash changed a median 3.2% of syllables (max 21%), Opus 1.3% (max 11%); none is over
  the 25% apply cap. PR #6758's gate found 10/40 changed pages worse. That gate was a span-level A/B read-off: a page
  counted as worse when the leaf showed the draft at more spans than the correction. This run uses the page-level
  judge, which does not see a few worse spans on a page that is better overall. So for the router question (which
  route gives the better page) the whole-page answer is that Flash helps. It does not overrule #6758's gate on an
  APPLY, where any span made worse is a regression written into the page.

### Router table (`estimator/router-table/2026-10-27-tibetan-30.md`, before: `2026-10-26-router-tests`)

| route | P(acc >= 0.8), before → after | posterior mean [90%] |
|---|---|---|
| yigdzin>agy-flash-low | 0.85 → **0.96** | 0.88 [0.81, 0.94] |
| yigdzin>opus | 0.68 → 0.91 | 0.86 [0.78, 0.93] |

**Decision: HOLD → yigdzin>agy-flash-low becomes switch → yigdzin>agy-flash-low.** The cell clears the HOLD bar (P >=
0.9). Flash-low is the cheapest route within 0.05 of the best, and its wrong-text rate (5/60) equals the best route's,
so it is within the relative bar. Under the absolute 2% bar the cell would keep Opus (5/60 is 8%). No other cell
changes.

**Not in scope.** No routing-table (`scripts/lib/*-routing-table.json`) edits, and no writes to pages. The /quality

## 2026-10-27 · Does Opus translating from the LEAF rescue the Kangyur two-leaf frames? (#6948)

PRIOR ART: `2026-10-24-opus-translate-tibetan-sanskrit-gate-6948.md` (text-only Opus on the Yigdzin transcription:
Kangyur CANON 19/40 bad, 18 of the 28 Tibetan bad pages caused by the transcription); job tib-concept-opus-6948's
Bardo pilot (#6948, 2026-10-27 11:42Z: the same Opus given the leaf as full-resolution strips, `claude-translate.mjs
--images-dir`, 1/30 bad, but on clean print with 1.6 differing spans a page against 16.6 on Kangyur frames);
`2026-10-27-tibetan-translation-router-agy4-vs-opus10-6948.md` (Opus@10 27/30 on Flash-CORRECTED text);
`split-leaves-5771` (#5771: per-leaf re-reads, 21% bad). Harness: `scripts/eval/tib-leaf-translate-6948/draw.mjs`;
the auditor is `scripts/eval/opus-tib-sa-6948/audit.mjs`, unchanged.

**Question.** On the hard Kangyur manuscripts, does showing Opus the leaf replace the Flash correction pass? If the
translator reads the leaf and brackets where it departs from the transcription, the 10-24 OCR-caused failures
(seam lines invented or duplicated, truncated lines) should not reach the English.

### Pre-registration (written and pushed before any audit reply is read)

**Frame.** The 10-24 Kangyur CANON stratum, rebuilt today with the 10-24 `frame.mjs` unchanged (live Tibetan books,
Yigdzin transcription, no English, not withheld for source_loop / ocr_unreadable / invented_by_eye, not left to
84000) and the 10-24 CANON title regex. Dropped: any book with a page whose OCR is the Flash correction
(`ocr.pipeline: tib-correct-6560`; the uncorrected Yigdzin text is the point), and job tib-concept-opus-6948's six
books.

**Stage 1 draw (`draw.mjs stage1`, seed 6948).** 20 blocks of up to 10 consecutive frame pages, one book each.
- **PAIRED-BAD, 5 blocks:** five of the 10-24 CANON pages the auditor called bad, drawn by seed from the 19 whose
  stored transcription is byte-identical to what the 10-24 auditor saw. That page is the audited page of its block.
- **FRESH, 15 blocks:** from other CANON books, a random block and a random audited page in it.

**Amendment, 12:55Z, before any read (the draw only).** Frame pages are scattered in these volumes: most of their
neighbours already carry older English or are withheld, so 10 consecutive *frame* pages rarely exist, and the first
draw gave 2-page blocks and dropped every paired page. A block is now 10 consecutive pages with an uncorrected
Yigdzin transcription (not unreadable, not withheld for source_loop / ocr_unreadable / invented_by_eye), whether or
not they have English; the AUDITED page is always a frame page (no English). Nothing is written, so existing English
is untouched. The draw: 20 blocks, 200 pages; PAIRED-BAD = 10-24 a034, a008, a015, a011, a031.

**Strips (before any read).** The frames come from the R2 archived master (BL's IIIF serves a whole image at only
1,200 px) and are cut into 2–3 vertical strips (≤ ~1,600 source px wide, 6% overlap), read at 0.5–0.67 of native
scale, about the Bardo pilot's scale. The Bardo rule alone (aspect ≤ 1.8) gave one strip per 1.5:1 frame, at 0.33.

**Pacing (inbox note 15:23Z, acted on 15:31Z).** The account was spending ~2.4%/h of its week against ~0.5%/h, so the
reads went from 2 streams to 1. 38 pages had been read in 2 streams before the 12:57Z 5-hour stop.

**Translator.** Opus via `claude -p` on this box's subscription, `claude-translate.mjs read --images-dir`
(job tib-concept-opus-6948's change, carried in this PR): each page's scan as overlapping full-resolution strips,
Read only, "translate what the leaf says, bracket where it departs from the transcription". 10 pages a call,
`--fresh`, `CANDIDATE_READS=off`, the production block prompt and seed, the UNCORRECTED Yigdzin text. Only the audited
page of each block is judged.

**Audit.** `audit.mjs` unchanged: blind, sealed Opus, page image + full-resolution tiles, the stored transcription and
the English; 6 planted controls (4 reversals, 2 inventions) on other read pages of the blocks, shuffled in with opaque
ids. `audit.mjs attribute` splits bad pages into transcription-caused and translator-caused, as on 10-24.

**Bar (Stage 1 passes only if all hold):**
1. **Bad ≤ 1 of 20** audited pages (≤ 5%), the auditor's verdict taken as given (by eye can only add bad pages).
2. **0 invented and 0 wrong-leaf by eye** on 10 pages I open myself, strips at full resolution: all 5 PAIRED-BAD
   pages, every page the auditor flags for invention or wrong-leaf, then the rest by seed from the FRESH pages.
3. **Controls:** at least 5 of 6 caught, or the auditor's verdicts do not count.

Reported, not gated: FRESH alone (the unbiased rate) and PAIRED-BAD alone (before 5/5 bad → after k/5), with Wilson
95% intervals; OCR spans per page; leaf notes the translator added; attribution.

**Stage 2 (only if Stage 1 passes; still files only).** `draw.mjs stage2`, seed 69482: 30 blocks of 10 consecutive
frame pages from 30 CANON books not in Stage 1; same translator settings. 20 of the 30 blocks (seeded) get one

concurrency caveat (job tib-concept-opus-6948 reads on the same account at the same time). Stage 2's audit is
reported against the same ≤ 5% bar; it decides the recommendation, not a write.

agy. No page writes.

## 2026-10-27 · Flash-low correction pass into production, gated per volume (#6560)

PRIOR ART: `2026-10-15-tibetan-flash-pass-gate-6560.md` (the gate that failed: 10/40 pages worse with the tiled span
judge, bar <= 2) and `2026-10-27-tibetan-router-30-6740.md` (the router cell that switched to Yigdzin > agy Flash-low:
53/60 accepted against the image, whole-page judge, 1/30 pages worse). This entry reuses the #6758 pass machinery
(`scripts/eval/tibetan-correct-6560/pass/`) and adds the second judge to its audit.

### Pre-registration (written 2026-10-26, before any audit reply of the gate volume was read)

- **Gate volume:** `69e7aab880b52390feb197a8`, Thadrak Kanjur rGyud 'bum Ka, 525 frame pages: the first volume of
  `volume-ids.mjs order` that is not rGyud 'bum Kha (the #6758 gate volume).
- **Read and dry apply:** `run-volume.sh <book> --no-apply` (Flash-low, the #6560 CORR prompt, the ya-btags leaf
  check by sealed Opus). Nothing is written.
- **Sample:** `leafcheck.mjs audit-req --n=40 --seed=6560`: 40 pages drawn from the changed pages apply would write.
- **Judge 1, tiled span judge:** `tiles-req` + sealed Opus (`run-claude-arm.py`), scored by `audit-score`. A page is
  worse when the leaf shows the draft at more changed spans than the correction.
- **Judge 2, whole-page judge:** `page-req`: the route-judge prompt (`route-judge-6740/judge.mjs` `judgePrompt`),
  sealed Opus, one output a call, the draft and the written text judged separately and blind. A page is worse when
  fidelity drops, accept is lost, or a wrong-text defect is added (judge.mjs `made_worse`); better when fidelity
  rises and it is not worse; else same.
- **Pooled verdict per page:** the judges agree → that; worse against better → same; one says same → the other's
  verdict; a page one judge did not answer takes the other's.
- **Bar (gate):** pooled worse <= 4/40 AND pooled better >= 3 × pooled worse. Both judges are reported separately.
- **PASS:** apply the gate volume (no `--mark-stale`), then volume by volume in `volume-ids` order, each audited on
  10 changed pages with both judges. **Stop** the run if a volume's pooled worse > 2/10 or the ya-btags guard fires
  on > 1% of its pages.
- **FAIL:** nothing is written; report the numbers and the kinds of span that go wrong, and stop. The bar is not
  tuned after the data.

### Result

**Run (2026-10-26).** `run-pass.sh gate 69e7aab880b52390feb197a8`.
- **Read:** 525 pages, Flash-low through agy (527 calls, 2 re-reads), 0 reused, $0. Nothing written.
- **Dry apply:** 521 pages would be written, 492 of them changed. Refused: 1 reply cut before `<<<END>>>` and 1
  page that changed 47% of the draft's syllables. Held by the ya-btags guard: 2 pages (0.4%). Sealed Opus kept 1 of
  those 2 changes and answered unclear on the other (controls 4/4).
- **Audit:** 40 changed pages, seed 6560. Tiled span judge: 40 Opus calls, 448 changed spans plus 80 controls.
  Whole-page judge: 80 Opus calls, the draft and the written text judged separately.

| judge | better / same / worse (of 40) | other measures |
|---|---|---|
| tiled span judge (`audit-score`) | 28 / 6 / **6** | the leaf shows the correction at 310 of 424 decided spans (73% [69, 77]); controls 72/80 right |
| whole-page judge (`page-req`, route-judge prompt) | 10 / 25 / **5** | accepted: draft 27/40, written 30/40; wrong-text defects: draft 15, written 9 |
| **pooled** (the pre-registered rule) | **27 / 7 / 6** | bar: worse <= 4 and better >= 3 × worse → **FAIL** (better passes, worse does not) |

- **The judges agree at chance on which pages are worse.** Ordinal α −0.07 over 40 pages, **not settled**. Both say
  worse on 1 page (523). The span judge's 6 worse pages are better or same to the whole-page judge, and the reverse
  holds for 4 of the page judge's 5.

| span judge \ page judge | better | same | worse |
|---|---|---|---|
| better | 7 | 18 | 3 |
| same | 2 | 3 | 1 |
| worse | 1 | 4 | 1 |

- **What goes wrong, by the span judge** (114 spans where the leaf shows the draft):
  - 48 substituted words (O6): ནི→ཡང, དབང→དགྲ, ཡང→བརྒྱད, པ→རྐྱེན, གཅོད→ཆད, འཛུག→འཛུད, and mantra syllables
    re-spelled (ཧྲཱིཾ→ཧྲཱིཿ, ཨོཾ་ཏྲི→ཨོ་ཌི).
  - 30 tshegs inserted or removed (O8). 26 of them are on one mantra page (p. 350), splitting དྷཱཿསརྦ into དྷཱཿ་སརྦ
    where the leaf writes it joined. Also ཡི་ས→ཡིས.
  - 25 mantra vowel length or anusvara normalised (O8): ཧུྃ→ཧཱུྃ ten times on p. 433, ྃ→ཾ, དྲུཾ→དྲཱུཾ.
  - 8 syllables dropped or added (O5), and 3 particles or final -s normalised (O8).
- **What goes wrong, by the whole-page judge** (its 5 worse pages):
  - 2 pages lose a whole line on one leaf: p. 488 and p. 78 (O5, wrong text added). The span judge scored both
    pages better, because it judges the spans it is shown and not what a page lacks.
  - 1 page has a verse doubled (p. 218, O4).
  - 1 page has its verse numbers put out of step (p. 523, O7).
  - 1 page has seed syllables misread (p. 359, O6).
- **The same classes as #6758.** Normalising toward the expected spelling (O8) and substituted words (O6) are both
  back. Dropped lines are new, and only the whole-page judge sees them.

**Served draft, checked by eye (containment).** The whole-page judge tagged the served Yigdzin draft O1 on 2 pages.
- p. 418: the lower leaf's first line is served as a loop (ག་པ་དང་། །ག་པ་དང་། །ག་པ་དཱ་པ་དཱ་པ…). The leaf reads
  གྲི་གུག་… ཕྲེང་… སྣ་ཚོགས་ཕྱག་མཚན་… (full-resolution tile, by eye). Confirmed: the served text is not on the leaf.
  The book is already held (`tibetan-retranslation-awaits-derek`, #4523), and the page has no English. So there is
  nothing to withhold. The repair is owed, and is logged on #6560.
- p. 174: the extra line is a near-duplicate (O4). I could not confirm it by eye at this resolution, so it is left.

**Decision.** The gate failed on worse pages (6/40, bar 4). As pre-registered, nothing is applied and the run stops
at the gate. The routing row records the router's pick and this gate (`scripts/lib/ocr-routing-table.json`, row
`tibetan`). Pages changed: 0. Re-translation load: 0.

**What this does and does not say.** On whole pages Flash-low helps: accepted pages go from 27 to 30 of 40, and
wrong-text defects from 15 to 9. That agrees with the router cell. It also writes errors the leaf contradicts into
most pages it changes, and 6 of 40 pages come out net worse by one judge or the other. Two options would change this:
- a correction whose apply keeps only the spans a leaf check confirms (the ya-btags guard, extended to every span);
- a prompt that forbids normalising mantra and tshegs, and forbids dropping a line, measured through this same gate on
  a new volume.

Either one is a new pre-registration, not a re-cut of this bar.

**Cost.** $0 paid. 527 agy Flash-low calls. 122 sealed Opus calls on this box's subscription (2 ya-btags, 40 tiled,
80 whole-page).

Artifacts: `scripts/eval/results/tibetan-correct-6560/pass-prod-gate-69e7aab880b52390feb197a8/`. That holds the reads,
the dry apply, the ya-btags files, both judges' requests and replies, the audit key, and `audit40-gate.json.gz` (per
page: both verdicts and the pooled one).

## 2026-10-27 · Invented repeated lines in Tibetan OCR, and Flash corrections under the severity rule (#6740)

PRIOR ART: `2026-10-27-tibetan-flash-pass-production-6560.md` (#7477: rGyud 'bum Ka gate, NO-GO pooled worse 6/40),
`2026-10-15-tibetan-flash-pass-gate-6560.md` (rGyud 'bum Kha, NO-GO 10/40), `2026-10-27-tibetan-router-30-6740.md`
(the 30 folios re-audited here), and job tib-flash-correct-vol1-6740 (Neyphug rGyud Tsha, not touched here). The
detector's walk shape is `scripts/audit/ocr-loop-corpus.mjs`.

**Brief** (Derek, 2026-10-26 23:15Z): find invented repeated lines corpus-wide, surface existing agy Flash corrections
that pass the new rule, and correct the flagged pages. **The rule:** write a correction when it passes the automatic
guards (25% cap, END sentinel, ya-btags), does not lower Derge identity by more than 0.01 where a parallel exists, and a
10-page audit per 1,000 pages written (Opus judge B with controls) finds a severe error introduced on fewer than 2 of
10. SEVERE means an invented, duplicated or dropped line, a change of meaning or negation, or a wrong mantra.

### 1. Detector (`scripts/audit/tibetan-duplicate-lines.mjs`)
- **Walk:** 2,402 Tibetan books, 889,974 pages with OCR, read-only, checkpointed per book, about 13 minutes.
- **Cut 0, the brief's scan** (two lines of 12 or more syllables sharing 50% of their syllable trigrams) misses p.128 itself.
  Yigdzin's copies differ every few syllables, which breaks trigrams. It was replaced by a syllable Smith-Waterman score.
- **Cut 1** (score of 15 or more, and one or more lines over the book's usual count): 20 pages checked by eye
  (`detector-calibration.json`, sets A and B). 14 real, 3 false, 3 undecided.
- **Cut 2, the shipped `flag`** (the extra line, plus a near-copy pair at most 3 lines apart, score of 15 or more and at least 40% of
  the shorter line): tuned on those 20 pages, where it kept every decided true page and dropped every false one.
  **Checked on fresh pages (set C): 2 real of 6 decided** (1 undecided, the rest not reached). This is far under the
  90% bar, so the detector was not used to choose writes.
- **Why text cannot do it.** On C8 the leaf repeats lines 2 and 4 nearly word for word, and the OCR is right. On C5, C7
  and C8 the frames are 8+8 lines in volumes whose usual frame is 7+7, so "one line too many" is the scribe's. A
  whole-line character-similarity measure does not separate them either: the false pages score 0.83 to 0.96.
- **An ink-row line counter** (a projection profile over a margin strip) was prototyped to read the leaf's own line
  count. In two tuning passes it was off by 2 to 5 lines on most frames, so it was dropped and not shipped.
- **Counts, for the worklist only:** 7,568 pages flagged in 849 books (761 public). 2,272 of them carry served English.
  By engine: Yigdzin 6,318, woodblock-easter2 1,038, Gemini 212. At the measured precision, expect about a third to
  be real.

### 2. Inventory of existing correction reads (R2 `candidate-reads`, all boxes)
| run | model | pages | written | draft still stored | under the rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tib-flash-pass-6560, rGyud 'bum Kha | Flash low | 415 | never | yes | not surfaced: #6758 judge B 10/40 worse; draft-wins include a lost negation (མ་ཡིན→མར), word swaps (གསུངས→བསམ, ཐོན→གནོད) and mantra changes |
| tib-flash-pass-6560, rGyud 'bum Ka | Flash low | 524 | never | yes | not surfaced: #7477 NO-GO; 48 substituted words, 2 dropped lines, 1 doubled verse in its 40-page audit |
| tib-g4-gate-6560, rGyud 'bum Kha | Gemini 4 Argon low | 426 | never | yes | not surfaced: its gate NO-GO (5/40), and the brief's rule is for Flash |
| tib-flash-correct-vol1-6740, wave 2 | Flash low | 120 (20 books) | never | yes | not surfaced: one-judge draft-wins that read as severe on about 11 of 38 audited pages; the confirmed run was cut off twice by session ends |
| tib-router-30-6740 | Flash low | 30 (30 books) | never | yes | **audited end to end: FAIL** (below) |
| tib-flash-correct-vol1-6740, Neyphug rGyud Tsha | Flash low | 960 | — | — | excluded: that job's volume |
The 6948 and 5771 pilots left no OCR correction reads in R2: 6948 was translation, and 5771 was Yigdzin re-reads.

### 3. The severity audit, run on router-30 (`pass/severity-batch.sh`)
- **Guards:** 30/30 pass. No ya-btags hits.
- **Derge guard (`derge-guard-allow.mjs`):** 30/30 placed. 0 refused. Mean identity rose from 0.944 to 0.967.
- **Audit:** 10 seeded pages.
  - Judge B with severity labels: 148 items.
  - A second sealed Opus on every severe draft-win (`confirm-req`).
  - The whole-page judge on the draft and on the correction (`page-req`).
- **Result:**
  - Severe error introduced on **4 of 10** pages, confirmed by both judges (bar: fewer than 2). **FAIL.**
  - Severe errors fixed on 7 of 10 pages: 17 severe spans fixed, 94 minor.
  - Controls 20/20, and the confirming judge's 10/10.
  - The introduced errors: བདུན་པ→བ་དགུ ("seventh"→"nine"), ཀར→པ་ན, བལ་གླང→བ་ལང, ཨཱ→ཞཱ (mantra), and བུ་མོས
    ("girl")→ཁྱིམ་ས་པ. The leaf shows the draft each time.
- **Read plainly.** Flash fixes more than it breaks on almost every page. But it puts a wrong word on about a third of
  pages, and the Derge identity guard cannot see it, because the many small fixes outweigh the one wrong word.

### 4. Pilot reads of flagged pages
56 of 120 flagged public pages were read by agy Flash-low with the CORR request. agy ran at 30–180 s a page, and two
session ends killed the run. Of those 56, Flash dropped one line of the detector's pair on only 2. It kept the same
line count on 27 and wrote fewer long lines on 14. Nothing was audited or written. The reads are kept in R2 (#7075).

### Undo
No page was written, so there is nothing to undo. `severity-batch.sh --apply` writes through `cli-ocr.mjs apply`
(`writePageText`, run id `cli-ocr-<stamp>`). `scripts/maintenance/revert-run.mjs --run-id <run>` undoes such a run.

Artifacts: `scripts/eval/results/tibetan-correct-6560/severity-6740/`.
Cost: $0. About 70 agy calls (56 reads plus re-reads) and about 45 Opus calls: 10 span, 20 page, 5 confirm, plus ya-btags checks for wave 2.

## 2026-10-27 · Tibetan correction: do error profiles in the prompt help, and can a diff-hunk QA replace the line-count refusal? (#6560, #6740)

**Status: DONE (results below).** Pre-registered in 0afde11a8 (amended in f75925f70) before any judge was run on any arm's output. The
results section is added after the run. Job `tib-corr-profiles-6560`. Eval only: no page was written.

## Decision it changes

What the Yigdzin → agy Gemini 3.8 Flash-low correction lane (#6740, job `tib-flash-correct-vol1-6740`) uses next:
- the current prompt, a prompt with error profiles, or neither;
- with or without a per-hunk leaf check (diff QA) in place of the blanket line-count refusal.

Today the lane refuses every correction that changes the number of text lines. That blocks a dropped line (brGyad stong
p.233, a real loss) and a removed Yigdzin duplicate (Neyphug p.128 and p.131, correct by eye) alike.

## Arms (Stage 1)

The corrector is the same in every arm: `agy` `gemini-3.8-flash-low`, one page a call, through
`scripts/eval/run-cli-arm.py --kind ocr --parallel 2`, with `CANDIDATE_READS=off`. $0.
- **A**: `corr-prompt.txt`, unchanged. The runner appends its marker sentence once more after the prompt, as in every
  earlier #6560 eval arm. That is the same in all three arms.
- **B**: A plus a **reader profile** of Yigdzin: `profiles-diffqa/profiles/reader.yigdzin-v1.tibetan.json`.
- **C**: B plus a **corrector profile** of Flash: `profiles-diffqa/profiles/corrector.gemini-3.8-flash-low.tibetan.json`.

Each profile is a data file, keyed by the reader or corrector model and the script. `arms.mjs` loads it, so another
script or OCR system can get its own file later. The profiles were written from measured counts before any arm ran.
- `profile-counts.py` counted every span a tiled span judge decided in four audits, 128 pages in all: #7477 (40),
  #7479 Neyphug (40), #7479 wave 2 (38) and #7483 router-30 (10).
- The route-judge whole-page defect rates on Yigdzin come from `route-judge-6740/results/*/ocr-defect-observations.jsonl`.
- The duplicate-line findings come from #7483.
- Counts of draft errors that Flash fixed: another word 326, mantra 179, vowel 144, tsheg 141, particle 50, line 6,
  ya-btags 4.
- Counts of errors Flash introduced: another word 76, mantra 42, tsheg 40, particle 16, vowel 8, plus whole lines
  dropped (#7477, brGyad p.233).

## Test set: DIAGNOSTIC, not a random sample of the lane

Built by `build-set.mjs`; the ids are in `results/.../profiles-diffqa-6560/sample.json`. There are 72 pages, each with
its Yigdzin draft resolved from `pages` or `page_revisions`:
- **g7477**, 6 pages: the #7477 gate's pooled-worse pages.
- **g7479**, 10 pages: the Neyphug gate's worse pages.
- **g7483**, 4 pages: router-30 pages with a severe error introduced.
- **brgyad**, 29 pages: every brGyad stong Ka Flash read in R2 (398 reads) whose text-line count differs from its draft.
  The brief said 32. 29 is what the kept reads give with tag lines not counted.
- **lines**, 3 pages: Neyphug p.128, p.131 and p.303.
- **wave2**, 20 pages: one per wave-2 book, seeded.

There are also **10 planted drafts**: `prep.py --reuse-plants`, 30 planted syllables on the 30-folio set's anchor
folios. These are used for the catch rate only and are not judged.

**Leak, stated before the run.** The profiles quote examples from the audits that also chose g7477, g7479 and g7483
(20 pages), for example དབང→དགྲ. Results are therefore also reported per group. brgyad, lines and wave2 (52 pages) are
the groups whose errors the profiles did not see as examples, although some wave2 pages were in the wave-2 audit.

## Judges (blind to arm, sealed Opus, Read only)

`profiles-diffqa/judge.mjs`, run through `replicate-6547/run-claude-arm.py --model opus`.
1. **Tiled span judge with severity.** This is leafcheck's `audit-req --severity` and `tiles-req`, word for word.
   - Every syllable hunk of the arm's output against the draft is one item, the two readings in random order, with
     2 known-answer controls per page, the frame and 4 full-resolution tiles.
   - A page that changes more than 25% of the draft's syllables is not span-judged. Only the whole-page judge reads
     it, and for the arm's own score it counts as worse with a severe error introduced, because the lane refuses it.
2. **Confirm judge** (leafcheck `confirm-req`). A fresh call takes every severe draft-win, and also every line-level
   hunk (one side has 6 or more syllables and the sides differ by 4 or more) whatever the first judge said.
3. **Whole-page judge** (route-judge `judgePrompt`, leafcheck `page-req`). It reads the draft and each distinct text
   once, each on its own.

A hunk is judged once per page. Its verdict is reused by every text that keeps it: the arms that wrote the same hunk,
the +qa texts and the +lane texts. The whole-page judge reads every distinct text.

## Stage 2: diff-hunk QA (on A, B and C)

- **Hunks.** These are syllable alignment hunks from `tibetan-yatags-guard.mjs` `diffSyllables`. A whole added or
  removed line is one hunk. Identical hunks (same draft run, same new syllables, same page) from different arms are
  one call.
- **One sealed Opus call per hunk.** The call gets:
  - the frame, plus a full-resolution band of the frame around the hunk's line;
  - the READOFF wording, with the two readings in random order;
  - one known-answer control item.
  - For a removed passage (a line-level hunk that removes syllables), the judge is also asked how many times the leaf
    shows the passage.
- **Keep or revert.**
  - A hunk is kept only where the judge saw the correction's reading. Revert, unclear, other or no answer puts the
    draft back.
  - For a removed passage, the count decides when it is given: keep the removal if the leaf shows the passage fewer
    times than the draft has it (copies found by syllable alignment at 60% or more identity).
- **Hunks that do not change syllables.** QA cannot revert a pure line-break change (two lines merged with every
  syllable kept). It stays in the +qa text.

**Amendment, 2026-10-27, before any judge was run.** Arm A's outputs came back with 1,154 hunks on 62 pages
(median about 20 a page; brGyad and wave-2 pages are corrected heavily). One call per hunk would be about 1,800 Opus
calls. The QA therefore makes **one sealed call per page line that has hunks**:
- the items are that line's distinct hunks from A, B and C, each with its two readings in random order, plus one
  known-answer control;
- **a removed passage still gets a call of its own**, with the count question;
- the band tile, the keep/revert rule and the dedupe are unchanged.

Nothing about the judges, the measures or the decision rule changed.

## Baseline: the lane as it runs now (+lane)

- A correction that changes the text-line count is refused.
- The 25% cap applies.
- The Latin-letter guard applies.
- Ya-btags changes go back to the draft. This is the guard with no leaf check, which is the same as Opus answering
  unclear.
- **The Derge guard is not reproduced** (there is no e-text index on this box). The baseline is therefore slightly more
  permissive than the lane.

## Measures (per variant: A, B, C, each plus qa and plus lane)

- **better / same / worse**, pooled. This is leafcheck's `gate` pooling of the span verdict (more leaf-shows-draft
  spans than leaf-shows-correction spans means worse) and the whole-page verdict (fidelity down, accept lost or a
  wrong_text defect added means worse).
- **Severe error introduced on a page.** Either a severe span where both the span judge and the confirm judge saw the
  draft on the leaf, or the whole-page judge finding more wrong_text defects in the text than in the draft, or one of a
  new class (leafcheck `severity-gate`). It is reported per 10 pages.
- **Plant catch rate.** A planted syllable is caught if the output does not have it at the aligned position
  (`score.py`'s survival rule). Restored to the original is also reported.
- **Line-count outcomes,** on every page whose text-line count changed:
  - **right**: every removed passage was seen as absent by both the span judge and the confirm judge, and the
    whole-page judge adds no O5 omission;
  - **loss**: both judges saw the passage on the leaf, or the whole-page judge adds an O5;
  - **unclear** otherwise; and line-break-only changes are counted on their own.
- **Anchors:** Neyphug p.128 and p.131 (a removal is right, by eye) and brGyad p.233 (a merge lost a line in the lane's
  read).
- **QA cost:** Opus calls and seconds, cost_usd_equiv as the CLI reports it, and hunks per page.

## Decision rule (fixed before any judge output)

Recommend the **cheapest** variant that passes all four:
1. **Derek's severity rule:** a severe error is introduced on fewer than 2 of 10 pages (under 20% of the 72).
2. **better ≥ 3 × worse**, pooled.
3. **Plant catch rate ≥ arm A's** (A without QA).
4. **Line removals:** p.128 and p.131 come out "right", and no page in the set is a "loss".

- **Cheapest order:** A, B, C, then A+qa, B+qa, C+qa. QA adds Opus calls, and a profile adds only prompt length.
- **The +lane variants** are the comparison. They cannot pass rule 4 by construction, because they refuse every
  line-count change.
- **If none passes,** this file says so, and names which rule each variant fails.
- **What a pass means.** The set was chosen from pages that went wrong before. A pass here is evidence for what to put
  through the lane's own gate on a fresh volume. It is not a write decision.

## Known weaknesses, stated before the run

- **The QA judge and the span judge are both Opus reading the same leaf.** A +qa text keeps exactly the hunks one Opus
  call saw as right, so its span-judge score is inflated by their agreement. The whole-page judge is the less
  correlated check on +qa, and the per-variant whole-page counts are reported beside the pooled ones.
- **The A arm is re-run.** Its outputs are not the lane's stored reads. The same prompt gives a different read on a
  re-run, so the g7477, g7479 and g7483 pages may not repeat their earlier failures.
- **This box's Claude account meter is empty** (`/root/.claude-limits/latest.json` has no limits for
  derek@playpowerlabs.com). The 89% weekly stop can only be honoured as "stop at the first limit reply".
- `/root/agy-quota/status.json` lives on main and is not readable from this box. agy errors stop the runner (exit 3).

## Results (2026-10-27)

**No variant passes the pre-registered rule.** Every one fails at least one of the four rules, so none is recommended.
On this diagnostic set, the full corrector-profile prompt (C) is the clearest improvement over the current prompt. The
diff-hunk QA as built is not a drop-in replacement for the line-count refusal. The results are below.

- **Calls:** agy Flash-low 248 (82 per arm, plus 2 re-reads of replies cut before `<<<END>>>` in C; $0).
- **Opus:** 1,484 sealed calls on this box's subscription: span 191, confirm 110, whole page 446, QA 737. That is
  $177 at API-equivalent prices; nothing was billed. No limit reply was received.
- **Judge controls:** span 366/382 (96%), confirm 208/220 (95%), QA 596 right / 3 wrong / 138 unclear. The QA's
  control is drawn anywhere on the page, so it often falls outside the band tile; hence the unclears.
- **Scores:** `results/.../profiles-diffqa-6560/score.json.gz` and `score.txt`.

### The table (72 pages; plants: 30 planted syllables on 10 folios)

| variant | better / same / worse (pooled) | pages with a severe error introduced | per 10 | plants caught | line-count changes: right / loss / unclear / breaks only | p.128 · p.131 · p.233 | rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** current prompt | 45 / 12 / 15 | 31 | 4.3 | 29/30 | 7 / 2 / 1 / 12 | right · right · kept | fails 1, 4 |
| **B** + reader profile | 49 / 14 / 9 | 33 | 4.6 | 27/30 | 6 / 0 / 5 / 11 | right · right · kept | fails 1, 3 |
| **C** + reader + corrector profile | 50 / 7 / 15 | 31 | 4.3 | **30/30** | 6 / 2 / 2 / 13 | unclear · right · +1 line, unclear | fails 1, 4 |
| A + lane guards (today) | 29 / 32 / 11 | 18 | 2.5 | 29/30 | refused | kept · kept · kept | fails 1, 2, 4 |
| B + lane guards | 31 / 35 / 6 | 20 | 2.8 | 27/30 | refused | kept · kept · kept | fails 1, 3, 4 |
| C + lane guards | 30 / 31 / 11 | 19 | 2.6 | 27/30 | refused | kept · kept · kept | fails 1, 2, 3, 4 |
| A + diff QA | 50 / 19 / 3 | 18 | 2.5 | 27/30 | 7 / 0 / 1 / 13 | right · right · kept | fails 1, 3 |
| **B + diff QA** | **52 / 19 / 1** | **13** | **1.8** | 25/30 | 6 / 2 / 0 / 10 | **kept** · right · kept | fails 3, 4 |
| C + diff QA | 51 / 16 / 5 | 17 | 2.4 | 27/30 | 5 / 2 / 3 / 12 | unclear · loss · +1, unclear | fails 1, 3, 4 |

Rules: (1) severe on fewer than 2 of 10 pages, (2) better ≥ 3 × worse, (3) plants ≥ A's 29/30, (4) p.128 and p.131
right and no loss.

**B + diff QA passes the severity rule (13/72) and better ≥ 3 × worse.** It fails the other two:
- it catches 25/30 plants, against A's 29;
- the QA put Yigdzin's duplicated line back on p.128 (8 lines again where the leaf has 7), and 2 line changes are
  losses.

### 1. Do the profiles help? They change WHICH errors Flash makes, not how many pages go wrong

Spans the leaf contradicts (the span judge saw the draft; 60 pages paired, not over the 25% cap):

| arm | errors introduced (spans) | mantra / Sanskrit | tsheg inside a cluster, split, join | another word | errors fixed (spans) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 166 | 39 | 36 | 67 | 966 |
| B | 136 | 37 | **6** | 70 | 1,030 |
| C | **116** | **4** | 8 | 74 | 1,042 |

- **C against A:** 65 fewer introduced spans, 95% interval [−143, −3] (bootstrap over pages). Most of the drop is on a
  few pages: 22 pages have fewer, 18 have more.
- **The reader profile alone (B) stops the tsheg insertions.** It does not stop mantra normalisation.
- **The corrector profile (C) stops mantra normalisation.** C against B on mantra: −32, [−78, −1].
- **Neither profile reduces word substitutions** (O6, about 70 spans in every arm), and those are what the severity
  rule mostly counts.
- **The profiles cost no fixes:** fixed spans went up from 966 to 1,042. C caught all 30 plants.
- **At page level:** worse pages were 15 / 9 / 15 for A / B / C, and pages with a severe error introduced were
  31 / 33 / 31. None of the three is under the bar.

### 2. Diff-hunk QA: it removes most confirmed severe spans, at about 8 Opus calls a page, but it is not a line-count judge

- **Confirmed severe spans** (both span judges saw the draft) fall from 22 pages to 5–7, and pooled worse falls from
  15 / 9 / 15 to 3 / 1 / 5.
- **The whole-page judge** still flags 10–14 pages in every +qa variant: more wrong_text defects than the draft, or a
  new class of one. Its "worse" verdicts stay at 4–5.
- **It costs right fixes.** Unclear means revert, so plants caught drop by 2 (A, B) or 3 (C), and pooled "better"
  barely moves.
- **Removed passages: the QA is unreliable at hunk granularity.** The syllable alignment splits a removed Yigdzin
  duplicate into fragments (p.128 had 8 "removal" hunks). The judge's answers and counts on the fragments disagree
  with each other. A partial revert can leave a hybrid line: on p.131, C + qa, the whole-page judge then called a
  restored fragment a near-copy, and the line outcome became a loss.
  - The by-eye truth on p.131 (job tib-opus-translate-6948) is 7 lines, with the anger sentence written twice on the
    leaf.
- **Cost, measured:**
  - 737 calls for 1,890 distinct hunks on 78 pages (three arms pooled), 3.3 hours of call time, $52.6 at API-equivalent
    prices.
  - For one arm alone: about 8 calls a page (A 633 calls on 82 pages), a median of 17 hunks a page, about $0.57 a page
    at API-equivalent prices.
  - On a 500-page volume that is about 4,000 Opus calls.

### 3. The lane's current guards (+lane) do not meet the bar either

On these pages, A + lane is 29 / 32 / 11 with 18 severe pages (2.5 per 10).
- The blanket line-count refusal sends 26 of the 72 pages back to the draft.
- It keeps the Yigdzin duplicate on p.128 and p.131.
- It does not stop word substitutions on the pages it passes.
- The Derge guard is not in this baseline (see above), so the real lane may be a little better.

### Where the severity count comes from (one caution)

- The whole-page judge's "a wrong_text defect of a new class" (leafcheck severity-gate (b)) raises 12–13 of the raw
  arms' 31–33 severe pages, and 10–14 of the +qa variants' 13–18. That is most of the +qa flags, often on pages the
  same judge scores better.
- The judge was not re-run on identical texts, so its noise floor is not measured.
- brGyad stong Ka, the heavily corrected volume, carries 16–20 of its 29 pages' severe flags in the raw arms. Wave-2
  pages carry 3–7 of 20.

### Decision

- **None passes the pre-registered rule.** Nothing here is a write decision.
- **What the evidence supports, for the lane's next gate** (each still needs its own pre-registered gate on a fresh
  volume):
  1. **Use profile C in the correction prompt.** It is free, keeps every fix, catches all plants, and removes the
     measured mantra and tsheg normalisation.
  2. **Keep the line-count refusal.** A per-hunk QA cannot tell a removed duplicate from a lost line. The next try
     should be a **line-level** check: one call per changed line, asking how many times the leaf shows the line. It
     should not use syllable hunks. Its known-answer controls should come from the same band.
  3. **Word substitutions (O6) are what remains.** Neither profile reaches them. The diff QA's leaf check removes most
     confirmed severe spans (22 pages → 5–7), at about 8 Opus calls a page.

### Deviations, all taken before scoring

- **QA calls per page line, not per hunk** (amendment f75925f70). Arm A came back with 1,154 hunks on 62 pages.
- **The count question decides only for a pure removal** (nothing in its place). For a long run replaced by a short
  one, "how often is this passage on the leaf" does not say which reading is right. This was seen on the first QA
  replies, before any scoring.
- **Arm C's 2 replies cut before `<<<END>>>` were read once more**, as `cli-ocr.mjs` does.
- **brGyad:** 29 reads change the line count, not the brief's 32 (R2 holds 398 reads; tag lines are not counted).
- **The Derge guard is not in +lane.** This box's Claude meter has no row for its account, so the 89% weekly stop
  could only be "stop on a limit reply". None came.

## 2026-10-27 · Siku pilot pages against Kanripo: OCR accuracy and are the images the right leaves? (#7503)

PRIOR ART: `scripts/eval/zh-skqs-5568-kanripo.mjs` (the #5568 leaf rule and its `drift` mode, imported),
`scripts/eval/ground-truth-5935/lib.mjs` (`bodyCer`), `scripts/eval/paddle-table-6388/` (align + CER, 30 pages).
Scripts and results: `scripts/eval/siku-kanripo-7503/` (README there).

**Question (Derek, 2026-10-27):** "OCR against Kanripo ... and yes, if the images are right." The pilot's 20 books
(PR #7543 `draw.json`, 2,926 pages) are CADAL scans of the Wenyuan Ge Siku Quanshu, and Kanripo transcribes that
edition (WYG witness). Every page can be checked with no model. $0, no model calls, read-only on Mongo.

### 1. Books → Kanripo
- **18 of 20 books** have a WYG branch. On 11 of them, the repo's `Readme.org` names the witness as `四庫全書・文淵閣`.
- **皇極經世書解 (KR3g0010):** there is no such repository in the kanripo org (404). Its 102 pilot pages are unchecked.
- **山堂肆考 vol 86 (KR3k0052, juan 193–194):** the repo stops at juan 56 (58 files), so its 142 pages are unchecked.
  The other 山堂肆考 volume (juan 12–14) is covered.
- **Licence.** None of the 18 repos has a licence field, a LICENSE file or a licence line in its Readme. The org
  profile says "Licensed as CC BY SA 4.0". Per-book rows, with the branch commit sha, are in `results/books.json`.
