## 2026-10-27 · A page-break drift guard for unpunctuated Chinese (#7503, job caseless-drift-7503)

PRIOR ART: `scripts/lib/block-drift.mjs` (#5021) is the guard; it made no claim on caseless scripts, because its
source test is a lowercase opening letter. Extended there, not beside it. The calibration set is #7518
(`2026-10-27-agy-pages-per-call-siku-7503.md`, `scripts/eval/agy-per-call-7503/`).

**Question.** Inside an agy block read of Siku pages, the model finishes the sentence that runs over a page break on
page N and opens N+1 at the next sentence (#7518: 2 of 26 in-block breaks at 2/call, 3 of 39 at 4/call). Can a rule
read from the text we hold catch that in Chinese, and stay quiet where no move can happen?

**The rule** (`detectCaselessDrift`). The English is cased, so the translation half of #5021 stands. The source half
is read from the SKQS column layout, since the OCR has no punctuation:
1. **The source runs over.** Page N's last prose column is full (within one character of the page's 75th-percentile
   column) and does not end on a final particle (也矣焉哉乎歟耶耳).
2. **N+1 opens no new entry.** No claim if N+1's source opens with 正義/案/按/注/疏/存疑, has 曰 within its first five
   characters (a speaker), or has a final particle on its first or second character.
3. **English N closes and English N+1 opens fresh.** N ends on sentence-final punctuation and N+1 opens on a capital
   or digit. Alternatively N ends on `;`, a list item closed on N, and N+1 may then open lowercase.
4. **Page N carries more English per source character than N+1** (`caselessShift > 0`). The clause has to have gone
   somewhere.

Rules 2 and the `;` branch were added after reading the misses and false flags, so the calibration numbers are
in-sample. The held-out floor below was not used to fit anything, except that its first 16 Flash-low flags were read
by eye (they gave rule 2).

### Calibration: #7518's reads (`calibrate.mjs`, `results.json`)

| set | flagged |
|---|---|
| the 5 by-eye moves | **5/5** |
| 1/call breaks (A1 + A1b), read as if they were blocks | **3/90 (3.3%)** |
| in-block breaks with no known move (B2 + C4) | 2/60 |
| C4 (4/call) in-block breaks, all | 3/39, the 3 known moves |

The 3 one-per-call flags: 大學衍義補 p.123 (`;` branch), 易通變 p.83 (A1b mistranslated 二分 as "equinoxes" and opened
fresh), 春明夢餘錄 p.70 (A1b re-opened 于厥後 with a capital). The 2 block flags: B2 天原發微 56→57, which finished
伏|羲來 on p.56 (two characters of a split word), and B2 御定佩文韻府 11→12.

The weakest catch is B2 論語商 37→38, with a shift of 0.02. B2 moved 10 characters and opened the next sentence fresh.
Any shift threshold above 0.02 loses it.

### Held-out floor: production Chinese translations (`floor.mjs`, `floor.json`)

About 400 sampled Chinese books, minus #7518's 15. Pairs are consecutive pages translated by the same call site, with
N+1's OCR in Han script. A one-page-per-call lane cannot move a clause it never saw, so its rate is the floor: false
flags plus words the reader finished across the break (`不可以及|遠` → "cannot reach far.").

| lane (call site, model) | pages per call | breaks | flagged |
|---|---|---|---|
| cli-translate.mjs, claude-opus-5-5 | 1 | 3,870 | **3.6%** |
| cli-translate.mjs, gemini-3.8-flash-low | 1 | 592 | **4.1%** |
| stale-retranslate-6567.mjs, gemini-3.8-flash-low | 1 | 6,897 | **6.3%** |
| translate-batch-chained.mjs, gemini-3-flash-preview | block | 23,534 | 9.4% |
| translate-batch-chained.mjs, gemini-3.1-flash-lite | block | 2,519 | 8.1% |

Raising the shift threshold to 0.03 brings the 6.3% lane to 4.5% and loses the B2 論語商 catch (sweep on an earlier
sample: 0.015 gives 5.1%, 0.05 gives 3.6%, 0.1 gives 2.2%). The shipped threshold is 0.

**Reading.**
- The block Batch lanes sit 3–5 points above the one-per-call floor. So roughly 3–5% of in-block breaks in Chinese
  English already served likely carry a clause a page early. That is the #5021 defect in the paid lanes, which this PR
  does not switch on.
- **Cost of a hit**: both pages are read again alone, never a wrong text. At 4/call on #7518's reads, 3 flags in 39
  breaks re-read 6 of 60 pages, taking the quota index from about 0.55 to about 0.65 of 1/call.

**Caveats.**
- n = 5 positives. The rule is fitted on them.
- The held-out floor counts word completions as flags, so it bounds the false-positive rate from above, not exactly.
- The held-out sample is a Mongo `$sample`, so it is not seeded. Two pulls gave 5.8% and 6.3% on the stale-retranslate
  lane.
- Han only. Tibetan (caseless, but punctuated by shad) has no calibration set and still makes no claim.

Files in `scripts/eval/caseless-drift-7503/`:
- `calibrate.mjs`, `results.json`
- `floor.mjs`, `floor.json`
- `ocr.json`: the OCR of #7518's pages, a Mongo snapshot from 2026-10-27

Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/block-drift/caseless-boundaries.json`. Read only, nothing written.

## 2026-10-27 · Does one per-book brief make page translations better? (#7499 row 6)

PRIOR ART: `2026-10-26-translation-prompt-v19-cognates-4741.md` (a general cognate rule failed; "a per-book glossary,
not a general rule"), `2026-10-16-seam-prompt-candidate-6742.md` (the CLI request reproduced call for call, the join
judge and the A-vs-A floor reused here), #4741 (the glossary proposal, from the curated vocabulary rather than per book).

**Who this is for.** Derek and the router. Today every page is translated with the prompt and the previous page's
English. The question was whether to build a step that writes ONE brief per book and gives it to every page call.

**Design** (preregistered and committed with the 10 briefs before any arm ran: `scripts/eval/PREREGISTRATION-book-brief-7499.md`).
- **Books:** a seeded draw (7499) from the xlref reference books: 3 Latin print (Erasmus *Enchiridion*, Bacon *Novum
  Organum*, Cicero *De officiis*), 2 vernacular (*Theologia deutsch*, Cabeza de Vaca *Naufragios*), 2 Greek (Burnet's
  Plato, *Republic* IX; the Didot Septuagint with its facing Latin), 1 Arabic (*al-Rawḍ al-ʿāṭir*), 2 Chinese with
  printed commentary (莊子旁注; Fazang's 大乘起信論義記). No live Sanskrit book with a printed commentary passed, so
  both commentary books are Chinese. Each book contributed 12 consecutive pages containing its reference page.
- **Brief:** written once per book by Opus (`claude -p`) from the metadata, the source-work line and the OCR of the first
  20 translatable pages *outside* the window. 295–393 words: the work, a 30-term glossary, layout notes, names. The
  briefs are in `results/book-brief-7499/briefs/`.
- **Arms:** A = v13 exactly as production composes it (Flash: `cli-translate` one page per call through agy; Opus:
  `claude-translate` blocks of up to 10). B = A plus the brief, placed where `--instructions-file` puts a line, under a header
  saying it describes the book and must not be added to a page. A2 = A again on 3 seeded books (the floor). Nothing was
  written to any page, R2 or the lane registry.
- **Judges** (all blind Opus, both orders in separate calls): a whole-page fidelity judge with omission, added and
  mistranslation flags; the #6742 join judge on 110 in-window joins; a brief-invention checker run on A pages too (A
  never saw the brief, so its flag rate is the checker's false-alarm floor); and the `translation-vs-reference` judge on
  the 10 reference pages. Term renderings were quoted by a blind extractor and scored mechanically.

**Result.**

| measure | A | B | B − A (95% CI) | A2 − A floor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| term consistency, modal share (48 terms on ≥ 2 pages) | 80.4% | 84.7% | **+4.3 (−8.4, +17.8)** | −19.4 (−66.7, +8.3), 3 books |
| renderings equal to the brief's | 77.1% | 90.3% | +13.2 | — |
| page judge, 120 pages: wins in both orders | 19 | 24 | L − W **−4.2 (−17.5, +7.5)** | A2 lost 3–8: +13.9 (0, +33.3) |
| omission pages (flagged in both orders) | 7.5% | 8.3% | +0.8 (−5.8, +8.3) | +2.8 (0, +8.3) |
| added-content pages | 13.3% | 3.3% | **−10.0 (−18.3, −3.3)** | +2.8 (−8.3, +16.7) |
| mistranslation pages | 8.3% | 10.0% | +1.7 (−1.7, +5.8) | +2.8 (0, +8.3) |
| defective joins per 100 (110 joins) | 16.4 | 17.3 | +0.9 (−13.6, +11.8) | +18.2 (0, +36.4) |
| pages the brief-invention checker flagged | 27.5% | 20.8% | −6.7 (−26.7, +7.5) | — |
| vs published reference, 10 pages (gate FAILED; forced) | 4.55 | 4.45 | 3 wins each, 4 ties | — |

- **Judge floors:** 10 of 10 identical page pairs and 40 of 40 identical join pairs were called tie.
- **Rule output: DON'T.** Consistency Δ +4.3 is below +5 and inside the A2 − A interval. The fidelity guard did not clear
  its +5 bound either (upper end +7.5), though the point estimate favours B.
- **Where consistency moved:** almost all of it came from one book. On 莊子旁注, A rendered 道 as both "dao" and "Way" and 神
  four ways, and B fixed both (41.7 → 93.8%). On the Latin and German books, A was already 68–95% consistent. Glossary
  coverage was thin: 48 of the 303 glossary terms recur on 2 or more window pages, because the brief comes from the
  book's opening and a window 270 pages in (the *Republic*) is in another dialogue. The sensitivity that strips
  possessives ("your father" vs "father"), added after reading the data and not registered, gives Δ +3.0 (−8.8, +14.9).
- **Brief invention: none found.** I read all 25 flagged B pages. None carries a fact that only the brief could have
  supplied. The flags are general-knowledge notes of the kind A writes more often (A was flagged on 33 pages),
  glossary renderings of terms the page does carry, and the Plato apparatus carried as the brief's layout note asked.
- **The layout notes are the hazard.** The brief writer was told not to summarise; it was not told not to legislate.
  The Septuagint brief said "translate the Greek base text, and use the Latin version only as an aid", and Flash B
  dropped the printed Latin column on pp. 287, 290 and 293 (A on none, A2 on one). The Fazang brief said "omit the
  running heads and folio numbers", and B dropped them on pp. 68 and 76. Five of Flash B's nine omission pages are
  omissions the brief ordered; the page judge caught all of them in both orders.
- **By engine** (exploratory, not registered; A2 − A on these books swings 13.9 points): on Opus, B won 14–4 with
  omission pages 10 → 1.7%; on Flash, B lost 10–15 with omission pages 5 → 15%, mostly the ordered drops above.
  Added content fell on both engines (Opus 8.3 → 0, Flash 18.3 → 6.7). The brief and its header line ("never add
  anything the page does not carry") were given together, so this run cannot say which of the two did it.
- **Reference judge:** the gate failed. j1 scored a wrong-page control 5/5 on *Naufragios* p. 30. The planted negation on
  莊子旁注 p. 100 landed inside a sentence both arms already mistranslated: both judges located it but scored it level with
  the base. Results are kept as `--force` (`ref-results.json`, `gate.forced: true`) and carry no weight here.

**Read by eye, with the image open** (5 pages):
- [Septuagint p. 287](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/6952e4b477f38f6761bc7d4c?page=287): the image has Deut. 18:9–19:5
  in facing Greek and Latin columns. A renders both. B renders only the Greek: a real omission, caused by the brief.
- [Fazang p. 68](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/6a3c6191879008ba7e15f0b2?page=68): the two arms are nearly identical
  and both are faithful. B bolds the root-text lemma, as its layout note says, and drops the fore-edge title
  起信論義記卷四 / 五, as its layout note ordered.
- [Plato p. 367](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/699376d2b0a84a5763961a97?page=367) (*Republic* 571c–572b): the body is
  faithful in both. B keeps the apparatus readings in Greek with the Latin translated ("sed κα in ras." → "but κα in
  erasure"). A turned the variant readings into English ("into rages] into rage"), which loses what each witness reads.
  Here the brief made the page better.
- [*Naufragios* p. 25](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/69ea0f5913a685002bb8deaf?page=25): both are faithful.
  "Isle of Misfortune" is B's gloss of the printed *Mal Hado*, not an invention. A's note adds an identification near
  Galveston that the page does not carry.
- [莊子旁注 p. 100](https://sourcelibrary.org/book/69e72c75a409200ea79f4976?page=100) (the reference page): for
  孰協唐許…心有睫, B gives "How far this falls short of Tang and Xu! … the mind has eyelashes", close to the source. A
  makes it an exclamation and invents a person, "Xie", from 協.

**What it means.**
- A brief is not worth a pipeline step for **consistency**. Production is already ~80% consistent on the terms that
  recur within a dozen pages, and the brief's measurable gain is smaller than the noise between two runs of the same
  prompt. The drift #4741 and #7169 document (a running head rendered ~28 ways over 33 pages) spans hundreds of pages.
  A 12-page window cannot see that scale, and a brief written from the opening pages does not cover a window deep
  into the book.
- A brief carries **policy** as well as vocabulary, and the model obeys it. A writer that may say "omit" will sometimes
  say it about content a reader needs. If a brief is ever built, its writer must describe the layout and never
  prescribe dropping anything, and the omission guard must run on the brief arm.
- The two exploratory signals are each worth one registered test: added content fell by ~10 points on both engines,
  and Opus with the brief won 14–4. Both come with the same confound, that the header's no-additions line came
  bundled with the brief.

**Replicated?** No. One run, 10 books.

**Spend.** $0 billed. agy (subscription): 144 Flash page calls, no lockout. Claude CLI (this box's subscription,
weekly meter 0 → 4%): 10 briefs, 36 Opus translation calls, 23 extractions, 69 page-judge, 34 join-judge and 60
brief-invention calls (≈ $41 list-equivalent), plus 6 reference-judge subagents.

**Artifact.** `scripts/eval/results/book-brief-7499/`: `report.json` (every measure and the rule output),
`draw.json`, `briefs/`, `reads.jsonl.gz` (all 276 reads), the judges' raw verdicts, `ref-results.json`.
Harness: `scripts/eval/book-brief-7499/{select,run}.mjs`.

## 2026-10-27 · Applied under Derek's 23:15Z rule, then diff-QA

**The rule.** Write a page when it passes the automatic guards and does not lower Derge identity by more than 0.01 (where
the draft has a parallel, identity ≥ 0.85). An audited page that introduced a severe error keeps Yigdzin. The re-score
(`pass/rescore.mjs`): SEVERE = line-level, negation or mantra; a page passes with net ≥ 0 and no severe error introduced.
This gate passed 35/38 pages.

**Reads.** 8,278 pages, by agy Flash-low on main ($0). Reads came back through R2.

**Derge placement.** 15 sample pages per volume against all of P000001, then the whole volume against those Derge volumes
± 1. Derge v103's Pagination layer has a single entry, which makes one enormous window, so it is left out.

**Written: 7,287 pages** in 19 volumes, through `writePageText` (runs: `results/.../pass-gate-wave2-6740/runs.json`; per
volume: `written-by-volume.md`).

| | pages |
|---|---|
| refused: line count changed | 349 |
| refused: 25% cap | 94 |
| refused: ya-btags, no leaf check | 46 |
| refused: adds Latin letters | 5 |

The **line-count guard** was added after the wave-A by-eye check. On Thadrak brGyad stong p.233, Flash merged two lines of
the upper leaf (the draft had 7, Flash wrote 6). A dropped line and a removed invented line cannot be told apart without
the image, so the draft stays. Moving or adding the leaf-break marker does not count as a line change.

**Restores (run `revert-lines-6740`):** brGyad p.233 and p.289, gZungs 'dus p.260 (a dropped negation, from the rolling
audit) and Neyphug p.303. Neyphug p.131 was restored and then put back on the Flash text (run `unrevert-lines-6740`): the
scribe repeats that sentence, as checked by eye by tib-opus-translate-6948.

**Rolling audit:** 10 seeded written pages, judge B. 9/10 pass; 90 errors fixed, 8 introduced, 1 severe introduced
(restored). Controls 19/20.

### Diff-QA (Derek 2026-10-27 05:10Z)
`pass/diffqa.mjs` diffs each written page against its Yigdzin draft and classifies every changed span.
- **LOW** (auto-accepted): tsheg/merge only, a particle swapped within its class, or a one-letter fix to a Derge dictionary word.
- **RISKY**: everything else; negation, number, mantra, added/dropped and > 8 syllables always are.
- **Calibration** on 680 spans already judged: LOW is right on 94% of decided spans, RISKY on 86%. The four known severe
  introductions of the router-30 reads all classify RISKY.
- **RISKY spans** go to the leaf: `leafcheck audit-req --pages --spans`, judge B, 2 controls a page. A span the leaf does not
  show as corrected is put back to the draft (`diffqa.mjs merge`, `write`; runs `diffqa-6740-*`).
- **Pilot, 40 pages:** 155/210 risky spans confirmed (74%), 38 show the draft. 55 spans were put back on 24 pages.
- **Tranche 1** covers the 3,757 + 634 written pages that carry a severe-type risky span; results follow in #6740.

## 2026-10-27 · How many 3.8 Flash low calls does the agy Gemini quota hold in a week? (#6740)

PRIOR ART: `scripts/eval/estimator/ocr/meter_quota_share.py` (the earlier figure, 229K calls per 30 days, from main's
`/root/agy-quota/calls.csv` and the call counts before each 429). It did not fit: that meter sees only main's calls,
and its stretch ran ~10K Argon-high calls, which cost several Flash calls each, so a "call" was not one unit.

**What the CLI says about its own quota.** `agy -p "/quota" --output-format json` (also `/usage`) spends no tokens and
returns, per model group, `remaining_fraction` and `reset_time` for a weekly and a 5-hour bucket. Its description:
"Within each group, models share a weekly limit and a 5-hour limit. Quota is consumed proportionally to the cost of the
tokens." Groups: *Gemini Models* (Gemini Flash, Gemini Pro; Argon is in it) and *Claude and GPT models*. The weekly
window is fixed, not rolling: it reset at 2026-10-30T21:59:44Z, seven days after the 10-19 lockout ended
(10-23T21:59:44Z).

**Design.** Read the weekly fraction once (2026-10-27T08:21Z: 0.7105, so 0.2895 used) and count every print-mode call
since the window opened, by model, from the CLI logs on all four boxes and the Mac (`Print mode: starting ...
model="..."` lines in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log`).

| where | 3.8 Flash low | 3.8 Flash high / medium | Argon high / medium |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 24,997 | 114 / 0 | 52 / 25 |
| cloudlayer | 3,597 | 158 / 1 | 0 |
| gex45 | 1,097 | 28 / 0 | 0 |
| l7a | 8 | 0 | 8 / 0 |
| Mac | 18 | 0 | 0 |
| **all** | **29,717** | **301** | **85** |

**Result.** 0.2895 / 30,018 Flash calls = **9.6e-6 of a week per Flash-low call, ~104K calls a week**. That is
2.25e-6 of a 30-day allowance, against the 4.36e-6 the router used. The 85 Argon calls are ignored; even at 10x a Flash
call they would be ~3% of the use. At $200 a month that is **~$0.45 per 1,000 Flash-low pages** (one page a call),
against $1.48 measured for Flash-Lite Batch.

**Cross-check, and why the short reading is not used.** A 10-minute reading the same morning (08:21 to 08:31Z, the
fraction sampled every 30 s, 200 other-box calls plus 11 test calls on the Mac): a drop of 0.0033, ~1.5e-5 a call,
~66K a week. But the weekly fraction stood still for 5 minutes under ~100 calls, then fell in jumps, and once went
back *up* (0.70716 -> 0.70726): the readings come from replicas that are not in step. Readings hours or days apart
are the usable ones.

**Not measured, on purpose.** Argon's cost per call: Derek stopped the test before its Argon blocks (2026-10-27). No
Argon call was made by this test.

**Replicated?** No: one weekly window. The next window's reading (after 10-30T21:59Z) is the replication.

**Artifact.** The quota series and the Mac's test reads were scratch (session scratchpad); the counts are in the table
above.

## 2026-10-27 · Gemini CLI translation, 1 vs 2 vs 4 pages per call, on Siku pages (#7503, job agy-per-call-7503)
<!-- PRIOR ART: #6443 (pages per call for Gemini IMAGE transcription; error 12% -> 22% at 5 per call). Nobody had tested translation from text. PR #7504 is the tool (claude-translate.mjs --cli=agy, call_usage in metas). -->

**Question.** An agy call carries a fixed CLI system prompt on top of our template. If 2 or 4 pages per call keeps quality, the ~1.37M-page Siku backlog (#5600) uses much less of the shared weekly Gemini pool.

**Draw** (`agy-per-call-7503/draw.mjs`, seed 7503, committed before any read). The frame is the 10,343 live books held as `paddle-zh-5600-ocr-only` or `gpu-backlog-5660`, minus the 20 books of the skqs-flash-pilot-5600 pilot. 15 books were drawn. From each, one run of 4 consecutive translatable pages with `ocr.source: paddle`, starting at a seeded random point: 60 pages, 167–557 OCR chars per page (`draw.json`).

**Arms.** All 60 pages in every arm, `--fresh`, `CANDIDATE_READS=off`, gemini-3.8-flash-low via agy. The four arms ran at the same time, so their wall times are comparable.
- **A1**: `cli-translate.mjs read`, the production single-page prompt, one page per call.
- **A1b**: A1 again. This is the noise floor.
- **B2**: `claude-translate.mjs read --cli=agy --per-call=2`, the block prompt.
- **C4**: the same with `--per-call=4`.

**Judge** (`prep.mjs`, `judge.mjs`). Opus via `claude -p`, one page per call, Read tool only. Each call got:
- the page image;
- the page's OCR, plus the OCR of the page before and after (so bleed can be seen);
- the four versions under shuffled letters W–Z, with `<summary>`/`<keywords>` cut.

The arm key is in `judge-key.json` and was never in a prompt.

**Controls.** Five controls were planted on 5 pages from 5 different books. Each control is a fifth version, made from a SEPARATE fresh 1/call read (arm CTL), so it could not be caught by diffing it against a shown arm:
- 3 had a middle sentence dropped;
- 2 had the next page's first sentence appended.

**All 5 were caught** (each drop flagged as an omission, each bleed as cross-page bleed, all marked unusable), so `status: ok`.

### Results (n = 60 pages / 15 books per arm; Wilson 95% CI on the share of pages)

| arm | usable | omission | addition | sense error | cross-page bleed | name/term garbled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 1/call | **49/60, 82%** [70–89] | 2 (3%) [1–11] | 5 (8%) [4–18] | 20 (33%) [23–46] | 0 [0–6] | 19 (32%) [21–44] |
| A1b 1/call again | **45/60, 75%** [63–84] | 5 (8%) [4–18] | 5 (8%) [4–18] | 20 (33%) [23–46] | 0 [0–6] | 18 (30%) [20–43] |
| B2 2/call | **48/60, 80%** [68–88] | 4 (7%) [3–16] | 8 (13%) [7–24] | 16 (27%) [17–39] | 1 (2%) [0–9] | 17 (28%) [19–41] |
| C4 4/call | **48/60, 80%** [68–88] | 6 (10%) [5–20] | 4 (7%) [3–16] | 18 (30%) [20–43] | 2 (3%) [1–11] | 11 (18%) [11–30] |

Paired difference in usable rate against A1, with a 95% bootstrap that resamples the 15 books:

| comparison | difference |
|---|---|
| A1b − A1 (the floor) | **−6.7 pts** [−16.7, +3.3] |
| B2 − A1 | −1.7 [−15.0, +10.0] |
| C4 − A1 | −1.7 [−16.7, +13.3] |

Pages whose usable verdict differs between two arms: A1~A1b 10/60, A1~B2 13, A1b~C4 13, A1~C4 17. Neither block arm is further from A1 than the two A1 runs are from each other.

Unusable pages cluster in the two 御定佩文韻府 volumes, a rhyme thesaurus of short quotations. They account for 5 of A1's 11 unusable pages, and every arm finds them hard.

| arm | calls (pages per call) | refused calls | input / page | of which cached | output / page | thinking | quota index / page | vs A1 | vs A1, uncached input only | English chars / page | wall (parallel) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | 60 (60×1) | 0 | 6,397 | 3,655 | 606 | 0 | 10,034 | **1.00** | 1.00 | 2,546 | 388 s |
| A1b | 60 (60×1) | 0 | 6,921 | 3,114 | 580 | 0 | 10,402 | 1.04 | 1.14 | 2,479 | 390 s |
| B2 | 34 (26×2, 8×1) | 0 | 3,941 | 1,896 | 519 | 0 | 7,056 | **0.70** | 0.81 | 2,221 | 263 s |
| C4 | 21 (12×4, 1×3, 1×2, 7×1) | 0 | 2,517 | 1,151 | 500 | 0 | 5,515 | **0.55** | 0.68 | 2,160 | 215 s |

How to read the token table:
- **The quota index** is input + 6 × (output + thinking) per page. The 6× weight is an ASSUMPTION (Gemini's list-price ratio), not a measured agy quota rate. The second "vs A1" column counts only uncached input.
- **The cache adds noise.** agy reports `cache_read` on about half the input, and it varied between the two identical A1 runs (3,655 vs 3,114 per page). So the uncached index carries about ±10% noise from caching luck alone.
- **The block arms were never refused.** No `page_tags_mismatch`, and no drift or seam re-reads.
- **Some pages are always read alone.** 5 of the 60 pages fall under translate-batch-seam's 200-char block floor (`MIN_OCR_CHARS_FOR_BLOCK`) and are read alone in every arm, which is part of why B2 and C4 have single calls. The share of Siku pages under that floor decides how much of the saving the full backlog gets.
- **Thinking was 0 on every call** (flash-low).

### The new defect: a sentence across a page break is finished on the earlier page

Every cross-page bleed the judge found in B2 and C4 is paired with an omission at the top of the next page in the same block. The model completes the sentence that runs over the page break on page N and starts page N+1 at the next sentence. Read by hand at the seam:

| book | break | arm | what the block reads put on page N | how A1 split it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 論語商 | p.37→38 | B2, C4 | 非與驕傲相反（若以謙恭解之便非本旨矣） | no fault at this break (both A1 runs) |
| 天原發微 | p.56→57 | C4 | 至哉言也學者宜深味之 | no fault at this break (both A1 runs) |
| 經濟類編 | p.63→64 | C4 | "Use a white flag for stone" | "For stones / , use a white flag" |
| 學易記 | p.122→123 | B2 | "…and cannot be disordered." | "…cannot be altered. / cannot be disrupted." |

Rates:
- B2: 2 of 26 in-block breaks.
- C4: 3 of 39 in-block breaks.

So the rate per break is about the same (~8%) at both block sizes, and 4/call has more in-block breaks per page. The two 1/call runs put no text on the wrong side of a page break.

Nothing is lost from the book and nothing is invented. One clause sits on the page before its own, which is exactly the error a page citation inherits. `scripts/lib/block-drift.mjs` exists to catch this move (#5021), but it makes no claim on caseless scripts: its first test is a lowercase opening letter. Unpunctuated SKQS OCR is invisible to it, and none of the five moves was re-read.

### Recommendation

**4 pages per call for the Siku lane**, after the drift guard learns caseless scripts.
- **Quality:** usable, sense errors and names are not distinguishable from one page per call; every difference lies inside the A1-vs-A1b floor.
- **Quota:** the index is 0.55 of one per call (0.68 counting uncached input only).
- **The page-break shift:** it happens at about the same rate per break at 2/call, so choosing 2 does not avoid it. The choice between 2 and 4 then comes down to quota, and 4 saves more.
- **Before switching the lane:** extend block-drift to Chinese. For example, flag an in-block break where page N+1's English opens on a capitalised fresh sentence while its OCR continues page N's (SKQS pages almost never begin a new sentence at the top of a half-leaf). Otherwise accept that roughly 5% of pages carry a clause one page early.

**Caveats:**
- **Prompt confound.** A1 uses the single-page production prompt (sentinel markers) and B2/C4 the block prompt, so this compares the lane as it is against the block lane, not pages per call alone.
- **Sample size.** At n = 60 across 15 books, a difference under about 15 points in usable rate is not detectable.
- **One judge.** A single Opus judge rated every version, which the controls validate only for gross faults.
- **Cost of the run:** about 180 agy calls; 60 judge calls at about $5.7 notional, on the subscription; Gemini weekly 70% → 69%.

Files: `scripts/eval/agy-per-call-7503/`
- `draw.json`, `page-ids.json`
- `controls.json`, `controls-tamper.json`
- `reads.jsonl` (every read, all arms)
- `calls-B2.jsonl`, `calls-C4.jsonl`
- `judge-verdicts.jsonl`, `judge-key.json`
- `tokens.json`, `results.json`

Re-score with `node scripts/eval/agy-per-call-7503/score.mjs --scratch=<dir with the arms>`. Nothing was written to pages or books. The readers recorded their book lists in `lane_job_books`, which is a label: nothing selects or skips a book from it.

## 2026-10-27 · agy OCR, 1 vs 2 vs 4 pages per call, German and Latin print (#7522, job ocr-percall-7522)
<!-- PRIOR ART: 2026-10-10-paddle-zh-random-qa-6388.md "Context arm" (PR #6443): Gemini 3.8 Flash-low on 10 Siku Chinese pages, mean CER 12.1% -> 21.6% at 5 pages a call, one page's text matching no page of the call. That is the "12% -> 22%" #7503 cites. 2026-10-27-agy-pages-per-call-siku-7503.md (PR #7518) is the translation version; its draw/judge/score were reused here. -->

**Question.** One agy call pays the CLI's own context and its agent turns once, however many images it carries. If OCR keeps quality at 2 or 4 pages a call, each pool reads more pages. The one earlier image result went the other way (Chinese, 5/call, mean CER 12% -> 22%, PR #6443).

**Tool.** `cli-ocr.mjs read --per-call=N` (this PR). It sends up to N consecutive pages of one book in one agy call, as `p01.jpg … pNN.jpg`, on the live OCR prompt plus a block wrapper (`agy-cli.mjs ocrBlockInstruction`). The reply is split only by `<<<PAGE n BEGIN>>>` / `<<<PAGE n END>>>`, and any mismatch refuses the whole call. A refused call is retried once, then its pages are read one per call. Every existing guard and the provenance stay. The kept-read variant names the call's page count.

**Draw** (`ocr-per-call-7522/draw.mjs`, seed 7522, committed before any read). Frame: 2,393 visible German or Latin printed books with `human_read_count > 0`, idle in the pipeline (not held). From each drawn book, one run of 4 consecutive pages, each with no OCR or only a Flash-Lite read, never among the first or last 4 images.
- Two rules were added after looking at the first draws, before any read: manuscripts out (the first draw took two BPH Kurrent manuscripts), and the last 4 images out (the second took Atlas minor's spine and edges).
- Result: 8 German and 7 Latin books. 14 books had Flash-Lite reads and 1 had no OCR.
- By eye (`script.json`), 5 books are Fraktur, all German. That is short of the "about half" in the brief. The seeded draw was kept rather than redrawn to hit the share.

**Arms.** All 60 pages in every arm, gemini-3.8-flash-low, `--fresh`, `CANDIDATE_READS=off`, 3 calls at a time, run one after another (`run-arms.sh`): A1 1/call; B2 2/call; C4 4/call; A1b 1/call again (the noise floor). CTL is a separate fresh 1/call read of the 5 control pages.

**Account.** The main pool, not the second one. `AGY_HOME=/root/.agy-james` showed 0.6% and then 0.00% of its Gemini week (reset 2026-11-03). Derek's inbox note of 13:00Z confirmed: Antigravity serves that account Starter quota. All arms therefore ran on the shared main pool.

**Judge** (`prep.mjs`, `judge.mjs`). Opus via `claude -p --restricted --tools Read`, one page per call. The call's folder holds `this.jpg` and `prev.jpg` / `next.jpg` (the neighbouring pages), and nothing else. The versions appear under shuffled letters, and the arm key never enters the prompt. Faults recorded: omission, addition (printed on none of the three pages), cross-page bleed (printed on a neighbour), order error, misread, and usable.
- **Controls: 5/5 caught.** 3 drops (one body line taken out) and 2 bleeds (the next page's first line appended). Each came from its own fresh read. This is a result, not probe_broken.

| arm | usable (Wilson 95%) | omission | addition | bleed | order | pages with a misread | in / out tok per page | token index vs A1* | calls | refused |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 1/call | **55/60** 92% [82–96] | 2 | 2 | 0 | 2 | 32 | 24,727 / 935 | **1.00** | 60 | 0 |
| A1b 1/call again | **59/60** 98% [91–100] | 1 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 29 | 26,764 / 933 | 1.07 | 60 | 0 |
| B2 2/call | **56/60** 93% [84–97] | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 39 | 20,724 / 934 | **0.87** | 31 | 1 block, passed on retry |
| C4 4/call | **58/60** 97% [89–99] | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 36 | 15,083 / 911 | **0.68** | 15 | 0 |

\*Input + 6 × (output + thinking) per page. The 6 is an assumption carried over from #7503, not a measured agy rate. Thinking was 0 on every call. Counting uncached input only (input − cache_read), the index is A1 1.00, A1b 1.20, B2 1.07, C4 0.89. Cached input varies between the two identical 1/call runs, so this variant carries about ±20% noise.

**Against the floor, not zero.** Paired difference in usable rate vs A1, with a 95% bootstrap that resamples the 15 books (`score.mjs`):
- A1b (the floor): +6.7 pts [0, +15.0]
- B2: +1.7 [−5.0, +8.3]
- C4: +5.0 [−3.3, +15.0]

Neither block arm is worse than A1, and both differ from it by less than A1b does. Usable verdicts disagree between A1 and A1b on 4 pages, A1 and B2 on 7, and A1 and C4 on 7.

**Page-break defects did not appear.** Cross-page bleed was 0 in all 240 judged reads. The block arms had no order errors. The #7503 translation defect (a sentence finished on the earlier page) has no OCR analogue here: each page held only its own printed lines.

**Misreads (a weak signal).** Pages where the judge listed at least one misread word, paired vs A1:
- B2: +11.7 pts [+1.7, +23.3]
- C4: +6.7 [−6.7, +21.7]
- A1b: −5.0 [−18.3, +6.7]

Fraktur usable was 20/20 in both 1/call runs and 19/20 in both block arms. The miss is the same page (Chymische Hochzeit p.132) and the same misread in both: *Leyter* read twice as *Leyer*. The two 1/call runs read it right.

**Unusable in the 1/call arms:** a footnote written twice (Jung p.73, both runs), long s read as f (Universae Geometriae p.564), a misread page count (Murr p.33), and a bracketed grammar table read out of order (Gaurico).

**Quota, measured: not usable here.** Before/after `/quota` per arm, the "after" taken 15 minutes past the arm's end (`results/quota.jsonl`). Weekly fraction used: A1 0.96 pts, B2 0.13, C4 0.14, A1b 0.20. In the same windows, other jobs on this box made 78–191 calls, and other boxes share the account but do not log here. The two identical 1/call arms differ about 5×, so these deltas measure the pool, not the arm. The 5-hour window also reset during B2. Quota per page per arm is **not measured**; the token index is the only cost figure.

**Decision (the rule in #7522).** A block arm is adopted if its paired usable difference vs A1 is no worse than the floor, and it shows no bleed that block-drift-style checks cannot catch. B2 and C4 both pass. Recommendation: **4 pages per call for agy OCR on print**. Its token index is 0.68 (0.81 uncached), and its quality cannot be told apart from 1/call at n = 60.

**Caveats**
- At n = 60, a difference under about 10 points is not detectable. Watch misreads in any rollout.
- The quota saving is inferred from tokens. Measure it on an idle pool before relying on it.
- These are good-to-moderate printed scans. Dense manuscripts and Chinese (#6443's 12% -> 22%) are not covered.
- 10 of 15 books are roman type. This draw does not test Fraktur at scale.

**Useful output.** Per page, the best judged read (usable, no omission, addition, bleed or order error, then fewest misreads; ties to the 1/call arms) was picked by `pick-best.mjs`. The picks went through `cli-ocr.mjs apply --apply --reason="#7522 best-of-arms, Opus-judged"`, run `cli-ocr-20261027144902`, with provenance kept.
- 59 pages had a clean pick (A1 35, A1b 12, B2 8, C4 4).
- **55 were written.** Four were refused by the foreign-script guard: real Greek in Irenaeus and the Assoziationsstudien, and real Hebrew in Galatinus. The guard was left as it is.
- One page (Gaurico p.107) had no clean read.
- Verified in Mongo by page id: 55/55 carry this run's gemini-3.8-flash-low OCR; 12 of them came from block calls.

**Contained in this run.** The 40% shared-words guard flagged Jung, *Zur Psychologie und Pathologie sogenannter occulter Phänomene* (1902, `69bd9abd46b01553e33bce57`).
- **102 of its 134 pages** serve Russian prose from another book as OCR and English.
- By eye, the images of pp. 30, 60, 73–76, 100 and 130 are Jung's German.
- The book is held as `russian-ocr-over-german-7522`, and the English of those 102 pages is withheld (`withhold-stale-translations.mjs --by-eye-pages`, revisions saved).
- A re-read is owed. Same shape as #5215 (Gesner).

Files: `scripts/eval/ocr-per-call-7522/` (draw, controls, prep, judge, score, quota, run-arms, pick-best) and `results/` (results.json with every verdict row, the letter key, tampers, quota readings, block call logs, choice.json, Opus verdicts). Spend: $0 (subscriptions). About 290 agy calls and 60 Opus calls.

## 2026-10-27 · Does agy 3.8 Flash low hold OCR quality at 2 pages per call, for a fresh read and for a correction? (#6740)

PRIOR ART: `scripts/eval/agy-per-call-7503/` (PR #7518: 1/2/4 pages per call for TRANSLATION; its quota index, its
A-vs-A noise floor and its planted controls are reused here); `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/judge.mjs` (the
image-grounded Opus judge prompt, imported unchanged); `scripts/eval/paddle-zh-qa-6388/kanripo.jsonl` and
`ground-truth-5935` (the Kanripo leaf rule and body CER); the #6443 context arm (Flash low, Siku, 1/call 12.1% vs
5/call 21.6% CER, one 5-page call returned text from none of its pages). Sibling: #7522 tests FRESH German/Latin
reads at 1/2/4; this entry is the Siku fresh read and the German CORRECTION request, and does not cover #7522.

**Why.** The agy pool is shared (~104K Flash-low calls a week, `2026-10-27-agy-quota-pool-6740.md`), and every agy OCR
and correction route reads one page per call. If 2 pages a call holds quality, each route costs less of the pool.

### Pre-registration (committed before any arm was scored)

**Pages** (`draw.mjs`, salt `6740-ppc`, `draw.json`): 15 books × 2 adjacent pages per task.
- **T1, fresh read, Siku Chinese:** the Kanripo-scored books of `paddle-zh-qa-6388/kanripo.jsonl`, seeded. Both pages
  of a pair have their own trusted Kanripo screen (dice ≥ 0.6) on adjacent Kanripo pages, ≥ 40 Han each.
- **T2, correction, German Flash-Lite drafts:** the router tests' `de-lite` pages (#7434), seeded, each with its next
  (else previous) page, also a Flash-Lite draft ≥ 300 characters. Drafts are frozen at draw time.

**Arms** (`read.mjs`, `gemini-3.8-flash-low`, nothing kept or written):
- **A1, A1b:** one page per call, twice (the noise floor). The request is `cli-ocr.mjs read`'s byte for byte: T1 the
  live OCR prompt + the sentinel image instruction; T2 the #5924 one-page correction template (`fc-prompt.mjs`), the
  router tests' `lite>agy-flash-low` request.
- **B2:** the pair in one call: the same prompt, both images attached as p01/p02, one answer per page under
  `===== PAGE pNN =====` markers inside the sentinels (T2: `correctInstruction(2)` adapted as `fc-prompt.mjs` adapts
  `correctInstruction(1)`). A reply without exactly p01, p02 in order is read once more, then each page alone (a
  REFUSED BLOCK, counted and paid for).
- **C3** (3 per call) only if B2 passes the rule below on a task.

**Measures.**
- **Accepted:** the route-judge's Opus judge (`judgePrompt`, one output per call, the page image attached, blind: the
  item ids are opaque and shuffled). T1 items carry the page's own Kanripo leaf as a reference, as the router tests'
  `zh-dice` cell did. A text two arms share exactly is judged once.
- **T1 CER:** body CER against the page's own Kanripo leaf (`bodyCer`, the #5935 window: the leaf and its neighbours).
- **Cross-page faults**, per page, mechanical (`score.mjs`), every flag then checked by eye against the reference
  (T1 Kanripo leaf, T2 the frozen drafts):
  - an empty or failed page;
  - a swap: the output is closer to the other page of the pair (Han bigram dice for T1, word-trigram overlap for T2)
    than to its own;
  - bleed / moved lines: T1, a run of ≥ 8 Han that is in the other page's leaf and not in the own leaf; T2, a line of
    ≥ 25 letters that matches a line of the other page's draft (trigram Jaccard ≥ 0.6) and nothing in its own (< 0.3).
  The same checks run on A1 and A1b, so a flag a 1/call arm also raises is the detector's noise, not a block fault.
- **Quota per page:** from agy's own usage on every call made (refused and re-read calls count), the #7518 index
  input + 6 × (output + thinking) per page (the 6× weight is an assumption, not a measured agy rate), and the
  uncached variant. `agy -p /quota` is read before and after each arm, as a coarse check only.
- **Controls:** 5 per task, built from A1b reads (seeded): 3 with a middle line dropped, 2 with the first line of
  the next page's A1b read appended (a planted bleed). Judged blind among the others. The judge passes a task at
  ≥ 4/5 caught (not accepted, or a `wrong_text` defect); below that the task's acceptance is "probe broken". The two
  planted bleeds must also be flagged by the mechanical cross-page check, else that check is "probe broken".

**Decision rule, per task.** 2/call is adopted for the task if all three hold:
1. **Quality inside the noise floor:** B2's accepted count ≥ the lower of A1's and A1b's (and, T1, B2's mean CER ≤ the
   higher of A1's and A1b's).
2. **Cross-page faults:** 0 of 30 B2 pages, or every one is caught by a guard that runs without the eval's reference
   (the block-marker refusal, or for T2 the line check against the drafts the lane already holds).
3. **Saves quota:** B2's quota index per page is below both A1's and A1b's.
Otherwise one page per call stays. At n = 30 a difference under about 20 points of acceptance cannot be detected;
the rule asks only that 2/call is not visibly worse than 1/call is from itself.

**Limits.** $0 (subscriptions). agy Flash low only; ~160 agy calls, ~200 Opus judge calls. No page, book or R2
write; no routing-table edit.

### Amendment (before the final score, after the controls ran)

The pre-registered T2 line check (line-to-line trigram Jaccard) caught 0 of 2 planted bleeds: the reads and the
drafts break lines differently, and German letter trigrams are shared by any two pages. It now asks whether a line's
letter 8-grams are >= 70% in the other page's draft and < 30% in its own (2/2 caught). The 1/call baseline was also
made explicit in code: a block flag is a fault only if neither 1/call read of the page carries the same foreign run
(`score.mjs` `novel`), and each remaining flag was checked by eye (`by-eye.json`). No verdict had been read for the
decision at that point; the judge was still running.

### Results (2026-10-27, `results.json`, `pages.jsonl.gz`)

163 agy calls (gemini-3.8-flash-low, agy 1.4.8, this box's agy-guard), 0 quota replies; 182 Opus judge calls
(`claude -p --model opus`), 0 unparsed. **Controls: 5/5 caught by the judge in each task, and 2/2 planted bleeds
caught by the cross-page check in each task**, so neither probe is broken.

| task | arm | accepted (Wilson 95%) | Δ vs A1, pts [95% by book] | wrong text | CER mean / median | cross-page faults | calls | in / out tok per page | quota index (rel A1) | uncached rel | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 Siku fresh read | A1 1/call | 8/30 [14–44%] | — | 17 | 0.223 / 0.047 | — | 32 | 28,145 / 472 | 30,977 (1.00) | 1.00 | |
| T1 | A1b 1/call | 7/30 [12–41%] | −3.3 [−16.7, +10.0] | 15 | 0.231 / 0.060 | — | 34 | 28,136 / 470 | 30,954 (1.00) | 0.89 | |
| T1 | **B2 2/call** | **8/30** [14–44%] | 0.0 [−20.0, +16.7] | 18 | **0.159** / 0.065 | **0/30** (2 flags, both cleared by eye) | 17 | 22,886 / 465 | 25,677 (**0.83**) | 0.81 | **rule met** |
| T2 German correction | A1 1/call | 27/30 [74–97%] | — | 2 | — | — | 30 | 26,726 / 683 | 30,825 (1.00) | 1.00 | |
| T2 | A1b 1/call | 27/30 [74–97%] | 0.0 [−10.0, +10.0] | 3 | — | — | 30 | 28,403 / 688 | 32,531 (1.06) | 1.10 | |
| T2 | **B2 2/call** | **23/30** [59–88%] | −13.3 [−36.7, +6.7] | 3 | — | **0/30** | 15 | 19,531 / 626 | 23,287 (**0.76**) | 0.80 | **rule failed (quality)** |

Thinking tokens were 0 on every call. "Cross-page faults" counts block pages only; at 1/call there is no other page in
the call.

**T1, Siku fresh read: the rule is met.**
- Accepted 8/30, the same as A1 (A1b 7/30). Mean CER 0.159 against 0.223 and 0.231.
- The mean flatters B2. Gemini's safety filter ("This request was blocked by Gemini's filters") cut 4 A1, 8 A1b and 2 B2
  replies, on numeric 三易洞璣 and 佩文韻府 pages, and it is random. The one re-read rescued both B2 blocks but not 2 A1
  and 4 A1b pages, which score CER 1. **On the pages both arms read, paired CER B2 − A1 = −0.6 pts [−4.5, +2.9]**
  (28 pages), against A1b − A1 = −4.3 [−11.0, +0.1]: no difference either way.
- Cross-page check: 4 B2 flags, 2 of them shared with the 1/call reads. The other 2 are Kanripo's page break falling a
  column off the scan's: both 1/call reads carry the same text at the head of the second page. One B2 page also holds
  A1's entries in another order (CER counts that). No text moved between the two pages of a call (`by-eye.json`).
  #7518 saw a sentence finished early across the break in block translation; nothing like it shows here.
- Quota 0.83 of 1/call per page (0.81 uncached).
- Flash low is a poor Siku reader at any k: 22–23 of 30 pages are not accepted, mostly omissions (O5) and misread
  characters on dense dictionary pages. The rule allows 2/call; it does not make this a good route.

**T2, German correction of Flash-Lite drafts: the rule fails on quality.**
- B2 accepted 23/30, below both 1/call runs (27 and 27). B2 is rejected on 5 pages that both 1/call runs accept. They
  come from 3 books and include both pages of two blocks, so errors are correlated within a call. B2 gains 1 page that
  both 1/call runs reject (*Tuba visitationis* p. 19, where they read the facing page's edge strip as a column).
- The block corrector **makes correct drafts worse**. Counts of the word in draft / A1 / A1b / B2:
  - *Unparteiische Samlungen* pp. 34–35: line-break hyphens turned into a letter s: `Natiosnal` (0/0/0/1),
    `unserbitlichen` (0/0/0/1), `wesder` (0/0/0/1).
  - *Augsburgs Buchdruckergeschichte* p. 220: `immanissimo` (1/1/1/0) replaced by the Chinese characters 变形. That is
    two letters, so the wrong-script guard (3+ letters, `reread-lane-gate.mjs`) would let it through.
  - *Kreuter Buch* pp. 581–582: the draft's `Rölkraut` (3/0/0/3) is left as it is. Both 1/call runs restored
    `Kölkraut`.
- No cross-page fault: no text moved between pages, none swapped, none empty. The failure is in the correction itself.
- Quota 0.76 of 1/call per page (0.80 uncached).

**Why the saving is 17–25% and not ~30%.** At 1/call a call carries ~28K input tokens; at 2/call ~46K. So agy's fixed
context is ~10K tokens a call and each page image (with its share of the prompt) ~17–18K. Halving the calls saves only
the fixed part. Even unlimited pages per call would save at most ~37% on a fresh read. Translation saves more (#7518:
0.70 at 2/call) because its per-page input is text, not an image.

**The `/quota` meter cannot see an arm.** The weekly fraction moved 0.0003–0.0007 per 30-page arm, while every other
job drew on the same pool (`quota-readings.json`). Only the per-call tokens separate the arms.

**3 per call was not run.** T1 met the rule, but a C3 arm needs three adjacent Kanripo-aligned pages per book, i.e. a
new draw. Its best case is ~0.75 of 1/call, against 0.83 at 2/call, and the lane is one Flash reads badly.

**Caveats.**
- n = 30 pages in 15 pairs. A difference under ~20 points of acceptance is not detectable. T2's −13 pts
  [−37, +7] is a failure of the pre-registered rule, not a measured effect size.
- The T1 judge had the Kanripo leaf as a reference, as the router tests' zh-dice cell did.
- One account and one day. The filter-block rate on these Siku pages is its own finding: 14 of 163 replies.

**Writes:** none to pages, books, page_revisions or R2; no routing table edited; every read is in `reads.jsonl.gz`.

## 2026-10-27 · Can agy OCR read more pages from the same quota, and where should the spare quota go? (#7558)

**Why.** The main agy pool (Ultra) was about two-thirds used: 63% of the Gemini week left at 16:00Z on 2026-10-27, with
the reset at 2026-10-30 22:00Z. The straight line to the reset was 46%. In the last 24 h the pool spent ~9.5% of a week
a day against ~14% affordable. Derek, 2026-10-27: "more pages and 4 pages". Everything here is agy (Gemini 3.8 Flash low)
on the main pool, $0 API. The judge is Opus via `claude -p`.

**1. The view_file turn is not redundant** (`agy-read-file-7558/attach-probe.mjs`, 2 pages, agy 1.4.8).
- With read_file denied, the model answered "The image @./page.jpg is not present in the message context" (both
  pages). `@./file` puts a path in the prompt, not an image.
- `--input-format=stream-json` refuses an image content block: `stream input content block type "image" is not
  supported (only "text")`.
- So the model sees a page only through its own read_file turn. That turn is the read.
- What a call does waste: the old sentence ("The page image to transcribe is attached: @./p.jpg") sent the model to
  try a shell first on **every** call (`run_command:deny`, 56/56), so the whole context was sent once more.
- Telling it "do not call any tool" did not stop the read_file call. Naming the file and the one tool did.
  `cli-ocr.mjs --prompt-variant=read-file-7558` says "the file ./p.jpg in this directory. Open it with read_file (or
  view_file): that is the only tool available here, and running commands, cropping or any other tool is disabled."

**2. A/B on German/Latin print** (`agy-read-file-7558/`, `results/de-la-56/`). The 56 pages are #7522's draw, 14 books
× 4 consecutive pages, minus the contained Jung book. Every arm read all 56 pages fresh (`--fresh`,
`CANDIDATE_READS=off`). The judge was #7522's `judge.mjs`, blind and one page per call with its neighbours. Controls
were 4 plants in a copy of a new-1/call read (2 dropped lines, 2 lines bled in from the next page): **4/4 caught**.

| arm | usable (Wilson 95%) | omission | addition | order | input tok / page | uncached | out | denied-tool turns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| old 1/call (production) | **53/56** [85–98] | 1 | 2 | 1 | 27,541 | 20,579 | 1,731 | 56 |
| new 1/call | **53/56** [85–98] | 2 | 1 | 1 | **17,486** | 11,829 | 878 | 0 |
| old 4/call | **56/56** [94–100] | 0 | 1 | 1 | 14,040 | 10,417 | 915 | 14 |
| new 4/call | **54/56** [88–99] | 0 | 1 | 3 | **6,789** | 4,976 | 897 | 2 |

- Paired by page: at 1/call, new is worse on 3 pages and better on 3. At 4/call, new is worse on 2 and better on 0.
- The two 4/call misses are table pages: the two-column footnotes of Irenaeus p.527 and the Gaurico grammar table
  p.109. #7522's 1/call arms also failed the Gaurico page.
- Against what the lane ran before (old prompt, 1/call), new 4/call is 54 vs 53 usable at **0.25× the input**.
- Bleed was 0 in every arm, as in #7522.

**3. Arabic, the held queue** (`draw-arabic.mjs`, `results/arabic-20/`). Frame: the 568 Arabic-script books held for
the CLI OCR lane. On 2026-10-27 the lane's readable queue was 439 Arabic books (2,591 pages) and 1 Sanskrit book (8
pages). Draw: 5 books × 4 consecutive interior pages, seed 7558. **All 5 are handwritten**, so this queue is
manuscripts, not the Arabic print that #7341's Kraus test measured. Controls 4/4.

| arm | usable | omission | addition | input tok / page | calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| old 1/call (production) | 13/20 | 3 | 7 | 32,665 | 23 |
| new 1/call | **16/20** | 2 | 5 | 19,138 | 22 |
| old 4/call | 14/20 | 7 | 6 | 18,927 | 10 |
| new 4/call | 15/20 | 1 | 5 | 8,590 | 9 |

- The additions are word- and phrase-level misreads, plus Gemini filter-block messages. The wrapper guard refuses a
  reply cut before `<<<END>>>` at write.
- At 4/call two phrases appear that are on none of the three pages (Bahr-al-Jawahar p.6, Tanwir p.7). 1/call had none
  of that kind.
- One 4-page block (Bahr-al-Jawahar pp.6–9) was cut mid-reply in both 4/call arms. The strict marker split refused
  it, and its pages were read one at a time.
- No page carried another page's text or a whole invented page, so there was no containment.
- **Arabic stays at 1/call** (on the new prompt). The pool's problem is unused quota, not tokens.
- Not settled: whether Flash-low should read these manuscripts at all (old 1/call: 13/20 usable). That is #7341's
  routing, measured on print.

**4. The correction queue, and a lane for it** (`cli-ocr-lane.mjs correct`).
- **Route.** lite>agy-flash-low, from the 2026-10-26 router tests:

  | cell | lite>agy-flash-low accepted | wrong text | served lite draft accepted | wrong text |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | German | 28/30 | 2/30 | 21/30 | 5/30 |
  | French | 27/29 | 2/29 | 22/30 | 6/30 |

  The router itself prefers lite>opus for German (28/30, 1/30 wrong): agy's 2/30 misses its +2% wrong-text bar.
  Opus cannot run at this scale on Claude points. So this lane improves on what is served, and does not rule out an
  Opus pass later.
- **Frame:** the router test's. A visible, idle German or French book that is not held. A page whose OCR is a
  Flash-Lite draft of 300+ characters, not handwritten, not human-edited, not withheld, interior (15–95% of the book).
- **Queue: 335,862 pages** (German 250,041 in 1,299 books; French 85,821 in 376). Before those filters, the same books
  hold 609,722 lite pages (571,033 in visible books).
- **Three bugs found before the first write.**
  - `apply` had no handling for the template's `UNCHANGED` / `CONTAIN:` answers: it would have written the word as OCR.
  - The header check summed `<page-type>` and `<scan-quality>`. That refused 24/24 pilot corrections of drafts that
    have `<page-type>` but no `<scan-quality>`.
  - Two parallel applies in the same second shared a run id.
- **Measured run on gex45, 2026-10-27 16:38–17:25Z.** 3 books at a time, 40-page chunks, `--apply`:
  - 696 pages taken: **418 written (60%), 131 UNCHANGED (19%), 4 CONTAIN, 143 held (21%)**.
  - The held ones are almost all the 25% change guard. Checked: Mysterium Magnum p.518's correction has 179 words
    against the draft's 431, a ~250-word passage dropped, and the guard held it. Those pages stay on the lite draft.
  - The 4 CONTAIN claims are all in one book (`6a2121ed…40a2`). By eye (p.13), the image is an unsplit two-page spread
    and the draft is that image's own text in two columns. Not invented, not wrong-leaf: a split problem, not a
    containment.
  - By eye, Mysterium Magnum p.513: the correction changed 5 words, 4 to the print's reading (*Essentz*, *gebiehret*,
    *Wurtzel*, *Eigenschafft*) and 1 away from it (*ihn* → *ihm*).
  - With the 24-page pilot: 440 pages written, stamped `ocr.pipeline=agy-correct-lite-7558`. Each run can be undone
    with `revert-run.mjs --run-id cli-ocr-…`.
- **Throughput:** 14.8 pages/min at 3 books, about 1,400 per 95-minute cron run, or ~16,800 a day at 12 runs.

**5. Quota per page (noisy).**
- Gemini weekly remaining went 61.97% (16:38:27Z) → 60.78% (17:26Z) over the run: 1.19 pts.
- Taking out the pool's other traffic at its 24 h average (~9.5%/day ≈ 0.31 pts in 47 min) leaves **~0.9 pts for 696
  correction pages ≈ 1.3e-5 of a week per page**.
- `/quota` readings seconds apart jump by ~0.5 pt (seen here and in #7498), and other boxes share the pool without a
  shared ledger. Treat this as ±50%.
- Token cost of one correction call: ~33K input, ~1K output, because the #5924 template still pays the denied-shell
  turn. It was kept as judged; a read-file variant of the template is untested.

**Pages a day, before and after** (main pool; the held lane plus the new correction lane).

| | before (2026-10-26/27) | after |
|---|---|---|
| CLI OCR lane (held books) | ≤120 pages / 2 h run, 1 at a time (~1,440/day cap; ~38 min of 110 used) | up to ~2,300 / run (4 books, deadline 95 min); queue 2,599 pages, drained in ~2 runs |
| input tokens / page, print | 27.5K (old prompt, 1/call) | 6.8K (new prompt, 4/call) |
| input tokens / page, Arabic | 32.7K (old, 1/call) | 19.1K (new, 1/call) |
| correction lane | none | ~1,400 / run ceiling. At the quota floor: ~3,800/day steady (4.8 pts/day of spare pace ÷ 1.3e-5), plus ~12,000 pages to spend the 15 pts the pool is ahead of its line before the 10-30 reset |

**Caveats.**
- n = 56 and 20: differences under ~10 points cannot be detected.
- Quota per page is one noisy measurement on a shared pool.
- The correction lane's quality is the router test's (n = 30 per cell), not re-judged. Its UNCHANGED, CONTAIN and
  held rates come from 696 pages of the first books in queue order.
- Watch the ledger's outcome mix for drift.

## 2026-10-26 · Can the production vLLM Yigdzin reader replace the HF reader on gex45? (#6871 row 4, #5771; job yig-vllm-6871)
<!-- PRIOR ART: 2026-10-20-tibetan-guttered-pages-yigdzin-page-mode-6871.md (the HF page-mode lane this replaces; its vLLM arm hung); 2026-10-14-yigdzin-rest-withheld-and-unread-tibetan-4523.md (the same worker on vLLM 0.29.0 on L4s, 0.73–0.97 pages/s); scripts/eval/split-leaf-5771/yig_leaf_read.py on job-split-leaves-5771 (the HF port of the worker that 81-split-leaf-5771 ran). -->

**Speed: yes.** The engine is about 440× faster than HF per leaf and about 530× per guttered page, on the same model, revision and decode settings.

**Parity: on the medians, but not on the line rule.**
- Median character similarity to the HF read is 0.9994 on the leaves and 1.000 on the guttered pages.
- One leaf in 64 has a vLLM-repeated line that the leaf does not show. The bar posted before the run forbids that.
- In the other direction, HF drops a line that vLLM keeps on 1 leaf in 64, and loses a whole page that vLLM reads on 1 of 200 T pages.

At this sample size, the errors look like numerical noise between two kernels running the same model. vLLM does not look worse.

### Why the vLLM path hung (and the fix)
The hang was the parent process's OpenMP pool, not the card or the CUDA build.
- **What happened.** vLLM forks its EngineCore. Task 73 (vLLM 0.31) and run 1 of this task both exported `OMP_NUM_THREADS=8`, so the parent had a live 8-thread libgomp pool when it forked. The child then deadlocked on its first CPU tensor.
- **The stack.** py-spy on the stuck EngineCore, 2026-10-26: `gpu_input_batch.py:134 torch.zeros → at::native::fill_kernel → libgomp`, idle at 224 MiB.
- **The fix.** With the variable unset, vLLM pins torch to 1 thread itself ("Reducing Torch threads from 14 to 1"). The engine then comes up in 39 s, including a 10.6 s torch.compile, with CUDA graphs on.
- **The 0.31 venv.** The same fix probably unblocks `vv` (vLLM 0.31.0) as well, with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`. That was not tested.

### Setup
- **Environment.** Venv `/root/jobs/yig-vllm-6871/venv`, built by `scripts/gpu/yigdzin-vllm/setup-venv.sh`.
  - Versions: vllm 0.29.0 · torch 2.13.0+cu132 (its arch list includes sm_120) · transformers 5.20.2 · flashinfer-python 0.6.18 · triton 3.7.1 · seqpos plugin @ 50506eb6 · driver 595.91.07 (CUDA 13.2).
  - Full freeze: `results-vllm029/venv-freeze.txt`.
  - Environment variables: `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0`, `OCR_VLLM_IMAGE_TOKEN_POSITIONS=sequential`, `--gpu-util 0.6`.
  - vLLM 0.29 falls back to the V1 runner on its own ("Model Runner V2 does not yet support custom logits processors").
- **Worker.** The production `yig_leaf_worker.py` (ops `handoffs/data/2026-09-25-yig-leaf/`) is now committed at `scripts/gpu/yigdzin-vllm/`.
  - The read path is unchanged: 2400-px prep, DRY 0.8/1.75/12, loop retry at T 0.4 with n=2, and the short-read re-decode.
  - The only additions are crop rows, `--gpu-util` and `--enforce-eager`.
- **The bar** was posted on #6871 before any vLLM read existed (comment 6411135905): median character similarity ≥ 0.95 on each set, and no vLLM-added line unless the image shows it.
- **Sets.** gpu-queue task `83a-yig-vllm029-parity-r2`, 2026-10-26 09:25–09:30Z:
  - **L**: all 188 #5771 crops read; 64 have HF reads (81 was stopped at 64/187 by Derek's session).
  - **P**: 30 guttered pages, `pick-parity30.py`, seed 6871, HF read ≥ 100 tokens; `yig_vllm.py` page mode, the HF page reader's recipe.
  - **T**: 200 more guttered pages with HF reads, throughput only.

### Results
| set | n scored | median char sim | median syllable id | ≥ 0.95 | added lines (posted test) | dropped lines | throughput (model load excluded) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L leaves | 64 | **0.9994** | 0.9965 | 61/64 | 0 (by eye: **1**, a006-L2) | 1 | **2.10 leaves/s** · 0.48 s/leaf (HF 211 s) |
| P pages | 30 | **1.000** | 1.000 | 30/30 | 0 | 0 | 1.92 pages/s (batch 30) |
| T pages | 190 (+10 blank both) | 1.000 | 1.000 | 189/190 | 18 in 3 pages (2 are line breaks only, 1 = HF empty) | 0 | **2.21 pages/s** · 0.44 s/page (HF 235 s) |

**VRAM.** Peak was 14.7–15.0 GB per process. That is the 0.6 reservation: weights 1.65 GiB, KV cache 11.63 GiB (469K tokens, 57× concurrency at 8,192), CUDA graphs 0.19 GiB. The work itself needs far less KV, so a 0.3 reservation would leave the card shareable. The card was back to 2 MiB after each arm.

**Run 1 hung.** It sat for 6 min at 224 MiB and was stopped by hand. The fix is the OMP section above.

### By eye (8 items where the reads differ most; crop or page image open)
| item | sim | which read matches the image |
|---|---|---|
| L a028-L1 | 0.83 | **vLLM.** The leaf has 7 lines. HF reads 6 and skips the body (ལུས་ཀྱི) clause. |
| L a006-L2 | 0.85 | **HF.** The leaf has 7 lines. vLLM inserts an 8th, a garbled second pass over line 6 (…མི་སྦྱོར་བར་མི་སྦྱོར་རོ…). This is the one vLLM-added line. |
| L a013-L2 | 0.98 | **Neither.** Both skip leaf line 2 (ཀུན་ནས་ཉོན་མོངས་པ… རྣམ་པར་བྱང་བར). The rest is the same text; HF breaks two lines differently. |
| L a018-L1 | 0.92 | **Neither.** A blank leaf with only the margin ཀ. Both write the same Latin junk ("empty paged paget…"). |
| L a019-L1 | 0.96 | **Tie.** The formula is འགོག་པ་ལ་གནས་པ. HF slips on lines 5 and 7, where vLLM is right. vLLM slips elsewhere (དང་དང་, མགོག, རྣམས་པར). |
| P …58ab1 | 0.97 | **Undecidable.** A binarized, degraded woodblock leaf with interlinear gloss. The reads part where the print breaks up. |
| T …5af6a | 0.006 | **vLLM.** A full 6-line page. HF stopped after ༄༅།. vLLM's line 1 (…པ་ལ། །ཕ་མོའི་རྒོལ་བའི་བསམ་ངན་…) matches the print. |
| T …5b44e | 0.99 | **vLLM on layout.** The text is the same. Line 2 ends in a dotted filler, which vLLM writes as a tsheg run with the line break kept. HF merges lines 2 and 3. |

**Tally.** vLLM matches better on 3 items, HF on 1. Two are ties or undecidable, and two have the same error on both.

### The #4523 write rule on these items
The rule is `first-ocr-guard` + ≥ 150 syllables. It was run on both reads of all eight items, plus T …58a16 and …58a9b:
- T …5af6a: the HF read is withheld (0 units); the vLLM read is written (258).
- T …58a16 and …58a9b: both reads are written. The text is identical (similarity 1.000) and only the line breaks differ.
- L a006-L2: **the repeated vLLM line is written** (354 units). The guard and the floor do not catch a duplicated line.
- L a018-L1: **the Latin junk is written on both engines** (261 / 271 units). The guard counts Latin words as units.

### A worker defect both engines share (#5771 must handle it before any apply)
5 of 188 vLLM leaf reads are mostly Latin letters (a018-L1, a051-L3, a072-L1, a045-L2, a078-L1):
- **Blank leaves.** The short-read re-decode (`min_tokens` 300) forces text out of a blank leaf. It is kept because it is longer and loop-free.
- **Retries.** The retry keeps the least repetitive of its candidates. `repetition_score` counts tsheg syllables and Latin junk has none, so the junk wins.

The HF port copies both rules, and its one read in this set (a018-L1) is the same junk. Stage 2 needs a reject: Latin letters > Tibetan letters means the leaf is blank or unread. Without it, about 2.7% of leaves would be written as junk.

### Follow-ups (plans only, not queued)
1. **Gutter remainder on vLLM.** `full/` holds 1,297 of 5,132 HF reads, so 3,835 pages are left.
   - **Run:** `yig_vllm.py --mode page --batch 64 --gpu-util 0.6` (no `OMP_NUM_THREADS`), to a new dir `/root/jobs/tib-gutter-6871/full-vllm`, as a new task such as `86-tib-gutter-vllm-rest`.
   - **Cost:** about 3,835 / 2.2 ≈ 29 GPU-min plus 1 min to load, against about 10 GPU-days on HF. Reading all 5,132 takes 39 min and puts the lane on one engine.
   - **Writes:** files only. The apply (v4 judge + first-ocr-guard + 150-syllable floor) stays Derek's.
2. **#5771 stage 2** (~157K leaves).
   - **Rate:** at 0.48 s/leaf that is about 21 GPU-hours, about 1 GPU-day at `--gpu-util 0.6`, against about 380 GPU-days on HF at 211 s/leaf.
   - **Fetch:** the worker fetches frames itself at 5 req/s from our own host. That is about 4.4 h for about 78K frames, and it overlaps with reading.
   - **Before any apply:** the Latin-junk reject above, and a duplicate-line check. Neither is in the write rule today.

## 2026-10-26 · Does a "prefer cognates, keep the author's distinctions" line make Latin translations keep the author's vocabulary? (#4741)

**Question.** Spinoza's *concordia* was rendered "harmony" on 35 pages across four editions (corrected 2026-10-26).
That erased a distinction Spinoza draws himself: Ethics I App. dismisses *harmonia*. Would a general line in the
prompt fix this class of error? The candidate line says to use the English cognate where its meaning matches, never
to render two source words with one English word, and to watch for false friends.

**Design.**
- Arms: `v13a` (the live default), `v13b` (v13 again, the A-vs-A noise floor) and `v19` (v13 plus the KEY TERMS
  block). The block's examples name only *concordia* and *consonantia*.
- Pages: 48 Latin books, one page each, in three strata:
  - T, 24 books: key terms (concord / consonan / sympath / proporti / symmetri / temperament);
  - F, 12 books: false-friend candidates (virtus / experimentum / convenientia / religio);
  - C, 12 books: control.
- Calls: realtime `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, temperature 1.0, thinking off, no continuity text.
- Pre-registration: `PREREGISTRATION-translation-cognate-4741.md`, committed and pushed before any output.
- Runner: `translation-cognate-ab-4741.mjs`.
- Blind pairwise judge: 8 Claude Opus subagents; 108 pairs, of which 48 cand, 48 noise and 12 same-arm controls.
- Spend: **$0.30** for 144 calls, with no failures or refusals.

**Result: not established; keep v13.**

| measure | v13a | v13b (noise) | v19 |
|---|---|---|---|
| named terms (*concordia*, *consonantia*) kept as cognate, 9 pages | 44% | 67% | **89%** |
| held-out terms kept as cognate, 17 pages | 53% | 53% | 53% (instrument defect, below) |
| "harmony" in the body where the Latin has no *harmonia* | 3 | 2 | **0** |

| judge, 48 pairs per kind | v19 vs v13a | v13b vs v13a (noise) |
|---|---|---|
| fidelity (first / second / tie) | 16 / 19 / 13 | 13 / 14 / 21 |
| readability (first / second / tie) | **4 / 28 / 16** | 13 / 17 / 18 |
| serious meaning errors (first, second) | 30, 35 | 30, 28 |
| false-friend errors (first, second) | 36, 32 | 28, 24 |

Here "first" means v19 in the cand pairs and v13b in the noise pairs. The same-arm control tie rate is **100%**
(12 of 12), so the judge is not inventing differences.

**Pre-registered rule.**
1. Held-out fidelity +0.00: **fails**. The failure is an instrument defect plus a ceiling (see below).
2. False friends in F: 11 vs 7, which **fails** the +1 margin. The noise pair in F is 10 vs 8.
3. Serious errors: 30 vs 35, passes.
4. Readability in C: net −4 against a noise |−3| + 2, passes narrowly. Overall readability is 4 wins to 28 losses
   against a noise of 13 / 17, which is the clearest signal in the run.
5. Control ties: 100%, passes.

**Why.**
- **The default is already the cognate.** Every genuine held-out Latin term (*proportio*, *sympathia*,
  *temperamentum*) was rendered with its cognate by all three arms. The *concordia* error is narrower: it happens
  where English has a more idiomatic near-synonym ("live in harmony" for *concorditer vivere*).
- **A general rule overcorrects.** The judges' reasons on v19's losses name new false friends:
  - *schedulae* → "schedules";
  - "insinuate his death";
  - *habitus* → "habit";
  - "interpellating", "provocation".
  The prose is also stiffer. The warning sentence about false friends did not hold the line.

**Instrument defects, reported, not fixed in the score.**
- **Held-out matches were not Latin.** All 8 *symmetri* hits in stratum T were the English word "symmetrical" in
  `<image-desc>` captions inside the OCR, which the translations move into `<note>`, outside the scored body. So
  none of the three arms could score there. The corrected held-out set (genuine Latin terms only) is 100% for every
  arm: no headroom.
- **Packet bug.** The first packet build attached a page's English to the previous page's Latin on 36 of 108 pairs
  (a `slice(-3)` on units with two pairs). Two judges flagged it. The bug was fixed, and the 36 pairs were rebuilt
  with unchanged ids and A/B order (`judge-key.json` is byte-identical) and judged fresh. Their first verdicts are
  discarded by the scorer (`rejudge-ids.json`).

**Grade.** 48 books, `directional`; one judge per pair, so there is no α.

**Next.** Target the trap rather than the habit. The per-book glossary (#4741) can carry the pairs that actually go
wrong (*concordia*/concord vs *harmonia*/harmony, using the harmony concepts added in #7409) without telling the
model to prefer cognates everywhere. A second held-out set should be chosen for idiomatic-near-synonym traps
(*imaginatio*, *affectus*, *commercium*, *ingenium*), not for terms the default already renders as cognates.

## 2026-10-27 · Applied under Derek's 23:15Z rule, then diff-QA

**The rule.** Write a page when it passes the automatic guards and does not lower Derge identity by more than 0.01 (where
the draft has a parallel, identity ≥ 0.85). An audited page that introduced a severe error keeps Yigdzin. The re-score
(`pass/rescore.mjs`): SEVERE = line-level, negation or mantra; a page passes with net ≥ 0 and no severe error introduced.
This gate passed 35/38 pages.

**Reads.** 8,278 pages, by agy Flash-low on main ($0). Reads came back through R2.

**Derge placement.** 15 sample pages per volume against all of P000001, then the whole volume against those Derge volumes
± 1. Derge v103's Pagination layer has a single entry, which makes one enormous window, so it is left out.

**Written: 7,287 pages** in 19 volumes, through `writePageText` (runs: `results/.../pass-gate-wave2-6740/runs.json`; per
volume: `written-by-volume.md`).

| | pages |
|---|---|
| refused: line count changed | 349 |
| refused: 25% cap | 94 |
| refused: ya-btags, no leaf check | 46 |
| refused: adds Latin letters | 5 |

The **line-count guard** was added after the wave-A by-eye check. On Thadrak brGyad stong p.233, Flash merged two lines of
the upper leaf (the draft had 7, Flash wrote 6). A dropped line and a removed invented line cannot be told apart without
the image, so the draft stays. Moving or adding the leaf-break marker does not count as a line change.

**Restores (run `revert-lines-6740`):** brGyad p.233 and p.289, gZungs 'dus p.260 (a dropped negation, from the rolling
audit) and Neyphug p.303. Neyphug p.131 was restored and then put back on the Flash text (run `unrevert-lines-6740`): the
scribe repeats that sentence, as checked by eye by tib-opus-translate-6948.

**Rolling audit:** 10 seeded written pages, judge B. 9/10 pass; 90 errors fixed, 8 introduced, 1 severe introduced
(restored). Controls 19/20.

### Diff-QA (Derek 2026-10-27 05:10Z)
`pass/diffqa.mjs` diffs each written page against its Yigdzin draft and classifies every changed span.
- **LOW** (auto-accepted): tsheg/merge only, a particle swapped within its class, or a one-letter fix to a Derge dictionary word.
- **RISKY**: everything else; negation, number, mantra, added/dropped and > 8 syllables always are.
- **Calibration** on 680 spans already judged: LOW is right on 94% of decided spans, RISKY on 86%. The four known severe
  introductions of the router-30 reads all classify RISKY.
- **RISKY spans** go to the leaf: `leafcheck audit-req --pages --spans`, judge B, 2 controls a page. A span the leaf does not
  show as corrected is put back to the draft (`diffqa.mjs merge`, `write`; runs `diffqa-6740-*`).
- **Pilot, 40 pages:** 155/210 risky spans confirmed (74%), 38 show the draft. 55 spans were put back on 24 pages.
- **Tranche 1** covers the 3,757 + 634 written pages that carry a severe-type risky span; results follow in #6740.

**Totals.** Strict P@5 = 35/75 = 0.47; lenient = 49/75 = 0.65.

**Where the misses come from.**
- **Subjects the sample lacks.** Strict misses concentrate in green lion, monochord, zodiac man and comet. For all four, the crop row shows the model finds the subject when it exists, so the 100K random sample (5 pages per book) most likely just has none. That is a recall limit of the pilot, not of the model.
- **Text pages.** SigLIP reads words: q15 comet returned four text pages about comets, and n06 two pages about the masonic triangle.

**Hubness.** 592 distinct pages fill 700 pilot top-10 slots, and only 2 pages appear in ≥ 5 queries:
- an ornamental Euclid title page;
- a pastedown with two bookplates. Bookplates repeat across every book of a provenance, so the full set will hold many near-copies of each.

The crop index has 695 distinct images in 700 slots and no hubs.

**Not done.** No filter at manifest time: blank pages and covers do not dominate, and the vectors are files, so a page can be dropped at serve time. The serving PR should:
- cap hits per book;
- suppress near-duplicate bookplates and blank pages, by vector similarity to a few exemplars or by #5122's page classes.

### Fetch fix (20K-page shard, gex45, 2026-10-26)
| | pilot (urllib, 24 threads in the GPU process, via images.sourcelibrary.org) | fix (`fetchlib.py`: 12 processes × 8 threads, keep-alive R2 S3 API) |
|---|---|---|
| end-to-end img/s | 15.8 | 44.4 / 43.1 (two 10K shards); chunk 000 shard 0: 45.9 |
| GPU busy | 0.33 | 0.95 / 0.98 |
| GPU-only img/s | 47.8 | 46.6 / 44.0 |
| vectors vs pilot path | — | same 512 pages: mean cosine 0.99999, min 0.9986 |

The card is now the limit. Batch 128 did not raise GPU-only throughput (44.4 img/s), so batch stays 64. VRAM peaks at 3.45 GB under the 0.6 cap.

### Manifest and cost (`build-full-manifest.mjs`, 2026-10-26 17:01Z)
- **Walked.** 335,016 books with pages, 30.59M pages. 21.55M have a usable archived master on images.sourcelibrary.org: 13.53M from 70,954 live books and 8.01M from hidden ones. 9.04M have no master, and 104 are on another host.
- **Cost.** Every row is one R2 GetObject (Class B, $0.36/M), $7.76 in total. There are no Worker requests, because the fetch bypasses the images.sourcelibrary.org Worker. R2 egress is free.
- **What the old path would have cost.** Through the Worker it would have been about $14: 21.55M Worker requests at $0.30/M plus the same reads.
- **Volume.** About 18 TB read at ~0.85 MB/page, which is inbound traffic to Hetzner. Vectors are 2.3 GB per 1M, about 50 GB in total.

### Chunk plan
- **Chunks.** 16 chunks of 1.5M rows (`chunk-009` holds 35K, the live tail). Each is about 9.5 h at 44 img/s, under a 12 h timeout and an 11.5 h between-shard deadline.
- **Queueing.** Tasks are named `zz-siglip2-full-cNNN`, so every digit-prefixed task sorts ahead of them. `siglip2-requeue.sh` (gex45 cron :02/:32) adds the next chunk only when nothing else is pending, keeps at most 2 embedding chunks pending or running, checks for ≥ 30 GB free on the root disk, and re-queues a deadline-stopped chunk as `-rK` (it resumes from its shard checkpoints).
- **ETA.** About 5.7 GPU-days, or around 2026-11-01 if no transcription task cuts in.

## 2026-10-26 · Router tests on idle quota: six test-next cells, judged against the image (#6740)

PRIOR ART: `2026-10-26-router-table-beta-binomial-6740.md` (#7417) ranked the cells. `2026-10-25-route-judge-qualitative-pilot-6740.md`
(#7376) is the instrument. The cells were added to its harness, `scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/judge.mjs`, in the
same shape; this is not a second harness.

**Instrument.** One judge, Opus through `claude -p`, reads one output at a time against the page image. The prompt is
the pilot's. The one change: on zh-dice the Kanripo leaf goes in as a REFERENCE (another edition; the image decides).
Each route has two wrong-page controls, and every control passed.

**Draws.** Seeded, one page per book, books not held. The exception is the Chinese Paddle lane: every one of its books
carries an OCR-only lane hold (`paddle-zh-5600-ocr-only` and the like). Those holds keep translation off; they are not
containment. They were allowed and every other hold was not.

**Correctors.** Each corrector read the STORED draft and the image:
- Opus: `correct.mjs`, one page a call, since there is one page per book.
- agy: `cli-ocr.mjs` correct mode, on the #5924 one-page template rebuilt from the live prompt (`fc-prompt.mjs`, hash check passed).

Both ran with `CANDIDATE_READS=off --fresh`. Their reads stay in the job's scratch. Nothing was written to pages,
books, page_revisions or R2.

**Name check (Chinese).** One Opus call per page with an accepted candidate gave the checker the image, the Kanripo
leaf and the page's accepted candidates, blind (27 pages). The checker named every person and place on the leaf.
`score` then flags a name the checker reads on the image that a candidate does not contain.

Strictly character by character, Opus drops from 29 to 17. Most flags are glyph variants, not wrong names (荆/荊,
温/溫, 恵/惠, 逹/達). The checker copied Kanripo's form as "the image's".

Classed by eye, two flags are different characters:
- **釋齊巳 / 齊已 / 齊己.** 己, 已 and 巳 are one glyph in this woodblock type, so this one is not separable from the image.
