## 2026-10-13 · What share of the pages readers are served carries a serious error, by lane? (#6691)
<!-- PRIOR ART: 2026-10-13-quality-sprint-round-2-public-frame-6056.md (10 random public books, 3 pages each: 4/30 pages serious) and the fortnightly spot check (_series-fortnightly-spot-check.md). Both draw uniform over books and cannot say which LANE the errors come from; this run stratifies by lane with one page per book. -->

**Question.** Every engine test so far scored engines on test sets. What do readers actually get today, and in which OCR × script × form × translation lane are the errors?

**Design.**
- **Frame.** 23,256 live books (`visible`, `pages_count > 0`) with a translated page.
- **Screen.** `served-draw.mjs`, seed 6691. The first 3,000 books in seeded order, uniform per book. For each, ONE translated page with `page_number > 0`, uniform over the book's translated pages, and its lane:
  - OCR engine family;
  - script family, from `books.language`;
  - form, from a catalogue heuristic (print, manuscript or e-text);
  - translation model family.
- **Strata.** The 20 lane cells with ≥ 10 screened books are strata; the rest is one stratum, `rest`. 10 books per stratum, 210 in all. A stratum's weight is its share of the screen.
- **Not reviewed.** 10 ETCSL Sumerian books: typed corpus text with a published translation and no image. No page in the screen was made by Claude, so no page needed a Gemini reviewer.
- **Review.** `run-reviewers.sh`: Opus via `claude -p`, 3 calls in flight, 22 packets of 9–10 books. The brief is the frozen `REVIEWER.md` plus the new `SERVED-ADDENDUM.md`, which asks for a review-vocabulary `kind` on each serious error, the form seen, a `not_this_leaf` call and a page verdict. 200 pages; $34.46 API-eq on the subscription, $0 billed.
- **Pilot.** The first book of each stratum (20 books) ran first; the full run used the same brief unchanged.
- **Scoring.** `served-score.mjs`: k of n books with Wilson 95% intervals (`kOfNBooks`). The headline is served pages only; exposure was taken at the draw.
- **By-eye checks.** Every `not_this_leaf` call that claimed a passage or more was re-read by the session with the image open.

**Result.** Measured 2026-10-13. 184 served books, 16 withheld. All 10 BDRC Tibetan pages in the sample were already withheld, so that stratum has no served book.

| | served books |
|---|---|
| serious error, unweighted | **62 of 184 (34%, 95% CI 27–41%)** |
| serious error, frame-weighted | 22% (19 strata, 93% of the frame) |
| a passage or the whole text not of this leaf, confirmed by eye | **10 of 184 (5%, 3–10%)**, all contained |
| image and text of different leaves (image fault, text right) | 3 of 184 (2%, 1–5%) |
| reviewer `not_this_leaf` calls, any size | 27 of 184 (15%, 10–21%) |
| page verdict, all 200 | show 74 · caveat 59 · do not show 67 |

- **Kinds** among served books with a serious error (a book can carry more than one): misread 21, confabulation 13, omission 11, mistranslation 10, illegible fill 9, added gloss 7, other 4, wrong leaf 3, carry-over 3, layout 3, show-through 1. Classes: O6 20, T7 19, O1 11, T10 8, T8 6, O5 5.
- **The 27 `not_this_leaf` calls**, sorted:
  - 10 contained (below).
  - 3 are image faults: the text is of the right IA leaf and the served image is not.
  - 1 page was already withheld.
  - 13 are a clause or line, kept as findings. Of these, 4 are seam completions, where the English finishes a sentence the leaf breaks off; 4 are a line or phrase of fill on a hard leaf; 3 are notes or image descriptions (a library stamp named wrongly, a heading, a citation); 1 is an edition-text recitation; 1 is the next page's sentence.
  - So "text not on the leaf" in the vocabulary's sense is 15%, but whole-passage invention is about a third of that.
- **By the form the reviewer saw (served):** manuscript 28 of 44 (64%, 49–76%); print 25 of 116 (22%, 15–30%); plate 6 of 13; blank 3 of 11.
- **Per stratum** (each n ≈ 10; intervals about ± 25–30 points): `report.md`. Highest rates: Latin manuscript / 3 Flash / lite translation 8 of 10; Greek manuscript 6 of 10; Paddle CJK with lite translation 6 of 10; lite CJK 6 of 10 and 4 of 5. Lowest: Latin print, 1–2 of 10 in each of the four big Latin-print strata; Tibetan Esukhia e-text 0 of 10.
- **Where repair pays most** (share × frame × rate, so volume counts): the two big Latin-print strata, Gemini lite or 3 Flash OCR with lite translation (≈ 940 and ≈ 670 books with a serious page; 1–2 of 10 each), then Latin print with 3 Flash both ways (≈ 580). The high-rate strata are each under 1% of the frame. With n = 10 these ranks are not stable: a stratum's 1/10 and 2/10 overlap almost entirely.

**Contained** (`containment-on-finding.md`: books held for `served-audit-6691`, the named page withheld with a `page_revisions` snapshot; undo `restore-withheld-translation.mjs`):

| book | page | what the leaf shows vs the stored text |
|---|---:|---|
| Year book reports 1332–1337 `69f32f7f876dd827cbc45808` | 201 | about 50 lines of law hand; 16 stored lines that loop stock phrases from line 5 |
| Thucydides, Vat. gr. 126 `6993837f50654cbbe2916cba` | 250 | Thuc. 5.45.4 legible; the top half of the stored text is invented ("περὶ τὴν Κύπρον") |
| Tangut Avatamsaka `69f1341dc8d07a681065333c` | 4 | ~30 varied columns; the transcription loops 4 glyphs; the English calls it a glossary |
| Zohar MS `69b3e677304c1c6b3950b41f` | 547 | Aramaic Zohar (Terumah, fol. 271); the stored text is a Hebrew essay that is not on the leaf |
| Disputatio de aetatibus `6a4f1ddbdd60b16646ccecf3` | 2 | Bregelana / Reusner / Meiovio; the stored text gives Königsberg / Kanter / 1717 |
| 臺灣番社風俗 `6992f412c8c6ac61574e753f` | 10 | plate 収貯; the English adds a 刈禾 reaping scene that is not on the leaf |
| Graha Kaumudi `69906d5364d44bd0a0ef5344` | 3 | 13 lines of verse; the English invents a planet table |
| Fragmenta Herculanensia `6953cc3677f38f6761be156e` | 172 | a drawing only; the English appends another page's apparatus |
| Khunrath, Urim & Thurim `6a267d456c1f37c9c4f391d6` | 21 | the leaf ends "Parentis mul-ti-"; the English goes on for four paragraphs |
| Genji Monogatari Ekotoba `69dfede38d34461cbe7f4db6` | 17 | the English is not a translation of the stored (correct) Japanese |

**Image faults, not contained** (the text is right, so withholding it fixes nothing):
- Galen vol. 8 (`69b0081de8cbd2498149b813`) and Sorel, *Réflexions sur la violence* (`69aeaaf167e6731bc136594f`). Both are `bulk_jp2` archives one leaf behind (#3368). In the Galen volume the shift starts between images 21 and 25: at image 20 image and text agree, from image 26 on the image is one leaf behind.
- 西洋新法曆書 (`69af118e7feb16bd9d149210`). The display images are swapped in pairs (page 3 ↔ 0004, page 4 ↔ 0003, 5 ↔ 6).

**What this teaches about sample size (for the weekly audit, #6688).**
- At 10 books a stratum, a Wilson interval spans about 50 points: 1/10 is 2–40% and 6/10 is 31–83%. Ten books separate only the extremes (Latin print vs manuscripts). To tell a 10% lane from a 25% lane (power 0.8) needs about 100 books per lane; ± 10 points at 30% needs about 80.
- The pooled served rate is already usable at n = 184 (± 7 points). A weekly audit should report the pooled rate and a handful of grouped lanes (print vs manuscript, Latin vs other scripts, lite vs Flash translation), each with ≥ 40 books. Cell-level rates should accumulate across weeks.
- One reviewer's `not_this_leaf` overcounts whole-page invention by about 3× (27 calls, 10 passages confirmed). The audit needs the by-eye step, or a second reader on those calls, before it quotes "invented".
- The lane frame is dominated by Latin print (≈ 70%). Proportional allocation would spend the audit where the rate is lowest, and ten books per cell spends it where the volume is smallest. A Neyman-style allocation (∝ share × √(p(1−p))) puts about 60% of the books in the big Latin-print strata and the rest in manuscripts and non-Latin print.
- Three image faults in 184 books (2%) are invisible to any text-only detector. The weekly audit must keep opening the image.

**Limits.**
- One AI reviewer (Opus) per page. Class and kind labels were unstable across reads in #6174 (Jaccard 0.55–0.67).
- 6 pages were marked low confidence and 68 medium.
- The strata's form is a catalogue heuristic; the reviewer's by-eye form is reported separately.
- The 13 fragment-level `not_this_leaf` calls were not each re-checked by eye.
- One page per book says nothing about a book's other pages.

*Replicated?* No. Data: `scripts/eval/results/spot-check/served-2026-10-13/`: `sample.json` (draw, lanes, exposure), `draw-log.json`, `screen.json.gz`, `reviews/`, `report.md`, `report.json`. The packets are the reviewer view of `sample.json` and are not committed.

## 2026-10-13 · Does "short source, long English" find title leaves that were given a chapter? (#6297)

PRIOR ART: `isExcess` in `scripts/lib/translate-core.mjs` (the `runaway` tier) does not judge a source under 300
characters; `scripts/lib/illegible-source-gate.mjs` refuses a page nobody could read, and a title leaf is legible.
#6297 proposed the raw signal "source under 200 characters, English over 600" and named 14 Tengyur pages.

**Design.** Rule (`isRecited`): source weight under 300 and English body over max(600, 3 × weight). Source weight
is the transcription with tags removed and their contents kept, a Han, kana or Hangul character counted 16. English
body is `bodyLen`, which leaves out notes, summaries and keywords. Read-only, $0, no model call. Detector:
`scripts/audit/recited-short-source.mjs`.

**Result.**

| set | pages | fired | what the fires are |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Tengyur title leaves withheld by eye (4 on #6048, 3 here), text from `page_revisions` | 7 | 7 | positive controls |
| The other 11 of the 14 pages #6297 named, read from image | 11 | 0 | a translated title with a summary and keywords; 3 are four-line ornate leaves with a short verse |
| 213 Tengyur volumes, after the withholds | 128,329 translated, 35 short | 0 | |
| Random draw of 60,000 pages, 34,335 translated | 208 short | 5 | all 5 wrong by text: English for an empty or `[RECITATION_BLOCKED]` source, or a heading followed by a page of prose |
| Every `page_type: title-page` with English | 52,477, 9,474 short | 537 (349 books; 442 pages on public books) | see below |

Of the 537, a seeded random 20 were read as text: on all 20 the English carries paragraphs the transcription does not
hold. Most open with a continuity note and then give the previous or next page's text under the half-title
("PRECEPTS", "LUCULLUS", "BOOK III"). Five of the 20 were opened as images; all five leaves hold one line. So the
class is wider than recitation from memory: the same shape is produced when a neighbouring page's text lands on a
half-title. The reader meets it the same way, as English that is not on the page.

The raw signal over-counts. It measured the whole English string, so a one-line title with a `<summary>` and
`<keywords>` passed 600 characters: 11 of its 14 Tengyur pages were that.

**What this does not show.** The 203 short pages the rule did not fire on were not opened, so this gives no recall
figure outside the 7 controls. "Wrong by text" assumes the transcription is complete: a leaf whose transcription
missed most of the page would also fire, and the English would still not have come from that leaf's reading.

*Replicated?* No. One run, one reader.

## 2026-10-13 · Quality sprint round 2: what does a random draw of the public library look like, and which defect classes repeat across rounds? (#6056)
<!-- PRIOR ART: round 1, `scripts/eval/results/spot-check/sprint-2026-10-07-r1/` (canon frame, PR #6059; it has no entry here), and the month-0 entry `2026-10-06-random-book-spot-check-canon-shelves-5914.md`. Same draw, brief and scorer; this is the first sprint round on the public frame. -->

**Question.** Round 1 drew from the canon shelves, which lean to manuscripts and non-Latin scripts (15 of 30 pages serious). What does the same instrument find in a uniform draw of the public library, and which classes now appear in 3 or more distinct books?

**Design.**
- **Draw.** `draw.mjs --frame public --seed 2026101302 --n 10`: 10 books uniform per book from 22,820 public books with 3 or more translated pages, then one run of 3 consecutive reader-reachable pages each. No book was rejected. All 30 images returned 200.
- **Review.** 2 Claude Opus subagents, 5 books each, `REVIEWER.md` with nothing added, every page read against its image. Verdicts are not edited. $0 API.
- **Register and cluster.** `register.mjs --dir … --forms forms.json` gives one row per moderate or serious finding (`findings.json`, 60 rows, 7 serious). `register.mjs --cluster` pools rounds 1 and 2 by distinct book (`sprint-clusters.json`). Frames are counted apart, never pooled into one rate.

**Result.** Measured 2026-10-13.

| | round 2 (public) | round 1 (canon) |
|---|---:|---:|
| pages with a serious error | 4 of 30 | 15 of 30 |
| books with a serious error on a read page | 4 of 10 | not tabulated |
| books with an on-sight defect | 7 of 10 | 10 of 10 |
| wrong leaf | 0 of 30 | not tabulated |

- **Served text only.** One drawn book (the Tibetan fragments, `69e78f6213e67bd16d4e6bc2`) has its English withheld, so a reader does not see its one serious finding. Among the 9 served books, 3 have a serious error on a read page. The scorer's own headline counts the first page of each run only: 0 of 9 served books (95% CI 0–30%).
- **The serious findings** (4 pages, 7 errors):
  - Law disputation, Jena 1635 (`6a42fb76feb36226e8f0c975` p5): long s read as f about ten times, so the tract's key term *sors* (the principal of a loan) is transcribed *fors, fortis, forte*. The English still follows the argument.
  - Caccini, *Le nuove musiche* (`69dea1ce4d19ec2e9ba75548` p22): *soave* read as "for ue" and translated "fiercely"; Love and the heart swap roles twice.
  - Münster, *Cosmographey* 1578 (`6a26bd05d6b178e5aad87607` p8): an eye-skip drops the clause in which Münster says nobody before him wrote such a book in German. It is absent from the English too.
  - Tibetan fragments p57 (withheld): two ritual measures mistranslated. The reviewer marks its reading of the cursive as low confidence.
- **Clean on the pages read:** Dostoevsky's *Podrostok* (1911, pre-reform Russian), a 1690 medical dissertation, the Leonardo facsimile (blank leaves and one label).
- **Clusters across rounds 1 and 2** (serious only, by distinct book): O6 misread carried into the English, 4 books (2 canon, 2 public; all four are print). It is the only class at 3 or more books. Next: T7, O3, T10, O5, O1, T8, O15 at 2 books each.
- **Record-level findings, not page errors:** an English pamphlet catalogued as Latin and so served with an English "translation" that rewrites its titles of office (Westcott, *Dreams*, `69c8a2246c6f3cc53c85e367`); a 1,558-page book with text on 25 pages; two books served as unsplit openings or two leaves to a photograph; apparatus handled three different ways on three adjacent pages of a PTS edition.

**A detector that does not work.** Both long-s misreads in this round land on real words (*sorte* → *forte*, *sors* → *fors*) or on a split token ("for ue"). A list of f-for-s non-words (*funt, eft, effe, ipfe, caufa* …) run over the 9 Latin and Italian pages of the three early-print books finds none of the misreads: the engine errs toward words that exist. A non-word list is therefore not a detector for this class, and none of the 9 pages keeps a literal ſ.

**Conclusion.** The public library reads far better than the canon shelves under the same instrument, and what goes wrong is different: no invented text and no wrong leaf in 30 pages, but single misread words and one dropped clause that the English then carries. O6 is the one general candidate so far and already has an owner (#5137). Two rounds are 20 books; the sprint's target is 50.

**Limits.**
- 10 books. A round's own rate swings by about ± 15 points by chance, and the two rounds are different frames.
- Reviewers are AI reading at stored image resolution. The Tibetan pages are marked low confidence by the reviewer.
- `forms.json` (print or MS) was assigned from the reviewers' structure notes and the catalogue, not by a separate look at the images.

*Replicated?* No. Data: `scripts/eval/results/spot-check/sprint-2026-10-13-r2/` (sample, packets, reviews, results, findings, report) and `scripts/eval/results/spot-check/sprint-clusters.json`.

## 2026-10-13 · Is Opus a better translator than Gemini 3.8 Flash Low on the #6559 Nahuatl books?

**Why.** On 2026-10-13 Derek switched the #6559 translation lane to Opus, on the evidence of #6545. The condition: first run a paired check on about 30 pages Gemini had already translated, with a blind judge from the other family. If Opus is not better, say so and stop.

**Design.**
- **Pages.** 10 consecutive pages (pp. 60–69) from each of 3 Nahuatl books: the *Sermonario* dedicated *A Iesu Christo S.N.* (`6acc3c2677e6be3481e74709`), the *Evangeliarium, epistolarium et lectionarium Aztecum* (`6acc3b31c1411f8cc628f943`), and Paredes's *Promptuario manual mexicano* (`6acc3ae4c1411f8cc628f4e5`). In each book this was the first run of 10 pages from p. 60 on that the Gemini reads covered (`selection.json`). The OCR on all of them is the Opus OCR written 2026-10-13.
- **Arms.**
  - Gemini: `cli-translate.mjs`, `agy -p`, `gemini-3.8-flash-low`. One page per call, seeded with its own previous page.
  - Opus: `claude-translate.mjs`, `claude -p --model opus` (resolved `claude-opus-5-5`), with translate-core's block prompt over p. 60–69. p. 60 had no seed, because no translation was stored.
- **Judge.** `agy`, `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, `run-cli-arm.py --kind judge` (`judge-prompt.md`). Each call had the page image, the OCR and both translations as A and B; the `<summary>`/`<keywords>` blocks were stripped from both. The judge scored each 1–5 for fidelity and listed omitted, added and mistranslated passages. A first run with a seeded A/B order showed heavy position bias, so every page was judged again with A and B swapped (`key-swap.json`). The scores are the mean of both orders (`score.py`).

**Result.**

| book | pages | Opus | Gemini | Opus − Gemini | judge preferred, O/G (2 orders × 10) | omitted O/G | added O/G | mistranslated O/G |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *Sermonario* | 10 | 3.40 | 4.10 | −0.70 | 5/15 | 27/13 | 8/10 | 45/17 |
| *Evangeliarium* | 10 | 3.80 | 3.60 | +0.20 | 11/9 | 13/19 | 6/7 | 35/38 |
| *Promptuario* | 10 | 3.55 | 4.15 | −0.60 | 5/15 | 29/12 | 9/13 | 27/19 |
| **all** | 30 | **3.58** | **3.95** | **−0.37** (bootstrap 95% CI −0.77 to +0.03) | 21/39 | 69/44 | 23/30 | 107/74 |

- Per page: Opus was higher on 7, tied on 10, and Gemini was higher on 13.
- **Position bias:** Opus − Gemini was +0.20 with Opus shown as A and −0.93 with Opus as B (n = 30 each). The judge preferred the same translation in both orders on only 17 of 30 pages.
- **Checked by eye (on the text):**
  - *Sermonario* p. 62 is on Romans 13:12, *induamur arma lucis*. Gemini's "armour of light" for *teotlahuiztli in tlanextlahuiztli* is right; Opus's "the shining radiance" is wrong.
  - Opus dropped a running header (*Sermonario* p. 64).
  - *Promptuario* p. 67: the OCR marks many doubtful words as `<unclear>`, and Opus copied those Nahuatl words through untranslated ("never will we <unclear>timiquizque</unclear>"). Gemini translated inside the tags.

**Limits.**
- The judge is the same family as the Gemini arm.
- The position effect is larger than the gap.
- n = 30, all Nahuatl prose (sermons, lectionary). No Maya or Kaqchikel pages were included.
- The seeding was unequal on p. 60 only.

**Decision.** None taken. Derek's rule was "if Opus is not better, say so and stop to ask". Under this judge Opus is not better, so the 48 untranslated #6559 books wait for his call (posted on #6559).

## 2026-10-13 · Does Opus translation hold its quality at 10 pages per call? (#6690)

**Decision it changes:** how much translation Opus can take on. #6545 routed Persian, Sanskrit, Chinese, Greek and Hebrew to Opus "where capacity allows". For OCR, Opus held its accuracy at 10 pages per call (#6388, PR #6443). If translation holds too, the same subscription covers several times more pages.

### Design

- **Pages:** 50, in five runs of 10 consecutive pages, one book per language. Each run starts at a #6545 panel page (the anchor) and takes the 9 pages after it.

  | run | book | pages | published translation |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Persian | Saʿdī, *Golestān* ch. 5 | 76–85 | Rehatsek 1888 (literal) |
  | Sanskrit | *Arthaśāstra* II.27–30 | 160–169 | Shamasastry 1915 (literal) |
  | Chinese | *Sanguo yanyi* ch. 4, with Mao's commentary | 22–31 | Brewitt-Taylor 1925 (free) |
  | Greek | Plato, *Republic* IX 571c–578b (Burnet) | 367–376 | Jowett 1892 (free) |
  | Hebrew | *Sefer ha-Yirah*, 1627 print | 37–46 | Kerber 2007 (literal; Vilna recension) |

- **Arms.** Both arms are Opus 5.5 via `claude -p` on the subscription, with no tools and the same pinned v13 translation prompt. Neither gets a previous-page translation as context.
  - **O1, one page per call.** The #6545 OPUS request: `buildTranslationPrompt` plus #6545's marker suffix. On the 5 anchor pages the request is byte-identical to #6545's, so the #6545 output is reused. The other 45 pages are new calls.
  - **O10, ten pages per call.** Production's block request (`buildBlockTranslationPrompt`, a `<translation page="N">` block per page) with the same marker suffix. A reply counts only if its blocks are exactly the 10 pages sent, in order; otherwise it is retried once and then refused whole (claude-ocr.mjs's rule).
  - The Persian run went first as a pilot. It split cleanly, so the other four followed unchanged.
- **References.**
  - Anchor pages keep their #6545 reference.
  - Persian, Sanskrit, Chinese and Greek: each new page gets a slice of the published translation. The slice is located by word overlap with both arms' English pooled, so neither arm is favoured, then widened by 40% at each end. The judge is told the excerpt may run into the neighbouring pages.
  - Hebrew: the 1627 print orders its sections differently from Kerber's Vilna text. Each page gets the Kerber sections it holds, listed by hand.
  - Spot checks: the slices run in page order and contain the expected landmarks (the Kashgar story, Shaodi's poem, the ship-superintendent chapter, the "lamentation" sentence of 578a).
- **Judge:** one judge, `gemini-3.8-flash-high` via `agy -p`, from the other model family as the issue asks. One item per call; each item holds the page with both arms, blind and shuffled. The rubric is #6545's `JUDGE-PROMPT-PRO.md`, unchanged: fidelity 1–5, omission, invention (including "boundary": text from the neighbouring page), reversal, page span, and error spans. Each item also carries the end of the previous page's source and the start of the next page's.
- **Controls** (all in the same round):
  - 10 planted errors in O1 copies (5 negations, 3 dropped clauses, a number, a name), shown beside O10. A catch must be located at the planted span.
  - 10 repeats with the labels reshuffled.
- **Bleed, measured two ways.**
  1. The judge's boundary inventions and seam-related accuracy spans.
  2. A mechanical count. A sentence of one arm's page is "moved" when ≥ 60% of its content words appear on the other arm's neighbouring page and < 40% on its own page. It is counted in both directions. On a synthetic test (6 sentences moved across 3 turns) it flagged all 3 turns and 4 of the 6 sentences.
- **Intervals:** 95%, 2,000 bootstrap draws by page. A second interval resamples books first and then pages within them, because pages of one book are not independent.

### Result

**Reads.**
- O10: 5 of 5 block replies split into exactly their 10 pages on the first try. No retry, no refusal, no fallback.
- O1: 45 of 45 new pages read.
- The judge returned all 70 items.

**Fidelity** (judge gemini-3.8-flash-high):

| | n | O1 | O10 | O10 − O1 [95% CI by page] | O10 better / worse / tie | omission flagged O1 / O10 | accuracy spans per page O1 / O10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **all** | 50 | **4.78** [4.64, 4.90] | **4.48** [4.32, 4.64] | **−0.30 [−0.54, −0.08]**; by book then page [−0.60, −0.02] | 10 / 23 / 17 | 4% / 22% | 0.34 / 0.98 |
| Persian | 10 | 4.9 | 4.8 | −0.1 [−0.4, +0.2] | 1 / 2 / 7 | 0% / 0% | 0.3 / 0.2 |
| Sanskrit | 10 | 4.6 | 4.3 | −0.3 [−0.8, +0.3] | 3 / 6 / 1 | 10% / 40% | 0.6 / 1.5 |
| Chinese | 10 | 4.6 | 4.3 | −0.3 [−0.9, +0.4] | 4 / 6 / 0 | 10% / 30% | 0.6 / 1.4 |
| Greek | 10 | 4.8 | 4.7 | −0.1 [−0.5, +0.3] | 2 / 3 / 5 | 0% / 10% | 0.2 / 0.5 |
| Hebrew | 10 | 5.0 | 4.3 | −0.7 [−1.1, −0.3] | 0 / 6 / 4 | 0% / 30% | 0.0 / 1.3 |

- **Reversals:** none in either arm. Major accuracy spans: none in O1; 2 in O10.
  - Hebrew p.40: "A commandment is worth keeping whatever harm may come." The source says the commandment *guards you* from all harm, as O1 has it.
  - Chinese p.30: an interpolated narrative sentence.
- **Pages worse.** On all 23 pages where O10 is worse, it gets 4 against O1's 5, except two pages that get 3.
- **What O10 loses** (the judge's spans, checked by eye on four pages) are small items:
  - a dropped qualifier ("Commandant of Cavalry" for 越騎校尉, losing *Yue*);
  - a term or a list item left out (*saṃmohana* from the arts taught; *puccham*, "tail", from the hides rendered annually);
  - commentary left untranslated in `<unclear>` (Chinese);
  - a wrong reading ("until the middle of the month" for רובו של חדש, "most of the month"; "four times the shank" for चतुर्हस्त उत्सेधः, "height four cubits").

  O1 has some of these too, and is the worse arm on 10 pages. One example is "ten armed men" for 武士十八人 on Chinese p.22.
- **Shorter English.** O10's page body (notes and summary removed) is a median 0.91 of O1's (p10 0.82). O10 also writes about half as many `<note>`s (158 against 298) and far fewer inline `<gloss>`es. On the shortest page (Arthaśāstra p.168, 0.65) the difference is mostly apparatus. But the judge also found three content slips there.
- **Position in the block does not matter much.** O10 − O1 by page position: first −0.0 (n = 5), 2nd–5th −0.3, 6th–9th −0.4, 10th −0.2. Quality does not fall away towards the end of a call.

**Page-boundary bleed (text moved between pages): small.**
- **Mechanical count:** 0 moved sentences in either direction across all 45 page turns.
- **Judge:** boundary inventions on 3 pages of O10 and 4 of O1. Seam-related accuracy spans (a straddling verb rendered on the wrong side, a catchword or a hanging clause dropped or welded) number 12 on 7 pages of O10, against 7 on 6 pages of O1.
  - The clearest case is Greek pp. 371–372: O10 put θρέψει, the first word of p.372, at the end of p.371, and the judge marked it on both pages.
  - So bleed in O10 happens at the scale of a word or clause at the turn. It is not whole sentences, and it is not the main source of the gap.

**Usage per 100 pages**, from the CLI's own usage block per call:

| | calls | output tokens | cache-write tokens | list-price equivalent | seconds per page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 (45 pages measured) | 100 | 202 K | 1.25 M | $14.20 | 22.8 |
| O10 (50 pages) | 10 | 174 K | 0.22 M | $5.29 | 16.4 |

- O10 uses about **2.7× less** per page at list price. Most of O1's extra cost is the CLI's fixed prompt overhead, written to cache on every call. Output per page is only 1.16× higher in O1.
- The OCR figure (~8×, #6443) does not carry over, because translation is dominated by output.
- **Weekly-meter percent per 100 pages: not measurable on this account today.** The meter is an integer and the account is shared.
  - From 15:55 to 16:30 UTC, both arms ran ($9.04 list) and the weekly meter rose 2 points (4 → 6).
  - From 16:30 to 17:20 UTC this job made no Claude call, and the meter still rose 3 points (6 → 9) from other jobs.
  - Upper bound, attributing the whole arm window to the arms: O1 ≤ 4.7 and O10 ≤ 1.8 weekly-points per 100 pages. The true figures are lower by an unknown share.
  - If the meter tracks list-equivalent usage, the ratio between the arms is the 2.7× above.

**The judge.**
- Planted errors: located 10 of 10, and scored lower than the same page's unplanted O1 on 8 of 10. The two misses were dropped clauses on pages where O1 itself had a 3 or a 4.
- Repeats: 16 of 20 scores identical, mean absolute difference 0.20. The sign of O10 − O1 matched on 8 of 10 repeated pages.

### Threats and limits

- **One judge, one family:** Gemini, the other family from both arms. The arms are the same model, so self-preference cannot favour either. There is no second judge to check the size of the gap. #6545 found its Opus and Pro judges agree only moderately (alpha ≈ 0.6).
- **n = 50 pages in 5 books.** Per-language intervals are wide, and only Hebrew's excludes 0 on its own. The pooled result holds under the book-level bootstrap, but only just (upper end −0.02).
- **References for 45 of the 50 pages were cut by script** (40 pages), or listed by section by hand from a different recension (Hebrew, 9 pages). The same reference serves both arms on each page, so the paired difference is fair. Absolute levels are less certain than #6545's.
- **Hebrew's −0.7.** Its pages are two-column prints whose OCR order does not follow reading order. O1 often noted the column order; O10, working across ten such pages, welded clauses across column breaks. The loss may be specific to this layout.
- **Not tested here:**
  - 3.8 Flash on these pages. Whether Opus at 10 per call still beats 3.8 Flash (+0.47 to +0.52 at one per call in #6545, under a different judge) needs a same-round arm.
  - 5 pages per call.
  - A previous-page context for O1.
- **Weekly percent:** see above. Only list-equivalent usage is measured exactly.

### Routing

- **Keep Opus translation at one page per call** where #6545 routes it. Ten per call is about 2.7× cheaper, but it loses 0.30 on the judge's 1–5 scale, mostly through small omissions, and Hebrew loses 0.7.
- **Before using ten per call to stretch capacity,** add a 3.8 Flash arm to these 50 pages and judge all three arms in one round. If O10 still clearly beats 3.8 Flash, ten per call is the better use of a limited Opus allowance than leaving pages to 3.8 Flash. The interval here does not settle that.

*Measure:* judged against a published translation by one cross-family AI judge. It is not accuracy in the sense of eval-design §2. *Grade:* moderate-to-low. 50 pages in 5 books, one judge, script-cut references, and a judge that passed its plant and repeat controls. *Replicated?* No.

*Cost:* $0. Opus through `claude -p` and Gemini through `agy -p`, both on the subscription. No API key, no database write.

*Files:* `scripts/eval/opus10-6690/` (load-runs.mjs, run-claude.py, build-refs.py, build-packet.py, score.py), `scripts/eval/results/opus10-6690/{scores.json, key.json}`. The arm outputs, references and judge packets quote published translations and stay on the box (`$JOB_SCRATCH/w/`).

## 2026-10-13 · Does the Opus read pass the calibration gate (#6559)?

**Why.** Derek decided on 2026-10-12 that Opus reads the Nahuatl and Mayan-language books. The brief set a gate before any write: a blind judge from the other model family; mean fidelity ≥ 4.0; at least 2 of 3 planted errors caught; and no read that invents text.

**Design.**
- **Reader:** `scripts/batch/claude-ocr.mjs` (Opus `claude-opus-5-5`, sealed `claude -p`, 10 pages per call, live OCR prompt v19.1 with the orthography slot).
- **Calibration set:** 150 pages, all read: *Cathecismo cenca yn tech monequi…* (1683, Nahuatl print, 16 pp); the Códice Aubin, León y Gama's copy (Nahuatl manuscript, 78 pp); *Libro de pláticas* (1662, Kaqchikel manuscript), pp. 1–56.
- **Blind sample:** 5 text pages per book, drawn with a seeded RNG (`build-packet.mjs.txt`). Plants: 3 copies of reads, one per book: about 8 words dropped from mid-paragraph (Aubin), an invented Nahuatl line (Cathecismo), and one respelled word, *ruyaom → royaom* (Kaqchikel). The 18 items ran under random ids. The judge saw the image and one transcription only, with no engine names; the key stayed on l7a.
- **Judge:** Gemini through `agy` on the main box (`judge-prompt.md`). The brief named 3.1 Pro, but every call failed on 2026-10-13: 3.1 Pro had been withdrawn from `agy`, which now offers only 3.8 Flash Low/Medium/High plus Claude models. So the judge is **gemini-3.8-flash-high**, the strongest Gemini still offered.

**Result.**

| book | n | fidelity per page | mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| Códice Aubin copy (Nahuatl MS) | 5 | 4, 4, 4, 4, 3 | 3.8 |
| Cathecismo 1683 (Nahuatl print) | 5 | 4, 4, 4, 5, 2 | 3.8 |
| Libro de pláticas (Kaqchikel MS) | 5 | 4, 4, 4, 3, 4 | 3.8 |
| **all** | **15** | | **3.80** |

- **Plants caught: 3 of 3.** The dropped words were quoted exactly (fidelity 2). The invented line was quoted exactly (fidelity 2). The respelling was listed as a misread (fidelity 4, as the rubric gives for one word-level slip).
- **Invented text on real pages: one flag, and it is the judge's error.** On Cathecismo p. 11 the judge called *huan … çencane- / chtequipachohua yca mochi innoani-* "a garbled duplicate line". Checked by eye against the image (2026-10-13), both lines are printed on the page, and the Opus read matches the page line for line. Its one true error on that page is *ocçepa* → *occepa* (a dropped cedilla). Rescored by eye, that page is 4, and the mean would be 3.93: still under the gate.
- **Error profile:** 0 dropped and 0 invented on the other 14 real pages. The judge listed 31 word-level misreads (mean 2.1 per page) and 10 normalisations. These were not checked by eye; the p. 11 false positive shows the judge's lists contain errors of its own.
- **Reads:** 150 of 150 calibration pages ok, 0 page-marker refusals; about $0.05/page at list price on the subscription.

**Caveats.**
- n = 15 pages from 3 books, one judge, one run; no A-vs-A noise floor.
- The judge is 3.8 Flash. The screening eval found that model the *weaker* reader of these languages (it normalises Mayan letters), so as a judge it may mark correct colonial spellings as misreads.
- The 0.2 gap to the gate is within one page's rescoring.

**What it means.** By the brief's rule, the Opus lane does not clear the gate as measured, and nothing was written. Opus never invented text in this sample and kept the orthography; its errors are letter-level. The decision owed: accept 3.8–3.9 with these caveats and apply, or re-judge with a stronger judge (a second judge family, or by-eye spot checks of the listed misreads) before deciding. Owner: #6559.

**Artifacts.** `scripts/eval/results/opus-ocr-calibration-6559/`: `KEY.json` (uid → page, plants), `judge-prompt.md`, `judge-out-gemini-3.8-flash-high.jsonl`, `build-packet.mjs.txt`. The packet (`items.json`) is on branch `eval/blind-judge-6559`.

*Replicated?* No.

## 2026-10-13 · OCR route: does Opus correcting the stored text in place match lane B (Gemini read + Opus adjudication)? (#6694)

**Frame.** `results/run/queue-next-1000.json` ranks 201–300 minus the one `lane_block` book (Theatrum regularium):
99 books, 976 pages chosen by `driver.mjs select` as main200 was (756 by page views, the rest a seeded spread).
Latin 490, Chinese 166, German 160, Greek 100, Arabic 50, Hebrew 10 pages. Same pages, same stored text in both arms
(0 pages changed between the arms' snapshots). Nothing written until the verdict.

**Arms.**
- **A, lane B unchanged:** `cli-ocr.mjs read --model=gemini-3.8-flash-low` (3 at a time; the 41 failed reads were read
  once more, 23 still failed), then `driver.mjs compare → packets (T = 0.01) → adjudicate (Opus, 8 at a time) → decide`.
- **B, Opus corrects in place:** new `scripts/batch/ocr-convergence/correct.mjs`. One sealed `claude -p --model opus
  --restricted --tools Read` call per book, with that book's 10 images and 10 stored texts in the folder. It uses the
  live OCR prompt plus a correction block. For each page the answer is a corrected transcription, `UNCHANGED`, or
  `CONTAIN: reason`, under `===== PAGE pNN =====` markers. A page with no answer, no marker, or a transcript showing it
  never opened its image or draft is "no answer", never a write. The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY strip of #6589 is kept.
  A correction that normalises to the stored text counts as `keep`. A correction in a translate-lane book is `defer`,
  by the same rule as A.

| action | A (lane B) | B (correct) |
|---|---:|---:|
| agree (A: CER < 0.01) | 83 | — |
| keep (stored text stands) | 331 | 167 (160 UNCHANGED + 7 no-op corrections) |
| write | 177 | 689 |
| defer (translate lane) | 12 | 120 |
| residual (A: merge or low confidence) | 336 | — |
| contain | 12 | 0 |
| no second read / no answer / pending | 23 / — / 2 | 0 |

The two arms' final texts differ on 806 pages in 98 books. They agree on 170, mostly where both kept the stored text.

**Judging (blind, as #6694 sets out).** 196 differing pages (≤ 2 per book, seeded) plus 40 agreeing controls. Each
page went to a fresh Opus (sealed, chunks of 5) and to `gemini-3.8-flash-high` via agy (one page per call). Each judge
saw the image, the stored text S and the two revisions under per-page X/Y labels (`JUDGE.md` v1). It rated each
revision better, same or worse than S, and preferred one of the two.

Every one of the 236 Opus verdicts shows the image opened. For Gemini, only verdicts whose tool-gate log shows
`view_file` count. In the first pass 12 of 27 lacked it: 9 said "no image" and 3 answered without opening the image.
The request wrapper (not the brief) then told the judge to open the attachment first. The 12 were re-run, and the
final 236 all opened the image.

| group | judged | Opus: B worse / changed | Gemini: B worse / changed | Opus: A worse / changed | Gemini: A worse / changed | Opus pref A–B–same | Gemini pref A–B–same |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Latin | 116 | 1 / 98 | 3 / 98 | 0 / 22 | 0 / 22 | 4–78–16 | 10–76–12 |
| German | 41 | 0 / 32 | 5 / 32 | 1 / 8 | 1 / 8 | 1–25–6 | 6–22–4 |
| Greek | 26 | 0 / 20 | 0 / 20 | 0 / 5 | 0 / 5 | 0–17–3 | 0–17–3 |
| Chinese | 41 | 0 / 34 | 1 / 34 | 0 / 4 | 0 / 4 | 0–28–6 | 2–25–7 |
| Arabic | 10 | 0 / 10 | 0 / 10 | 0 / 6 | 0 / 6 | 1–8–1 | 2–7–1 |
| Hebrew | 2 | 0 / 2 | 0 / 2 | 0 / 1 | 0 / 1 | 0–2–0 | 1–1–0 |
| **all** | 236 | **1 / 196** (0.5%, CI 0–1.5) | **9 / 196** (4.6%, CI 2.0–7.7) | 1 / 46 | 1 / 46 | 6–158–32 | 21–148–27 |

- B "better than stored" on its changed pages: Opus 173 of 196, Gemini 167 of 196.
- Head-to-head (losses minus wins vs A): Opus −77.6 pts (CI −84.7 to −69.9); Gemini −64.8 pts (CI −74.0 to −55.1).
- Controls: all 40 were pages where both arms kept the stored text; 0 worse. One control note found a stored misread
  both arms missed ('Scabra' for the printed 'Exesa').
- CIs are book-clustered bootstraps (`pareto-stats.mjs clusterCI`).
- Gemini's 9 "B worse" pages are mostly single-letter disputes with Opus: halbe-/halb-, Cosa/Consa, jezigen/jetzigen,
  Geseze/Gesetze, krut/kraut, gibet/gesetzet, and one Chinese numeral. One is a real loss: on Fludd's anatomy amphitheatre
  p.6, B marked a legible John 8 inscription unclear. Both judges agree on one: *Aphorismi confessariorum* p.146, where
  B changed the page number 342 to 142.
- German carries the highest Gemini rate: 5 of 32.

**Preregistered rule.** Adopt B iff, under both judges, B's worse rate is ≤ 5% of its changed pages and its
head-to-head is ≤ 5 points. Opus: 0.5% and −77.6, pass. Gemini: 4.6% and −64.8, pass. **Rule outcome: B.** The Gemini
interval runs to 7.7%, so the 5% bar is met on the point estimate, not with room.

**Write gate (40 of B's writes, blind, `AUDITOR.md`).**
- Opus: 37 better, 3 same, 0 worse.
- Gemini 3.8 Flash high: 36 better, 1 same, **3 worse** (40 of 40 opened the image). All 3 are in Greek books:
  - Nonnus *Dionysiaca* (Cunaeus) p.130: *nouam/nouum* and the æ endings, in the Latin;
  - *Anthologia* p.406: *κενὸς ἥξεις / κερδοπλήξας*;
  - Ptolemy *Tetrabiblos* p.18: *σειρῶδες / στειρῶδες*.

  The judge found Greek 0 of 20.
- Each is a direct Opus/Gemini disagreement about the leaf. 3 > 2/40, so the gate is **STOP**: none of B's 689 writes
  were applied.
- main200a passed a Gemini 3/40 as GO after relabelling those pages. This run follows the rule as written; whether to
  write B's pages is a decision for Derek (#6694).

**Contained (containment-on-finding.md).** A's Opus adjudicator, with the image open, found the stored text invented
or garbled ("neither read is usable") on 12 pages in 8 books. These were contained with `driver.mjs apply --no-writes`:
hold `ocr-unsettled-6420` (7 new holds, *Sancai tuhui* juan 85 already held), English withheld (12 revisions), plus
99 `book_checks` rows. The pages:
- Pal. lat. 1339 p.6, Pal. lat. 1340 p.11, Pal. lat. 1369 p.296
- Codex Gigas p.1
- *Etymologicum magnum* p.3
- *Sancai tuhui* juan 85 pp.56, 85, 113
- *Huiming jing* pp.19, 126, 127
- a *Thousand and One Nights* MS flyleaf p.11

B said CONTAIN on none of the 976 pages, these 12 included: it wrote a correction for each.

**Cost.**

| | A (lane B) | B (correct) |
|---|---|---|
| Opus calls | 35 adjudication chunks (870 pages); list-price equivalent $88.81, 2.2 Opus-hours | 98 calls (+7 pilot calls); list-price equivalent $96.07, 5.7 Opus-hours |
| Gemini calls | 1,109 `gemini-3.8-flash-low` reads (2 quota stops of 30 min, 4 timeouts); about 6 hours wall-clock | none |

- Judging used 48 Opus calls and 251 Gemini 3.8 Flash high calls. The audit used 4 Opus and 41 Gemini calls.
- Everything ran on subscriptions ($0 spend). "% of week" was not measured: `climits` is not on this box.
- B costs about the same Opus as A's adjudication step and saves every Gemini read. But it changes about 4× as many
  pages, so it also queues about 4× as many re-translations (`translation_stale`) when written.

**Replicated?** No: one run, one Opus read per page in each arm. The Opus judge grades Opus's own corrections, so its
1/196 may carry self-preference. The cross-family judge is the binding one, and it sits at the bar.

**Artifacts.**
- `scripts/batch/ocr-convergence/results/run/q300/`: arm A, with pages.json, frame, compare, adjudications, decisions.
- `q300/arm-b/`:
  - B's decisions and call log;
  - `reads.tar.gz` (the corrected texts in the claude-ocr read-dir shape, which `cli-ocr.mjs apply` can write);
  - `judge/` (frame, key, both judges' verdicts, result.json.gz);
  - `audit/`.
- Code: `correct.mjs`, `judge-6694.mjs`, `JUDGE.md`. `driver.mjs`'s Gemini audit now counts only verdicts that opened
  the image.

**After (2026-10-14, job opus-route-6694).** Derek overrode the audit stop.
- q300 B's writes went through `cli-ocr.mjs apply` with the shared-words guard on and `--mark-stale=convergent-ocr-6420`:
  - **600 written** (Latin 356, German 124, Greek 63, Arabic 38, Hebrew 10, Chinese 9);
  - 17 refused by the guard;
  - excluded: pages in held books, the contained pages, and the 3 disputed Greek pages.
